body.tip_zh: body 的 o 唸嘴巴張大的 [ɑ]，不要照拼字唸成圓唇的 [o]，變成「波迪」。重音在第一音節 [bɑ]，第二音節 [dɪ] 短而輕。美式英語裡，夾在兩個母音中間的 [d] 常唸成舌尖在齒齦上快速輕彈一下，不用用力。nobody 的後半部也是同樣的唸法。
body.tip_en: The o in body is the wide-open [ɑ]; don't read it as the rounded [o], making “bo-di”. The stress is on the first syllable [bɑ], and the second syllable [dɪ] is short and light. In American English, a [d] between two vowels is often a quick, light tap of the tongue tip on the ridge, with no force. The second half of nobody is said the same way.

examples.en: Exercise is good for your body.
examples.zh: 運動對身體很好。

examples.en: Point to each part of your body.
examples.zh: 指出你身體的每個部位。

boil.tip_zh: boil 的 oi 唸 [ɔɪ]：嘴巴先張開略圓唸 [ɔ]，再滑向「伊」，接著舌尖往上頂住上排牙齒後方，完成暗 [l]。常見錯誤是唸成「波伊歐」三拍，或省掉 [l]，聽起來像 boy。整個字是一個音節，[ɔɪ] 和 [l] 要連起來。它和 oil 押韻；和 bowl [o]、bell [ɛ] 比較，差在母音。
boil.tip_en: The oi in boil says [ɔɪ]: start with an open, slightly rounded [ɔ], glide toward “ee”, then lift the tongue tip behind the upper teeth to finish the dark [l]. Common mistakes are three beats like “bo-yi-o”, or dropping [l] so it sounds like boy. The whole word is one syllable, with [ɔɪ] and [l] linked. It rhymes with oil; compared with bowl [o] and bell [ɛ], the difference is the vowel.

examples.en: Wait for the water to boil.
examples.zh: 等水煮開。

examples.en: Mom will boil some eggs for breakfast.
examples.zh: 媽媽會煮幾顆蛋當早餐。

book.tip_zh: book 的母音是短而放鬆的 [ʊ]，常被拉長成 [u]，聽起來像 boo-k。[ʊ] 嘴唇只微微圓、時間很短，跟 look、cook 是同一個音。結尾 [k] 舌根頂住上顎就停，不要再多送出一個「ㄜ」。練習時可以把 book、look、cook 連著唸，三個字的母音都要一樣短。
book.tip_en: The vowel in book is a short, relaxed [ʊ]; it is often stretched into [u], so it sounds like boo-k. For [ʊ] the lips are only slightly rounded and the sound is short, the same as in look and cook. For the final [k], the back of the tongue presses the roof of the mouth and stops; don't add an extra 'uh'. Practice book, look and cook in a row; all three vowels should be equally short.

examples.en: I am reading a book about dogs.
examples.zh: 我正在讀一本關於狗的書。

examples.en: Can I borrow your book, please?
examples.zh: 可以借我你的書嗎？

book.spelling_zh: oo 在這裡唸短的 [ʊ]，不是長的 [u]。
book.spelling_en: oo here is the short [ʊ], not the long [u].

bookstore.tip_zh: 重音在前面的 book。[k] 和 [st] 接在一起時，中間常多插母音，唸成 book-ku-su-tore。[k] 只在舌根卡一下就接 [s]，[s] 後面的 [t] 不送氣、聽起來接近 [d]；結尾 [ɔr] 嘴巴張圓再捲舌。把它想成 book 加 store，中間不停頓，後半的 store 稍微輕一點。
bookstore.tip_en: The stress is on the first part, book. Where [k] meets [st], learners often insert vowels and say book-ku-su-tore. Just catch [k] briefly at the back of the tongue and go straight into [s]; the [t] after [s] has no puff of air and sounds close to [d]. For the final [ɔr], open the mouth round, then curl the tongue. Think of it as book plus store with no pause between them, the second part a little lighter.

examples.en: There is a new bookstore near my school.
examples.zh: 我學校附近有一家新的書店。

examples.en: We bought two comic books at the bookstore.
examples.zh: 我們在書店買了兩本漫畫。

bored.tip_zh: bored 只有一個音節，-ed 只唸 [d]，不要唸成兩拍的 bor-ed。結尾是 [rd]：[ɔ] 之後舌頭往後捲成 [r]，再讓舌尖輕點上排牙齦收 [d]。少了 [d] 就像 bore；它和 board（木板）的唸法相同。可以把 bored 和 bore 輪流唸，仔細聽有沒有結尾的 [d]。
bored.tip_en: Bored has only one syllable; -ed is just [d], so don't say two beats, bor-ed. It ends in [rd]: after [ɔ], curl the tongue back for [r], then tap the tongue tip on the gum ridge for [d]. Without [d] it sounds like bore. It is pronounced the same as board. Alternate bored and bore, and listen carefully for the final [d].

examples.en: I am bored. Let's play a game.
examples.zh: 我好無聊，我們來玩遊戲吧。

examples.en: The kids felt bored on the long bus ride.
examples.zh: 孩子們在長途公車上覺得很無聊。

boring.tip_zh: 第一音節 [bɔr] 的 [r] 常被省掉，唸成 bo-ing。[ɔ] 之後舌頭要往後捲，再順勢滑進 [ɪŋ]，舌尖不碰上顎，也不要換成 [l]。結尾 [ŋ] 舌根貼住上顎、氣從鼻子出來，不要收成 [n]。重音在第一音節，第二音節 [rɪŋ] 輕而短。
boring.tip_en: The [r] in the first syllable [bɔr] is often dropped, giving bo-ing. After [ɔ], curl the tongue back, then glide into [ɪŋ]; the tongue tip doesn't touch the roof of the mouth, and don't switch it to [l]. For the final [ŋ], the back of the tongue presses the roof of the mouth and air goes out the nose; don't end with [n]. Stress the first syllable; the second, [rɪŋ], is light and short.

examples.en: This movie is so boring.
examples.zh: 這部電影好無聊。

examples.en: Math is not boring when we play games.
examples.zh: 我們玩遊戲的時候，數學一點也不無聊。

born.tip_zh: born 結尾有 [r] 和 [n] 兩個子音，常只剩其中一個。順序是：嘴巴張圓發 [ɔ]，舌頭往後捲成 [r]，最後舌尖貼上排牙齦發 [n]，三步都要聽得到。它和 bored 只差最後一個音：born 收鼻音 [n]，bored 收 [d]。練習 I was born 時，born 要唸成一拍，不要拖成兩個音節。
born.tip_en: Born ends with two consonants, [r] and [n], and learners often keep only one. The order: open the mouth round for [ɔ], curl the tongue back for [r], then press the tongue tip on the upper gum ridge for [n]; all three steps should be heard. It differs from bored only in the last sound: born ends in nasal [n], bored in [d]. When practicing I was born, say born as one beat; don't drag it into two syllables.

examples.en: I was born in Taipei.
examples.zh: 我在台北出生。

examples.en: My baby sister was born in May.
examples.zh: 我的小妹妹是五月出生的。

borrow.tip_zh: 重音在第一音節 [bɑ]，嘴巴要張大。中間的 rr 只唸一個 [r]，舌頭往後捲、不碰上顎，常被唸成 [l] 變成 ba-low。結尾 [o] 嘴唇從半開收圓，跟 tomorrow 的結尾一樣。可以先慢慢唸 [bɑ]、[ro] 兩段，再加快連成一個字。
borrow.tip_en: The stress is on the first syllable [bɑ], with the mouth wide open. The double rr is just one [r]: curl the tongue back without touching the roof of the mouth; it is often turned into [l], giving ba-low. For the final [o], the lips move from half-open to round, like the end of tomorrow. First say [bɑ] and [ro] slowly as two parts, then speed up and join them into one word.

examples.en: Can I borrow your eraser?
examples.zh: 可以借我你的橡皮擦嗎？

examples.en: I borrow books from the library every week.
examples.zh: 我每個星期都向圖書館借書。

boss.tip_zh: boss 的母音是嘴巴張大的 [ɑ]，下巴往下，像看醫生時說「啊」。如果嘴巴只半開、唸得短，就會變成 bus 的 [ʌ]。結尾 ss 只吹出一個 [s]，不要再加母音唸成「巴斯」。可以把 boss 和 bus 連著唸，比比看嘴巴張開的大小。
boss.tip_en: The vowel in boss is [ɑ] with the mouth wide open and the jaw dropped, like saying 'ah' at the doctor's. If the mouth is only half open and the vowel is short, it turns into the [ʌ] of bus. The final ss is a single hissed [s]; don't add a vowel after it. Say boss and bus one after the other and compare how wide your mouth opens.

examples.en: My dad's boss is very nice.
examples.zh: 我爸爸的老闆人很好。

examples.en: Who is the boss in this game?
examples.zh: 這個遊戲裡誰是老大？

boss.variant_zh: 也有很多美國人唸 [bɔs]，嘴唇稍圓。
boss.variant_en: Many Americans also say [bɔs], with slightly rounded lips.

both.tip_zh: 結尾的 [θ] 常被唸成 [s]，聽起來像 bose，也有人換成 [f]。唸完 [o] 後，把舌尖輕輕伸到上下排牙齒之間吹氣，聲帶不震動。[o] 要從半開滑到嘴唇收圓，不要只唸成短短的「歐」。照鏡子檢查：發 [θ] 時應該看得到舌尖。
both.tip_en: The final [θ] is often turned into [s], so it sounds like bose; some learners use [f] instead. After [o], put the tongue tip lightly between the upper and lower teeth and blow, with no voice. The [o] should glide from half-open to rounded lips, not a short flat 'o'. Check in a mirror: you should see your tongue tip on [θ].

examples.en: Both of my parents like coffee.
examples.zh: 我爸媽兩個都喜歡咖啡。

examples.en: I like both cats and dogs.
examples.zh: 貓和狗我都喜歡。

bottle.tip_zh: 美式發音中，bottle 中間的 tt 會變成輕快的閃音：舌尖輕彈一下上排牙齦，聽起來像很快的 [d]。結尾 [ḷ] 沒有母音，舌尖停在上排牙齦、舌頭後部抬起，不要唸成「八透」或把 l 省掉。
bottle.tip_en: In American English the tt in the middle of bottle becomes a quick flap: the tongue tip taps the upper gum ridge once, sounding like a fast [d]. The final [ḷ] has no vowel: keep the tongue tip on the upper gum ridge with the back of the tongue raised. Don't say 'ba-tou' or drop the l.

examples.en: Please fill my water bottle.
examples.zh: 請幫我把水壺裝滿。

examples.en: There is a bottle of milk in the fridge.
examples.zh: 冰箱裡有一瓶牛奶。

bottom.tip_zh: bottom 的結尾是 [əm]，最後雙唇一定要閉起來，這是它和 bottle（舌尖收 [ḷ]）的差別。第二音節是弱讀的 [ə]，不要唸成響亮的 tom。中間的 tt 美式唸得很輕快，接近一個短短的 [d]。練習 at the bottom 時，重音放在 bot。
bottom.tip_en: Bottom ends in [əm], so the lips must close at the end; that is how it differs from bottle, which ends with the tongue tip for [ḷ]. The second syllable is a weak [ə]; don't say a loud 'tom'. The tt in the middle is quick in American English, close to a short [d]. When practicing at the bottom, put the stress on bot.

examples.en: Write your name at the bottom of the page.
examples.zh: 把你的名字寫在這一頁的最下面。

examples.en: The ball is at the bottom of the pool.
examples.zh: 球在泳池的底部。

bowl.tip_zh: bowl 的 ow 唸 [o]，不是 cow 的 [aʊ]。[o] 嘴唇從半開滑到收圓之後，舌頭後部往上抬、舌尖碰上排牙齦，發出暗 [l]；常見錯誤是把 l 省掉，只剩 bow。也別唸成 ball 的 [ɔ]，那個嘴巴開得比較大。練習 a bowl of rice 時，把 [l] 和後面的 of 連起來，l 就不容易掉。
bowl.tip_en: In bowl, ow is [o], not the [aʊ] of cow. After the lips glide from half-open to round for [o], raise the back of the tongue and touch the tongue tip to the upper gum ridge for a dark [l]. A common mistake is dropping the l, leaving just bow. Also don't say the [ɔ] of ball, which opens the mouth wider. Practice a bowl of rice and link [l] to the following of, so the l doesn't drop.

examples.en: I eat a bowl of rice every day.
examples.zh: 我每天吃一碗飯。

examples.en: Put the soup in the big bowl.
examples.zh: 把湯倒進那個大碗裡。

bowl.spelling_zh: ow 唸 [o]（同 snow），不是 cow 的 [aʊ]。
bowl.spelling_en: ow is [o] (as in snow), not the [aʊ] of cow.

box.tip_zh: x 代表 [ks] 兩個子音。常見錯誤是在中間或結尾加母音，唸成「巴克斯」。[ɑ] 嘴巴張大之後，舌根只在 [k] 卡一下，馬上接著吹出 [s]，後面不再出聲。跟 fox、socks 同韻。複數 boxes 唸 [ˈbɑksɪz]，多一個音節。
box.tip_en: The x stands for two consonants, [ks]. A common mistake is adding vowels in between or at the end, like 'ba-ke-si'. After opening the mouth wide for [ɑ], the back of the tongue catches [k] only for a moment, then goes straight into a hissed [s], with nothing after it. It rhymes with fox and socks. The plural boxes is [ˈbɑksɪz], with one more syllable.

examples.en: There is a cat in the box.
examples.zh: 箱子裡有一隻貓。

examples.en: Put your toys back in the box.
examples.zh: 把你的玩具放回盒子裡。

boy.tip_zh: boy 的 [ɔɪ] 是雙母音：嘴巴先張開、嘴唇稍圓發 [ɔ]，再滑到 [ɪ]，兩段都要有。起點若放成張大嘴的 [a]，就會變成 buy 或 by。跟 toy、joy 同韻，可以一起練。練習時把 boy、buy 輪流唸，聽清楚起點的不同：boy 一開始嘴唇是圓的。
boy.tip_en: The [ɔɪ] in boy is a diphthong: open the mouth with slightly rounded lips for [ɔ], then glide to [ɪ]; both parts must be there. If the starting point becomes a wide-open [a], it turns into buy or by. It rhymes with toy and joy, so practice them together. Alternate boy and buy and listen to the different starting points: at the start of boy the lips are round.

examples.en: That boy is my best friend.
examples.zh: 那個男孩是我最好的朋友。

examples.en: The boy is playing soccer in the park.
examples.zh: 那個男孩在公園踢足球。

brave.tip_zh: 結尾 [v] 常被唸成 [f] 或乾脆省略。[v] 要上排牙齒輕碰下唇，同時讓聲帶震動，摸喉嚨會麻麻的。開頭 [br] 是連在一起的兩個子音，[b] 後直接捲舌，不要插入「ㄅㄨ」變成 bu-rave。跟 save、wave 同韻，三個字的結尾都要震動。
brave.tip_en: The final [v] is often said as [f] or left out. For [v], rest the upper teeth lightly on the lower lip and let the vocal cords vibrate; your throat should buzz. The opening [br] is two consonants joined: curl the tongue right after [b], without inserting a 'bu' to make bu-rave. It rhymes with save and wave; the ending should buzz in all three.

examples.en: The brave girl helped her friend.
examples.zh: 那個勇敢的女孩幫助了她的朋友。

examples.en: Be brave and try again!
examples.zh: 勇敢一點，再試一次！

bread.tip_zh: bread 的 ea 唸短的 [ɛ]，跟 bed、head 同韻，常被照著 eat 唸成長的 [i]，變成 breed。[br] 中間不要加母音；結尾 [d] 舌尖輕碰上排牙齦就收，不要唸成「ㄉㄜ」。可以把 bread、bed、red 連著唸，三個母音都一樣短。整個字只有一拍，母音不要拖長。
bread.tip_en: The ea in bread is the short [ɛ], rhyming with bed and head; learners often read it like eat, with a long [i], and say breed. Don't put a vowel inside [br]. For the final [d], touch the tongue tip lightly to the upper gum ridge and stop; don't say 'duh'. Say bread, bed and red in a row; all three vowels are equally short. The whole word is one beat; don't drag out the vowel.

examples.en: I have bread and milk for breakfast.
examples.zh: 我早餐吃麵包配牛奶。

examples.en: Mom bought some fresh bread today.
examples.zh: 媽媽今天買了新鮮的麵包。

bread.spelling_zh: ea 唸短的 [ɛ]，不是 eat 的 [i]。
bread.spelling_en: ea is the short [ɛ], not the [i] of eat.

break.tip_zh: break 的 ea 唸 [e]，跟 make、cake 同韻，常被照著 eat 唸成 breek。[e] 要從 [e] 滑向 [ɪ]，嘴角往兩邊拉。結尾 [k] 舌根頂住上顎就停；它跟 brave 只差最後一個音，[k] 不震動、[v] 要震動。練習 take a break 時，take 和 break 的母音一樣都是 [e]。整個字只有一個音節。
break.tip_en: In break, ea is [e], rhyming with make and cake; learners often read it like eat and say breek. The [e] glides toward [ɪ] with the corners of the mouth pulled back. For the final [k], the back of the tongue presses the roof of the mouth and stops. It differs from brave only in the last sound: [k] has no voice, [v] does. When practicing take a break, take and break share the same vowel, [e]. The whole word is one syllable.

examples.en: Please don't break my new crayons.
examples.zh: 請不要弄斷我的新蠟筆。

examples.en: Be careful not to break the glass.
examples.zh: 小心不要打破玻璃杯。

break.spelling_zh: ea 唸 [e]，跟 brake（煞車）同音。
break.spelling_en: ea is [e]; it sounds the same as brake.

breakfast.tip_zh: 拼法雖然有 break，第一音節卻唸短的 [ɛ]，像 bread 的母音，不是 break 的 [e]。第二音節弱讀成 [fəst]，不是 fast 的 [æ]。重音在第一音節；結尾 [st] 舌尖收住，不要加母音唸成「斯特」。可以先唸 bread 的母音，再接上 [k] 和輕輕的 [fəst]。
breakfast.tip_en: Even though it is spelled with break, the first syllable is the short [ɛ], like the vowel in bread, not the [e] of break. The second syllable is weak, [fəst], not the [æ] of fast. Stress the first syllable; end [st] with the tongue tip and don't add a vowel like 'si-te'. Start from the vowel of bread, then add [k] and a light [fəst].

examples.en: What did you eat for breakfast?
examples.zh: 你早餐吃了什麼？

examples.en: We have breakfast at seven o'clock.
examples.zh: 我們七點吃早餐。

bridge.tip_zh: bridge 的母音是短的 [ɪ]，不要拉長成 [i]。結尾 dge 合起來只唸一個 [dʒ]：嘴唇微微往前噘，舌頭從上排牙齦後方放開，聲帶要震動，發完就停，不要再加「ㄐㄩ」。它和 bring 開頭相同，靠結尾分辨。
bridge.tip_en: The vowel in bridge is the short [ɪ]; don't stretch it into [i]. The final dge is a single [dʒ]: push the lips slightly forward, release the tongue from just behind the upper gum ridge, with voice, and stop; don't add a 'ju' sound. It starts the same as bring; the ending tells them apart.

examples.en: We walked across the bridge.
examples.zh: 我們走過那座橋。

examples.en: There is a long bridge over the river.
examples.zh: 河上有一座長長的橋。

bridge.spelling_zh: dge 合起來唸 [dʒ]，d 不另外發音。
bridge.spelling_en: dge together is [dʒ]; the d is not said separately.

bright.tip_zh: bright 的 gh 不發音，igh 唸 [aɪ]，要從張大嘴的 [a] 滑到 [ɪ]。最常見的問題在結尾：[t] 被省掉，只剩 bry。舌尖頂住上排牙齦把氣擋住就好，不用送氣，也不要加「ㄜ」。跟 bite、fight 同韻。練習 bright light 時，兩個字的 igh 都唸 [aɪ]。
bright.tip_en: The gh in bright is silent; igh is [aɪ], gliding from a wide-open [a] to [ɪ]. The most common problem is at the end: the [t] gets dropped, leaving bry. Just press the tongue tip on the upper gum ridge to stop the air; no puff is needed, and don't add 'uh'. It rhymes with bite and fight. In bright light, both igh spellings are [aɪ].

examples.en: The sun is very bright today.
examples.zh: 今天的太陽很亮。

examples.en: She has a bright yellow raincoat.
examples.zh: 她有一件亮黃色的雨衣。

bring.tip_zh: 開頭 [br] 兩個子音要黏在一起，不要唸成「布-ring」多出一拍。結尾 [ɪŋ] 的 [ŋ] 用舌根抬起貼住上顎、氣從鼻子出來，嘴巴不要閉；若舌尖去碰牙齦，就變成 [n]，聽起來像 brin。跟 king、sing 同韻。過去式 brought 唸 [brɔt]，母音不同，別混在一起。
bring.tip_en: The opening [br] must stick together; don't say 'bu-ring' with an extra beat. For the [ŋ] in the final [ɪŋ], raise the back of the tongue against the roof of the mouth and let air out through the nose, mouth open. If the tongue tip touches the gum ridge it becomes [n] and sounds like brin. It rhymes with king and sing. The past tense brought is [brɔt], with a different vowel; don't mix them up.

examples.en: Please bring your lunch box tomorrow.
examples.zh: 明天請帶你的便當盒來。

examples.en: Can you bring me a pencil?
examples.zh: 你可以拿一支鉛筆給我嗎？

brother.tip_zh: 第二音節的 [ð] 學生常唸成 [d] 或 [z]，聽起來像 bruh-der。[ð] 要把舌尖輕放在上下牙齒中間，喉嚨同時震動，用手摸喉嚨應該感覺得到。接著舌頭往後捲發 [ɚ]，結尾一定要有捲舌音。第一音節 [brʌ] 的 o 唸短而放鬆的 [ʌ]，嘴巴不要張成 [ɑ]，[br] 中間也不能多加母音。
brother.tip_en: Students often say the [ð] in the second syllable as [d] or [z], so it sounds like 'bruh-der'. For [ð], rest the tongue tip lightly between the upper and lower teeth while the throat vibrates — you should feel it if you touch your throat. Then pull the tongue back and curl it for [ɚ]; the ending must have the r sound. The o in the first syllable [brʌ] is a short, relaxed [ʌ] — don't open the mouth to [ɑ] — and no extra vowel goes between [b] and [r].

examples.en: My brother is two years older than me.
examples.zh: 我哥哥比我大兩歲。

examples.en: Do you have a brother or a sister?
examples.zh: 你有兄弟或姊妹嗎？

brother.spelling_zh: o 唸短的 [ʌ]，跟 mother、other 一樣，不唸 [o]。
brother.spelling_en: The o is a short [ʌ], as in 'mother' and 'other', not [o].

brown.tip_zh: brown 的 ow 唸 [aʊ]：從張大嘴的 [a] 滑到嘴唇收圓的 [ʊ]，然後舌尖貼上排牙齦收 [n]。台灣學生常把結尾收成舌根的 [ŋ]，聽起來像 brong。跟 down、town 同韻，可以連著練。開頭 [br] 也不要插入「ㄅㄨ」唸成 bu-rown。整個字只有一拍。
brown.tip_en: In brown, ow is [aʊ]: glide from a wide-open [a] to rounded lips for [ʊ], then press the tongue tip on the upper gum ridge for [n]. Taiwanese learners often end with the back-of-tongue [ŋ], so it sounds like brong. It rhymes with down and town; practice them in a row. Also don't insert a 'bu' into the opening [br], making bu-rown. The whole word is one beat.

examples.en: My dog has brown eyes.
examples.zh: 我的狗有棕色的眼睛。

examples.en: She is wearing brown shoes.
examples.zh: 她穿著棕色的鞋子。

brush.tip_zh: brush 的 [ʌ] 嘴巴半開、短而放鬆，不是張大的「ㄚ」。結尾 [ʃ] 嘴唇往前噘、舌頭不碰牙齒，像要人安靜時的「噓」聲；常被唸成扁嘴的「ㄒ」，或後面多加母音變成「刷舒」。發完 [ʃ] 就停。練習 brush your teeth 時，[ʃ] 後面直接接 your，不要停頓。
brush.tip_en: The [ʌ] in brush is short and relaxed with the mouth half open, not a wide 'ah'. For the final [ʃ], push the lips forward and keep the tongue off the teeth, like the 'shh' you make to ask for quiet. It is often said with flat lips like Mandarin x, or with an extra vowel after it. Stop right after [ʃ]. In brush your teeth, go from [ʃ] straight into your without a pause.

examples.en: Brush your teeth before bed.
examples.zh: 睡覺前要刷牙。

examples.en: I need a brush to paint the wall.
examples.zh: 我需要一支刷子來漆牆壁。

bug.tip_zh: bug 的 [ʌ] 嘴巴半開、放鬆，不要張大成 bag 的 [æ]，也不要縮成 big 的 [ɪ]。結尾 [g] 要有聲：舌根頂住上顎，喉嚨震動，輕輕收住；唸成無聲的 [k] 就像 buck，後面加「ㄜ」也不對。跟 hug、rug 同韻，可以一起練。整個字只有一拍。
bug.tip_en: The [ʌ] in bug is relaxed with the mouth half open; don't open wide to the [æ] of bag or close to the [ɪ] of big. The final [g] is voiced: the back of the tongue presses the roof of the mouth while the throat buzzes, then a gentle stop. A voiceless [k] makes it sound like buck, and adding 'uh' is also wrong. It rhymes with hug and rug; practice them together. The whole word is one beat.

examples.en: There is a little bug on my desk.
examples.zh: 我的桌子上有一隻小蟲。

examples.en: Look! A green bug is on the leaf.
examples.zh: 你看！葉子上有一隻綠色的蟲。

build.tip_zh: build 的 ui 只唸短的 [ɪ]，u 不發音。結尾是 [ld]：舌尖先貼上排牙齦發暗 [l]，舌頭不離開，直接放出 [d]。最常見的錯誤是把 [l] 吞掉，聽起來像 bid；也不要唸成 bu-ild 兩拍。過去式 built 唸 [bɪlt]，同樣要保留 [l]。
build.tip_en: In build, ui is just the short [ɪ]; the u is silent. It ends in [ld]: put the tongue tip on the upper gum ridge for a dark [l], and without moving the tongue, release [d]. The most common mistake is swallowing the [l], which sounds like bid. Also don't split it into two beats, bu-ild. The past tense built is [bɪlt]; keep the [l] there too.

examples.en: Let's build a sandcastle at the beach.
examples.zh: 我們在海邊堆沙堡吧。

examples.en: Birds build nests in spring.
examples.zh: 鳥在春天築巢。

build.spelling_en: The u is silent; ui is [ɪ].

bun.tip_zh: bun 的母音是短而放鬆的 [ʌ]，跟 fun、run 一樣。結尾 [n] 要用舌尖貼住上排牙齦；若改成舌根收音，就變成 [ŋ]，像 bung。也別把母音捲舌，那會變成 burn 的 [ɝ]。可以把 bun、burn、bean 三個字對比，只有 bun 是短的 [ʌ]。
bun.tip_en: The vowel in bun is a short, relaxed [ʌ], as in fun and run. For the final [n], press the tongue tip against the upper gum ridge; ending with the back of the tongue gives [ŋ], like bung. Also don't curl the tongue on the vowel, which turns it into the [ɝ] of burn. Contrast bun, burn and bean; only bun has the short [ʌ].

examples.en: I want a bun with red bean paste.
examples.zh: 我想要一個紅豆餡的小圓麵包。

examples.en: She ate a warm bun for breakfast.
examples.zh: 她早餐吃了一個熱熱的小圓麵包。

burn.tip_zh: burn 的 ur 唸捲舌母音 [ɝ]：舌頭往後捲、嘴唇微圓，整個母音都帶著 r 的音色，跟 learn、turn 同韻。不捲舌的話會變成 bun 的 [ʌ]。最後舌尖貼上排牙齦收 [n]，不要收成 [ŋ]。可以先發 bird 的母音，再接上 [n]。
burn.tip_en: In burn, ur is the r-colored vowel [ɝ]: curl the tongue back with slightly rounded lips, so the whole vowel carries the r sound, rhyming with learn and turn. Without the curl it becomes the [ʌ] of bun. Finally, press the tongue tip on the upper gum ridge for [n], not [ŋ]. Start from the vowel of bird, then add [n].

examples.en: Be careful not to burn the toast.
examples.zh: 小心不要把吐司烤焦了。

examples.en: The candles burn brightly on my birthday cake.
examples.zh: 我生日蛋糕上的蠟燭燒得很亮。

bus.tip_zh: 受到外來語「巴士」影響，常唸成張大嘴的「ㄚ」再加一個「士」。bus 的 [ʌ] 嘴巴只半開、短而放鬆；張太大會接近 boss 的 [ɑ]。結尾 [s] 只吹氣，舌尖靠近牙齦，後面不要再加母音。複數 buses 唸 [ˈbʌsɪz]，多一個音節。
bus.tip_en: Influenced by the loanword 巴士, learners often say a wide 'ah' plus an extra 'shi'. The [ʌ] in bus is short and relaxed with the mouth only half open; opening too wide moves it toward the [ɑ] of boss. The final [s] is just air with the tongue tip near the gum ridge, with no vowel after it. The plural buses is [ˈbʌsɪz], with one more syllable.

examples.en: I take the bus to school.
examples.zh: 我搭公車上學。

examples.en: Our school bus is yellow.
examples.zh: 我們的校車是黃色的。

business.tip_zh: business 只有兩個音節 [bɪz·nəs]，拼字中間的 i 不發音，常被唸成 bu-si-ness 三拍。第一個 u 唸短的 [ɪ]，s 唸有聲的 [z]，喉嚨要震動；重音在第一音節，後面的 [nəs] 輕輕帶過。可以記成 biz 加 ness 兩拍，前重後輕。
business.tip_en: Business has only two syllables, [bɪz·nəs]; the i in the middle of the spelling is silent, but learners often say three beats, bu-si-ness. The u is the short [ɪ], and the s is a voiced [z], so the throat buzzes. Stress the first syllable and say [nəs] lightly. Remember it as two beats, biz plus ness, strong then light.

examples.en: My mom has her own business.
examples.zh: 我媽媽自己做生意。

examples.en: My uncle went to Japan on business.
examples.zh: 我叔叔去日本出差。

business.spelling_zh: u 唸 [ɪ]，中間的 i 不發音。
business.spelling_en: The u is said [ɪ]; the i in the middle is silent.

businessman.tip_zh: 最大的陷阱是照拼字唸成 bus-i-ness-man，多出一個音節。business 只有兩個音節 [bɪz] 和 [nəs]：u 唸 [ɪ]，s 唸有聲的 [z]，中間的 i 不發音。整個字是三個音節，重音在第一音節 [bɪz]；最後的 [mæn] 嘴巴張大，舌尖頂住牙齦把 [n] 收好。
businessman.tip_en: The biggest trap is reading the spelling as bus-i-ness-man, which adds an extra syllable. 'Business' has only two syllables, [bɪz] and [nəs]: the u is said [ɪ], the s is a voiced [z], and the i in the middle is silent. The whole word has three syllables, with the stress on the first, [bɪz]; for the last part [mæn], open the mouth wide and finish the [n] with the tongue tip on the gum ridge.

examples.en: My uncle is a businessman in Taipei.
examples.zh: 我叔叔是台北的一位商人。

examples.en: The businessman is carrying a black bag.
examples.zh: 那位商人提著一個黑色的包包。

businessman.variant_zh: 字尾 man 也常輕讀成 [mən]：[ˈbɪznəsmən]。
businessman.variant_en: The ending man is also often reduced to [mən]: [ˈbɪznəsmən].
businessman.spelling_zh: busi- 的 u 唸 [ɪ]，i 不發音，不要唸成 bus。
businessman.spelling_en: In busi-, the u is said [ɪ] and the i is silent — don't say 'bus'.

busy.tip_zh: busy 的 u 唸短的 [ɪ]，不是 bus 的 [ʌ]，常被照字面唸成 bu-sy。中間的 s 唸有聲的 [z]，摸喉嚨會震動，唸成 [s] 就不對。兩個音節都是短 [ɪ]，重音在第一個。練習時拍兩下手：第一下重、第二下輕。
busy.tip_en: In busy, the u is the short [ɪ], not the [ʌ] of bus; learners often read it as spelled, bu-sy. The s in the middle is a voiced [z]; you should feel the throat buzz, so [s] is wrong. Both syllables have the short [ɪ], with stress on the first. Clap twice as you practice: the first strong, the second light.

examples.en: My dad is very busy today.
examples.zh: 我爸爸今天很忙。

examples.en: I am busy with my homework.
examples.zh: 我在忙著寫功課。

busy.spelling_en: The u is said [ɪ] and the s is said [z].

but.tip_zh: but 的 [ʌ] 嘴巴半開、放鬆，不要張大成 bat 的 [æ]。結尾 [t] 舌尖頂住上排牙齦就停住，美國人常不把氣放出來，台灣學生則常多加一個「ㄜ」。在句子裡 but 通常輕讀，母音會更弱，接近 [ə]。在 but I 裡，[t] 會跟 I 連讀，常變成輕快的閃音。
but.tip_en: The [ʌ] in but is relaxed with the mouth half open; don't open wide to the [æ] of bat. For the final [t], press the tongue tip on the upper gum ridge and hold; Americans often don't release the air, while Taiwanese learners often add an 'uh'. In sentences but is usually unstressed and its vowel weakens toward [ə]. In but I, the [t] links to I and often becomes a quick flap.

examples.en: I like apples, but I don't like bananas.
examples.zh: 我喜歡蘋果，但是我不喜歡香蕉。

examples.en: It's small, but it's very fast.
examples.zh: 它很小，但是跑得很快。

butter.tip_zh: butter 中間的 tt 美式唸成閃音：舌尖輕彈一下上排牙齦，聽起來像很快的 [d]，不要用力送氣。結尾 [ɚ] 要捲舌，舌頭往後縮，常被唸成「巴特」不捲舌。重音在第一音節 [bʌ]。它和美式的 better、water 用的是同一個閃音。
butter.tip_en: In American English the tt in butter is a flap: the tongue tip taps the upper gum ridge once, sounding like a quick [d], without a strong puff of air. The final [ɚ] needs a curled tongue pulled back; learners often say 'ba-te' with no r. Stress the first syllable, [bʌ]. It uses the same flap as American better and water.

examples.en: I like butter on my toast.
examples.zh: 我喜歡在吐司上抹奶油。

examples.en: Please pass the butter.
examples.zh: 請把奶油遞給我。

butterfly.tip_zh: 學生常照中文習慣唸成「巴特福來」：[ʌ] 張太大變成 [ɑ]、[t] 唸得太重、[ɚ] 沒有捲舌。美式唸法裡 [ʌ] 短而放鬆；中間的 [t] 夾在兩個母音之間，舌尖在牙齦輕彈一下，像很快的 d；接著捲舌唸 [ɚ]。最後 [flaɪ] 的 [f] 和 [l] 中間不加母音。重音在第一音節。
butterfly.tip_en: Students often say it the Mandarin way, like 'ba-te-fu-lai': the [ʌ] opens too wide into [ɑ], the [t] is too heavy, and the [ɚ] isn't curled. In the American pronunciation, [ʌ] is short and relaxed; the middle [t] sits between two vowels, so the tongue tip just flicks the gum ridge once, like a quick d; then curl the tongue for [ɚ]. In the last part [flaɪ], no vowel goes between [f] and [l]. The stress is on the first syllable.

examples.en: A butterfly landed on my hand!
examples.zh: 一隻蝴蝶停在我的手上！

examples.en: We saw a yellow butterfly in the garden.
examples.zh: 我們在花園裡看到一隻黃色的蝴蝶。

button.tip_zh: button 的第二音節 [tṇ] 沒有母音，常被唸成「巴頓」或 but-ton 兩個完整音節。做法是：舌尖貼住上排牙齦發 [t]，舌頭不放開，直接讓氣從鼻子出來發 [ṇ]。美式口語的 tt 常變成喉嚨輕輕一頓。
button.tip_en: The second syllable of button, [tṇ], has no vowel; learners often say 'ba-dun' or two full syllables, but-ton. Here is how: put the tongue tip on the upper gum ridge for [t], keep it there, and let the air go out through the nose for [ṇ]. In casual American speech the tt often becomes a small catch in the throat.

examples.en: Press the red button to start.
examples.zh: 按紅色按鈕開始。

examples.en: A button fell off my shirt.
examples.zh: 我的襯衫掉了一顆鈕扣。

buy.tip_zh: buy 和 by、bye 唸法完全一樣，都是 [baɪ]，u 不發音。[aɪ] 要從張大嘴的 [a] 滑到 [ɪ]，滑完整；只唸前半就像「八」。起點不要放成圓唇的 [ɔ]，那會變成 boy。過去式 bought 唸 [bɔt]，母音完全不同。在 buy it 裡，[aɪ] 會自然滑進下一個字的母音。
buy.tip_en: Buy is pronounced exactly like by and bye: [baɪ]; the u is silent. The [aɪ] must glide all the way from a wide-open [a] to [ɪ]; saying only the first half sounds like 'ba'. Don't start with the rounded [ɔ], which turns it into boy. The past tense bought is [bɔt], with a completely different vowel. In buy it, the [aɪ] glides naturally into the next word's vowel.

examples.en: I want to buy a new pencil box.
examples.zh: 我想買一個新的鉛筆盒。

examples.en: Mom will buy some apples at the market.
examples.zh: 媽媽會在市場買一些蘋果。

buy.spelling_zh: u 不發音；跟 by、bye 同音。
buy.spelling_en: The u is silent; it sounds the same as by and bye.

by.tip_zh: by 結尾的 y 唸 [aɪ]，跟 my、fly 一樣，不要照 baby 字尾唸成 [ɪ]。在句子裡 by 不重讀，速度很快，但 [aɪ] 仍要滑到 [ɪ]，例如 by bus 兩個字要連成一口氣。它和 buy 同音。它也和 bye-bye 的 bye 同音，可以用這個熟悉的字來練。
by.tip_en: The y at the end of by is [aɪ], as in my and fly; don't read it like the end of baby, [ɪ]. In sentences by is unstressed and quick, but the [aɪ] still has to glide to [ɪ]; for example, by bus should flow as one breath. It sounds the same as buy. It also sounds like the bye in bye-bye, a familiar word to practice with.

examples.en: I go to school by bus.
examples.zh: 我搭公車上學。

examples.en: Please finish this by Friday.
examples.zh: 請在星期五前完成這個。

cake.tip_zh: [e] 在美式英語裡是會滑動的長音，從 [e] 滑向 [ɪ]，跟 make、name 的 a 一樣；學生常唸成短而平的 [ɛ]，變成 [kɛk]。字尾的 [k] 中文沒有，學生常多唸一個「克」，或乾脆不發。唸完母音後，舌根往上頂住軟顎把氣堵住，輕輕放開就好，不要再加母音。
cake.tip_en: In American English, [e] is a long gliding sound that moves from [e] toward [ɪ], like the a in 'make' and 'name'; students often say a short, flat [ɛ], making it [kɛk]. Mandarin has no final [k], so students often add an extra 'kuh' or leave it out. After the vowel, raise the back of the tongue against the soft palate to block the air and release it gently — don't add a vowel.

examples.en: Mom made a chocolate cake for my birthday.
examples.zh: 媽媽為我的生日做了一個巧克力蛋糕。

examples.en: Can I have another piece of cake, please?
examples.zh: 請問我可以再吃一塊蛋糕嗎？

call.tip_zh: call 的 [ɔ] 嘴巴要張開、嘴唇稍圓、下巴放低，不要收成較閉的 [o]，那會像 coal。結尾 ll 是暗 [l]：舌頭後部往上抬，舌尖碰上排牙齦。台灣學生常把 l 省掉，唸成「扣」，美國人會聽不出是 call。
call.tip_en: The [ɔ] in call needs an open mouth, slightly rounded lips and a lowered jaw; don't close it to [o], which sounds like coal. The final ll is a dark [l]: raise the back of the tongue and touch the tongue tip to the upper gum ridge. Taiwanese learners often drop the l and say 'kou', and Americans can't tell it is call.

examples.en: Please call me after school.
examples.zh: 放學後請打電話給我。

examples.en: I will call Grandma tonight.
examples.zh: 我今晚會打電話給奶奶。

camera.tip_zh: 學生常受「卡麥拉」影響，把三個音節唸得一樣重，而且都用 [ɑ]。英文重音在第一音節 [kæ]，嘴巴張大、嘴角往兩旁拉；後面的 [mərə] 要很快帶過：[mə] 輕輕一點，接著捲舌唸 [rə]，不是響亮的「拉」。
camera.tip_en: Students are often influenced by the Taiwanese slang 'ka-mai-la', saying all three syllables equally strongly and all with [ɑ]. In English the stress is on the first syllable [kæ] — open the mouth wide and pull the lip corners sideways; the following [mərə] goes by quickly: [mə] is just a light touch, then curl the tongue for [rə], not a loud 'la'.

examples.en: Dad took our picture with his new camera.
examples.zh: 爸爸用他的新相機幫我們拍照。

examples.en: Smile at the camera, everyone!
examples.zh: 大家看鏡頭，笑一個！

camera.variant_zh: 美國人也常唸成兩個音節 [ˈkæmrə]。
camera.variant_en: Americans also often say it in two syllables: [ˈkæmrə].

camp.tip_zh: camp 的 [æ] 嘴巴要張大、嘴角往兩邊拉，介於「ㄚ」和「ㄝ」之間，常被唸成較窄的 [ɛ]。結尾 [mp]：先閉唇發 [m]，嘴唇保持閉著，再輕輕放出 [p]，後面不加母音。跟 lamp、stamp 同韻。練 camping 時，[p] 輕輕放出後接 [ɪŋ]。整個字只有一拍。
camp.tip_en: The [æ] in camp needs a wide-open mouth with the corners pulled back, between 'ah' and 'eh'; learners often make it the narrower [ɛ]. For the final [mp], close the lips for [m], keep them closed, then release a light [p] with no vowel after it. It rhymes with lamp and stamp. In camping, release a light [p] and go into [ɪŋ]. The whole word is one beat.

examples.en: We camp in the mountains every summer.
examples.zh: 我們每年夏天都在山上露營。

examples.en: My brother is going to summer camp.
examples.zh: 我哥哥要去參加夏令營。

can.tip_zh: 單獨唸或強調時，can 是 [kæn]，[æ] 嘴巴張大。但在句子裡 can 通常輕讀成 [kən]，例如 I can swim；如果每次都唸重的 [kæn]，美國人可能會以為你說的是 can't。結尾 [n] 用舌尖收，不要收成 [ŋ]。相反地，can't 的 [æ] 會重讀，後面接一個短促的 [t] 停頓。
can.tip_en: Said alone or with emphasis, can is [kæn], with a wide-open [æ]. But inside a sentence can is usually weak, [kən], as in I can swim; if you always say a strong [kæn], Americans may think you said can't. End [n] with the tongue tip, not [ŋ]. Can't, by contrast, has a stressed [æ] followed by a short [t] stop.

examples.en: I can ride a bike.
examples.zh: 我會騎腳踏車。

examples.en: Can you help me, please?
examples.zh: 你可以幫我一下嗎？

can.variant_zh: 句子中常弱讀成 [kən]，例如 I can swim。
can.variant_en: In sentences it is often weak, [kən], as in I can swim.

candle.tip_zh: 結尾的 [dḷ] 是重點：學生常唸成「肯豆」，把 [l] 變成像「歐」的母音，或在 [l] 前面多加一個母音。正確做法是舌尖發完 [d] 後留在牙齦上不動，只讓舌頭兩側放下來讓氣流出去，這就是 [ḷ]。前面的 [kæn] 是重音，[æ] 嘴巴張大，[n] 也要用舌尖頂住。
candle.tip_en: The ending [dḷ] is the key: students often say 'ken-do', turning [l] into an 'o'-like vowel, or add a vowel before the [l]. The right way: after [d], leave the tongue tip on the gum ridge without moving it, and only drop the sides of the tongue to let the air out — that is [ḷ]. The first part [kæn] is stressed; open the mouth wide for [æ], and make [n] with the tongue tip pressed up too.

examples.en: Make a wish and blow out the candle!
examples.zh: 許個願，然後吹熄蠟燭！

examples.en: Grandma put a candle on the table.
examples.zh: 奶奶在桌上放了一根蠟燭。

candy.tip_zh: 重音在第一音節 [kæn]，[æ] 嘴巴要張大、嘴角拉開，常被唸成較窄的「肯」。接著舌尖貼在上排牙齦發 [n]，舌頭不移開，直接放出 [d]，中間不要停。結尾 y 唸輕短的 [ɪ]。跟 handy 同韻，可以一起練。
candy.tip_en: Stress the first syllable, [kæn]. The [æ] needs a wide-open mouth with the corners pulled back; learners often make it a narrower 'ken'. Then put the tongue tip on the upper gum ridge for [n] and, without moving it, release [d], with no break in between. The final y is a light, short [ɪ]. It rhymes with handy; practice them together.

examples.en: Don't eat too much candy.
examples.zh: 不要吃太多糖果。

examples.en: The kids got candy on Halloween.
examples.zh: 孩子們在萬聖節拿到了糖果。

cap.tip_zh: cap 的 [æ] 嘴巴要張大，若唸成嘴巴半開的 [ʌ]，就變成 cup（杯子），意思完全不同。結尾 [p] 雙唇閉起來就停，不要再送出「ㄆㄜ」。可以用 map、clap 練同一個 [æp] 結尾。練習時把 cap、cup 輪流唸，一個嘴巴張大、一個半開。
cap.tip_en: The [æ] in cap needs a wide-open mouth; if you say the half-open [ʌ], it becomes cup, a completely different word. For the final [p], close the lips and stop; don't puff out a 'puh'. Practice the same [æp] ending with map and clap. Alternate cap and cup as you practice: one with the mouth wide open, the other half open.

examples.en: He is wearing a blue cap.
examples.zh: 他戴著一頂藍色的棒球帽。

examples.en: Put on your cap. It's sunny.
examples.zh: 戴上你的帽子，外面出太陽了。

car.tip_zh: 美式 car 結尾的 [r] 一定要捲：[ɑ] 嘴巴張大之後，舌頭往後捲起、不碰上顎。只唸「卡」聽起來不完整，像英式發音。它和 care 的差別在母音：car 是張大嘴的 [ɑ]，care 是較窄的 [ɛ]。跟 far、star 同韻。整個字只有一拍。
car.tip_en: In American English the final [r] of car must be curled: after the wide-open [ɑ], curl the tongue back without touching the roof of the mouth. Saying just 'ka' sounds incomplete, like British English. It differs from care in the vowel: car has the wide-open [ɑ], care the narrower [ɛ]. It rhymes with far and star. The whole word is one beat.

examples.en: My dad drives a red car.
examples.zh: 我爸爸開一台紅色的車。

examples.en: We went to the beach by car.
examples.zh: 我們開車去海邊。

card.tip_zh: card 結尾有 [rd] 兩個子音：[ɑ] 張大嘴之後捲舌 [r]，再讓舌尖輕點上排牙齦收 [d]。少了 [d] 就變成 car，少了 [r] 則接近 cod。[d] 只要輕輕收住，不要多加「ㄉㄜ」。跟 hard、yard 同韻。可以和 car 對比練習：card 最後舌尖要碰一下牙齦。
card.tip_en: Card ends with two consonants, [rd]: after the wide-open [ɑ], curl the tongue for [r], then tap the tongue tip on the upper gum ridge for [d]. Without [d] it becomes car; without [r] it is close to cod. Just stop lightly on [d] without adding 'duh'. It rhymes with hard and yard. Practice it against car: card ends with the tongue tip touching the gum ridge.

examples.en: I made a birthday card for Mom.
examples.zh: 我做了一張生日卡片給媽媽。

examples.en: Write your name on the card.
examples.zh: 把你的名字寫在卡片上。

care.tip_zh: care 只有一個音節：嘴巴開到 [ɛ]，舌頭立刻往後捲進 [r]，不要拆成「ㄎㄟ-兒」兩拍。[ɛ] 比 car 的 [ɑ] 嘴巴閉一些、嘴角往旁邊拉，唸成 [ɑ] 就變成 car。跟 hair、chair 同韻，結尾 e 不發音。careful、careless 裡的 care 也唸 [kɛr]。練習 take care 時，兩個字之間的 [k] 只唸一次。
care.tip_en: Care is one syllable: open the mouth to [ɛ] and immediately curl the tongue back into [r]; don't split it into two beats like 'kei-er'. [ɛ] is less open than the [ɑ] of car, with the corners of the mouth pulled sideways; saying [ɑ] turns it into car. It rhymes with hair and chair, and the final e is silent. The care in careful and careless is also [kɛr]. In take care, the [k] between the two words is said only once.

examples.en: Take care of your little brother.
examples.zh: 好好照顧你的弟弟。

examples.en: I care about my friends.
examples.zh: 我很在乎我的朋友。

careful.tip_zh: 重音在 care，後面的 -ful 要弱讀成 [fḷ]，常被唸成重重的 full [fʊl]。[r] 捲完後，上排牙齒直接碰下唇發 [f]，接著舌尖貼上排牙齦留住暗 [l]，不要省略 l 只唸成「佛」。唸成 care-full 兩個重拍是常見問題，要一重一輕。
careful.tip_en: The stress is on care, and the -ful after it is weak, [fḷ]; learners often say a heavy full, [fʊl]. After curling for [r], put the upper teeth straight onto the lower lip for [f], then keep a dark [l] with the tongue tip on the upper gum ridge; don't drop the l and end on just 'fo'. Saying two heavy beats, care-full, is a common problem; make it strong then weak.

examples.en: Be careful when you cross the street.
examples.zh: 過馬路時要小心。

examples.en: Please be careful with the glass.
examples.zh: 拿玻璃杯時請小心。

carry.tip_zh: carry 中間的 rr 只唸一個 [r]：舌頭往後捲、不碰上顎，常被唸成 [l]，變成 ca-lly。第一音節 [kæ] 嘴巴張大，重音在這裡；第二音節 y 唸輕短的 [ɪ]。第三人稱 carries 唸 [ˈkærɪz]，結尾是有聲的 [z]。練習 carry it 時，把重音放在 car 上。
carry.tip_en: The double rr in carry is a single [r]: curl the tongue back without touching the roof of the mouth; learners often turn it into [l], giving ca-lly. The first syllable [kæ] has a wide-open mouth and carries the stress; the y in the second syllable is a light, short [ɪ]. The third-person form carries is [ˈkærɪz], ending in a voiced [z]. When practicing carry it, put the stress on car.

examples.en: Can you carry this bag for me?
examples.zh: 你可以幫我拿這個袋子嗎？

examples.en: I carry my lunch in a box.
examples.zh: 我把午餐裝在盒子裡帶著。

carry.variant_zh: 很多美國人唸 [ˈkɛrɪ]，第一音節像 care。
carry.variant_en: Many Americans say [ˈkɛrɪ], with a first syllable like care.

case.tip_zh: case 結尾的 se 唸無聲的 [s]，只吹氣、喉嚨不震動，常被誤唸成 [z]。母音 [e] 要從 [e] 滑向 [ɪ]，嘴角往兩邊拉，跟 face、place 同韻。[s] 之後不要加母音，唸成「凱斯」就多了一拍。可以用手摸喉嚨，確認 [s] 沒有震動。
case.tip_en: The se at the end of case is a voiceless [s], just air with no buzz in the throat; learners often say [z] by mistake. The vowel [e] glides toward [ɪ] with the corners of the mouth pulled back, rhyming with face and place. Don't add a vowel after [s]; 'kai-si' has an extra beat. Touch your throat to check that [s] doesn't vibrate.

examples.en: Put your glasses in the case.
examples.zh: 把你的眼鏡放進盒子裡。

examples.en: My pencil case is blue.
examples.zh: 我的鉛筆盒是藍色的。

castle.tip_zh: castle 的 t 不發音，學生看到拼字常唸成 [kæstḷ]。正確是 [s] 直接接 [ḷ]：發完 [s] 後舌尖往上頂住牙齦，讓氣從舌頭兩側出去，中間不要加母音，也不要唸成「索」。重音在第一音節，[æ] 嘴巴張大、嘴角往兩旁拉，不要只唸成中文的「卡」。
castle.tip_en: The t in castle is silent; seeing the spelling, students often say [kæstḷ]. The right way is [s] going straight into [ḷ]: after [s], raise the tongue tip to the gum ridge and let the air out at the sides of the tongue, without adding a vowel in between and without making it 'so'. The stress is on the first syllable; open the mouth wide for [æ] and pull the lip corners sideways — not just Mandarin 'ka'.

examples.en: The princess lives in a big castle.
examples.zh: 公主住在一座大城堡裡。

examples.en: We built a sand castle at the beach.
examples.zh: 我們在海邊堆了一座沙堡。

castle.spelling_zh: t 不發音，跟 listen 的 t 一樣。
castle.spelling_en: The t is silent, like the t in 'listen'.

cat.tip_zh: [æ] 是 cat 的核心：下巴要比唸 bed 的 [ɛ] 更往下掉，嘴角往兩旁拉。學生常唸成 [ɛ]，聽起來像 ket，或用中文「卡」的母音，兩種都不夠準，也容易和 cut 混在一起。字尾的 [t] 舌尖頂住牙齦就停，不必把氣放出來，更不要多唸一個「特」。
cat.tip_en: [æ] is the heart of cat: drop the jaw lower than for the [ɛ] in 'bed', and pull the lip corners sideways. Students often say [ɛ], so it sounds like 'ket', or use the vowel of Mandarin 'ka'; neither is accurate, and both are easy to mix up with 'cut'. Stop the final [t] with the tongue tip on the gum ridge — no need to release the air, and never add an extra 'tuh'.

examples.en: Our cat sleeps on the sofa all day.
examples.zh: 我們家的貓整天都在沙發上睡覺。

examples.en: The little cat is playing with a ball.
examples.zh: 那隻小貓在玩球。

catch.tip_zh: catch 的 [æ] 嘴巴張大、嘴角拉開。tch 合起來只唸一個 [tʃ]：嘴唇往前噘，舌尖從上排牙齦後方放開，氣流出去就停，常被唸成「ㄑㄧ」多出一個母音。整個字只有一拍。跟 match 同韻。整個字只有一拍。
catch.tip_en: The [æ] in catch has a wide-open mouth with the corners pulled back. The tch together is a single [tʃ]: push the lips forward, release the tongue tip from just behind the upper gum ridge, let the air out and stop; learners often add a vowel like Mandarin 'qi'. The whole word is one beat. It rhymes with match. The whole word is one beat.

examples.en: Can you catch the ball?
examples.zh: 你接得到球嗎？

examples.en: Hurry, or we won't catch the bus!
examples.zh: 快一點，不然我們趕不上公車！

catch.spelling_zh: t 不另外發音，tch 唸 [tʃ]。
catch.spelling_en: The t is not said separately; tch is [tʃ].

celebrate.tip_zh: 重音在第一音節 [sɛ]，學生常把重音放到第二音節，唸成 ce-LE-brate。正確節奏是「重、輕、中」：[sɛ] 響亮，[lə] 輕輕帶過，最後的 [bret] 是次重音，[e] 要唸完整並滑向 [ɪ]；[br] 中間不加母音，字尾 [t] 收住，不唸「特」。開頭的 c 唸 [s]。
celebrate.tip_en: The stress is on the first syllable [sɛ]; students often move it to the second, saying ce-LE-brate. The right rhythm is strong–weak–medium: [sɛ] is loud, [lə] is passed over lightly, and the last part [bret] has secondary stress — say its [e] fully, gliding toward [ɪ]; put no vowel between [b] and [r], and close the final [t] without saying 'tuh'. The c at the start is said [s].

examples.en: We celebrate Chinese New Year with our family.
examples.zh: 我們和家人一起慶祝農曆新年。

examples.en: Let's celebrate Dad's birthday with a big cake!
examples.zh: 我們用一個大蛋糕來慶祝爸爸的生日吧！

cellphone.tip_zh: 開頭 c 唸 [s]。cell 結尾的暗 [l] 很容易被吞掉，變成 se-phone：舌尖先碰上排牙齦發 [l]，再換成上排牙齒碰下唇發 [f]，ph 就是 [f]。重音在 cell，結尾 [on] 用舌尖收 [n]。練習時先慢唸 cell，確認舌尖碰到牙齦，再接 phone。
cellphone.tip_en: The c at the start is [s]. The dark [l] at the end of cell is easily swallowed, giving se-phone: touch the tongue tip to the upper gum ridge for [l], then switch to upper teeth on lower lip for [f]; ph is [f]. Stress cell, and end [on] with the tongue tip on [n]. Practice by saying cell slowly, making sure the tongue tip touches the gum ridge, then add phone.

examples.en: My cellphone is in my backpack.
examples.zh: 我的手機在我的背包裡。

examples.en: Please turn off your cellphone in class.
examples.zh: 上課時請把手機關機。

cellphone.spelling_en: The c is [s] and ph is [f].

cent.tip_zh: cent 的 c 唸 [s]，跟 sent 同音。結尾 [nt]：舌尖貼著上排牙齦先發 [n]，舌頭不離開，在原位頓住收 [t]。常見錯誤是唸成有聲的 [d] 變成 send，或後面多加母音唸成 sen-tu。複數 cents 唸 [sɛnts]，結尾三個子音都要有。
cent.tip_en: The c in cent is [s]; it sounds the same as sent. For the final [nt], put the tongue tip on the upper gum ridge for [n], keep it there, and stop for [t] in the same place. Common mistakes are a voiced [d], which turns it into send, or an extra vowel, sen-tu. The plural cents is [sɛnts]; all three final consonants should be there.

examples.en: I found a cent under the sofa.
examples.zh: 我在沙發下找到一分錢。

examples.en: A dime is ten cents, and a penny is one cent.
examples.zh: 一角是十分錢，一分硬幣是一分錢。

cent.spelling_zh: c 唸 [s]，跟 sent 同音。
cent.spelling_en: The c is [s]; it sounds like sent.

center.tip_zh: center 的 c 唸 [s]，重音在第一音節。結尾 -ter 唸捲舌的 [ɚ]，常被唸成不捲舌的「特」。美式口語中，[n] 後面的 [t] 常變得很輕甚至不唸，所以會聽到像 sen-er 的說法，兩種都正確。也不要把開頭的 c 唸成 [k]。
center.tip_en: The c in center is [s], and the stress is on the first syllable. The ending -ter is the r-colored [ɚ]; learners often say a flat 'te' with no curl. In casual American speech the [t] after [n] often becomes very light or disappears, so you will hear something like sen-er; both are correct. Also don't say the first c as [k].

examples.en: Stand in the center of the circle.
examples.zh: 站到圓圈的中間。

examples.en: We went to the science center last Sunday.
examples.zh: 上星期天我們去了科學中心。

center.variant_en: In casual speech the t is often dropped: [ˈsɛnɚ].

centimeter.tip_zh: 這個字有四個音節，重音在第一音節 [sɛn]，第三音節 [mi] 是次重音。學生常把每個音節都唸得一樣重，還把 [tə] 唸成響亮的「踢」。[tə] 要又短又輕；結尾 [tɚ] 的 [t] 夾在母音中間，美國人常輕彈成像 d 的音，最後一定要捲舌，不要唸到「特」就結束。
centimeter.tip_en: This word has four syllables, with the main stress on the first, [sɛn], and secondary stress on the third, [mi]. Students often say every syllable equally hard and turn [tə] into a loud 'tee'. Keep [tə] short and light. In the ending [tɚ], the [t] sits between vowels, so Americans often flick it into a d-like sound, and the word must end with a curled tongue — don't stop at 'te'.

examples.en: The ant is only one centimeter long.
examples.zh: 那隻螞蟻只有一公分長。

examples.en: Each square on this paper is one centimeter wide.
examples.zh: 這張紙上的每個格子都是一公分寬。

centimeter.spelling_zh: 美式拼法是 -meter，英式是 -metre；美式字尾唸捲舌的 [ɚ]。
centimeter.spelling_en: American spelling is -meter, British is -metre; in American English the ending is the curled [ɚ].

chair.tip_zh: 開頭的 [tʃ] 嘴唇要往前噘、稍微圓起來，舌頭前端頂住牙齦後方再放開；學生常用中文「切」的發音，嘴角往兩旁拉，聽起來太扁。後面的 [ɛr] 要先張開嘴發 [ɛ]，再把舌頭往後捲成 [r]，不要只唸到「切」就結束，也不要唸成 cheer 的 [ɪr]。
chair.tip_en: For the opening [tʃ], push the lips forward and round them slightly, press the front of the tongue just behind the gum ridge, then release; students often use Mandarin 'qie', with the lip corners pulled sideways, which sounds too flat. For the following [ɛr], first open the mouth for [ɛ], then curl the tongue back into [r] — don't stop at 'qie', and don't say the [ɪr] of 'cheer'.

examples.en: Please sit on the chair and wait.
examples.zh: 請坐在椅子上等一下。

examples.en: There is a small chair next to my desk.
examples.zh: 我的書桌旁邊有一張小椅子。

chalk.tip_zh: chalk 的 l 不發音，跟 talk、walk 一樣，不要唸成 chal-k。開頭 [tʃ] 嘴唇要往前噘，不是扁嘴的「ㄑ」；接著嘴巴張大發 [ɑ]，最後舌根頂住上顎收 [k]，不要加「ㄜ」。也別把 chalk 和 check 弄混，兩者母音不同。結尾 [k] 不要送出「ㄎㄜ」的母音。
chalk.tip_en: The l in chalk is silent, just like in talk and walk; don't say chal-k. For the opening [tʃ] push the lips forward, unlike the flat-lipped Mandarin q; then open the mouth wide for [ɑ], and finish with the back of the tongue against the roof of the mouth for [k], without adding 'uh'. Also don't confuse chalk with check; their vowels are different. Don't add a vowel after the final [k].

examples.en: The teacher writes with white chalk.
examples.zh: 老師用白色粉筆寫字。

examples.en: We drew pictures with chalk on the ground.
examples.zh: 我們用粉筆在地上畫畫。

chalk.variant_en: Also often said [tʃɔk], with slightly rounded lips.
chalk.spelling_en: The l is silent (as in talk and walk).

chance.tip_zh: chance 的 [æ] 嘴巴張大、嘴角拉開。結尾 nce 唸 [ns]：舌尖貼上排牙齦發 [n]，接著直接吹出 [s]，e 不發音。常見錯誤是多唸一個「斯」，變成 chan-si 兩拍。跟 dance 同韻。練習 a chance 時，a 輕輕帶過，重音落在 chance 的 [æ]。整個字只有一拍。
chance.tip_en: The [æ] in chance has a wide-open mouth with the corners pulled back. The ending nce is [ns]: put the tongue tip on the upper gum ridge for [n], then blow out [s] directly; the e is silent. A common mistake is adding an extra 'si', making two beats, chan-si. It rhymes with dance. When practicing a chance, say a lightly and put the stress on the [æ] of chance. The whole word is one beat.

examples.en: Give me one more chance, please.
examples.zh: 請再給我一次機會。

examples.en: This is your chance to sing!
examples.zh: 這是你唱歌的好機會！

change.tip_zh: change 的 a 唸 [e]，要從 [e] 滑向 [ɪ]，不是 chance 的 [æ]。結尾 [ndʒ]：舌尖先貼上排牙齦發 [n]，接著嘴唇稍噘、放出有聲的 [dʒ]，e 不發音。不要在最後加上「ㄐㄧ」多出一拍。跟 strange 同韻，可以一起練。整個字只有一個音節，雖然拼法很長。
change.tip_en: The a in change is [e], gliding toward [ɪ], not the [æ] of chance. For the ending [ndʒ], put the tongue tip on the upper gum ridge for [n], then push the lips forward a little and release a voiced [dʒ]; the e is silent. Don't add a 'ji' at the end and create an extra beat. It rhymes with strange; practice them together. Though the spelling is long, the whole word is one syllable.

examples.en: Let's change seats with each other.
examples.zh: 我們互相換位子吧。

examples.en: Here is your change. Thank you!
examples.zh: 這是找您的零錢，謝謝！

cheap.tip_zh: cheap 的 ea 唸長而緊的 [i]，嘴角往兩邊拉；母音太短會變成 chip。開頭 [tʃ] 舌頭先擋住氣再放開，跟 sheep 一直吹氣的 [ʃ] 不同，兩個字別混。結尾 [p] 閉唇就停，不要送出「ㄆㄜ」。跟 keep、sleep 同韻，可以一起練。
cheap.tip_en: The ea in cheap is a long, tense [i] with the corners of the mouth pulled back; too short a vowel turns it into chip. For the opening [tʃ], the tongue blocks the air first and then releases it, unlike the steady air of [ʃ] in sheep; don't mix the two words up. For the final [p], close the lips and stop without a 'puh'. It rhymes with keep and sleep; practice them together.

examples.en: These pencils are very cheap.
examples.zh: 這些鉛筆很便宜。

examples.en: The toy was cheap, but it was fun.
examples.zh: 那個玩具很便宜，但是很好玩。

cheat.tip_zh: cheat 和 cheap 只差最後一個音：cheat 是舌尖頂住上排牙齦收 [t]，cheap 是雙唇閉起收 [p]。結尾要做到位，但不用送氣、也不要加母音。[i] 要長而緊，唸太短會像 chit。跟 eat、meat 同韻，可以先唸 eat 再在前面加上 [tʃ]。
cheat.tip_en: Cheat and cheap differ only in the last sound: cheat ends with the tongue tip pressing the upper gum ridge for [t], cheap with closed lips for [p]. Make the ending clearly, but without a puff of air or an added vowel. The [i] must be long and tense; too short sounds like chit. It rhymes with eat and meat; say eat first, then add [tʃ] in front.

examples.en: Don't cheat on the test.
examples.zh: 考試不可以作弊。

examples.en: It's not fair to cheat in a game.
examples.zh: 玩遊戲作弊不公平。

check.tip_zh: check 的 [ɛ] 短、嘴巴半開，常被拉長成 [e]，聽起來像 chake。ck 只唸一個 [k]，舌根頂住上顎就停，不要加「ㄜ」。開頭 [tʃ] 嘴唇稍噘；母音若張太大變 [ɑ]，就接近 chalk。跟 neck 同韻。練習 check your answers 時，[k] 和 your 之間不要停頓。整個字只有一拍。
check.tip_en: The [ɛ] in check is short with the mouth half open; learners often stretch it to [e], so it sounds like chake. The ck is just one [k]: the back of the tongue presses the roof of the mouth and stops, with no 'uh'. Push the lips forward a little for the opening [tʃ]; if the vowel opens too wide to [ɑ], it gets close to chalk. It rhymes with neck. When practicing check your answers, don't pause between [k] and your. The whole word is one beat.

examples.en: Check your answers before you hand in the test.
examples.zh: 交考卷前要檢查你的答案。

examples.en: Can you check my homework?
examples.zh: 你可以幫我檢查功課嗎？

cheer.tip_zh: cheer 的 eer 唸 [ɪr]，整個字只有一個音節。[ɪ] 一出來舌頭就往後捲成 [r]，常被拆成「七-兒」兩拍。開頭 [tʃ] 嘴唇往前噘；母音太開會變成 chair 的 [ɛr]。跟 dear、clear 同韻。練 cheer up 時，[r] 會和 up 連起來，像一個字。練習時嘴角先拉開，舌頭再往後捲。
cheer.tip_en: In cheer, eer is [ɪr], and the whole word is one syllable. As soon as [ɪ] starts, curl the tongue back into [r]; learners often split it into two beats like 'chi-er'. Push the lips forward for the opening [tʃ]; if the vowel opens too much it becomes the [ɛr] of chair. It rhymes with dear and clear. In cheer up, the [r] links into up, like one word. As you practice, spread the lips first, then curl the tongue back.

examples.en: We cheer for our team.
examples.zh: 我們為我們的隊伍加油。

examples.en: Let's cheer for the runners!
examples.zh: 我們來為跑者歡呼吧！

cheese.tip_zh: cheese 結尾的 se 唸有聲的 [z]，喉嚨要持續震動，像蜜蜂的嗡嗡聲，常被唸成無聲的 [s]。拍照時說 cheese 嘴角往兩邊拉，正是長 [i] 的口形，母音要拉長、不要縮短。開頭 [tʃ] 嘴唇稍噘。跟 please 同韻。
cheese.tip_en: The se at the end of cheese is a voiced [z]: keep the throat buzzing, like a bee; learners often say a voiceless [s]. When you say cheese for a photo, the corners of your mouth pull back; that is exactly the shape of the long [i], so keep the vowel long. Push the lips forward a little for the opening [tʃ]. It rhymes with please.

examples.en: I like cheese on my pizza.
examples.zh: 我喜歡披薩上有起司。

examples.en: Say cheese for the photo!
examples.zh: 拍照時說 cheese！

chicken.tip_zh: 重音在第一音節 [tʃɪ]，母音是短 [ɪ]，不要拉長成 cheek 的 [i]。第二音節 [kən] 要弱讀，母音輕而短，常被唸成響亮的「肯」。結尾 [n] 用舌尖貼上排牙齦收，不要收成 [ŋ]。它和 kitchen 很像，但子音順序相反，別混了。
chicken.tip_en: Stress the first syllable, [tʃɪ], whose vowel is the short [ɪ]; don't stretch it into the [i] of cheek. The second syllable [kən] is weak, with a light, short vowel; learners often say a loud 'ken'. End [n] with the tongue tip on the upper gum ridge, not [ŋ]. It is like kitchen but with the consonants in reverse order; don't mix them up.

examples.en: We had chicken soup for dinner.
examples.zh: 我們晚餐喝了雞湯。

examples.en: I like fried chicken.
examples.zh: 我喜歡炸雞。

child.tip_zh: child 的 i 唸 [aɪ]，但複數 children 的 i 卻是短 [ɪ]，兩個別混。結尾是 [ld]：舌尖貼上排牙齦先發暗 [l]，舌頭不離開，再放出 [d]。最常見的錯誤是吞掉 [l]，唸成 chide 的樣子。跟 mild、wild 同韻。練習 a child 時，child 要唸成一拍，[d] 輕輕收住就好。
child.tip_en: The i in child is [aɪ], but in the plural children it is the short [ɪ]; don't mix them up. It ends in [ld]: put the tongue tip on the upper gum ridge for a dark [l], keep it there, then release [d]. The most common mistake is swallowing the [l], so it sounds like chide. It rhymes with mild and wild. When practicing a child, say child as one beat and stop the [d] lightly.

examples.en: Every child needs a good breakfast.
examples.zh: 每個孩子都需要一頓好早餐。

examples.en: She was a happy child.
examples.zh: 她小時候是個快樂的孩子。

child.spelling_zh: child 的 i 唸 [aɪ]；children 的 i 唸 [ɪ]。
child.spelling_en: The i in child is [aɪ]; in children it is [ɪ].

china.tip_zh: China 重音在第一音節 [tʃaɪ]，[aɪ] 要滑完整；第二音節 [nə] 弱讀，母音輕而短，常被唸成跟第一音節一樣響亮的「那」。開頭 [tʃ] 嘴唇往前噘，不是扁唇的「ㄑ」。小寫的 china 是「瓷器」，唸法完全一樣。
china.tip_en: China is stressed on the first syllable, [tʃaɪ], and the [aɪ] must glide all the way; the second syllable [nə] is weak with a light, short vowel, but learners often say it as loudly as the first, 'na'. Push the lips forward for the opening [tʃ]; it is not the flat-lipped Mandarin q. Lowercase china means porcelain and is pronounced exactly the same.

examples.en: My aunt lives in China.
examples.zh: 我阿姨住在中國。

examples.en: China is a very big country.
examples.zh: 中國是一個很大的國家。

chinese.tip_zh: Chinese 的重音在第二音節 [niz]，跟 China 正好相反，常被唸成重音在前的 CHI-nese。第二音節的 [i] 要長，結尾 se 唸有聲的 [z]，喉嚨要震動，跟 cheese、please 同韻。第一音節 [tʃaɪ] 輕讀，但 [aɪ] 仍要滑完整。練習時可以想成先輕後重的兩拍。
chinese.tip_en: Chinese is stressed on the second syllable, [niz], the opposite of China; learners often say CHI-nese with stress at the front. The [i] in the second syllable is long, and the final se is a voiced [z] with a buzzing throat, rhyming with cheese and please. The first syllable [tʃaɪ] is light, but its [aɪ] still glides all the way. Practice it as two beats, light then strong.

examples.en: I speak Chinese at home.
examples.zh: 我在家說中文。

examples.en: We eat Chinese food every week.
examples.zh: 我們每個星期都吃中式料理。

chocolate.tip_zh: 學生常照「巧克力」或拼字唸成三個音節，結尾還唸成 late 的 [let]。美式最常見的唸法只有兩個音節 [tʃɔ] 和 [klət]：中間的 o 不發音，[k] 直接接 [l]，結尾的 -late 只是輕輕的 [lət]。重音在第一音節，[tʃ] 嘴唇稍微往前噘。
chocolate.tip_en: Students often say three syllables, following Mandarin 'qiao-ke-li' or the spelling, and say the ending like the [let] of 'late'. The most common American pronunciation has only two syllables, [tʃɔ] and [klət]: the middle o is silent, [k] goes straight into [l], and the ending -late is just a light [lət]. The stress is on the first syllable; push the lips slightly forward for [tʃ].

examples.en: I drink hot chocolate on cold days.
examples.zh: 天冷的時候，我會喝熱可可。

examples.en: Can I have a piece of chocolate after lunch?
examples.zh: 午餐後我可以吃一塊巧克力嗎？

chocolate.variant_zh: 也有人唸三個音節 [ˈtʃɔkələt]，但中間的 [ə] 很輕。
chocolate.variant_en: Some people say three syllables, [ˈtʃɔkələt], but the middle [ə] is very light.
chocolate.spelling_zh: 結尾 -late 唸 [lət]，不唸 late 的 [let]。
chocolate.spelling_en: The ending -late is [lət], not the [let] of 'late'.

choice.tip_zh: choice 的 oi 唸 [ɔɪ]：嘴巴先張開、嘴唇稍圓發 [ɔ]，再滑到 [ɪ]，跟 boy 的母音一樣。結尾 ce 唸無聲的 [s]，只吹氣，不要唸成 choose 的有聲 [z]，也不要多加「斯」。跟 voice 同韻。可以把 choice 和 choose 連著唸，感覺喉嚨有沒有震動的差別。
choice.tip_en: In choice, oi is [ɔɪ]: open the mouth with slightly rounded lips for [ɔ], then glide to [ɪ], the same vowel as in boy. The final ce is a voiceless [s], just air; don't make it the voiced [z] of choose, and don't add an extra 'si'. It rhymes with voice. Say choice and choose together and feel the difference in throat vibration.

examples.en: You have a choice: red or blue.
examples.zh: 你可以選：紅色或藍色。

examples.en: That was a good choice!
examples.zh: 那是個好選擇！

choose.tip_zh: choose 的 oo 唸長的 [u]，嘴唇噘圓往前。結尾 se 唸有聲的 [z]，喉嚨要持續震動；唸成 [s] 會不清楚。它和 cheese 只差母音：choose 是圓唇的 [u]，cheese 是嘴角拉開的 [i]。過去式 chose 唸 [tʃoz]，母音變成 [o]。跟 lose、news 同韻，可以一起練。
choose.tip_en: The oo in choose is a long [u] with the lips rounded and pushed forward. The final se is a voiced [z]; keep the throat buzzing, because [s] sounds unclear. It differs from cheese only in the vowel: choose has the rounded [u], cheese the spread-lip [i]. The past tense chose is [tʃoz]; the vowel changes to [o]. It rhymes with lose and news; practice them together.

examples.en: You can choose any book you like.
examples.zh: 你可以選任何一本你喜歡的書。

examples.en: Which color do you choose?
examples.zh: 你選哪一個顏色？

chopsticks.tip_zh: chopsticks 中間有 [pst]、結尾有 [ks] 兩組子音，常被插入母音，唸成 cha-pu-su-ti-ku-su。[tʃɑp] 的 [p] 閉唇但不送氣，直接接 [st]；結尾 [ks] 也不加母音，最後的 [s] 要清楚，因為筷子是一雙。重音在 chop，[ɑ] 嘴巴張大。整個字只有兩個音節。
chopsticks.tip_en: Chopsticks has two consonant groups, [pst] in the middle and [ks] at the end, and learners often insert vowels, saying cha-pu-su-ti-ku-su. The [p] in [tʃɑp] closes the lips without a puff and goes straight into [st]; the final [ks] has no vowel either, and the last [s] must be clear because chopsticks come in a pair. Stress chop, with the mouth wide open for [ɑ]. The whole word has only two syllables.

examples.en: I can eat noodles with chopsticks.
examples.zh: 我會用筷子吃麵。

examples.en: My American friend is learning to use chopsticks.
examples.zh: 我的美國朋友正在學用筷子。

christmas.tip_zh: 拼字裡的 h 和 t 都不發音：ch 唸 [k]，Christ 這部分只唸 [krɪs]，不是 [kraɪst]。學生常唸成「克里斯瑪斯」，在 [k] 和 [r] 中間、[s] 和 [m] 中間多加母音。[kr] 要一口氣連著唸，[ɪ] 短而放鬆，[s] 直接接 [m]；重音在第一音節，最後的 [məs] 輕輕帶過。
christmas.tip_en: The h and the t in the spelling are both silent: ch is said [k], and the Christ part is just [krɪs], not [kraɪst]. Students often say 'ke-li-si-ma-si', adding vowels between [k] and [r] and between [s] and [m]. Say [kr] in one go, keep [ɪ] short and relaxed, and go straight from [s] to [m]; stress the first syllable and pass lightly over the last part [məs].

examples.en: We put up a Christmas tree in our living room.
examples.zh: 我們在客廳擺了一棵聖誕樹。

examples.en: Merry Christmas to you and your family!
examples.zh: 祝你和你的家人聖誕快樂！

christmas.spelling_zh: ch 唸 [k]，h 和 t 都不發音。
christmas.spelling_en: ch is said [k]; the h and the t are both silent.

church.tip_zh: church 的 ur 唸捲舌的 [ɝ]，舌頭從頭到尾往後捲著，常被唸成不捲舌的「ㄑㄩ」。開頭和結尾都是 [tʃ]，嘴唇往前噘；結尾的 [tʃ] 放開就停，不要再加「ㄑㄧ」多出一拍。練習時可以先唸 her 的母音，再在前後加上 [tʃ]。
church.tip_en: In church, ur is the r-colored [ɝ]; keep the tongue curled back the whole time, though learners often say it flat with no curl. It starts and ends with [tʃ], with the lips pushed forward; release the final [tʃ] and stop, without adding a 'qi' that creates an extra beat. Practice by starting from the vowel of her, then adding [tʃ] before and after it.

examples.en: There is an old church in our town.
examples.zh: 我們鎮上有一座古老的教堂。

examples.en: My grandma goes to church on Sundays.
examples.zh: 我奶奶每個星期天都去教堂。

circle.tip_zh: circle 兩個音節都沒有一般的 a、e、i 母音：第一音節 [sɝ] 要把舌頭往後捲、嘴唇微圓，不能唸成平平的 [sə]。第二音節 [kḷ] 中間沒有母音，[k] 之後舌尖直接頂住上排牙齒後方的牙齦發暗 L。台灣學生常把字尾唸成 [o]，聽起來像「瑟扣」。收尾時舌尖停在上牙齦，不要張嘴把聲音放開。
circle.tip_en: Neither syllable of circle has a plain a, e or i vowel: for the first syllable [sɝ], curl the tongue back and round the lips slightly — don't say a flat [sə]. The second syllable [kḷ] has no vowel in the middle: right after [k], the tongue tip presses the gum ridge behind the upper teeth for a dark L. Taiwanese learners often end the word with [o], so it sounds like 'se-ko'. At the end, keep the tongue tip on the upper gum ridge; don't open the mouth to let the sound go.

examples.en: Please sit in a circle on the floor.
examples.zh: 請在地板上圍成一個圓圈坐下。

examples.en: Draw a big circle around the right answer.
examples.zh: 在正確答案外面畫一個大圓圈。

circle.spelling_zh: 第一個 c 唸 [s]，第二個 c 唸 [k]。
circle.spelling_en: The first c sounds [s]; the second c sounds [k].

city.tip_zh: city 的 c 唸 [s]，兩個音節都是短 [ɪ]，不要拉長成 [i]。美式發音中間的 t 會變成閃音：舌尖輕點一下上排牙齦，像很快的 [d]，不要用力送氣唸成「西替」。重音在第一音節。跟 pretty 同韻。
city.tip_en: The c in city is [s], and both syllables have the short [ɪ]; don't stretch it to [i]. In American English the t in the middle becomes a flap: the tongue tip taps the upper gum ridge once, like a quick [d], so don't puff it out like 'xi-ti'. Stress the first syllable. It rhymes with pretty.

examples.en: Taipei is a big city.
examples.zh: 台北是一個大城市。

examples.en: We visited a new city last summer.
examples.zh: 去年夏天我們去了一個新的城市。

clap.tip_zh: clap 開頭 [kl] 兩個子音要緊連：舌根擋住氣、放開的同時，舌尖已經貼在上排牙齦發 [l]，中間不要插入「ㄜ」變成 ke-lap。[æ] 嘴巴張大；結尾 [p] 閉唇就停。和 class 開頭相同，靠結尾分辨。過去式 clapped 唸 [klæpt]，仍然是一拍。
clap.tip_en: The opening [kl] of clap must be tight: as the back of the tongue releases the air, the tongue tip is already on the upper gum ridge for [l]; don't insert an 'uh' to make ke-lap. Open the mouth wide for [æ], and close the lips to stop on the final [p]. It starts like class; the ending tells them apart. The past tense clapped is [klæpt], still one beat.

examples.en: Clap your hands to the music.
examples.zh: 跟著音樂拍手。

examples.en: Let's clap for the winner!
examples.zh: 我們為贏家鼓掌吧！

class.tip_zh: 美式 class 唸 [æ]，嘴巴張大、嘴角往兩邊拉，不是英式的長 [ɑ]。開頭 [k] 不震動、要送氣，唸成有聲的 [g] 就變成 glass。[kl] 中間不加母音；結尾 ss 只唸一個 [s]。可以練 class、glass、grass，注意開頭有沒有震動。整個字只有一拍。
class.tip_en: American class has [æ], with a wide-open mouth and the corners pulled back, not the long British [ɑ]. The opening [k] has no voice and a puff of air; a voiced [g] turns it into glass. Don't add a vowel inside [kl], and the final ss is just one [s]. Practice class, glass and grass, noticing whether the first sound buzzes. The whole word is one beat.

examples.en: There are twenty students in my class.
examples.zh: 我們班上有二十個學生。

examples.en: Our English class starts at nine.
examples.zh: 我們的英文課九點開始。

classmate.tip_zh: 重音在 class，mate 是次重音。[s] 結束後雙唇要馬上閉起來發 [m]，中間常被插入母音，唸成 class-u-mate 三拍。後半 [met] 的 [e] 要滑向 [ɪ]，結尾 [t] 舌尖輕輕頂住就收，不要送氣。美式 class 的 [æ] 嘴巴要張大。整個字只有兩拍。
classmate.tip_en: The main stress is on class, with secondary stress on mate. Right after [s], close the lips for [m]; learners often insert a vowel here and say three beats, class-u-mate. In the second half, [met], the [e] glides toward [ɪ], and the final [t] is a light stop with the tongue tip, without a puff of air. In American English the [æ] of class needs a wide-open mouth. The whole word has only two beats.

examples.en: Amy is my classmate.
examples.zh: Amy 是我的同班同學。

examples.en: My classmate helped me with math.
examples.zh: 我的同學幫我做數學。

classroom.tip_zh: classroom 的難點在 [s] 接 [r]：[s] 之後舌頭立刻往後捲成 [r]，常被唸成 [l]，變成 class-loom，或在中間多加母音。重音在 class；room 的 [u] 長、嘴唇圓，結尾 [m] 雙唇閉起。有些美國人把 room 唸成較短的 [rʊm]，兩種都聽得到。
classroom.tip_en: The hard part of classroom is [s] followed by [r]: right after [s], curl the tongue back into [r]; learners often say [l], giving class-loom, or add a vowel in between. Stress class; the [u] in room is long with rounded lips, and the final [m] closes the lips. Some Americans say room with the shorter [rʊm]; you will hear both.

examples.en: Our classroom is on the second floor.
examples.zh: 我們的教室在二樓。

examples.en: Please keep the classroom clean.
examples.zh: 請保持教室乾淨。

clean.tip_zh: clean 的 ea 唸長而緊的 [i]，嘴角拉開。結尾 [n] 要用舌尖貼住上排牙齦；台灣學生常收成舌根的 [ŋ]，聽起來像 cling。開頭 [kl] 緊連，不要插入「ㄜ」。跟 bean、queen 同韻。練 clean up 時，[n] 會跟 up 連讀。整個字只有一拍，不要拖成兩拍。
clean.tip_en: The ea in clean is a long, tense [i] with the corners of the mouth pulled back. For the final [n], press the tongue tip against the upper gum ridge; Taiwanese learners often end with the back-of-tongue [ŋ], so it sounds like cling. Keep [kl] tight without an 'uh'. It rhymes with bean and queen. In clean up, the [n] links into up. The whole word is one beat; don't stretch it into two.

examples.en: Let's clean our classroom together.
examples.zh: 我們一起打掃教室吧。

examples.en: My room is clean now.
examples.zh: 我的房間現在很乾淨。

clear.tip_zh: clear 整個字只有一拍，常被唸成 ke-li-er 三拍。開頭 [kl] 緊連不加母音；ear 唸 [ɪr]，[ɪ] 一發出來舌頭就往後捲，不要再拖出一個「兒」的音節。舌尖在 [l] 時碰牙齦，到 [r] 時離開往後縮。跟 cheer、dear 同韻。
clear.tip_en: Clear is a single beat, but learners often say three, ke-li-er. Keep the opening [kl] tight with no vowel; ear is [ɪr], so curl the tongue back as soon as [ɪ] starts, without dragging out a separate 'er' syllable. The tongue tip touches the gum ridge for [l], then leaves it and pulls back for [r]. It rhymes with cheer and dear.

examples.en: The water in the lake is very clear.
examples.zh: 湖裡的水非常清澈。

examples.en: Your voice is loud and clear.
examples.zh: 你的聲音又大又清楚。

clerk.tip_zh: clerk 的 er 唸捲舌的 [ɝ]，跟 work 同韻；不要照字母唸成 [ɛ]，也不是英式的 [klɑk]。[ɝ] 舌頭往後捲、嘴唇微圓，整個母音都要捲。開頭 [kl] 不加母音，結尾 [k] 舌根頂住就停。練習時可以從 work 開始，把 [w] 換成 [kl]。
clerk.tip_en: In clerk, er is the r-colored [ɝ], rhyming with work; don't read the letter as [ɛ], and it is not the British [klɑk]. For [ɝ], curl the tongue back with slightly rounded lips and keep the whole vowel curled. Keep the opening [kl] free of vowels, and stop the final [k] with the back of the tongue. Practice by starting from work and replacing [w] with [kl].

examples.en: The clerk helped me find my size.
examples.zh: 店員幫我找到我的尺寸。

examples.en: Ask the clerk where the milk is.
examples.zh: 問店員牛奶放在哪裡。

clerk.spelling_en: er is [ɝ]; the e is not said [ɛ].

climb.tip_zh: climb 的 b 不發音，結尾只收 [m]，雙唇閉起來就好，常被唸成 climb-b 或 clim-ber。i 唸 [aɪ]，要從 [a] 滑到 [ɪ]。開頭 [kl] 緊連，不要插入母音唸成 ke-limb。跟 time 同韻。過去式 climbed 唸 [klaɪmd]，b 一樣不發音。名詞 climber 唸 [ˈklaɪmɚ]，b 同樣不唸。整個字只有一拍。
climb.tip_en: The b in climb is silent; the word ends on [m], just close the lips. Learners often say climb-b or clim-ber. The i is [aɪ], gliding from [a] to [ɪ]. Keep the opening [kl] tight without inserting a vowel, ke-limb. It rhymes with time. The past tense climbed is [klaɪmd]; the b is still silent. The noun climber is [ˈklaɪmɚ]; the b is silent there as well. The whole word is one beat.

examples.en: Monkeys like to climb trees.
examples.zh: 猴子喜歡爬樹。

examples.en: Let's climb the hill together.
examples.zh: 我們一起爬上那座小山吧。

clock.tip_zh: clock 開頭是 [kl] 子音串，k 和 l 中間不能加母音，學生常拉成三拍的「克拉克」。母音 [ɑ] 嘴巴要張大、下巴往下掉，比中文「啊」更開。字尾 [k] 只要舌根頂住軟顎收住，不要再送出一個「ㄜ」的尾音。
clock.tip_en: clock starts with the cluster [kl]: no vowel between k and l — learners often stretch it into three beats like 「克拉克」. The vowel [ɑ] needs a wide-open mouth with the jaw dropped, more open than Mandarin 「啊」. For the final [k], just close the back of the tongue against the soft palate; don't add an extra 'uh' after it.

examples.en: The clock on the wall is five minutes fast.
examples.zh: 牆上的時鐘快了五分鐘。

examples.en: Look at the clock. It's time for bed.
examples.zh: 看看時鐘，該睡覺了。

clothes.tip_zh: clothes 只有一個音節。結尾的 [ðz] 是兩個有聲子音連在一起：舌尖先輕放在上下門牙之間、喉嚨振動發 [ð]，再往後縮一點發 [z]。台灣學生常把結尾唸成無聲的 [s]，聽起來像「克漏斯」，或在中間多加母音唸成兩個音節。要一口氣唸完、喉嚨持續振動；如果 [ð] 來不及發，美國人日常也常唸 [kloz]，但結尾一定是有聲的 [z]，不是 [s]。
clothes.tip_en: Clothes has only one syllable. The ending [ðz] is two voiced consonants together: first rest the tongue tip lightly between the upper and lower front teeth and voice [ð], then pull back slightly for [z]. Taiwanese learners often end it with a voiceless [s], so it sounds like 'ke-lou-s', or add a vowel in the middle and make it two syllables. Say it in one breath with the throat buzzing the whole time; if [ð] is too quick to manage, Americans also often just say [kloz] — but the ending is always a voiced [z], never [s].

examples.en: Put your clothes in the closet, please.
examples.zh: 請把你的衣服放進衣櫃裡。

examples.en: My mom bought me new clothes for school.
examples.zh: 媽媽幫我買了上學穿的新衣服。

clothes.variant_zh: 日常口語也常唸 [kloz]，th 幾乎不發音。
clothes.variant_en: In everyday speech often [kloz], with the th almost dropped.

cloud.tip_zh: cloud 的 [aʊ] 要從張大嘴的 [a] 滑到圓唇的 [ʊ]，跟 how、now 的母音一樣，不要唸成單純的 [ɑ]。學生常把字尾 [d] 吞掉，只剩 [klaʊ]，聽起來像沒唸完。結尾舌尖要碰上齒齦停一下，輕輕收住 [d]，但不要加「的」那樣的母音。開頭 [kl] 也要黏在一起。
cloud.tip_en: In cloud, [aʊ] glides from an open-mouthed [a] to a rounded [ʊ], the same vowel as how and now — not a flat [ɑ]. Learners often swallow the final [d], leaving just [klaʊ], which sounds unfinished. At the end, touch the tongue tip to the ridge behind the upper teeth and gently close on [d], without adding a vowel like 「的」. Keep the opening [kl] stuck together too.

examples.en: That cloud looks like a big rabbit.
examples.zh: 那朵雲看起來像一隻大兔子。

examples.en: A dark cloud is coming, so let's go inside.
examples.zh: 一朵烏雲飄過來了，我們進去吧。

cloudy.tip_zh: cloudy 重音在第一音節 [klaʊ]，第二音節 [dɪ] 要輕短。美式口語中，夾在兩個母音之間的 [d] 會變成很快的閃音，舌尖輕輕彈一下上齒齦就好，不要唸成重重的「低」。[aʊ] 也要有滑向 [ʊ] 的動作，跟 cloud 一樣，別唸成扁平的 [ɑ]。
cloudy.tip_en: cloudy is stressed on the first syllable [klaʊ]; the second syllable [dɪ] is light and short. In casual American speech, a [d] between two vowels becomes a quick flap: the tongue tip just taps the ridge behind the upper teeth — don't say a heavy 「低」. The [aʊ] still needs its glide toward [ʊ], as in cloud, not a flat [ɑ].

examples.en: It's cloudy today, so take an umbrella.
examples.zh: 今天多雲，帶把傘吧。

examples.en: On cloudy days, we play games inside.
examples.zh: 陰天的時候，我們在室內玩遊戲。

club.tip_zh: club 的母音是短而放鬆的 [ʌ]，嘴巴半開，跟 cup、bus 一樣，學生常唸成太開的 [ɑ] 或圓唇的 [o]。字尾 [b] 是有聲的，雙唇閉起來收住就好，不要唸成清的 [p]，也不要在後面多加一個「ㄅㄜ」的母音。開頭 [kl] 中間也不能插母音。
club.tip_en: The vowel in club is the short, relaxed [ʌ] with the mouth half open, as in cup and bus; learners often make it too open ([ɑ]) or rounded ([o]). The final [b] is voiced: just close the lips to finish — don't turn it into a voiceless [p] or add a 「ㄅㄜ」 vowel after it. And no vowel inside the opening [kl].

examples.en: I joined the art club this year.
examples.zh: 我今年參加了美術社。

examples.en: Our English club meets every Friday.
examples.zh: 我們的英文社每週五聚會。

coat.tip_zh: coat 的 [o] 在美式發音裡是會滑動的長音，嘴唇從半圓慢慢收得更圓，學生常唸得太短太平，聽起來像 cut [kʌt]。字尾 [t] 舌尖頂上齒齦停住即可，不要送氣加出「特」的音節。把它跟 boat、goat 一起練，三個字的母音和結尾都一樣。
coat.tip_en: The [o] in coat is a long, gliding vowel in American English: the lips start half-round and close in rounder. Learners often make it too short and flat, so it sounds like cut [kʌt]. For the final [t], just stop with the tongue tip on the ridge behind the upper teeth — don't puff out an extra 「特」 syllable. Practice it with boat and goat; all three share the vowel and the ending.

examples.en: Put on your coat. It's cold outside.
examples.zh: 穿上外套，外面很冷。

examples.en: My coat has two big pockets.
examples.zh: 我的大衣有兩個大口袋。

coffee.tip_zh: coffee 重音在第一音節 [kɑ]，嘴巴張大、下巴放下。學生常受中文「咖啡」影響，把第二音節唸得又長又重，像「啡」一樣拉高；其實 [fɪ] 要輕短。[f] 要上排牙齒輕碰下唇吹氣，用雙唇的話會跟 copy [ˈkɑpɪ] 混在一起。
coffee.tip_en: coffee is stressed on the first syllable [kɑ], with the mouth open and the jaw down. Influenced by Mandarin 「咖啡」, learners often make the second syllable long and heavy, rising like 「啡」; in fact [fɪ] is light and short. Make [f] with the upper teeth lightly on the lower lip and blow — using both lips makes it blur into copy [ˈkɑpɪ].

examples.en: My dad drinks coffee every morning.
examples.zh: 我爸爸每天早上喝咖啡。

examples.en: This coffee shop sells yummy cakes too.
examples.zh: 這家咖啡店也賣好吃的蛋糕。

coffee.variant_zh: 也常聽到 [ˈkɔfɪ]，第一個母音嘴唇稍圓。
coffee.variant_en: You'll also hear [ˈkɔfɪ], with slightly rounded lips on the first vowel.

cold.tip_zh: cold 字尾有 [ld] 兩個子音，學生常只唸 [ko]，或把 l 含糊帶過，結果聽起來像 code 或 coat。[o] 唸完後舌尖抬起碰上齒齦做出 [l]，舌頭不放下，直接收成 [d]。可以先慢慢說 [kol]，再補上輕輕的 [d]；它跟 hold 只差開頭。
cold.tip_en: cold ends in two consonants, [ld]. Learners often say only [ko], or blur the l, so it sounds like code or coat. After [o], lift the tongue tip to the ridge behind the upper teeth for [l], and without dropping the tongue, close into [d]. Try saying [kol] slowly first, then add a light [d]; it differs from hold only in the first sound.

examples.en: It's cold today, so wear a hat.
examples.zh: 今天很冷，戴頂帽子吧。

examples.en: I'd like a glass of cold water, please.
examples.zh: 請給我一杯冰水。

collect.tip_zh: collect 重音在第二音節 [lɛkt]，第一音節 [kə] 要弱成很輕的 [ə]，學生常唸成重重的「扣」並把重音放前面。字尾 [kt] 是兩個子音，常被省成只剩 [k] 或 [t]；先用舌根擋一下做 [k]，再讓舌尖碰上齒齦收 [t]。中間是 [l]，別跟 correct 的 [r] 搞混。
collect.tip_en: collect is stressed on the second syllable [lɛkt]; the first syllable [kə] weakens to a very light [ə] — learners often say a heavy 「扣」 and put the stress up front. The ending [kt] is two consonants, often cut down to just [k] or [t]: first stop with the back of the tongue for [k], then touch the tongue tip to the ridge for [t]. The middle sound is [l] — don't mix it up with the [r] in correct.

examples.en: I collect stickers and keep them in a book.
examples.zh: 我收集貼紙，把它們收在一本冊子裡。

examples.en: The teacher will collect our notebooks after class.
examples.zh: 老師下課後會收我們的筆記本。

color.tip_zh: color 的拼字會騙人：第一音節其實是短而放鬆的 [ʌ]，跟 cup 一樣，不是 [o] 也不是 [ɑ]。第二音節 [lɚ] 舌尖先碰上齒齦做 [l]，接著舌頭往後捲成 [ɚ]，學生常唸成「樂」而沒有捲舌。整個字重音在前，後面輕輕帶過。
color.tip_en: The spelling of color is misleading: the first syllable is actually the short, relaxed [ʌ], as in cup — not [o] or [ɑ]. In the second syllable [lɚ], the tongue tip first touches the ridge for [l], then the tongue curls back into [ɚ]; learners often say 「樂」 with no r-curl. The stress is at the front; the end is light.

examples.en: What color is your new bike?
examples.zh: 你的新腳踏車是什麼顏色？

examples.en: Blue is my favorite color.
examples.zh: 藍色是我最喜歡的顏色。

color.spelling_zh: 拼字是 co-，但第一個母音唸 [ʌ]，不是 [o]。
color.spelling_en: It's spelled co-, but the first vowel is [ʌ], not [o].

comb.tip_zh: comb 字尾的 b 不發音，學生常照拼字唸出 [komb]，或乾脆唸成 come [kʌm]。正確是 [kom]：母音是嘴唇圓起來、會滑動的 [o]，跟 home 一樣；最後雙唇閉上做 [m]，讓鼻音持續一下就結束，嘴唇不要再打開放出 [b]。
comb.tip_en: The final b in comb is silent; learners often follow the spelling and say [komb], or just say come [kʌm]. The right form is [kom]: the vowel is the rounded, gliding [o], as in home; then close the lips for [m], let the nasal hum for a moment and stop — don't reopen the lips to release a [b].

examples.en: I use a comb to fix my hair.
examples.zh: 我用梳子整理頭髮。

examples.en: Where did I put my comb?
examples.zh: 我把梳子放到哪裡去了？

comb.spelling_zh: 字尾 b 不發音，跟 climb、thumb 一樣。
comb.spelling_en: The final b is silent, as in climb and thumb.

come.tip_zh: come 雖然拼字有 o 和 e，母音卻是短的 [ʌ]，嘴巴半開放鬆，跟 cup、some 一樣，不要唸成 comb [kom] 的圓唇 [o]。字尾 e 不發音。結尾 [m] 雙唇要確實閉上，學生常嘴巴沒閉就結束，聽起來只剩 [kʌ]。練習時可以把 come、some 放在一起唸，兩個字只差開頭。
come.tip_en: Although come is spelled with o and e, the vowel is the short [ʌ], mouth half open and relaxed, as in cup and some — not the rounded [o] of comb [kom]. The final e is silent. Close the lips firmly for the final [m]; learners often stop without closing them, so it sounds like just [kʌ]. Practice come and some together; they differ only in the first sound.

examples.en: Can you come to my birthday party?
examples.zh: 你可以來我的生日派對嗎？

examples.en: Come here and look at this bird!
examples.zh: 過來看看這隻鳥！

come.spelling_zh: o 唸 [ʌ]，字尾 e 不發音。
come.spelling_en: The o is said [ʌ], and the final e is silent.

comfortable.tip_zh: comfortable 的重音在第一音節 [ˈkʌm]，o 唸 [ʌ]，跟 come 一樣。台灣學生常照拼字唸成「康佛特伯」：把 for 唸成 [fɔr]、把重音放在 for 上，還把字尾 table 唸成桌子 table 的 [tebḷ]。其實後面三個音節都很輕：[fɚ] 輕輕捲舌，[tə] 是短短的 [ə]，最後 [bḷ] 收在暗 L。先唸熟 come，再把後面三個音節快速帶過。
comfortable.tip_en: The stress in comfortable is on the first syllable [ˈkʌm]; the o is [ʌ], as in come. Taiwanese learners often read it by spelling, like 'kang-fo-te-bo': they say for as [fɔr], put the stress on for, and say the ending table like the word table [tebḷ]. In fact the last three syllables are all light: [fɚ] with a light curl of the tongue, [tə] with a short [ə], and [bḷ] ending in a dark L. Get come right first, then run quickly through the last three syllables.

examples.en: This sofa is very comfortable.
examples.zh: 這張沙發很舒服。

examples.en: Wear comfortable shoes for the school trip.
examples.zh: 校外教學要穿舒適的鞋子。

comfortable.variant_zh: 美國人口語常唸成三音節 [ˈkʌmftɚbḷ]。
comfortable.variant_en: Americans often say it in three syllables: [ˈkʌmftɚbḷ].
comfortable.spelling_zh: 字尾 -table 不唸成單字 table 的 [tebḷ]。
comfortable.spelling_en: The ending -table is not said like the word table [tebḷ].

comic.tip_zh: comic 重音在第一音節 [kɑ]，嘴巴張大，不要唸成圓唇的「扣」。第二音節 [mɪk] 是短的 [ɪ]，嘴角放鬆，不要拉長成 [i]。字尾 [k] 用舌根輕輕收住，學生常把它丟掉，或在後面多唸一個母音，變成三個音節。
comic.tip_en: comic is stressed on the first syllable [kɑ] with the mouth wide open — not a rounded 「扣」. The second syllable [mɪk] has a short [ɪ] with relaxed lips; don't stretch it into [i]. Close the final [k] lightly with the back of the tongue; learners often drop it or add a vowel after it, turning the word into three syllables.

examples.en: I read a funny comic before bed.
examples.zh: 我睡前看了一本好笑的漫畫。

examples.en: My brother draws his own comic books.
examples.zh: 我哥哥自己畫漫畫書。

common.tip_zh: common 中間雖然有兩個 m，只唸一個 [m]。重音在第一音節 [kɑ]，嘴巴張大；第二音節弱化成 [ən]，學生常唸成清楚又用力的「門」。字尾是 [n]，舌尖要頂在上齒齦，不要讓舌根往後變成 [ŋ]，否則聽起來像 [ˈkɑmɪŋ]。
common.tip_en: common has two m's in the middle, but you say just one [m]. The stress is on the first syllable [kɑ], mouth wide open; the second syllable weakens to [ən] — learners often say a clear, forceful 「門」. The final sound is [n]: keep the tongue tip on the ridge behind the upper teeth, and don't let the back of the tongue turn it into [ŋ], or it sounds like [ˈkɑmɪŋ].

examples.en: Smith is a common name in America.
examples.zh: Smith 在美國是很常見的姓。

examples.en: Tom and I have a lot in common.
examples.zh: 我和 Tom 有很多共同點。

common.spelling_zh: 雙寫的 mm 只唸一個 [m]。
common.spelling_en: The double mm is said as a single [m].

computer.tip_zh: computer 的重音在第二音節 [ˈpju]，第一音節 [kəm] 要又短又輕。台灣學生常把重音放在 com，而且把 com 唸成飽滿的 [kɑm]；也常把 pu 唸成 [pu]，漏掉中間的 [j]。正確的 [pju] 就是 p 後面接英文字母 U 的唸法。最後的 [tɚ] 要捲舌；美式口語中 t 夾在兩個母音之間，常變成輕快的彈舌音，聽起來像很快的 [d]。
computer.tip_en: The stress in computer is on the second syllable [ˈpju]; the first syllable [kəm] is short and light. Taiwanese learners often stress com and say it as a full [kɑm]; they also often say pu as [pu], leaving out the [j]. The correct [pju] is p followed by the name of the letter U. The final [tɚ] needs a curled tongue; in American speech the t between two vowels often becomes a quick tap that sounds like a fast [d].

examples.en: We use the computer in English class.
examples.zh: 我們在英文課上使用電腦。

examples.en: My grandpa is learning to use a computer.
examples.zh: 我爺爺正在學習用電腦。

convenient.tip_zh: convenient 的重音在第二音節 [ˈvin]，[v] 要用上排門牙輕碰下唇、喉嚨振動，不能唸成 [w] 或 [b]。台灣學生常照拼字切成四個音節，把字尾 ent 唸成飽滿的 [ɛnt]。其實 ni 只是滑過去的 [nj]，字尾 [jənt] 很輕；最後 [nt] 舌尖頂住上牙齦，t 輕輕收住，不要多加母音。第一音節 [kən] 也要輕，不要唸成 [kɑn]。
convenient.tip_en: The stress in convenient is on the second syllable [ˈvin]; for [v], touch the upper front teeth to the lower lip and voice it — don't say [w] or [b]. Taiwanese learners often split it by spelling into four syllables and say the ending ent as a full [ɛnt]. In fact ni is just a gliding [nj], and the ending [jənt] is light; for the final [nt], press the tongue tip on the upper gum ridge and stop the t softly, without adding a vowel. The first syllable [kən] is light too — don't say [kɑn].

examples.en: The new MRT station is very convenient.
examples.zh: 新的捷運站很方便。

examples.en: Is Saturday morning convenient for you?
examples.zh: 星期六早上你方便嗎？

cook.tip_zh: cook 的 oo 在這裡是短的 [ʊ]，跟 book、look 一樣，嘴唇微圓、舌頭放鬆，不要唸成像 food 那樣拉長的 [u]。學生也常把字尾 [k] 吞掉，只剩 [kʊ]。練習時把 book、cook、look 排在一起說，母音和結尾都相同，只換開頭。
cook.tip_en: In cook, the oo is the short [ʊ], as in book and look: lips slightly rounded, tongue relaxed — not the long [u] of food. Learners also often swallow the final [k], leaving [kʊ]. Practice book, cook, look in a row: the vowel and ending are the same, only the first sound changes.

examples.en: My mom likes to cook dinner for us.
examples.zh: 我媽媽喜歡煮晚餐給我們吃。

examples.en: Can you cook fried rice by yourself?
examples.zh: 你會自己煮炒飯嗎？

cookie.tip_zh: cookie 第一音節是短的 [ʊ]，嘴唇微圓但不用力，學生常拉長成 [u]，唸成「酷奇」。重音在前，第二音節 [kɪ] 輕而短，不要拉長成 [i]。它其實就是 cook 加上 [ɪ]：先說 cook，再輕輕補一個 [ɪ]，母音長度就對了。
cookie.tip_en: The first syllable of cookie has the short [ʊ], lips slightly rounded but not tense; learners often stretch it into [u] and say 「酷奇」. The stress is at the front; the second syllable [kɪ] is light and short, not a long [i]. It's really cook plus [ɪ]: say cook, then lightly add [ɪ], and the vowel length comes out right.

examples.en: Can I have one more cookie, please?
examples.zh: 我可以再吃一塊餅乾嗎？

examples.en: This cookie is shaped like a star.
examples.zh: 這塊餅乾是星星形狀的。

cool.tip_zh: cool 字尾是暗 L：[u] 唸完後舌根往後抬、舌尖碰上齒齦。學生常省掉 l 只唸 [ku]，聽起來像中文「酷」，其實少了最後一個音。母音 [u] 嘴唇圓而突出，要拉長，不要唸成短的 [ʊ]。它跟 pool、school 押韻，可以一起練結尾。
cool.tip_en: cool ends in a dark L: after [u], raise the back of the tongue and touch the tongue tip to the ridge behind the upper teeth. Learners often drop the l and say just [ku], like Mandarin 「酷」 — missing the last sound. The vowel [u] needs rounded, pushed-out lips and should be long, not the short [ʊ]. It rhymes with pool and school; practice the ending with them.

examples.en: The water in the pool feels cool.
examples.zh: 泳池的水摸起來涼涼的。

examples.en: Your new shoes look so cool!
examples.zh: 你的新鞋看起來好酷！

copy.tip_zh: copy 的 o 唸張大嘴的 [ɑ]，不是圓唇的 [o]，學生常唸成「扣皮」。中間 [p] 雙唇閉起再爆開，不要讓上排牙齒碰下唇變成 [f]，否則會聽成 coffee [ˈkɑfɪ]。重音在第一音節，最後的 [ɪ] 輕短帶過。先慢慢說 [kɑ]，再輕輕接上 [pɪ]，就不會唸成兩個一樣重的音節。
copy.tip_en: The o in copy is the open-mouthed [ɑ], not a rounded [o] — learners often say 「扣皮」. The middle [p] closes both lips and pops them open; don't let the upper teeth touch the lower lip to make [f], or it will be heard as coffee [ˈkɑfɪ]. The stress is on the first syllable; the final [ɪ] is light and short. Say [kɑ] slowly first, then lightly add [pɪ], so the two syllables don't come out equally heavy.

examples.en: Please copy the new words into your notebook.
examples.zh: 請把新單字抄到筆記本上。

examples.en: Can you make a copy of this page?
examples.zh: 你可以把這一頁影印一份嗎？

corner.tip_zh: corner 有兩個捲舌音：第一音節 [kɔr] 的 [ɔ] 後面舌頭就要往後捲，第二音節 [nɚ] 再捲一次。學生常兩個都不捲，唸成「扣那」。重音在 [kɔr]，第二音節輕。練習時先說 [kɔr]，舌頭保持捲著，再接到 [nɚ]。
corner.tip_en: corner has two r-sounds: right after the [ɔ] in the first syllable [kɔr] the tongue curls back, and it curls again in the second syllable [nɚ]. Learners often curl neither and say 「扣那」. The stress is on [kɔr]; the second syllable is light. Practice by saying [kɔr], keep the tongue curled, then move on to [nɚ].

examples.en: Turn left at the next corner.
examples.zh: 在下一個轉角左轉。

examples.en: The cat is sleeping in the corner.
examples.zh: 貓在角落睡覺。
