correct.tip_zh: correct 的重音在第二音節 [ˈrɛkt]，第一音節 [kə] 要輕而短。台灣學生常照拼字把 cor 唸成很重的 [kɔr]，重音放在前面，聽起來像 core 再接一段。字尾 [kt] 兩個子音連在一起，常被多加母音，或乾脆丟掉 t。練法：[k] 只用舌根擋住、不放氣，馬上接 [t]。另外 correct 和 collect 只差在 r 和 l，第二音節開頭一定要捲舌，否則會被聽成 collect。
correct.tip_en: The stress in correct is on the second syllable [ˈrɛkt]; the first syllable [kə] is light and short. Taiwanese learners often read cor by spelling as a heavy [kɔr] and stress the front, so it sounds like core plus something. The ending [kt] is two consonants together, and learners often add a vowel or drop the t. Practice: block [k] with the back of the tongue without releasing air, then go straight into [t]. Also, correct and collect differ only in r versus l, so the second syllable must start with the curled tongue, or it will be heard as collect.

examples.en: Your answer is correct. Good job!
examples.zh: 你的答案是對的，做得好！

examples.en: Please check if the spelling is correct.
examples.zh: 請檢查拼字是否正確。

correct.kk_flag: Given [kɚˈɛkt] comes from CMU ER0+EH1; Taiwan KK dictionaries write [kəˈrɛkt], with r starting the stressed syllable. Sound is close, but [kɚ·ɛkt] suggests a break before the stressed vowel. Consider [kəˈrɛkt] / sylls kə·rɛkt.

cost.tip_zh: cost 字尾 [st] 是兩個子音，學生常只唸到 [s] 就停，或在後面加母音唸成「斯特」。[s] 吹氣之後，舌尖直接頂上齒齦收成 [t]，中間不要停頓。母音 [ɑ] 嘴巴張大，別唸成 coast 那種圓唇的 [o]，兩個字意思完全不同。
cost.tip_en: cost ends in two consonants, [st]. Learners often stop at [s], or add a vowel and say 「斯特」. After blowing the [s], put the tongue tip straight onto the ridge behind the upper teeth for [t], with no pause. The vowel [ɑ] needs a wide-open mouth — don't make it the rounded [o] of coast, a completely different word.

examples.en: How much does this pencil cost?
examples.zh: 這枝鉛筆多少錢？

examples.en: What is the cost of a bus ticket?
examples.zh: 一張公車票要多少錢？

cost.variant_en: Some speakers say [kɔst], with slightly rounded lips.

couch.tip_zh: couch 拼字是 ou，唸 [aʊ]，嘴巴先張大再收圓，跟 cow 一樣。字尾 [tʃ] 嘴唇要微微嘟起，舌面貼住上顎再一口氣放開，學生常唸得太輕或乾脆省掉，聽起來像 cow。母音也別唸成 [æ]，否則會變成 catch。
couch.tip_en: couch is spelled ou and said [aʊ]: open the mouth wide, then round it, as in cow. For the final [tʃ], push the lips out slightly, press the tongue against the roof of the mouth, and release it all at once; learners often make it too weak or drop it, so it sounds like cow. Don't make the vowel [æ] either, or it becomes catch.

examples.en: Dad fell asleep on the couch.
examples.zh: 爸爸在沙發上睡著了。

examples.en: Let's sit on the couch and read.
examples.zh: 我們坐在沙發上看書吧。

could.tip_zh: could 的 l 不發音，ould 只唸 [ʊd]，跟 good、should 同韻。常見錯誤是把 l 唸出來，或把母音拉長成 [u]。[ʊ] 短而放鬆，嘴唇微圓；結尾 [d] 舌尖輕點上排牙齦就收，不要加「ㄉㄜ」。在 could you 裡，[d] 和 you 常連成 [dʒ]。在句子裡 could 常輕讀，但 [ʊ] 仍要短。
could.tip_en: The l in could is silent; ould is just [ʊd], rhyming with good and should. Common mistakes are saying the l or stretching the vowel into [u]. The [ʊ] is short and relaxed with slightly rounded lips; for the final [d], tap the tongue tip on the upper gum ridge and stop, without adding 'duh'. In could you, the [d] and you often blend into [dʒ]. In sentences could is often unstressed, but the [ʊ] stays short.

examples.en: Could you open the door, please?
examples.zh: 可以請你開門嗎？

examples.en: I could swim when I was five.
examples.zh: 我五歲時就會游泳了。

count.tip_zh: count 的 [aʊ] 後面接 [nt]，學生常把 [n] 和 [t] 都吞掉，只剩 [kaʊ]，聽起來像 cow。[aʊ] 唸完，舌尖抬到上齒齦發 [n]，舌頭不離開，直接停住做 [t]。美國人常把這個 [t] 唸得很輕，但 [n] 一定要清楚。可以先說 cow，再把舌尖抬起補上 [nt]，聽聽差別。
count.tip_en: In count, [aʊ] is followed by [nt]. Learners often swallow both [n] and [t], leaving [kaʊ], which sounds like cow. After [aʊ], raise the tongue tip to the ridge for [n], keep it there, and stop for [t]. Americans often say this [t] very lightly, but the [n] must be clear. Try saying cow first, then lift the tongue tip to add [nt], and listen to the difference.

examples.en: Let's count from one to twenty.
examples.zh: 我們從一數到二十吧。

examples.en: Can you count the apples in the box?
examples.zh: 你可以數一數箱子裡的蘋果嗎？

country.tip_zh: country 的 ou 唸短的 [ʌ]，跟 cup 一樣，不是 count 的 [aʊ]，學生常被拼字騙。重音在第一音節 [kʌn]。第二音節 [trɪ] 的 t 和 r 要黏在一起，跟 tree 的開頭一樣，嘴唇微嘟、舌頭往後捲，不要在 t 後面加母音唸成「特瑞」。
country.tip_en: The ou in country is the short [ʌ], as in cup — not the [aʊ] of count; the spelling often fools learners. The stress is on the first syllable [kʌn]. In the second syllable [trɪ], t and r stick together like the start of tree: lips slightly pushed out, tongue curled back — don't add a vowel after t and say 「特瑞」.

examples.en: My grandparents live in the country.
examples.zh: 我的祖父母住在鄉下。

examples.en: Japan is a beautiful country.
examples.zh: 日本是個美麗的國家。

country.spelling_zh: ou 在這裡唸 [ʌ]，不是 out 的 [aʊ]。
country.spelling_en: Here ou is said [ʌ], not the [aʊ] of out.

course.tip_zh: course 只有一個音節 [kɔrs]，拼字的 ou 和字尾 e 都不另外發音。[ɔ] 後舌頭往後捲做 [r]，接著舌尖靠近上齒齦吹出 [s]。學生常省掉捲舌唸成「扣斯」，或在 s 後加母音。它和 horse 押韻，可以一起練。
course.tip_en: course has just one syllable, [kɔrs]; the ou and the final e don't add any extra sounds. After [ɔ], curl the tongue back for [r], then bring the tongue tip near the ridge and blow out [s]. Learners often skip the r-curl and say 「扣斯」, or add a vowel after the s. It rhymes with horse — practice them together.

examples.en: Of course you can play with us!
examples.zh: 你當然可以跟我們一起玩！

examples.en: My sister is taking a cooking course.
examples.zh: 我姊姊正在上烹飪課。

course.spelling_zh: 字尾 e 不發音，ou 加 r 合起來唸 [ɔr]。
course.spelling_en: The final e is silent; ou plus r together is said [ɔr].

cousin.tip_zh: cousin 的 ou 唸短的 [ʌ]，s 唸有聲的 [z]，學生常唸成「卡森」，母音太開又用了清的 [s]。[z] 要讓喉嚨震動，像蜜蜂嗡嗡聲。第二音節弱化成 [ən]，字尾 [n] 舌尖頂上齒齦，不要變成 [ŋ]。它和 dozen 押韻。重音在第一音節。
cousin.tip_en: In cousin, ou is the short [ʌ] and s is the voiced [z]; learners often say 「卡森」, with too open a vowel and a voiceless [s]. Make [z] buzz in the throat like a bee. The second syllable weakens to [ən]; for the final [n], keep the tongue tip on the ridge, not [ŋ]. It rhymes with dozen. The stress is on the first syllable.

examples.en: My cousin lives in Kaohsiung.
examples.zh: 我的表哥住在高雄。

examples.en: I play games with my cousin every summer.
examples.zh: 我每年夏天都和表妹一起玩遊戲。

cousin.spelling_zh: ou 唸 [ʌ]、s 唸 [z]，兩處都跟拼字直覺不同。
cousin.spelling_en: The ou is said [ʌ] and the s is [z] — neither matches what the spelling suggests.

cover.tip_zh: cover 的 o 唸 [ʌ]，跟 love、come 的母音一樣，不是 [o]。台灣學生常看拼字唸成 [ˈkovɚ]，或把中間的 [v] 唸成 [b]、[w]。[v] 要讓上排門牙輕碰下唇、喉嚨振動，氣從縫隙擠出來；接著 [ɚ] 舌頭往後捲。cover 和 color [ˈkʌlɚ] 前後完全一樣，只靠中間的 [v] 分辨，所以一定要咬唇發清楚。可以先唸 love，再換成 [kʌv]，最後加上捲舌的 [ɚ]。
cover.tip_en: The o in cover is [ʌ], the same vowel as in love and come, not [o]. Taiwanese learners often read it by spelling as [ˈkovɚ], or turn the middle [v] into [b] or [w]. For [v], touch the upper front teeth to the lower lip and voice it, pushing the air through the gap; then curl the tongue back for [ɚ]. Cover and color [ˈkʌlɚ] are identical except for the middle [v] versus [l], so the lip-and-teeth [v] must be clear. Say love first, switch to [kʌv], then add the curled [ɚ].

examples.en: Please cover your mouth when you cough.
examples.zh: 咳嗽的時候請摀住嘴巴。

examples.en: I love the cover of this book.
examples.zh: 我很喜歡這本書的封面。

cow.tip_zh: cow 的 ow 唸 [aʊ]，嘴巴要先張大到 [a]，再收圓滑到 [ʊ]，跟 how、now 一樣。學生常唸成 [ko]，那是 low、snow 的 ow。一個簡單的判斷：cow 押 how，不押 low。滑動要明顯，前半下巴張大，後半嘴唇收圓。字尾沒有子音，[ʊ] 收圓之後就結束，不要再加 [k] 或鼻音。
cow.tip_en: The ow in cow is [aʊ]: open the mouth wide for [a], then round it and glide to [ʊ], as in how and now. Learners often say [ko] — that's the ow of low and snow. An easy check: cow rhymes with how, not low. Make the glide clear: jaw wide open for the first half, lips rounded for the second. There's no final consonant: once the lips round into [ʊ], stop — don't add a [k] or a nasal.

examples.en: The cow is eating grass on the farm.
examples.zh: 那頭牛在農場上吃草。

examples.en: A cow gives us milk every day.
examples.zh: 乳牛每天給我們牛奶。

crazy.tip_zh: crazy 開頭 [kr] 要黏在一起，k 後面不加母音，舌頭直接往後捲進 [r]。重音在 [kre]，[e] 是會滑向 [ɪ] 的長音，像 day 的母音。中間的 z 唸有聲的 [z]，喉嚨要震動，學生常唸成清的 [s]。第二音節 [zɪ] 輕而短。
crazy.tip_en: The opening [kr] of crazy must stick together: no vowel after k, the tongue curls straight back into [r]. The stress is on [kre]; [e] is a long vowel that glides toward [ɪ], like the vowel of day. The middle z is the voiced [z] — the throat should vibrate; learners often say a voiceless [s]. The second syllable [zɪ] is light and short.

examples.en: My little brother is crazy about dinosaurs.
examples.zh: 我弟弟超級迷恐龍。

examples.en: That's a crazy idea, but let's try it!
examples.zh: 這個點子很瘋狂，不過我們試試看吧！

cross.tip_zh: cross 常見的錯是在 k 和 r 中間加母音，唸成「克羅斯」三拍。k 一放開，舌頭就已經往後捲好進入 [r]。母音是 [ɔ]，嘴巴張開、嘴唇只稍微圓，不是更圓更緊的 [o]。字尾 ss 只唸一個 [s]，吹氣就結束，不要加母音。
cross.tip_en: A common mistake with cross is putting a vowel between k and r and saying 「克羅斯」 in three beats. As soon as k releases, the tongue should already be curled back into [r]. The vowel is [ɔ]: mouth open, lips only slightly rounded — not the rounder, tighter [o]. The final ss is a single [s]: blow and stop, with no added vowel.

examples.en: Look both ways before you cross the street.
examples.zh: 過馬路前要先看看左右兩邊。

examples.en: Cross out the wrong answer with your pencil.
examples.zh: 用鉛筆把錯的答案劃掉。

cry.tip_zh: cry 的 y 唸 [aɪ]，嘴巴從張大的 [a] 滑到 [ɪ]，跟 try、dry 同韻。關鍵在開頭 [kr]：k 和 r 中間不能插母音唸成「克來」。k 放開時嘴唇已經微嘟、舌頭已往後捲好，直接滑進 [aɪ]。y 不要唸成 [ɪ] 或 [i]，它在這裡是完整的 [aɪ]。
cry.tip_en: The y in cry is [aɪ], gliding from an open [a] to [ɪ]; it rhymes with try and dry. The key is the opening [kr]: no vowel between k and r, as in 「克來」. When k releases, the lips are already slightly pushed out and the tongue already curled back, sliding straight into [aɪ]. Don't say the y as [ɪ] or [i]; here it's a full [aɪ].

examples.en: The baby starts to cry when she is hungry.
examples.zh: 小寶寶餓的時候就會開始哭。

examples.en: Don't cry. We can fix your toy.
examples.zh: 別哭，我們可以修好你的玩具。

cup.tip_zh: cup 的母音 [ʌ] 短而放鬆，嘴巴半開。學生常唸成嘴角拉開的 [æ]，變成 cap，或嘴巴張太大的 [ɑ]，變成 cop。字尾 [p] 雙唇閉上就收住，不要再張開送出「ㄆㄜ」的尾音。可以把 cup、come、cut 一起練，開頭和母音都相同。
cup.tip_en: The vowel [ʌ] in cup is short and relaxed, with the mouth half open. Learners often spread the lips into [æ], making cap, or open too wide into [ɑ], making cop. For the final [p], close the lips and stop — don't open them again to puff out a 「ㄆㄜ」. Practice cup, come, and cut together; they share the first sound and the vowel.

examples.en: Would you like a cup of tea?
examples.zh: 你要來杯茶嗎？

examples.en: I drink a cup of milk every morning.
examples.zh: 我每天早上喝一杯牛奶。

cut.tip_zh: cut 和 cat、coat 只差在母音：cut 是短而放鬆的 [ʌ]，嘴巴半開；cat 的 [æ] 嘴角要往兩邊拉；coat 的 [o] 嘴唇要圓。學生常三個唸成一樣。字尾 [t] 舌尖頂住上齒齦就停，不需要送氣，也不要加「特」。可以用鏡子看嘴型練習。
cut.tip_en: cut, cat, and coat differ only in the vowel: cut has the short, relaxed [ʌ] with the mouth half open; cat's [æ] spreads the corners of the mouth; coat's [o] rounds the lips. Learners often say all three the same. For the final [t], stop with the tongue tip on the ridge — no puff of air, and no added 「特」. You can practice the mouth shapes with a mirror.

examples.en: Please cut the cake into eight pieces.
examples.zh: 請把蛋糕切成八塊。

examples.en: I need scissors to cut this paper.
examples.zh: 我需要剪刀來剪這張紙。

cute.tip_zh: cute 的 u 唸 [ju]，k 後面要先帶出一個 [j] 再接長的 [u]，跟 you 的音一樣。學生常漏掉 [j] 唸成 [kut]，或把字尾 e 唸出來。少了 [j] 就不是 cute；字尾 [t] 輕輕收住，也別跟 cut [kʌt] 搞混。可以先說 you，再在前面加上 [k]，最後補 [t]，連起來就是 cute。
cute.tip_en: The u in cute is [ju]: after k, bring in a [j] and then a long [u], the same sound as you. Learners often leave out [j] and say [kut], or pronounce the final e. Without [j] it isn't cute. Close the final [t] lightly, and don't mix it up with cut [kʌt]. Say you first, put [k] in front of it, then add [t] at the end — together that's cute.

examples.en: Look at that cute little puppy!
examples.zh: 你看那隻可愛的小狗！

examples.en: Your drawing of the cat is so cute.
examples.zh: 你畫的貓好可愛。

cute.spelling_zh: 字尾 e 不發音，但讓 u 唸成 [ju]。
cute.spelling_en: The final e is silent but makes the u say [ju].

dance.tip_zh: dance 的 a 是 [æ]，嘴巴張大、嘴角往兩邊拉，像要笑的樣子，學生常張得不夠，唸成 [ɛ]。字尾 [ns]：舌尖先頂上齒齦做 [n]，再稍微放開讓氣流出成 [s]，學生常在 n 後面加母音唸成「丹斯」。拼字的 e 不發音。
dance.tip_en: The a in dance is [æ]: open the mouth wide and spread the corners as if smiling; learners often don't open enough and say [ɛ]. For the ending [ns], put the tongue tip on the ridge for [n], then loosen it slightly to let air out for [s] — learners often add a vowel after n and say 「丹斯」. The spelled e is silent.

examples.en: We dance to music in PE class.
examples.zh: 我們在體育課隨著音樂跳舞。

examples.en: Can you dance like a robot?
examples.zh: 你會跳機器人舞嗎？

dance.spelling_zh: 字尾 e 不發音，ce 唸 [s]。
dance.spelling_en: The final e is silent; ce is said [s].

dangerous.tip_zh: dangerous 的第一音節 [ˈden] 母音是 [e]，跟 danger、name 一樣；台灣學生常看到 a 就唸成 [æ] 或 [ɑ]，聽起來像「蛋」。重音放在第一音節，後面 [dʒə] 和 [rəs] 都要輕。[dʒ] 嘴唇稍微往前嘟，比中文的「ㄐ」更圓；接著舌頭往後捲發 [r]，最後 [rəs] 又短又輕，s 只吐氣，不要在後面多加母音。
dangerous.tip_en: The first syllable of dangerous, [ˈden], has the vowel [e], as in danger and name; Taiwanese learners often see the a and say [æ] or [ɑ], so it sounds like 'dan'. Stress the first syllable and keep [dʒə] and [rəs] light. For [dʒ], push the lips slightly forward — rounder than Mandarin 'j'; then curl the tongue back for [r]. The final [rəs] is short and light: the s is just a breath, with no extra vowel after it.

examples.en: Running on the stairs is dangerous.
examples.zh: 在樓梯上奔跑很危險。

examples.en: It is dangerous to play near the road.
examples.zh: 在馬路旁邊玩很危險。

dangerous.spelling_zh: 開頭的 a 唸 [e]，不是 [æ]。
dangerous.spelling_en: The a at the start sounds [e], not [æ].
dangerous.kk_flag: Notation only: Taiwan KK dictionaries write [ˈdendʒərəs]; the given [ɚə] (CMU ER0 AH0) sounds the same.

dark.tip_zh: dark 的 [ɑr]：嘴巴先張大唸 [ɑ]，接著舌頭往後捲。學生常不捲舌唸成「達克」，聽起來像 dock。最後舌根頂住軟顎收 [k]，不要再多送出一個母音。它和 park、mark 押韻，三個字的 [ɑrk] 完全一樣。母音要張到下巴明顯往下。
dark.tip_en: For the [ɑr] in dark, open the mouth wide for [ɑ], then curl the tongue back. Learners often skip the curl and say 「達克」, which sounds like dock. Finish with the back of the tongue against the soft palate for [k], without puffing out an extra vowel. It rhymes with park and mark; all three have the same [ɑrk]. Open the vowel until the jaw clearly drops.

examples.en: It gets dark early in winter.
examples.zh: 冬天天黑得很早。

examples.en: I'm not afraid of the dark.
examples.zh: 我不怕黑。

date.tip_zh: date 的 a 唸 [e]，是從 [e] 滑向 [ɪ] 的長音，跟 day 一樣，不要唸成短的 [ɛ]，否則會像 debt。字尾 [t] 舌尖頂住上齒齦停住，學生常省掉 t，結果只剩 day，或加母音唸成「得特」。可以先說 day，再把舌尖頂上去收一個不送氣的 [t]，就是 date。
date.tip_en: The a in date is [e], a long vowel gliding from [e] toward [ɪ], as in day — not the short [ɛ], or it sounds like debt. For the final [t], stop with the tongue tip on the ridge; learners often drop the t, leaving just day, or add a vowel and say 「得特」. Say day first, then raise the tongue tip to close on an unreleased [t] — that's date.

examples.en: What's the date today? It's May fifth.
examples.zh: 今天幾月幾號？五月五日。

examples.en: Write the date at the top of your paper.
examples.zh: 在你的紙上方寫上日期。

date.spelling_zh: 字尾 e 不發音，讓 a 唸長音 [e]。
date.spelling_en: The final e is silent and makes the a say the long [e].

daughter.tip_zh: daughter 的 augh 只唸一個母音 [ɔ]，gh 完全不發音；台灣學生常想把 gh 唸出來，或把 au 拆成兩個音。重音在第一音節 [ˈdɔ]，嘴巴張大、嘴唇微圓；第二音節 [tɚ] 要捲舌，不要唸成平平的「特」。daughter 跟 water 押韻，可以先唸 water，再把 w 換成 d。美式口語裡中間的 t 常變成輕快的彈舌音，像很快的 [d]。
daughter.tip_en: In daughter, augh is a single vowel [ɔ] and the gh is completely silent; Taiwanese learners often try to pronounce the gh or split au into two sounds. The stress is on the first syllable [ˈdɔ], with the mouth open and lips slightly rounded; the second syllable [tɚ] needs a curled tongue, not a flat 'te'. Daughter rhymes with water, so say water first and then swap w for d. In American speech the middle t often becomes a quick tap, like a fast [d].

examples.en: Mr. Lin's daughter is in my class.
examples.zh: 林先生的女兒跟我同班。

examples.en: She is the youngest daughter in her family.
examples.zh: 她是家裡最小的女兒。

daughter.spelling_en: The gh is silent; augh is just [ɔ].

day.tip_zh: day 的母音 [e] 在美式英語裡會從 [e] 滑向 [ɪ]，就像英文字母 A 的唸法。台灣學生常唸得太短太平，只剩 [dɛ]，聽起來像沒唸完。發音時嘴巴先半開，再往上收、嘴角往兩邊拉，把聲音稍微拉長，讓滑音完整出現。開頭的 [d] 舌尖輕點上牙齦就放開。day 跟 may、hey、birthday 押韻，可以連在一起練習。
day.tip_en: The vowel [e] in day glides from [e] toward [ɪ] in American English, just like the name of the letter A. Taiwanese learners often say it too short and flat, leaving only [dɛ], which sounds unfinished. Start with the mouth half open, then close it upward and pull the lip corners sideways, stretching the sound a little so the glide comes through. For the opening [d], tap the tongue tip on the upper gum ridge and release. Day rhymes with may, hey and birthday, so practice them together.

examples.en: We had a fun day at the beach.
examples.zh: 我們在海邊玩了開心的一天。

examples.en: I brush my teeth twice a day.
examples.zh: 我一天刷兩次牙。

deal.tip_zh: deal 的 [i] 要拉長、嘴角往兩邊拉，結尾是暗 L：舌尖碰上齒齦，舌根同時往後抬。學生常省掉 l 唸成「低」，或唸成「低歐」多出一拍。[i] 滑到暗 L 時會自然帶出一點過渡音，但整個字只有一個音節。
deal.tip_en: In deal, stretch the [i] with the lips spread; the ending is a dark L: tongue tip on the ridge while the back of the tongue lifts. Learners often drop the l and say 「低」, or say 「低歐」 with an extra beat. Moving from [i] into the dark L naturally creates a little transition sound, but the whole word is still one syllable.

examples.en: Let's make a deal: I wash, you dry.
examples.zh: 我們來約定：我洗碗，你擦乾。

examples.en: Teachers deal with many questions every day.
examples.zh: 老師每天要處理很多問題。

dear.tip_zh: dear 在 KK 寫成 [dɪr]，[ɪ] 後面舌頭往後捲做 [r]。學生常唸成「低兒」兩拍，或捲舌不夠，只剩 [dɪ]。整個字只有一拍：嘴角微拉先發 [ɪ]，舌頭一路滑向捲舌。它和 near、year 押韻，跟 door [dɔr] 只差母音。舌頭捲起後不要再放開發出母音。
dear.tip_en: dear is written [dɪr] in KK: after [ɪ], the tongue curls back for [r]. Learners often say 「低兒」 in two beats, or don't curl enough, leaving just [dɪ]. The whole word is one beat: lips slightly spread for [ɪ], then the tongue slides all the way into the curl. It rhymes with near and year, and differs from door [dɔr] only in the vowel. Once the tongue curls, don't release it into another vowel.

examples.en: My dear friend sent me a card.
examples.zh: 我親愛的朋友寄給我一張卡片。

examples.en: Dear Grandma, thank you for the gift.
examples.zh: 親愛的奶奶，謝謝您的禮物。

december.tip_zh: December 的重音在第二音節 [ˈsɛm]，第一音節 [dɪ] 要短而輕。台灣學生常把重音放在第一個音節，唸成飽滿的 [di]，或把 cem 唸成 [sim]。[sɛm] 嘴巴要張開些，母音跟 men 一樣；[m] 雙唇閉起後直接接 [b]，嘴唇不要先打開加母音；最後 [bɚ] 舌頭往後捲。December 和 September、November、remember 結尾相同，可以四個字一起練節奏。
december.tip_en: The stress in December is on the second syllable [ˈsɛm]; the first syllable [dɪ] is short and light. Taiwanese learners often stress the first syllable and say a full [di], or say cem as [sim]. Open the mouth a bit more for [sɛm], the same vowel as in men; after closing the lips for [m], go straight into [b] without opening them to add a vowel; then curl the tongue back for the final [bɚ]. December ends the same way as September, November and remember, so practice the rhythm of all four together.

examples.en: My birthday is in December.
examples.zh: 我的生日在十二月。

examples.en: We have a Christmas party every December.
examples.zh: 我們每年十二月都會辦聖誕派對。

decide.tip_zh: decide 重音在第二音節 [saɪd]，學生常把重音放在 de 上。第一音節 [dɪ] 輕而短。c 在 i 前面唸 [s]，不是 [k]。字尾 [d] 常被吞掉：[aɪ] 唸完，舌尖要頂上齒齦收住 [d]，但不要加母音。它跟 beside 押韻。唸的時候可以拍手兩下，第二下拍重一點。
decide.tip_en: decide is stressed on the second syllable [saɪd]; learners often put the stress on de. The first syllable [dɪ] is light and short. The c before i is [s], not [k]. The final [d] is often swallowed: after [aɪ], put the tongue tip on the ridge to close the [d], but don't add a vowel. It rhymes with beside. Clap twice as you say it, the second clap louder.

examples.en: I can't decide which ice cream to get.
examples.zh: 我決定不了要買哪種冰淇淋。

examples.en: Let's decide where to go this weekend.
examples.zh: 我們來決定這週末要去哪裡吧。

decide.spelling_zh: c 在 i 前面唸 [s]；字尾 e 不發音。
decide.spelling_en: The c before i is said [s]; the final e is silent.

deep.tip_zh: deep 的 ee 唸長的 [i]，嘴角往兩邊拉、維持久一點，學生常唸太短，變成 dip [dɪp]。字尾 [p] 雙唇閉住停一下就好，不要再張開多送出一個音節。可以把 deep 和 dip 對比練習：長的 [i] 是深的 deep，短的 [ɪ] 是沾一下的 dip。
deep.tip_en: The ee in deep is the long [i]: spread the lips and hold it a little longer; learners often make it too short, so it becomes dip [dɪp]. For the final [p], close the lips and hold briefly — don't open them again to add an extra syllable. Contrast deep and dip: the long [i] is deep, the short [ɪ] is dip.

examples.en: The lake is very deep.
examples.zh: 這個湖很深。

examples.en: Take a deep breath and relax.
examples.zh: 深呼吸，放輕鬆。

define.tip_zh: define 重音在第二音節 [faɪn]，第一音節 [dɪ] 要輕短，學生常唸成重重的「低」，並把重音放在前面。[f] 要上排牙齒輕碰下唇吹氣，不要用雙唇。字尾 [n] 舌尖頂住上齒齦，不要後縮成 [ŋ]；後半其實就跟 fine 一樣。
define.tip_en: define is stressed on the second syllable [faɪn]; the first syllable [dɪ] is light and short — learners often say a heavy 「低」 and put the stress up front. Make [f] with the upper teeth lightly on the lower lip and blow, not with both lips. For the final [n], keep the tongue tip on the ridge instead of pulling back to [ŋ]; the second half sounds just like fine.

examples.en: Can you define this word in English?
examples.zh: 你可以用英文解釋這個字的意思嗎？

examples.en: A dictionary helps us define new words.
examples.zh: 字典幫我們弄懂新單字的意思。

delicious.tip_zh: delicious 只有三個音節，重音在中間的 [ˈlɪ]。台灣學生常把 cious 拆開，唸成「西歐斯」多出一個音節，或把 ci 唸成 [s]。其實 ci 在這裡唸 [ʃ]，跟 she 的開頭一樣，嘴唇往前嘟，後面只接一個輕輕的 [əs]。[lɪ] 的母音是短的 [ɪ]，不要拉長成 [li]；第一音節 [dɪ] 也要輕。整個字唸成三拍：輕、重、輕。
delicious.tip_en: Delicious has only three syllables, with the stress on the middle one, [ˈlɪ]. Taiwanese learners often split cious apart into 'si-o-s', adding an extra syllable, or say ci as [s]. Here ci is [ʃ], like the start of she, with the lips pushed forward, followed only by a light [əs]. The vowel in [lɪ] is the short [ɪ], not a stretched [li]; the first syllable [dɪ] is light too. Say the word in three beats: light, strong, light.

examples.en: Grandma's dumplings are so delicious!
examples.zh: 奶奶包的水餃好好吃！

examples.en: This mango shaved ice is delicious.
examples.zh: 這碗芒果冰很好吃。

delicious.spelling_zh: ci 唸 [ʃ]，cious 只算一個音節 [ʃəs]。
delicious.spelling_en: ci sounds [ʃ]; cious is a single syllable [ʃəs].

dentist.tip_zh: dentist 重音在第一音節 [dɛn]，母音是 [ɛ]，不是嘴角拉開的 [æ]。第一個 [t] 跟在 [n] 後面，口語中常唸得很輕。最容易出錯的是字尾 [st]：學生常只唸到 [s]，或加母音變成「斯特」；[s] 吹完氣，舌尖直接頂住上齒齦收 [t]。
dentist.tip_en: dentist is stressed on the first syllable [dɛn]; the vowel is [ɛ], not the spread [æ]. The first [t] follows [n] and is often very light in speech. The trickiest part is the ending [st]: learners often stop at [s] or add a vowel and say 「斯特」. After blowing the [s], put the tongue tip straight on the ridge for [t].

examples.en: I go to the dentist twice a year.
examples.zh: 我一年看兩次牙醫。

examples.en: The dentist says my teeth are healthy.
examples.zh: 牙醫說我的牙齒很健康。

dentist.variant_zh: 口語中第一個 t 常省略，聽起來像 [ˈdɛnɪst]。
dentist.variant_en: In casual speech the first t is often dropped: [ˈdɛnɪst].

desk.tip_zh: desk 字尾 [sk] 兩個子音緊接，學生常只唸 [dɛs]，或加母音變成「得斯克」。[ɛ] 嘴巴半開，不要拉開成 [æ]。[s] 吹氣後，舌根馬上抬起頂住軟顎收 [k]，中間不換氣，也不要在 [k] 後面再補一個母音。
desk.tip_en: desk ends in two consonants back to back, [sk]. Learners often say only [dɛs], or add vowels and say 「得斯克」. The [ɛ] is half-open, not spread into [æ]. After blowing [s], lift the back of the tongue right away against the soft palate for [k], without a breath in between and without a vowel after [k].

examples.en: My desk is next to the window.
examples.zh: 我的書桌在窗戶旁邊。

examples.en: Please keep your desk clean.
examples.zh: 請保持你的書桌整潔。

dictionary.tip_zh: dictionary 有四個音節，重音在第一音節 [ˈdɪk]，第三音節 [nɛ] 帶次重音，中間的 [ʃə] 最輕最短。台灣學生常把重音移到後面，或把字尾 ary 唸成 [ɑrɪ]。美式唸法的字尾 [nɛrɪ]，母音和 very、strawberry 的結尾一樣，是嘴巴張開的 [ɛ]。另外 [dɪk] 的 [k] 要確實收住再接 [ʃ]，不要省掉，也不要在 [k] 後面多加母音。
dictionary.tip_en: Dictionary has four syllables: the main stress is on the first syllable [ˈdɪk], the third syllable [nɛ] has secondary stress, and the middle [ʃə] is the lightest and shortest. Taiwanese learners often move the stress toward the end, or say the ending ary as [ɑrɪ]. In the American pronunciation the ending [nɛrɪ] has the same open-mouth [ɛ] as the endings of very and strawberry. Also, finish the [k] in [dɪk] before going into [ʃ] — don't drop it, and don't add a vowel after it.

examples.en: Look up the new word in your dictionary.
examples.zh: 用你的字典查這個新單字。

examples.en: My teacher gave me an English dictionary.
examples.zh: 老師送我一本英文字典。

different.tip_zh: different 的重音在第一音節 [ˈdɪ]，後面都要輕。台灣學生常把重音放在中間，唸成 [dɪˈfɛrənt]，或把 [dɪ] 拉成長長的 [di]。中間的 fer 不是 [fɛr]，而是很輕的 [fə]，再捲舌接 [rənt]；美國人說快時常把它縮成兩個音節 [ˈdɪfrənt]。字尾 [ənt] 的 n 和 t 連在一起，舌尖頂住上牙齦收住，不要在後面多唸一個「特」。
different.tip_en: The stress in different is on the first syllable [ˈdɪ], and everything after it is light. Taiwanese learners often stress the middle, saying [dɪˈfɛrənt], or stretch [dɪ] into a long [di]. The middle fer is not [fɛr] but a light [fə], followed by a curled [rənt]; when Americans speak quickly they often shrink the word to two syllables, [ˈdɪfrənt]. In the ending [ənt], n and t go together: press the tongue tip on the upper gum ridge and stop there, without adding an extra 'te' after it.

examples.en: My sister and I like different colors.
examples.zh: 我和妹妹喜歡不同的顏色。

examples.en: This game is different from that one.
examples.zh: 這個遊戲跟那個不一樣。

different.variant_en: In speech often shortened to two syllables: [ˈdɪfrənt].
different.kk_flag: Notation only: Taiwan KK dictionaries write [ˈdɪfərənt]; the given [ɚə] (CMU ER0 AH0) sounds the same.

difficult.tip_zh: difficult 的重音在第一音節 [ˈdɪ]，第二音節 [fə] 又輕又短。台灣學生常把三個音節唸得一樣重，像「低飛卡特」，或把重音移到中間。最難的是字尾 [kḷt]：l 是暗 L，舌尖頂住上牙齦、舌根同時往後抬，接著舌尖不離開就直接收 [t]，t 後面不要多加母音。可以先慢慢唸 [kḷ]，確定舌尖有碰到上牙齦，再補上 [t]。
difficult.tip_en: The stress in difficult is on the first syllable [ˈdɪ]; the second syllable [fə] is light and short. Taiwanese learners often give all three syllables equal weight, like 'di-fei-ka-te', or move the stress to the middle. The hardest part is the ending [kḷt]: the l is a dark L — press the tongue tip on the upper gum ridge while lifting the back of the tongue — then, without moving the tongue tip away, finish with [t], adding no vowel after it. Say [kḷ] slowly first, making sure the tongue tip touches the gum ridge, then add the [t].

examples.en: This math problem is difficult for me.
examples.zh: 這題數學對我來說很難。

examples.en: Riding a bike is not difficult.
examples.zh: 騎腳踏車並不難。

dig.tip_zh: dig 的 i 是短的 [ɪ]，嘴巴放鬆，不要拉長成 [i]。字尾 [g] 是有聲的，舌根頂住軟顎、喉嚨帶一點震動就收住，學生常唸成清的 [k]，變成 [dɪk]，或加母音唸成「迪格」。它跟 big、pig 押韻，可以一起練。
dig.tip_en: The i in dig is the short [ɪ], relaxed, not stretched into [i]. The final [g] is voiced: back of the tongue against the soft palate with a little throat vibration, then stop. Learners often make it the voiceless [k], giving [dɪk], or add a vowel and say 「迪格」. It rhymes with big and pig — practice them together.

examples.en: The dog likes to dig in the garden.
examples.zh: 小狗喜歡在花園裡挖土。

examples.en: Let's dig a big hole in the sand.
examples.zh: 我們在沙子裡挖個大洞吧。

dinner.tip_zh: dinner 第一音節是短的 [ɪ]，雙寫的 nn 提醒你它是短音，不是 diner [ˈdaɪnɚ] 的 [aɪ]。重音在 [dɪ]。第二音節 [nɚ] 舌尖碰上齒齦後，舌頭往後捲成 [ɚ]，學生常唸成「低那」，不捲舌。唸的時候第一拍重、第二拍輕，可以拍手練習節奏。
dinner.tip_en: The first syllable of dinner has the short [ɪ] — the double nn is the clue that it's short, not the [aɪ] of diner [ˈdaɪnɚ]. The stress is on [dɪ]. In the second syllable [nɚ], the tongue tip touches the ridge and then curls back into [ɚ]; learners often say 「低那」 with no curl. Say it strong-weak; clapping the rhythm helps.

examples.en: What's for dinner tonight?
examples.zh: 今晚晚餐吃什麼？

examples.en: We eat dinner together at seven.
examples.zh: 我們七點一起吃晚餐。

dinner.spelling_zh: nn 只唸一個 [n]，它讓前面的 i 保持短音。
dinner.spelling_en: The nn is a single [n]; it keeps the i before it short.

dirty.tip_zh: dirty 的 ir 唸捲舌的 [ɝ]，舌頭往後捲、嘴唇微圓，學生常唸成「德」或「達」而沒有捲舌。中間的 [t] 夾在母音之間，美式口語中會變成舌尖輕彈的閃音，聽起來接近輕的 [d]。重音在前；它和 thirty 只差開頭的 [d] 和 [θ]。
dirty.tip_en: The ir in dirty is the r-colored [ɝ]: tongue curled back, lips slightly rounded; learners often say 「德」 or 「達」 with no curl. The middle [t] sits between vowels, so in casual American speech it becomes a quick tongue-tip flap, close to a light [d]. The stress is at the front; it differs from thirty only in the first sound, [d] versus [θ].

examples.en: My shoes are dirty after the game.
examples.zh: 比賽完我的鞋子髒了。

examples.en: Put your dirty clothes in the basket.
examples.zh: 把你的髒衣服放進籃子裡。

dish.tip_zh: dish 字尾是 [ʃ]，嘴唇要嘟起來、舌頭往後縮一點再吹氣，學生常唸成扁嘴的 [s]，變成 [dɪs]。母音是短的 [ɪ]，不要拉長成 [i]。練習時可以先說 fish、wish，再把開頭換成 [d]，結尾的嘴型就對了。
dish.tip_en: dish ends in [ʃ]: push the lips out, pull the tongue back a little, and blow. Learners often use flat lips and say [s], giving [dɪs]. The vowel is the short [ɪ], not a long [i]. Practice by saying fish and wish first, then switch the first sound to [d]; the ending mouth shape will be right.

examples.en: Please put this dish on the table.
examples.zh: 請把這道菜放到桌上。

examples.en: My favorite dish is beef noodles.
examples.zh: 我最喜歡的菜是牛肉麵。

do.tip_zh: do 單獨唸或強調時是長的 [u]，嘴唇圓而突出。學生常受中文「都」影響唸成 [o]，聽起來像 dough。另外，在 Do you…? 這類問句裡說得快時，美國人常把它弱化成 [də]。所以先練好完整的 [du]，再去聽懂弱讀的版本。
do.tip_en: On its own or when stressed, do has the long [u], with rounded, pushed-out lips. Influenced by Mandarin 「都」, learners often say [o], which sounds like dough. Also, in fast questions like Do you…?, Americans often weaken it to [də]. So first master the full [du], then learn to recognize the weak form.

examples.en: What do you want to do this weekend?
examples.zh: 你這週末想做什麼？

examples.en: I always do my homework after dinner.
examples.zh: 我總是在晚餐後寫功課。

doctor.tip_zh: doctor 的重音在第一音節 [ˈdɑk]，o 唸嘴巴張大的 [ɑ]，跟 hot、stop 的母音一樣。台灣學生常照拼字把 tor 唸成飽滿的 [tɔr]，結果兩個音節一樣重。其實第二音節很輕，只是捲舌的 [tɚ]，跟 teacher、water 的結尾相同。中間的 [kt] 也要注意：[k] 用舌根擋住後不要放出母音，直接接 [t]，不要唸成「達克特」三拍。
doctor.tip_en: The stress in doctor is on the first syllable [ˈdɑk]; the o is an open-mouth [ɑ], the same vowel as in hot and stop. Taiwanese learners often read tor by spelling as a full [tɔr], so both syllables come out equally strong. In fact the second syllable is light — just a curled [tɚ], the same ending as teacher and water. Watch the middle [kt] too: after blocking [k] with the back of the tongue, don't release a vowel; go straight into [t] instead of saying three beats like 'da-ke-te'.

examples.en: I went to see the doctor yesterday.
examples.zh: 我昨天去看醫生。

examples.en: My aunt is a doctor at a hospital.
examples.zh: 我阿姨是醫院的醫生。

dog.tip_zh: dog 的 [ɔ] 嘴巴張開、嘴唇稍微圓，不要唸成很圓、很緊的「多」[o]。字尾 [g] 是有聲的，舌根頂住軟顎收住，學生常唸成 [k] 變成 [dɔk]，或加母音變成「多個」。它跟 dig 只差母音，可以一起練。
dog.tip_en: The [ɔ] in dog has an open mouth with only slightly rounded lips — not the very round, tight 「多」 [o]. The final [g] is voiced: close with the back of the tongue on the soft palate. Learners often turn it into [k], giving [dɔk], or add a vowel and say 「多個」. It differs from dig only in the vowel; practice them together.

examples.en: My dog loves to run in the park.
examples.zh: 我的狗喜歡在公園跑。

examples.en: Can I pet your dog?
examples.zh: 我可以摸摸你的狗嗎？

doll.tip_zh: doll 的 o 是嘴巴張大的 [ɑ]，結尾是暗 L：舌尖頂上齒齦、舌根往後抬。學生常把 l 省掉唸成「達」，或用圓唇的 [o]。雙寫的 ll 只唸一個 [l]。別跟 deal [dil] 搞混：doll 下巴張大，deal 嘴角往兩邊拉。結尾舌尖留在上齒齦，讓聲音停一下再結束。
doll.tip_en: The o in doll is the open-mouthed [ɑ], and it ends in a dark L: tongue tip on the ridge, back of the tongue lifted. Learners often drop the l and say 「達」, or use a rounded [o]. The double ll is a single [l]. Don't confuse it with deal [dil]: doll has a dropped jaw, deal has spread lips. At the end, keep the tongue tip on the ridge and let the sound hold briefly before stopping.

examples.en: My sister has a doll with long hair.
examples.zh: 我妹妹有一個長頭髮的洋娃娃。

examples.en: She gave her doll a new dress.
examples.zh: 她幫她的洋娃娃換了一件新洋裝。

dollar.tip_zh: dollar 重音在第一音節 [dɑ]，嘴巴張大，不要唸成圓唇的「多」。第二音節 [lɚ] 舌尖先碰上齒齦做 [l]，再往後捲成 [ɚ]，學生常唸成「拉」而不捲舌。拼字是 -ar，但這裡唸輕的 [ɚ]，不是 car 那種清楚的 [ɑr]。
dollar.tip_en: dollar is stressed on the first syllable [dɑ] with the mouth wide open — not a rounded 「多」. In the second syllable [lɚ], the tongue tip touches the ridge for [l], then curls back into [ɚ]; learners often say 「拉」 with no curl. It's spelled -ar, but here it's the light [ɚ], not the full [ɑr] of car.

examples.en: This notebook costs one dollar.
examples.zh: 這本筆記本一元。

examples.en: I found a dollar under the sofa.
examples.zh: 我在沙發底下找到一塊錢。

dollar.spelling_zh: 字尾 -ar 唸輕的 [ɚ]，不是 [ɑr]；ll 只唸一個 [l]。
dollar.spelling_en: The final -ar is the light [ɚ], not [ɑr]; ll is a single [l].

door.tip_zh: door 只有一個音節，oo 在這裡唸 [ɔ]，接著舌頭往後捲做 [r]。學生常唸成「多兒」兩拍，或把 oo 唸成 food 的 [u]。它跟 four、more 押韻；跟 dear [dɪr] 只差母音，一個嘴巴張開，一個嘴角微拉。捲舌之後就停，不要再加母音。
door.tip_en: door has one syllable: the oo here is [ɔ], then the tongue curls back for [r]. Learners often say 「多兒」 in two beats, or read oo as the [u] of food. It rhymes with four and more, and differs from dear [dɪr] only in the vowel — one with an open mouth, the other with slightly spread lips. Stop once the tongue curls, with no extra vowel.

examples.en: Please close the door when you leave.
examples.zh: 你離開時請把門關上。

examples.en: Someone is knocking on the door.
examples.zh: 有人在敲門。

dot.tip_zh: dot 的 o 唸張大嘴的 [ɑ]，不是圓唇的「多」。字尾 [t] 舌尖頂住上齒齦就停，學生常加母音唸成「達特」，或把 t 丟掉只剩 [dɑ]。可以和 hot、not 一起練，三個字同韻；也別跟 date [det] 搞混。字尾 [t] 不送氣也沒關係，但舌尖一定要頂上去。
dot.tip_en: The o in dot is the open-mouthed [ɑ], not a rounded 「多」. For the final [t], just stop with the tongue tip on the ridge; learners often add a vowel and say 「達特」, or drop the t, leaving [dɑ]. Practice it with hot and not — all three rhyme — and don't confuse it with date [det]. The final [t] doesn't need a puff of air, but the tongue tip must go up.

examples.en: Draw a red dot in the middle of the circle.
examples.zh: 在圓圈中間畫一個紅點。

examples.en: There is a small dot on the map.
examples.zh: 地圖上有一個小點。

down.tip_zh: down 的 ow 唸 [aʊ]，嘴巴先張大再收圓，跟 town、brown 一樣。字尾是 [n]，舌尖要頂住上齒齦結束，學生常讓舌根往後收，唸成 [daʊŋ]。結尾時舌尖留在上齒齦、鼻子出聲；可以把 down 和 town 一起練，結尾一模一樣。
down.tip_en: The ow in down is [aʊ]: open wide, then round, as in town and brown. It ends in [n], finishing with the tongue tip on the ridge; learners often pull the back of the tongue back and say [daʊŋ]. At the end, keep the tongue tip on the ridge and let the sound come through the nose; practice down with town — the endings are identical.

examples.en: Please sit down and open your book.
examples.zh: 請坐下並打開你的書。

examples.en: The cat walked down the stairs.
examples.zh: 貓走下樓梯。

download.tip_zh: download 是 down 加 load 組成的，重音在 down，load 是次重音，不要兩邊一樣重或把重音放後面。[n] 和 [l] 舌尖都在上齒齦，從 [n] 直接滑到 [l]，中間不要停頓或加母音。load 的 [o] 要圓唇滑動，字尾 [d] 輕輕收住。
download.tip_en: download is made of down plus load. The stress is on down, with lighter stress on load — don't make both equally heavy or move the stress to the end. Both [n] and [l] are made with the tongue tip on the ridge, so slide straight from [n] into [l] with no pause or added vowel. The [o] of load is rounded and gliding, and the final [d] closes gently.

examples.en: Ask your parents before you download an app.
examples.zh: 下載應用程式之前要先問爸媽。

examples.en: It takes a minute to download this song.
examples.zh: 下載這首歌要一分鐘。

dozen.tip_zh: dozen 的 o 唸短的 [ʌ]，不是 [o]，學生常唸成「都森」。中間的 z 是有聲的 [z]，把手放在喉嚨上應該感覺到震動。第二音節弱化成 [ən]，字尾 [n] 舌尖頂上齒齦。它和 cousin 押韻，兩個字的母音和子音順序完全一樣。
dozen.tip_en: The o in dozen is the short [ʌ], not [o]; learners often say 「都森」. The middle z is the voiced [z] — with a hand on your throat you should feel a buzz. The second syllable weakens to [ən], and the final [n] has the tongue tip on the ridge. It rhymes with cousin; the two words have the same vowels and consonant pattern.

examples.en: Mom bought a dozen eggs at the market.
examples.zh: 媽媽在市場買了一打蛋。

examples.en: There are a dozen pencils in the box.
examples.zh: 盒子裡有十二枝鉛筆。

dozen.spelling_zh: o 唸 [ʌ]，跟 love、come 一樣。
dozen.spelling_en: The o is said [ʌ], as in love and come.

draw.tip_zh: draw 開頭 [dr] 在美式發音中聽起來接近 [dʒr]，嘴唇微嘟、舌頭往後捲，d 後面不要加母音。母音 [ɔ] 嘴巴張開、嘴唇稍圓。拼字有 w，但結尾不發 [w]，學生也常在最後多加捲舌，聽起來像 drawer；draw 的嘴型張開就停。
draw.tip_en: The opening [dr] of draw sounds close to [dʒr] in American English: lips slightly pushed out, tongue curled back, and no vowel after d. The vowel [ɔ] has an open mouth with slightly rounded lips. It's spelled with w, but there's no [w] at the end; learners also often add an r-curl at the end, which sounds like drawer. For draw, open the mouth and just stop.

examples.en: I like to draw animals in my notebook.
examples.zh: 我喜歡在筆記本裡畫動物。

examples.en: Can you draw a map to your house?
examples.zh: 你可以畫一張到你家的地圖嗎？

draw.spelling_zh: aw 合起來唸 [ɔ]，w 不另外發音。
draw.spelling_en: The aw together is said [ɔ]; the w is not pronounced separately.

drawer.tip_zh: drawer 在美式發音常只唸一個音節 [drɔr]，聽起來就是 draw 後面加上捲舌。學生常照拼字唸成三拍，或把 er 唸得太清楚。開頭 [dr] 黏在一起，嘴唇微嘟；[ɔ] 之後舌頭往後捲，整個字一口氣唸完。
drawer.tip_en: In American English, drawer is often just one syllable, [drɔr] — it sounds like draw with an r-curl added. Learners often follow the spelling and say three beats, or pronounce the er too clearly. Keep the opening [dr] together with lips slightly pushed out; after [ɔ], curl the tongue back, and say the whole word in one breath.

examples.en: My socks are in the top drawer.
examples.zh: 我的襪子在最上面的抽屜裡。

examples.en: Put the scissors back in the drawer.
examples.zh: 把剪刀放回抽屜裡。

drawer.variant_en: Some people say it in two syllables: [ˈdrɔɚ].

dream.tip_zh: dream 的 ea 唸長的 [i]，嘴角往兩邊拉，學生常唸太短，或在 [dr] 中間加母音唸成「德瑞姆」。字尾 [m] 雙唇要閉上停住，讓鼻音響一下；嘴巴沒閉就只剩 [dri]。別和 drum [drʌm] 搞混，兩個字只差母音。
dream.tip_en: The ea in dream is the long [i] with spread lips; learners often make it too short, or put a vowel inside [dr] and say 「德瑞姆」. For the final [m], close the lips and hold so the nasal hums; if the mouth stays open you get only [dri]. Don't confuse it with drum [drʌm] — they differ only in the vowel.

examples.en: I had a funny dream last night.
examples.zh: 我昨晚做了一個好笑的夢。

examples.en: My dream is to be a teacher.
examples.zh: 我的夢想是當老師。

dress.tip_zh: dress 最常見的問題是在 d 和 r 中間塞母音，唸成「德瑞斯」三拍。練法：嘴唇先嘟起、舌頭捲好，再讓 d 直接衝進 r，聽起來會有點像 [dʒr]。母音是短的 [ɛ]，嘴巴半開，不是會滑動的 [e]。字尾 ss 只唸一個 [s]，吹氣就結束。
dress.tip_en: The most common problem with dress is squeezing a vowel between d and r, saying 「德瑞斯」 in three beats. To practice: push the lips out and curl the tongue first, then let d rush straight into r — it will sound a bit like [dʒr]. The vowel is the short [ɛ], half-open, not the gliding [e]. The final ss is a single [s]: blow and stop.

examples.en: She wore a pink dress to the party.
examples.zh: 她穿了一件粉紅色洋裝去派對。

examples.en: This dress has big pockets.
examples.zh: 這件洋裝有大口袋。

drink.tip_zh: drink 字尾 [ŋk]：n 在這裡唸舌根鼻音 [ŋ]，舌根頂住軟顎、鼻子出聲，然後直接放開成 [k]。學生常唸成舌尖的 [n]，或漏掉最後的 [k]。母音是短的 [ɪ]，不要拉長成 [i]。開頭 [dr] 也不要加母音。可以先說 pink，再換開頭成 [dr] 練習。
drink.tip_en: drink ends in [ŋk]: here the n is the back-of-tongue nasal [ŋ] — back of the tongue against the soft palate, sound through the nose — then release straight into [k]. Learners often use a tongue-tip [n] or drop the final [k]. The vowel is the short [ɪ], not a long [i]. No vowel inside the opening [dr], either. Practice by saying pink first, then swapping the opening to [dr].

examples.en: Drink some water after you run.
examples.zh: 跑完步要喝點水。

examples.en: What would you like to drink?
examples.zh: 你想喝什麼？

drink.spelling_zh: nk 的 n 唸 [ŋ]，跟 pink、think 一樣。
drink.spelling_en: The n in nk is said [ŋ], as in pink and think.

drive.tip_zh: drive 字尾 [v] 是上排牙齒輕碰下唇、喉嚨震動，學生常唸成 [f]、用雙唇發成 [b]，甚至直接省掉。母音 [aɪ] 從張大嘴滑到 [ɪ]。字尾 e 不發音，所以結尾停在震動的 [v]，不要再加母音。它跟 arrive 押韻。
drive.tip_en: drive ends in [v]: upper teeth lightly on the lower lip, with the throat vibrating. Learners often say [f], use both lips for a [b], or drop it entirely. The vowel [aɪ] glides from an open mouth to [ɪ]. The final e is silent, so the word ends on the buzzing [v] with no vowel added. It rhymes with arrive.

examples.en: My dad will drive us to school today.
examples.zh: 爸爸今天會開車送我們上學。

examples.en: When I grow up, I want to drive a bus.
examples.zh: 我長大後想開公車。

driver.tip_zh: driver 開頭的 [dr] 是兩個子音連在一起，台灣學生常在中間多加母音，唸成「德賴佛」。發 [d] 時嘴唇就先微圓、舌頭準備往後捲，[d] 一放開就滑進 [r]，中間不停。重音在 [ˈdraɪ]，[aɪ] 要從 [a] 滑到 [ɪ]。第二音節 [vɚ] 的 [v] 要用上排門牙輕碰下唇、喉嚨振動，不是 [f] 或 [w]；最後捲舌收 [ɚ]。
driver.tip_en: The opening [dr] in driver is two consonants together, and Taiwanese learners often put a vowel between them, saying something like 'de-lai-fo'. While making [d], already round the lips slightly and get the tongue ready to curl back, so that as soon as [d] releases it slides into [r] without a pause. The stress is on [ˈdraɪ], where [aɪ] glides from [a] to [ɪ]. In the second syllable [vɚ], the [v] is made by touching the upper front teeth to the lower lip with voice — not [f] or [w]; finish by curling the tongue for [ɚ].

examples.en: The bus driver says good morning to us.
examples.zh: 公車司機跟我們說早安。

examples.en: My dad is a careful driver.
examples.zh: 我爸爸是個很小心的駕駛。

drop.tip_zh: drop 的 o 唸嘴巴張大的 [ɑ]，學生常唸成圓唇的 [o]。開頭 [dr] 一口氣唸完，嘴唇微嘟、舌頭捲起，不要在中間加母音。字尾 [p] 雙唇閉上停住即可，不要送氣多出一個音節。可以想成 top、shop 的結尾加上 [dr] 開頭。
drop.tip_en: The o in drop is the open-mouthed [ɑ]; learners often use a rounded [o]. Say the opening [dr] in one go — lips slightly pushed out, tongue curled — with no vowel in between. For the final [p], close the lips and stop, without a puff that adds a syllable. Think of the ending of top and shop with a [dr] at the front.

examples.en: Be careful not to drop the eggs.
examples.zh: 小心不要把蛋掉到地上。

examples.en: Please drop your trash in the bin.
examples.zh: 請把垃圾丟進垃圾桶。

drop.variant_en: Some speakers say [drɔp], with slightly rounded lips.

drum.tip_zh: drum 的 u 唸短而放鬆的 [ʌ]，嘴巴半開，學生常照拼字唸成圓唇的 [u]。結尾 [m] 雙唇閉上讓鼻音持續，別張著嘴結束。它跟 dream [drim] 只差母音：drum 嘴巴放鬆半開，dream 嘴角往兩邊拉。開頭 [dr] 不加母音。
drum.tip_en: The u in drum is the short, relaxed [ʌ], mouth half open; learners often follow the spelling and use a rounded [u]. For the final [m], close the lips and let the nasal hum — don't end with the mouth open. It differs from dream [drim] only in the vowel: drum is relaxed and half-open, dream has spread lips. No vowel inside the opening [dr].

examples.en: My brother plays the drum in a band.
examples.zh: 我哥哥在樂團裡打鼓。

examples.en: Hit the drum softly, please.
examples.zh: 請輕輕地敲鼓。

dry.tip_zh: dry 的 y 唸 [aɪ]，從張大嘴滑到 [ɪ]，跟 cry、try 同韻。學生有時會把它跟 draw [drɔ] 唸混，或在 [dr] 中間加母音。開頭 d 和 r 黏在一起，嘴唇微嘟、舌頭往後捲，接著下巴張大進入 [aɪ]，最後收小。整個字只有一個音節，不要拆成兩拍。
dry.tip_en: The y in dry is [aɪ], gliding from an open mouth to [ɪ]; it rhymes with cry and try. Learners sometimes blur it with draw [drɔ], or put a vowel inside [dr]. Keep d and r stuck together — lips slightly pushed out, tongue curled back — then drop the jaw into [aɪ] and close it smaller at the end. The whole word is one syllable; don't split it into two beats.

examples.en: My shirt is dry now, so I can wear it.
examples.zh: 我的襯衫乾了，所以可以穿了。

examples.en: The weather is dry and sunny today.
examples.zh: 今天的天氣乾燥又晴朗。

duck.tip_zh: duck 的 u 唸短的 [ʌ]，嘴巴半開放鬆，學生常張得太開，唸成「達克」，聽起來像 dock [dɑk]。字尾 ck 只唸一個 [k]，舌根頂住軟顎收住就好，不要再加母音。可以把 duck 和 dock 對比練習，感覺下巴張開的大小。
duck.tip_en: The u in duck is the short [ʌ], mouth half open and relaxed; learners often open too wide and say 「達克」, which sounds like dock [dɑk]. The ck is a single [k]: close with the back of the tongue on the soft palate, with no added vowel. Contrast duck and dock to feel how far the jaw opens.

examples.en: The duck is swimming in the pond.
examples.zh: 鴨子在池塘裡游泳。

examples.en: A little duck followed its mother.
examples.zh: 一隻小鴨子跟著牠的媽媽。

during.tip_zh: during 重音在第一音節 [dʊ]，嘴唇微圓、短而放鬆，接著舌頭往後捲進 [r]。學生常加一個 [j] 唸成 [ˈdjʊrɪŋ]，但美式通常不帶 [j]；或 r 沒捲，聽起來像「肚林」。第二音節結尾是舌根鼻音 [ŋ]，不要唸成舌尖的 [n]。
during.tip_en: during is stressed on the first syllable [dʊ]: lips slightly rounded, short and relaxed, then the tongue curls back into [r]. Learners often add a [j] and say [ˈdjʊrɪŋ], but American English usually has no [j]; or they skip the curl, so it sounds like 「肚林」. The second syllable ends in the back-of-tongue nasal [ŋ], not a tongue-tip [n].

examples.en: Don't talk during the test.
examples.zh: 考試時不要講話。

examples.en: We went camping during summer vacation.
examples.zh: 我們暑假期間去露營了。

during.variant_zh: 也常聽到 [ˈdɝɪŋ]，第一音節整個捲舌。
during.variant_en: You'll also hear [ˈdɝɪŋ], with the whole first syllable r-colored.

each.tip_zh: each 的 ea 唸長的 [i]，嘴角往兩邊拉；字尾 [tʃ] 嘴唇嘟起、舌面貼上顎再爆開。學生常把結尾唸得太弱或變成 [t]，聽起來像 eat，或只剩摩擦的 [ʃ]。從 [i] 到 [tʃ] 要先讓舌頭擋住停一下再放開，才聽得出 ch。
each.tip_en: The ea in each is the long [i] with spread lips; the ending [tʃ] pushes the lips out, presses the tongue to the roof of the mouth and bursts. Learners often make the ending too weak or turn it into [t], so it sounds like eat, or leave only a hissing [ʃ]. Between [i] and [tʃ], block with the tongue for a moment before releasing — that's what makes the ch audible.

examples.en: Each student has a name card.
examples.zh: 每個學生都有一張名牌。

examples.en: Each of us gets one cookie.
examples.zh: 我們每個人拿一塊餅乾。

ear.tip_zh: ear 只有一個音節 [ɪr]，直接從母音 [ɪ] 開始，再把舌頭往後捲成 [r]。台灣學生常在前面多加一個 [j] 的滑音，結果唸成 year [jɪr]，意思變成「年」；也有人拆成兩拍，唸成「一兒」。練法：從放鬆的短 [ɪ] 直接起音，前面不要有滑音，再平順地捲舌。ear 和 hear、here 押韻，可以先唸 hear，再把 [h] 拿掉。
ear.tip_en: Ear is one syllable, [ɪr]: it starts straight on the vowel [ɪ], then the tongue curls back into [r]. Taiwanese learners often add a [j] glide in front, which turns it into year [jɪr], meaning 'year'; others split it into two beats, like 'yi-er'. Practice: start directly on a relaxed, short [ɪ] with no glide before it, then curl the tongue smoothly. Ear rhymes with hear and here, so say hear first and then drop the [h].

examples.en: The doctor looked inside my ear.
examples.zh: 醫生看了看我的耳朵裡面。

examples.en: My cat's ear is soft and pink.
examples.zh: 我家貓咪的耳朵軟軟的、粉粉的。

early.tip_zh: early 一開口就是捲舌的 [ɝ]，舌頭往後捲、嘴唇微圓，學生常照拼字唸成「耳」或「餓」開頭，沒有捲舌。接著舌尖抬到上齒齦做 [l]，最後是輕短的 [ɪ]。重音在 [ɝ]。從 [ɝ] 到 [l] 舌頭要從捲起變成往前頂，先慢慢練。
early.tip_en: early starts right away with the r-colored [ɝ]: tongue curled back, lips slightly rounded; learners often follow the spelling and begin with 「耳」 or 「餓」, with no curl. Then raise the tongue tip to the ridge for [l], and end with a light, short [ɪ]. The stress is on [ɝ]. Going from [ɝ] to [l], the tongue moves from curled back to pressing forward — practice it slowly first.

examples.en: I get up early on school days.
examples.zh: 上學日我很早起床。

examples.en: We came early to get good seats.
examples.zh: 我們早點來，才能坐到好位子。

early.spelling_zh: ear 在這裡唸 [ɝ]，不是 ear 這個字的 [ɪr]。
early.spelling_en: Here ear is said [ɝ], not like the word ear [ɪr].

earth.tip_zh: earth 雖然拼字裡有 ear，但不唸 ear 的 [ɪr]，而是捲舌的 [ɝ]，跟 bird、girl 的母音一樣。台灣學生常把結尾的 [θ] 唸成 [s] 或 [f]，聽起來像「餓斯」。正確做法：先把舌頭往後捲發 [ɝ]，再把舌尖往前伸到上下門牙之間，輕輕吹氣發 [θ]，喉嚨不振動。兩個動作方向相反，可以分三步慢慢練：[ɝ]、舌尖前伸、吹出 [θ]。
earth.tip_en: Although earth is spelled with ear, it isn't the [ɪr] of ear but the curled [ɝ], the same vowel as in bird and girl. Taiwanese learners often turn the final [θ] into [s] or [f], so it sounds like 'er-s'. Do it this way: first curl the tongue back for [ɝ], then push the tongue tip forward between the upper and lower front teeth and blow gently for [θ], with no voice. The two moves go in opposite directions, so practice slowly in three steps: [ɝ], tongue tip forward, blow out [θ].

examples.en: We all live on the planet Earth.
examples.zh: 我們都住在地球這顆行星上。

examples.en: Let's keep the earth clean and green.
examples.zh: 讓我們一起讓地球保持乾淨、綠意滿滿。

earth.spelling_zh: 拼字有 ear，但唸 [ɝ]，不是 ear 的 [ɪr]。
earth.spelling_en: Spelled with ear, but said [ɝ], not the [ɪr] of ear.

earthquake.tip_zh: earthquake 由 earth 和 quake 組成，重音在前面的 [ˈɝθ]，quake 帶次重音。難在 [θ] 後面馬上接 [kw]：台灣學生常為了趕快接到 quake，就把 [θ] 省掉或唸成 [s]，變成 [ˈɝsˌkwek]。練法：舌尖伸到門牙之間吹完 [θ]，再把舌頭往後縮發 [k]，同時嘴唇嘟圓準備 [w]。quake 的 qu 唸 [kw]，母音是 [e]，跟 cake、make 押韻。
earthquake.tip_en: Earthquake is made of earth and quake; the main stress is on the front part [ˈɝθ], and quake has secondary stress. The hard part is that [kw] comes right after [θ]: Taiwanese learners, rushing to reach quake, often drop the [θ] or turn it into [s], giving [ˈɝsˌkwek]. Practice: put the tongue tip between the front teeth and finish blowing [θ], then pull the tongue back for [k] while rounding the lips for [w]. The qu in quake is [kw], and its vowel is [e], so it rhymes with cake and make.

examples.en: We learned what to do in an earthquake.
examples.zh: 我們學了地震時該怎麼做。

examples.en: Our school has an earthquake drill today.
examples.zh: 我們學校今天有地震演練。

east.tip_zh: east 的 ea 唸長的 [i]，要拉長、嘴角往兩邊拉。字尾 [st] 兩個子音：學生常只唸到 [s] 就停，或加母音唸成「依斯特」三拍。[s] 吹氣之後，舌尖直接頂住上齒齦收 [t]，中間不換氣，整個字只有一拍。
east.tip_en: The ea in east is the long [i]: stretch it with spread lips. The ending [st] has two consonants; learners often stop at [s], or add vowels and say 「依斯特」 in three beats. After blowing [s], put the tongue tip straight on the ridge for [t], without a breath in between — the whole word is one beat.

examples.en: The sun comes up in the east.
examples.zh: 太陽從東方升起。

examples.en: My school is on the east side of town.
examples.zh: 我的學校在城鎮的東邊。

easter.tip_zh: Easter 重音在第一音節，[i] 拉長、嘴角往兩邊拉。中間 [st] 要連在一起，學生常在 s 後面加母音，唸成「依斯特兒」四拍。第二音節 [tɚ] 舌尖碰上齒齦後舌頭往後捲，不要唸成「特」。整個字只有兩個音節。
easter.tip_en: Easter is stressed on the first syllable; stretch the [i] with spread lips. The middle [st] stays together — learners often add a vowel after s and say 「依斯特兒」 in four beats. In the second syllable [tɚ], the tongue tip touches the ridge and then curls back; don't say 「特」. The whole word has only two syllables.

examples.en: We paint colorful eggs at Easter every year.
examples.zh: 我們每年復活節都會彩繪蛋。

examples.en: The Easter bunny hid candy in the garden.
examples.zh: 復活節兔子把糖果藏在花園裡。

easy.tip_zh: easy 中間的 s 唸有聲的 [z]，喉嚨要震動，學生常唸成清的 [s]，變成「依西」。重音在第一音節 [i]，要拉長；第二音節 [zɪ] 輕而短。可以先發出持續的 [zzz]，感覺舌尖附近在震，再接到 [ɪ]。字尾 y 唸輕短的 [ɪ]。
easy.tip_en: The middle s in easy is the voiced [z] — the throat vibrates; learners often say a voiceless [s], giving 「依西」. The stress is on the first syllable [i], which is long; the second syllable [zɪ] is light and short. Try making a steady [zzz] first, feeling the buzz near the tongue tip, then move into [ɪ]. The final y is a light, short [ɪ].

examples.en: This math question is easy for me.
examples.zh: 這題數學對我來說很簡單。

examples.en: Riding a bike is easy after some practice.
examples.zh: 練習一下之後，騎腳踏車就很簡單。

easy.spelling_en: The s here is said [z], not [s].

eat.tip_zh: eat 的 ea 是長的 [i]，嘴角往兩邊拉、維持久一點，學生常唸太短，變成 it [ɪt]，兩個字意思完全不同。字尾 [t] 舌尖頂住上齒齦停住，不要送出「特」。練習時把 eat 和 it 輪流說，感覺長短和嘴型的差別。
eat.tip_en: The ea in eat is the long [i]: spread the lips and hold it a little longer. Learners often make it too short, so it becomes it [ɪt], a completely different word. For the final [t], stop with the tongue tip on the ridge, without puffing out 「特」. Practice saying eat and it in turn to feel the difference in length and mouth shape.

examples.en: Let's eat lunch under the tree.
examples.zh: 我們在樹下吃午餐吧。

examples.en: Do you eat breakfast every day?
examples.zh: 你每天都吃早餐嗎？

egg.tip_zh: egg 的母音是短的 [ɛ]，嘴巴半開，學生常唸成會滑動的 [e]，像字母 A 的音，或在後面加母音變成兩拍。字尾 [g] 是有聲的，舌根頂住軟顎、喉嚨震動，不要唸成 [k]。雙寫的 gg 只唸一個 [g]。
egg.tip_en: The vowel in egg is the short [ɛ], mouth half open; learners often use the gliding [e], like the letter A, or add a vowel after it, making two beats. The final [g] is voiced: back of the tongue on the soft palate with the throat vibrating — not [k]. The double gg is a single [g].

examples.en: I eat an egg for breakfast.
examples.zh: 我早餐吃一顆蛋。

examples.en: The bird laid an egg in its nest.
examples.zh: 小鳥在巢裡下了一顆蛋。

eight.tip_zh: eight 的 eigh 只唸一個音 [e]。美式英語的 [e] 要從 [e] 滑到 [ɪ]，像英文字母 A；台灣學生常唸成短短的 [ɛ]，又在字尾 t 後面加母音，變成「欸特」兩拍。正確是一拍：嘴角往兩邊拉、把 [e] 滑完，舌尖頂住上牙齦停住發 [t]，氣可以不放出來。eight 和 date、great 押韻，可以一起練，也要和 it [ɪt]、at [æt] 分清楚。
eight.tip_en: In eight, eigh is a single sound, [e]. The American [e] glides from [e] to [ɪ], like the letter A; Taiwanese learners often say a short [ɛ] and add a vowel after the final t, making two beats like 'ei-te'. It should be one beat: pull the lip corners sideways, complete the [e] glide, and stop with the tongue tip on the upper gum ridge for [t] — the air doesn't have to be released. Eight rhymes with date and great, so practice them together, and keep it distinct from it [ɪt] and at [æt].

examples.en: I get up at eight every morning.
examples.zh: 我每天早上八點起床。

examples.en: There are eight students in our group.
examples.zh: 我們這組有八個學生。

eight.spelling_en: The gh is silent; eigh sounds [e].

eighteen.tip_zh: 單獨說 eighteen 時，重音在第二音節 [ˈtin]，母音是拉長的 [i]，最後一定要收 [n]。台灣學生常把重音放在前面、[n] 又收得不清楚，結果聽起來像 eighty [ˈetɪ]（八十）。分辨方法：eighteen 把 teen 唸長、唸重，舌尖頂住上牙齦把 [n] 收完整；eighty 則是重音在前、ty 很短。第一音節 [e] 也要滑完整，不要唸成短短的 [ɛ]。
eighteen.tip_en: Said on its own, eighteen has the stress on the second syllable [ˈtin], with a long [i] and a final [n] that must be pronounced. Taiwanese learners often put the stress at the front and leave the [n] unclear, so it sounds like eighty [ˈetɪ] (80). To tell them apart: in eighteen, make teen long and strong and finish the [n] fully with the tongue tip on the upper gum ridge; eighty has the stress at the front and a very short ty. The first syllable [e] also needs its full glide — not a short [ɛ].

examples.en: My cousin is eighteen years old.
examples.zh: 我表哥十八歲。

examples.en: There are eighteen books on the shelf.
examples.zh: 書架上有十八本書。

eighteen.variant_zh: 數數或後面接名詞時，重音常移到前面 [ˈeˌtin]。
eighteen.variant_en: When counting or before a noun, stress often moves forward: [ˈeˌtin].
eighteen.spelling_zh: gh 不發音，eigh 唸 [e]；t 只唸一次。
eighteen.spelling_en: The gh is silent and eigh sounds [e]; the t is said only once.

eighty.tip_zh: 開頭的 eigh 只唸一個 [e]，gh 完全不發音；嘴巴要從 [e] 滑向 [ɪ]，不要縮成短促的 [ɛ]。重音在第一音節，第二音節 [tɪ] 又短又輕，結尾是短的 [ɪ]，不要拉長成 [tin]，否則聽起來像 eighteen。美國人說快時，中間的 [t] 常輕輕彈一下，接近很快的 d。
eighty.tip_en: The opening eigh is just one sound, [e]; the gh is completely silent. Glide from [e] toward [ɪ] instead of cutting it short to [ɛ]. Stress the first syllable; the second syllable [tɪ] is short and light and ends in a short [ɪ]. Don't stretch it into [tin], or it sounds like eighteen. In fast American speech the middle [t] is often a quick tap, close to a fast d.

examples.en: My grandpa will turn eighty next month.
examples.zh: 我爺爺下個月就滿八十歲了。

examples.en: There are eighty students in the school band.
examples.zh: 學校樂隊裡有八十個學生。

eighty.spelling_en: eigh says just [e]; the gh is silent.

either.tip_zh: either 的 th 唸有聲的 [ð]：舌尖輕放在上下門牙之間，喉嚨振動，讓聲音從舌頭和牙齒的縫隙出來。台灣學生常把它唸成 [d] 或 [z]，聽起來像「衣得」。第一音節 [ˈi] 是重音，母音要拉長；第二音節 [ðɚ] 要捲舌，不是平平的 [ə]。美國人也常唸 [ˈaɪðɚ]，兩種都對，但中間 [ð] 的做法一樣，舌尖都要碰到牙齒。
either.tip_en: The th in either is the voiced [ð]: rest the tongue tip lightly between the upper and lower front teeth and voice it, letting the sound come out through the gap between tongue and teeth. Taiwanese learners often say [d] or [z] instead, so it sounds like 'yi-de'. The first syllable [ˈi] is stressed, with a long vowel; the second syllable [ðɚ] needs a curled tongue, not a flat [ə]. Americans also often say [ˈaɪðɚ]; both are correct, but the middle [ð] is made the same way, with the tongue tip touching the teeth.

examples.en: I don't like carrots either.
examples.zh: 我也不喜歡紅蘿蔔。

examples.en: My brother can't swim, and I can't either.
examples.zh: 我哥哥不會游泳，我也不會。

elephant.tip_zh: elephant 的重音在第一音節 [ˈɛ]，嘴巴張開，母音和 egg 的開頭一樣。台灣學生常把第二音節唸成清楚的 [li] 或 [lɛ]，甚至把重音移到 le 上。其實 [lə] 和 [fənt] 都只用輕輕的 [ə]，整個字是「重、輕、輕」三拍。ph 唸 [f]，上排門牙輕碰下唇吹氣；最後的 [nt] 舌尖頂住上牙齦，n 和 t 一起收住，不要在 t 後面多加母音。
elephant.tip_en: The stress in elephant is on the first syllable [ˈɛ], with the mouth open — the same vowel as the start of egg. Taiwanese learners often say the second syllable as a clear [li] or [lɛ], or even move the stress onto le. In fact [lə] and [fənt] both use only a light [ə], so the word goes strong-light-light. The ph is [f]: touch the upper front teeth to the lower lip and blow; for the final [nt], press the tongue tip on the upper gum ridge and stop n and t together, without adding a vowel after the t.

examples.en: The baby elephant is playing in the water.
examples.zh: 小象正在水裡玩。

examples.en: An elephant has a long nose and big ears.
examples.zh: 大象有長長的鼻子和大大的耳朵。

eleven.tip_zh: eleven 的重音在第二音節 [ˈlɛ]，第一音節 [ɪ] 又短又輕。台灣學生常把開頭唸成長長的 [i] 並加重，或把 [v] 唸成 [w]、[b]，變成「衣累溫」。[v] 要讓上排門牙輕碰下唇、喉嚨振動；最後的 [vən] 收在 [n]，舌尖頂住上牙齦，不要變成 [ŋ]。eleven 和 seven 的結尾一樣，可以先唸 seven，再把開頭換成 [ɪˈl]。
eleven.tip_en: The stress in eleven is on the second syllable [ˈlɛ]; the first syllable [ɪ] is short and light. Taiwanese learners often make the start a long, stressed [i], or turn [v] into [w] or [b], so it sounds like 'yi-lei-wen'. For [v], touch the upper front teeth to the lower lip and voice it; the final [vən] ends in [n] with the tongue tip on the upper gum ridge — don't let it become [ŋ]. Eleven ends the same way as seven, so say seven first, then change the start to [ɪˈl].

examples.en: There are eleven players on a soccer team.
examples.zh: 一支足球隊有十一名球員。

examples.en: My brother is eleven years old.
examples.zh: 我哥哥十一歲。

else.tip_zh: 這個字只有一個音節 [ɛls]，字尾是 [l] 加 [s] 兩個子音連在一起。常見的錯誤是把 [l] 省掉，聽起來像 [ɛs]，或在最後多加一個母音，唸成兩三拍的「哀爾瑟」。發完 [ɛ] 後舌尖先抬到上排牙齦停住，再直接放氣發 [s]；字尾的 e 不發音。
else.tip_en: This word is one syllable, [ɛls], ending in two consonants together, [l] plus [s]. A common mistake is dropping the [l] so it sounds like [ɛs], or adding a vowel at the end so it becomes two or three beats. After [ɛ], raise the tongue tip to the upper gum ridge and hold it, then let the air out straight into [s]. The final e is silent.

examples.en: Do you want anything else to eat?
examples.zh: 你還想吃別的東西嗎？

examples.en: Everyone else is already in the classroom.
examples.zh: 其他人都已經在教室裡了。

end.tip_zh: end 的 [ɛ] 嘴巴半開就好，不要張得像 and 的 [æ] 那麼大，否則 end 和 and 會聽起來一樣。字尾 [nd] 兩個子音都要有：舌尖頂住上排牙齦發 [n]，舌頭不動，直接輕輕放開變成 [d]。不要把 [d] 吞掉只剩鼻音，也不要多加母音唸成「恩德」。
end.tip_en: The [ɛ] in end is only half open; don't open as wide as the [æ] in and, or end and and will sound the same. Both consonants of the final [nd] must be there: press the tongue tip on the upper gum ridge for [n], keep it still, and gently release it into [d]. Don't swallow the [d] and leave only the nasal, and don't add a vowel to make it "en-de".

examples.en: The movie will end at eight o'clock.
examples.zh: 電影八點會結束。

examples.en: We read the story to the end.
examples.zh: 我們把故事讀到最後。

engineer.tip_zh: engineer 的主重音在最後一個音節 [nɪr]，不是開頭的 [ɛn]；學生常照中文習慣把第一拍唸最重，聽起來像「EN-ji-near」。第一音節 [ɛn] 只是次重音，中間的 [dʒə] 要輕又短。結尾 [nɪr] 的 [ɪ] 短而放鬆，接著舌尖往後捲成 r、不碰上顎，和 year、near 押韻。
engineer.tip_en: The main stress of engineer is on the last syllable [nɪr], not on the first syllable [ɛn]; students often follow their Chinese habit and say the first beat loudest, so it sounds like 'EN-ji-near'. The first syllable [ɛn] only has secondary stress, and the middle [dʒə] should be light and short. In the final [nɪr], the [ɪ] is short and relaxed, then the tongue tip curls back for r without touching the roof of the mouth; it rhymes with year and near.

examples.en: My aunt is an engineer who builds bridges.
examples.zh: 我阿姨是一位建造橋樑的工程師。

examples.en: Do you want to be an engineer someday?
examples.zh: 你以後想當工程師嗎？

engineer.kk_flag: General American puts the primary stress on the LAST syllable: [ˌɛndʒəˈnɪr]. The given KK marks two primary stresses, and stressed_syllable=1 points at the wrong syllable (should be 3).

english.tip_zh: English 只有兩個音節 [ɪŋ] 和 [glɪʃ]。常見錯誤是在 [g] 和 [l] 中間多塞一個母音，唸成三拍的「英格利序」；[g] 只是舌根輕碰一下，馬上接舌尖的 [l]。字尾 [ʃ] 嘴唇往前嘟、只送氣不出聲，後面不要再多加母音。第一個 [ɪ] 短而放鬆，不要拉成長長的 [i]。
english.tip_en: English has only two syllables, [ɪŋ] and [glɪʃ]. A common mistake is squeezing a vowel between [g] and [l], making three beats like 'ying-ge-li-shu'; [g] is only a quick touch of the back of the tongue, followed right away by [l] with the tongue tip. For the final [ʃ], push the lips forward and let out air only, no voice, and don't add a vowel after it. The first [ɪ] is short and relaxed; don't stretch it into a long [i].

examples.en: We have English class every Monday morning.
examples.zh: 我們每個星期一早上有英文課。

examples.en: My little brother can sing songs in English.
examples.zh: 我弟弟會用英文唱歌。

english.variant_zh: 也常聽到不發 [g] 的唸法 [ˈɪŋlɪʃ]。

enjoy.tip_zh: 重音在第二音節 [dʒɔɪ]，常有人把第一音節 [ɛn] 唸得比較重，節奏就反了。[dʒ] 嘴唇要往前嘟，比注音ㄐ更圓、更有力；[ɔɪ] 是從嘴唇微圓、張開的 [ɔ] 滑到 [ɪ]，和 boy、toy 的母音一樣。第一音節輕輕帶過就好。
enjoy.tip_en: The stress is on the second syllable [dʒɔɪ]; learners often say the first syllable [ɛn] more strongly, which flips the rhythm. For [dʒ], push the lips forward, rounder and stronger than Mandarin ㄐ. [ɔɪ] slides from an open, slightly rounded [ɔ] to [ɪ], the same vowel as in boy and toy. Just pass lightly over the first syllable.

examples.en: I really enjoy reading comics after dinner.
examples.zh: 我很喜歡在晚餐後看漫畫。

examples.en: Did you enjoy the school trip?
examples.zh: 你喜歡這次校外教學嗎？

enjoy.variant_zh: 第一音節也常唸成較輕的 [ɪn]：[ɪnˈdʒɔɪ]。
enjoy.variant_en: The first syllable is also often a lighter [ɪn]: [ɪnˈdʒɔɪ].

enough.tip_zh: 拼字很容易誤導：ough 在這裡唸 [ʌf]，gh 要發成 [f]，上排牙齒輕碰下唇吹氣，不能省略，也不要唸成 [g]。重音在第二音節 [nʌf]，第一音節只是很輕的 [ɪ]，不要唸成重重的長音 [i]。[ʌ] 嘴巴放鬆微開，像 up 的開頭。
enough.tip_en: The spelling is misleading: ough here is [ʌf], and the gh must be [f], with the upper teeth lightly touching the lower lip as you blow; don't drop it or say [g]. The stress is on the second syllable [nʌf]; the first syllable is only a very light [ɪ], not a heavy long [i]. For [ʌ], relax the mouth slightly open, like the start of up.

examples.en: We have enough chairs for everyone.
examples.zh: 我們的椅子夠每個人坐。

examples.en: Is the water warm enough for swimming?
examples.zh: 水夠溫暖可以游泳嗎？

enough.spelling_zh: ough 唸 [ʌf]，gh 發 [f] 的音。
enough.spelling_en: ough says [ʌf]; the gh sounds like [f].

enter.tip_zh: 重音在第一音節 [ɛn]，第二音節 [tɚ] 輕而短。字尾 -er 是捲舌的 [ɚ]：舌尖往後捲、不碰任何地方，不要唸成平平的「特」或沒有捲舌的 [tə]。[ɛ] 嘴巴半開即可，不要張大成 [æ]，也不要唸成會滑動的 [e]。
enter.tip_en: Stress the first syllable [ɛn]; the second syllable [tɚ] is light and short. The final -er is an r-colored [ɚ]: curl the tongue tip back without touching anything; don't say a flat "te" or an uncurled [tə]. Open the mouth only halfway for [ɛ]; don't widen it to [æ] or turn it into the gliding [e].

examples.en: Please knock before you enter the room.
examples.zh: 進房間前請先敲門。

examples.en: Enter your name on the first line.
examples.zh: 在第一行填上你的名字。

enter.variant_zh: 美國人說快時常把 [t] 省掉，聽起來像 [ˈɛnɚ]。
enter.variant_en: In fast American speech the [t] is often dropped, sounding like [ˈɛnɚ].

envelope.tip_zh: envelope 重音在第一音節 [ˈɛn]，不要把結尾的 lope 唸得最重。[n] 之後馬上接 [v]：舌尖先頂住上牙齦發 [n]，再把下唇輕碰上排牙齒，發出有聲的 [v]，不要換成 [w] 或 [b]。中間的 e 只是輕輕的 [ə]，不是 [ɛ]。字尾 [p] 雙唇閉上就停，後面不要多加母音。
envelope.tip_en: Envelope is stressed on the first syllable [ˈɛn]; don't make the final lope the loudest part. [v] comes right after [n]: first press the tongue tip on the upper gum ridge for [n], then touch the lower lip lightly to the upper teeth for a voiced [v], not [w] or [b]. The middle e is only a light [ə], not [ɛ]. For the final [p], close the lips and stop; don't add a vowel after it.

examples.en: Please put the letter in the envelope.
examples.zh: 請把信放進信封裡。

examples.en: I wrote Grandma's address on the envelope.
examples.zh: 我在信封上寫了奶奶的地址。

eraser.tip_zh: eraser 重音在第二音節 [ˈre]，不在開頭；開頭的 e 唸短而輕的 [ɪ]，不要唸成長長的 [i]。[re] 的 [e] 嘴角往兩邊拉，尾巴帶一點滑向 [ɪ] 的音，就像 erase 的後半。字尾 [sɚ] 先發清楚的 [s]，再把舌尖往後捲成 [ɚ]，不要只發一個沒有捲舌的輕聲就結束。
eraser.tip_en: Eraser is stressed on the second syllable [ˈre], not at the start; the opening e is a short, light [ɪ], not a long [i]. For the [e] in [re], spread the corners of the mouth and let it glide slightly toward [ɪ] at the end, just like the second half of erase. For the final [sɚ], say a clear [s] first, then curl the tongue tip back into [ɚ]; don't end with a light sound that has no r-curl.

examples.en: Can I borrow your eraser, please?
examples.zh: 我可以借你的橡皮擦嗎？

examples.en: My new eraser smells like strawberries.
examples.zh: 我的新橡皮擦聞起來像草莓。

error.tip_zh: 這個字有兩次捲舌：[ɛ] 後面舌頭馬上往後捲進入 [r]，結尾的 -or 也是捲舌的 [ɚ]，不是 [ɔr]。常見的錯誤是第一個 [r] 沒捲，結尾又唸成圓唇的 [o]。重音在第一音節 [ɛ]，從 [r] 開始舌頭幾乎一直保持捲起，到最後才放鬆。
error.tip_en: This word has r-color twice: right after [ɛ] the tongue curls back into [r], and the final -or is also an r-colored [ɚ], not [ɔr]. A common mistake is not curling the first [r] and then ending on a round-lipped [o]. Stress the first syllable [ɛ]; from the [r] on, the tongue stays curled almost the whole time and relaxes only at the very end.

examples.en: I found an error in my math homework.
examples.zh: 我在數學作業裡發現一個錯誤。

examples.en: The teacher marked the spelling error in red.
examples.zh: 老師用紅筆標出拼字錯誤。

eve.tip_zh: eve 只有一個音節 [iv]：長母音 [i] 嘴角往兩邊拉開，接著上排牙齒輕碰下唇、喉嚨震動發 [v]。常見的錯誤是把 [v] 唸成無聲的 [f]，或乾脆省掉，只剩長長的 [i]；也有人在後面多加母音唸成兩拍。字尾的 e 不發音。
eve.tip_en: eve is one syllable, [iv]: for the long [i], pull the corners of the mouth wide, then touch the upper teeth to the lower lip and voice [v] with the throat buzzing. Common mistakes are turning [v] into a voiceless [f], dropping it so only a long [i] is left, or adding a vowel to make two beats. The final e is silent.

examples.en: We eat dumplings on New Year's Eve.
examples.zh: 我們在除夕吃水餃。

examples.en: The kids stayed up late on Christmas Eve.
examples.zh: 孩子們在聖誕夜很晚才睡。

even.tip_zh: even 的 [v] 最容易出問題：學生常把它唸成 [b] 或 [w]，聽起來像「ibin」或「iwin」。發 [v] 時下唇輕碰上排牙齒，喉嚨同時震動。第一個 [i] 是長音，嘴角往兩邊拉；第二音節很輕。字尾 [n] 舌尖要頂住上牙齦收尾，不要滑到舌根變成 [ŋ]，否則聽起來像「eving」。
even.tip_en: The [v] in even is the usual problem: students often turn it into [b] or [w], so it sounds like 'ibin' or 'iwin'. For [v], touch the lower lip lightly to the upper teeth and voice it at the same time. The first [i] is long, with the mouth corners spread; the second syllable is light. Finish the final [n] with the tongue tip pressed on the upper gum ridge; don't slide back to [ŋ], or it sounds like 'eving'.

examples.en: My dad can even cook Japanese food.
examples.zh: 我爸爸甚至會做日本料理。

examples.en: Even my baby sister likes this song.
examples.zh: 連我的小妹妹都喜歡這首歌。

even.kk_flag: Minor: General American and Taiwan KK dictionaries usually give [ˈivən] with a reduced [ə] in the second syllable; [ˈivɪn] is CMU's IH0 and acceptable, but [ˈivən] is the usual reference form.

evening.tip_zh: evening 只有兩個音節 [iv] 和 [nɪŋ]。學生常照拼字唸成三拍的 e-ve-ning，在 [v] 和 [n] 中間多出一個母音。正確做法是下唇碰上齒發完 [v] 後不放鬆，直接把舌尖頂上牙齦接 [n]。字尾 [ŋ] 用舌根抵住軟顎，讓聲音從鼻子出來，和 morning 的結尾一樣。
evening.tip_en: Evening has only two syllables, [iv] and [nɪŋ]. Students often follow the spelling and say three beats, e-ve-ning, adding a vowel between [v] and [n]. Instead, after the lower lip touches the upper teeth for [v], don't relax; move the tongue tip straight to the upper gum ridge for [n]. For the final [ŋ], press the back of the tongue against the soft palate and let the sound come out through the nose, the same ending as morning.

examples.en: We take a walk in the evening.
examples.zh: 我們傍晚會去散步。

examples.en: Good evening, Mr. Lin! How are you?
examples.zh: 林先生，晚安！您好嗎？

evening.spelling_zh: 中間的 e 不發音，整個字只有兩拍。
evening.spelling_en: The middle e is silent; the word has only two beats.

ever.tip_zh: ever 開頭是 [ɛ]，跟 egg 的開頭一樣，嘴巴半開、嘴唇放鬆；不要把嘴唇圓起來唸成 over 的 [o]，兩個字意思完全不同。中間的 [v] 是下唇碰上排牙齒的有聲音，不能換成 [b]。字尾 [ɚ] 舌尖往後捲、不碰上顎，和 never 的結尾相同，整個字只有兩拍。
ever.tip_en: Ever starts with [ɛ], the same as the start of egg: mouth half open, lips relaxed. Don't round the lips into the [o] of over; the two words mean completely different things. The middle [v] is a voiced sound made with the lower lip on the upper teeth and can't be swapped for [b]. For the final [ɚ], curl the tongue tip back without touching the roof of the mouth, the same ending as never; the whole word has just two beats.

examples.en: Have you ever seen a rainbow?
examples.zh: 你曾經看過彩虹嗎？

examples.en: This is the best pizza ever!
examples.zh: 這是史上最好吃的披薩！

every.tip_zh: every 拼字有三個母音字母，學生常一個一個唸成 e-ve-ry，中間唸成清楚的 [ɛ]。其實中間的 e 幾乎不發音，[v] 之後直接捲舌接 [rɪ]，只有 ev-ry 兩拍，跟 everyone 的開頭一樣。重音永遠在第一音節 [ɛ]，[v] 要用下唇碰上排牙齒並發出聲音。
every.tip_en: Every has three vowel letters, and students often say them one by one, e-ve-ry, with a clear [ɛ] in the middle. In fact the middle e is almost silent: after [v] the tongue curls straight into [rɪ], giving just two beats, ev-ry, the same as the start of everyone. The stress is always on the first syllable [ɛ], and [v] is made with the lower lip on the upper teeth, with voice.

examples.en: I brush my teeth every morning.
examples.zh: 我每天早上刷牙。

examples.en: Every student has a new book.
examples.zh: 每個學生都有一本新書。

every.variant_zh: 慢慢唸時也有人唸成三個音節 [ˈɛvərɪ]。
every.variant_en: In slow, careful speech some people say three syllables: [ˈɛvərɪ].
every.kk_flag: Acceptable as a careful three-syllable form, but everyday General American is two syllables [ˈɛvrɪ] (the CMU variant, and the form most dictionaries give); consider making [ˈɛvrɪ] the headline KK.

everyone.tip_zh: everyone 結尾的 one 唸 [wʌn]，跟 won 同音；學生常唸成 [wɑn]，或把嘴唇圓起來唸成 [won]。[ʌ] 嘴巴微開、舌頭放平放鬆，跟 fun、run 的母音一樣。前面的 every 只唸兩拍 [ɛvrɪ]，[v] 和 [r] 緊緊相連，中間不加母音。整個字三拍，重音在 [ɛv]，最後的 [n] 用舌尖頂住上牙齦。
everyone.tip_en: The one at the end of everyone is said [wʌn], the same as won; students often say [wɑn], or round the lips into [won]. For [ʌ], open the mouth slightly and keep the tongue flat and relaxed, the same vowel as fun and run. The every part is only two beats, [ɛvrɪ], with [v] and [r] tightly joined and no vowel between them. The whole word has three beats, stressed on [ɛv], and the final [n] is made with the tongue tip on the upper gum ridge.

examples.en: Everyone in my class likes music.
examples.zh: 我們班每個人都喜歡音樂。

examples.en: Good morning, everyone! Let's start our lesson.
examples.zh: 大家早安！我們開始上課吧。

everyone.spelling_zh: one 的部分開頭有 [w] 音，但拼字裡沒有 w。
everyone.spelling_en: The one part starts with a [w] sound, but has no w.

everything.tip_zh: everything 的難點在第三音節 [θɪŋ]：學生常把 [θ] 唸成 [s]，變成「every-sing」，聽起來像在說唱歌。從前面的 [rɪ] 接過來時，把舌尖往前伸，輕輕放在上下牙齒之間吹氣，喉嚨不要震動。字尾 [ŋ] 舌根抵住軟顎，跟單獨唸 thing 時一樣。前面的 every 只有兩拍 [ɛvrɪ]，重音在最前面。
everything.tip_en: The hard part of everything is the third syllable [θɪŋ]: students often turn [θ] into [s], making 'every-sing', which sounds like singing. Coming from the [rɪ] before it, push the tongue tip forward and rest it lightly between the upper and lower teeth, then blow air without voicing. For the final [ŋ], press the back of the tongue against the soft palate, just as when saying thing on its own. The every part has only two beats, [ɛvrɪ], with the stress at the very front.

examples.en: Mom packed everything for our trip.
examples.zh: 媽媽把旅行要帶的東西都打包好了。

examples.en: Everything in this store is so cute!
examples.zh: 這家店裡的每樣東西都好可愛！

example.tip_zh: example 的 x 在這裡唸有聲的 [gz]，不是 [ks]；學生常照 ex 的拼法唸成 [ɛks]，開頭又重又硬。其實開頭 [ɪg] 輕而短，重音落在第二音節 [zæm]，[æ] 要把下巴往下拉、嘴角往兩邊開。結尾 [pḷ] 雙唇閉一下就把舌尖抬到上牙齦，發出暗 L，不要多加一個母音變成另一拍。
example.tip_en: In example, the x is the voiced [gz], not [ks]; students often follow the ex spelling and say [ɛks], making the start loud and hard. In fact the opening [ɪg] is light and short, and the stress falls on the second syllable [zæm]; for [æ], drop the jaw and spread the mouth corners. For the final [pḷ], close the lips briefly, then lift the tongue tip to the upper gum ridge for a dark L; don't add a vowel that makes an extra beat.

examples.en: Can you give me an example?
examples.zh: 你可以舉個例子嗎？

examples.en: Our teacher wrote an example on the board.
examples.zh: 老師在黑板上寫了一個例子。

excellent.tip_zh: excellent 重音在第一音節 [ɛk]，學生常受 excel 影響，把重音移到第二音節，唸成「ex-CEL-lent」。後面兩拍 [sə] 和 [lənt] 都要輕，母音弱化成 [ə]。結尾 [nt] 是子音串：舌尖頂住上牙齦發 [n]，舌頭不動直接放出 [t]，不要多加母音，也不要把 [t] 吞掉只剩 [n]。
excellent.tip_en: Excellent is stressed on the first syllable [ɛk]; students are often influenced by excel and move the stress to the second syllable, saying 'ex-CEL-lent'. The last two beats, [sə] and [lənt], are both light, with the vowels reduced to [ə]. The final [nt] is a consonant cluster: press the tongue tip on the upper gum ridge for [n], then release [t] without moving the tongue; don't add a vowel, and don't swallow the [t] so that only [n] is left.

examples.en: Excellent work! You got every answer right.
examples.zh: 做得太好了！你每一題都答對了。

examples.en: The food at this restaurant is excellent.
examples.zh: 這家餐廳的食物非常好吃。

excellent.spelling_zh: xc 合起來只唸 [ks]，c 不再多發一個音。
excellent.spelling_en: xc together make just [ks]; the c adds no sound.

except.tip_zh: 重音在第二音節 [sɛpt]，第一音節 [ɪk] 輕而短，不要唸成重重的 [ɛk]。x 在這裡是 [ks]，[k] 和 [s] 分屬兩個音節。字尾 [pt] 兩個子音連在一起：雙唇閉一下發 [p]，馬上用舌尖頂牙齦收成 [t]，中間不加母音，也不要把 [t] 吞掉。
except.tip_en: Stress the second syllable [sɛpt]; the first syllable [ɪk] is light and short, not a heavy [ɛk]. The x here is [ks], with [k] and [s] in different syllables. The final [pt] is two consonants together: close the lips briefly for [p], then right away stop with the tongue tip on the gum ridge for [t], with no vowel in between and without swallowing the [t].

examples.en: Everyone came to the party except Tom.
examples.zh: 除了湯姆以外，大家都來參加派對了。

examples.en: The shop is open every day except Monday.
examples.zh: 這家店除了星期一以外每天都開。

excited.tip_zh: excited 重音在第二音節 [saɪ]，[aɪ] 要從張大的 [a] 滑到 [ɪ]，唸得飽滿。最常見的問題是把結尾 [təd] 吞掉，聽起來像 excite，或和 exciting 分不清楚。[t] 後面的 -ed 要多唸一拍 [əd]，舌尖碰上牙齦兩次。開頭 [ɪk] 輕而短，不要唸成又重又長的 [ɛk]。
excited.tip_en: Excited is stressed on the second syllable [saɪ]; glide [aɪ] fully from a wide-open [a] to [ɪ]. The most common problem is swallowing the ending [təd], so it sounds like excite or gets mixed up with exciting. After [t], the -ed adds a whole extra beat, [əd], with the tongue tip touching the upper gum ridge twice. The opening [ɪk] is light and short; don't make it a heavy, long [ɛk].

examples.en: I am so excited about the school trip!
examples.zh: 我對校外教學超級興奮！

examples.en: The kids were excited to see the snow.
examples.zh: 孩子們看到雪都很興奮。

exciting.tip_zh: exciting 和 excited 只差在結尾：這裡是 [tɪŋ]，[ɪ] 短而放鬆，最後的 [ŋ] 用舌根往上抵住軟顎，讓聲音從鼻子出來。學生常把 [ŋ] 收成舌尖的 [n]，或把 [ɪ] 拉長成 [i]。重音放在中間的 [saɪ]，[s] 要清楚吹氣；前面的 [ɪk] 輕輕帶過，整個字三拍。
exciting.tip_en: Exciting differs from excited only in the ending: here it is [tɪŋ], with a short, relaxed [ɪ], and the final [ŋ] made by pressing the back of the tongue up against the soft palate so the sound comes out through the nose. Students often end with a tongue-tip [n] instead of [ŋ], or stretch [ɪ] into [i]. Put the stress on the middle [saɪ] with a clear, hissing [s]; pass lightly over the opening [ɪk]. The whole word has three beats.

examples.en: The soccer game was really exciting!
examples.zh: 那場足球賽真的很刺激！

examples.en: We read an exciting story about a dragon.
examples.zh: 我們讀了一個關於龍的精彩故事。

exercise.tip_zh: exercise 結尾的 se 唸有聲的 [z]，學生常唸成無聲的 [s]，聽起來像「exer-sice」。發 [z] 時舌頭位置和 [s] 一樣，但喉嚨要震動，像蜜蜂的嗡嗡聲。中間的 [sɚ] 要捲舌，不要唸成平平的 [sɛ]。重音在第一音節 [ɛk]，最後的 [saɪz] 是次重音，[aɪ] 要滑完整再接 [z]。
exercise.tip_en: The se at the end of exercise is a voiced [z]; students often say a voiceless [s], so it sounds like 'exer-sice'. For [z], the tongue is in the same place as for [s], but the throat vibrates, like a bee buzzing. The middle [sɚ] needs the r-curl; don't flatten it into [sɛ]. The stress is on the first syllable [ɛk], and the last syllable [saɪz] has secondary stress; glide [aɪ] all the way before adding [z].

examples.en: We exercise in the park every morning.
examples.zh: 我們每天早上在公園運動。

examples.en: Exercise is good for your body.
examples.zh: 運動對身體很好。

exercise.spelling_zh: 字尾 -ise 的 s 唸 [z]，e 不發音。
exercise.spelling_en: In the final -ise, the s is [z] and the e is silent.

expect.tip_zh: 中間 [ksp] 三個子音連在一起，最容易被拆開、加進母音，唸成「依克斯配克特」。[s] 後面的 [p] 不送氣，聽起來有點像 b，這是正常的。重音在第二音節 [spɛkt]；字尾 [kt] 舌根頂一下就接舌尖的 [t]，不要多加母音。
expect.tip_en: The middle [ksp] is three consonants in a row and is the part most easily broken up with added vowels. The [p] after [s] has no puff of air, so it sounds a bit like b; that is normal. Stress the second syllable [spɛkt]; for the final [kt], the back of the tongue taps once and goes straight into the tongue-tip [t], with no extra vowel.

examples.en: I expect it will rain this afternoon.
examples.zh: 我預料今天下午會下雨。

examples.en: Mom expects us home before six.
examples.zh: 媽媽期待我們六點前到家。

expensive.tip_zh: expensive 重音在第二音節 [spɛn]。[s] 後面的 [p] 不送氣，聽起來比較接近 [b]，不必用力噴氣。結尾 [sɪv] 是最容易漏掉的地方：學生常把 [v] 唸成 [f]，或乾脆不發，只剩「expensi」。發 [v] 時下唇貼住上排牙齒，同時讓喉嚨震動，收尾後不要再加母音。
expensive.tip_en: Expensive is stressed on the second syllable [spɛn]. The [p] after [s] is unaspirated, so it sounds closer to [b]; there is no need to push out a puff of air. The ending [sɪv] is the part most often lost: students often say [v] as [f], or drop it so only 'expensi' is left. For [v], rest the lower lip against the upper teeth and voice it at the same time, and don't add a vowel after it.

examples.en: This toy is too expensive for me.
examples.zh: 這個玩具對我來說太貴了。

examples.en: Wow, your new bike looks expensive!
examples.zh: 哇，你的新腳踏車看起來好貴！

experience.tip_zh: experience 有四拍，重音在第二音節 [spɪ]。學生常把它唸成 ex-pe-ri-ence，第二音節用了 [ɛ]，或把重音放到第三音節。[spɪ] 的 [ɪ] 後面緊接捲舌的 [r]，舌尖往後捲、不碰上顎。最後的 [əns] 很輕：母音弱化成 [ə]，[n] 頂住上牙齦後直接吹出 [s]，不要再加母音多出一拍。
experience.tip_en: Experience has four beats, stressed on the second syllable [spɪ]. Students often say ex-pe-ri-ence with an [ɛ] in the second syllable, or put the stress on the third syllable. The [ɪ] in [spɪ] is followed closely by an r-curled [r]: curl the tongue tip back without touching the roof of the mouth. The final [əns] is light: the vowel reduces to [ə], and after [n] on the upper gum ridge you blow straight out into [s]; don't add a vowel that makes an extra beat.

examples.en: Camping was a fun experience for our family.
examples.zh: 露營對我們家來說是一次很好玩的經驗。

examples.en: Do you have any experience with pets?
examples.zh: 你有養寵物的經驗嗎？

explain.tip_zh: 重音在第二音節 [splen]，[s]、[p]、[l] 三個子音要一口氣連著唸，中間不加母音：雙唇還閉著準備 [p] 時，舌尖就先抬到牙齦等著發 [l]。ai 唸 [e]，要從 [e] 滑向 [ɪ]，不要縮成短的 [ɛ]。字尾用舌尖頂上排牙齦收成 [n]，不要唸成 [ŋ]。
explain.tip_en: Stress the second syllable [splen]; say [s], [p] and [l] in one go with no vowel inserted: while the lips are still closed for [p], the tongue tip is already up on the gum ridge waiting for [l]. ai is [e], gliding from [e] toward [ɪ], not shrunk to a short [ɛ]. Finish with the tongue tip on the upper gum ridge for [n], not [ŋ].

examples.en: Can you explain this word to me?
examples.zh: 你可以跟我解釋這個字嗎？

examples.en: The teacher will explain the rules of the game.
examples.zh: 老師會解釋這個遊戲的規則。

eye.tip_zh: eye 只唸一個雙母音 [aɪ]，和 I 同音。學生常像中文第四聲那樣一下子往下掉，[ɪ] 還沒滑到就收掉了。發音時下巴先張大發 [a]，再慢慢合上滑到 [ɪ]，聲音平穩或微微下降。說複數 eyes 時結尾是有聲的 [z]，喉嚨要震動，不要唸成 [s]。可以用 my、bye 練習同一個母音。
eye.tip_en: Eye is a single diphthong [aɪ], the same sound as I. Students often drop it sharply like a Mandarin fourth tone and cut it off before reaching [ɪ]. Open the jaw wide for [a] first, then close it gradually as you glide to [ɪ], keeping the pitch level or falling only slightly. In the plural eyes, the ending is a voiced [z] with throat vibration, not [s]. Practice the same vowel with my and bye.

examples.en: I have something in my eye.
examples.zh: 我的眼睛裡有東西。

examples.en: The cat has one blue eye and one green eye.
examples.zh: 那隻貓有一隻藍眼睛和一隻綠眼睛。

eye.spelling_zh: 拼字有三個字母，但整個字只唸 [aɪ]，跟 I 同音。
eye.spelling_en: Three letters, but the word is just [aɪ], like I.

face.tip_zh: [e] 要唸飽滿，從 [e] 滑到 [ɪ]，不要縮成短促的 [ɛ]，否則聽起來不像 face。字尾 [s] 是無聲的，舌尖靠近上排牙齦送氣即可，不要唸成有聲的 [z]，也不要多加母音變成「費斯」兩拍。最後的 e 不發音；c 在這裡唸 [s]，不是 [k]。
face.tip_en: Make [e] full, gliding from [e] to [ɪ]; don't shrink it to a short [ɛ], or it won't sound like face. The final [s] is voiceless: bring the tongue tip near the upper gum ridge and just let the air through. Don't voice it as [z], and don't add a vowel to make two beats. The last e is silent, and the c here is [s], not [k].

examples.en: Wash your face before you go to bed.
examples.zh: 睡覺前要洗臉。

examples.en: Our classroom windows face the playground.
examples.zh: 我們教室的窗戶面向操場。

fact.tip_zh: [æ] 下巴要往下拉、嘴角往兩邊開，不要唸成較小的 [ɛ]。字尾 [kt] 是兩個子音：舌根頂一下發 [k]，不放氣就直接用舌尖發 [t]。常見的錯誤是把 [k] 省掉，fact 就變成 fat；或在最後多加母音，唸成「費克特」三拍。
fact.tip_en: For [æ], drop the jaw and spread the corners of the mouth; don't make the smaller [ɛ]. The final [kt] is two consonants: tap the back of the tongue for [k], then without releasing air go straight to the tongue-tip [t]. Common mistakes are dropping the [k], which turns fact into fat, or adding vowels at the end to make three beats.

examples.en: Here is a fun fact about frogs.
examples.zh: 這裡有一個關於青蛙的有趣事實。

examples.en: In fact, I finished my homework early.
examples.zh: 事實上，我很早就寫完功課了。

factory.tip_zh: factory 的 -tory 不要照 story 唸成 [tɔrɪ]；這裡是很輕的 [tərɪ]，[tə] 輕輕帶過、再捲舌接 [rɪ]，口語中幾乎只剩 [trɪ]。第一音節 [fæk] 才是重點，[æ] 要把下巴往下拉、嘴角往兩邊開，不要縮成 [ɛ]。[k] 和 [t] 之間不要插入母音，舌根頂一下就直接換成舌尖。
factory.tip_en: Don't say the -tory of factory like story, [tɔrɪ]; here it is a very light [tərɪ]: pass over [tə] quickly, then curl the tongue for [rɪ], and in speech it is almost just [trɪ]. The first syllable [fæk] is the important one: for [æ], drop the jaw and spread the mouth corners; don't shrink it to [ɛ]. Don't insert a vowel between [k] and [t]: the back of the tongue touches once, then switch straight to the tongue tip.

examples.en: My uncle works at a toy factory.
