examples.zh: 我叔叔在玩具工廠上班。

examples.en: We visited a chocolate factory on our trip.
examples.zh: 我們旅行時參觀了一間巧克力工廠。

factory.variant_en: In fast speech often two syllables: [ˈfæktrɪ].

fail.tip_zh: ai 唸 [e]，要從 [e] 滑向 [ɪ] 再接 [l]；如果縮成短的 [ɛ]，fail 會聽起來像 fell。字尾一定要發出 [l]：舌尖抬到上排牙齦停住，舌根同時往後壓，發出比較暗的 L。常見錯誤是把 [l] 省掉，只剩 [fe]，或在最後多加一個「歐」的母音。
fail.tip_en: ai is [e], gliding from [e] toward [ɪ] before the [l]; if you shrink it to a short [ɛ], fail sounds like fell. You must sound the final [l]: lift the tongue tip to the upper gum ridge and hold it while pressing the back of the tongue back, giving a darker L. Common mistakes are dropping the [l] so only [fe] is left, or adding an "o" vowel at the end.

examples.en: Don't worry if you fail the first time.
examples.zh: 第一次失敗了也不要擔心。

examples.en: If we practice, we won't fail the test.
examples.zh: 如果我們練習，考試就不會不及格。

fall.tip_zh: a 在這裡唸 [ɔ]，嘴巴張開、嘴唇稍微圓起來，不是 [æ]，也不是嘴型更小的 [o]。字尾的 ll 是暗 L：舌尖頂住上排牙齦，舌根往後壓，聲音持續到最後。常見的錯誤是省略 [l]，只剩一個圓唇母音，聽起來像在說「佛」。
fall.tip_en: The a here is [ɔ]: open the mouth and round the lips slightly; it is not [æ], and not the smaller [o]. The final ll is a dark L: press the tongue tip on the upper gum ridge, pull the back of the tongue back, and keep the sound going to the end. A common mistake is dropping the [l] so only a round vowel is left.

examples.en: The leaves turn red and yellow in fall.
examples.zh: 秋天時葉子會變紅、變黃。

examples.en: My favorite season is fall.
examples.zh: 我最喜歡的季節是秋天。

fall.variant_en: A more open [fɑl] is also common.

family.tip_zh: family 的第一音節 [fæ] 嘴巴要張大、下巴往下拉；學生常唸成比較扁的 [ɛ]，聽起來像「femily」。中間的 [mə] 非常輕，美國人說快時幾乎跳過，變成兩拍 [ˈfæmlɪ]；不要把三個音節唸得一樣重。最後的 [lɪ] 舌尖輕碰上牙齦，[ɪ] 短而放鬆。
family.tip_en: For the first syllable [fæ] of family, open the mouth wide and drop the jaw; students often say a flatter [ɛ], so it sounds like 'femily'. The middle [mə] is very light, and Americans speaking fast almost skip it, making two beats, [ˈfæmlɪ]; don't give all three syllables equal weight. For the final [lɪ], touch the tongue tip lightly to the upper gum ridge and keep [ɪ] short and relaxed.

examples.en: There are five people in my family.
examples.zh: 我家有五個人。

examples.en: My family eats dinner together every night.
examples.zh: 我們家每天晚上一起吃晚餐。

family.variant_en: In everyday speech often two syllables: [ˈfæmlɪ].

famous.tip_zh: 重音在第一音節 [fe]，[e] 要唸飽滿。第二音節的 -ous 只是很輕的 [əs]，不要照拼字唸成 [aʊs] 或 [us]，也不要把兩個音節唸得一樣重。[m] 雙唇閉合後直接帶出輕輕的 [ə]，最後以無聲的 [s] 收尾。
famous.tip_en: Stress the first syllable [fe] and make the [e] full. The -ous of the second syllable is just a light [əs]; don't read it from the spelling as [aʊs] or [us], and don't make the two syllables equally strong. Close the lips for [m], let a light [ə] come straight out, and finish with a voiceless [s].

examples.en: This town is famous for its beef noodles.
examples.zh: 這個小鎮以牛肉麵出名。

examples.en: She wants to be a famous singer one day.
examples.zh: 她希望有一天成為有名的歌手。

fan.tip_zh: [æ] 是這個字的關鍵：下巴往下拉、嘴角往兩邊咧開，不要唸成 [ɛ]，否則像在說 fen。字尾是舌尖的 [n]：舌尖頂住上排牙齦收尾，不要讓舌根抬起變成 [ŋ]，否則聽起來像 fang。可以把手指放在下巴，感覺 [æ] 時下巴明顯往下。
fan.tip_en: [æ] is the key: drop the jaw and spread the corners of the mouth; don't say [ɛ], or it sounds like fen. End with tongue-tip [n], pressing the tip on the upper gum ridge; don't raise the back of the tongue into [ŋ], or it sounds like fang. Put a finger on your chin and feel the jaw drop clearly for [æ].

examples.en: Please turn on the fan. It's hot.
examples.zh: 請打開電扇，好熱。

examples.en: My dad is a big baseball fan.
examples.zh: 我爸爸是個超級棒球迷。

far.tip_zh: [ɑ] 嘴巴要張大、舌頭放低，接著舌尖往後捲成 [r]。常見的錯誤是沒有捲舌，只剩「發」的音；或捲得太晚、太弱。far 的母音比 for 的 [ɔ] 更開，嘴唇不要變圓，這兩個字才分得清楚。
far.tip_en: For [ɑ], open the mouth wide with the tongue low, then curl the tongue tip back into [r]. A common mistake is leaving out the curl so only a bare "fa" is left, or curling too late and too weakly. The vowel in far is more open than the [ɔ] in for; keep the lips unrounded so the two words stay distinct.

examples.en: Is the park far from your home?
examples.zh: 公園離你家遠嗎？

examples.en: The bird flew far away.
examples.zh: 那隻鳥飛得好遠。

farm.tip_zh: [ɑr] 之後雙唇要閉起來發 [m]，[r] 和 [m] 都要有。常見的錯誤是把 [r] 省掉，變成 [fɑm]；或閉唇後又多加一個母音，唸成兩拍。練法：張大嘴說 [ɑ]，舌尖往後捲，最後輕輕閉上雙唇，讓聲音從鼻子出來就結束。
farm.tip_en: After [ɑr], close the lips for [m]; both [r] and [m] must be there. Common mistakes are dropping the [r] so it becomes [fɑm], or adding a vowel after closing the lips so it becomes two beats. Practice: say [ɑ] with the mouth open wide, curl the tongue tip back, and finally close the lips gently, letting the sound come out through the nose, and stop.

examples.en: My uncle has a farm with cows and pigs.
examples.zh: 我叔叔有一座養牛和豬的農場。

examples.en: We picked strawberries on a farm last weekend.
examples.zh: 上週末我們去農場採草莓。

farmer.tip_zh: 這個字有兩個捲舌音：第一音節 [fɑr] 的 [r]，和字尾 -er 的 [ɚ]。常見的錯誤是第一個 [r] 沒捲，直接從 [ɑ] 跳到 [m]，或字尾唸成平平的 [ə]。重音在第一音節 [fɑr]，第二音節 [mɚ] 輕輕帶過，但舌頭仍要捲起。
farmer.tip_en: This word has two r-colored sounds: the [r] in the first syllable [fɑr] and the [ɚ] of the final -er. Common mistakes are skipping the first [r], jumping straight from [ɑ] to [m], or ending on a flat [ə]. Stress the first syllable [fɑr]; pass lightly over the second syllable [mɚ], but keep the tongue curled.

examples.en: The farmer grows rice and corn.
examples.zh: 那位農夫種稻米和玉米。

examples.en: The farmer gave us some fresh eggs.
examples.zh: 農夫給了我們一些新鮮的雞蛋。

fast.tip_zh: [æ] 嘴巴要張大、嘴角往兩邊開，不要唸成 [ɛ]，也不要捲舌，否則容易和 first [fɝst] 搞混。字尾 [st] 兩個子音都要發：先送氣發 [s]，舌尖接著頂住牙齦發 [t]。不要把 [t] 吞掉，也不要多加母音唸成「費斯特」。
fast.tip_en: For [æ], open the mouth wide and spread its corners; don't say [ɛ], and don't curl the tongue, or it is easily confused with first [fɝst]. Pronounce both consonants of the final [st]: blow out the [s], then press the tongue tip on the gum ridge for [t]. Don't swallow the [t], and don't add vowels.

examples.en: My brother can run very fast.
examples.zh: 我弟弟跑得很快。

examples.en: The fast train gets to Taipei in an hour.
examples.zh: 快車一個小時就到台北。

fat.tip_zh: 母音 [æ] 下巴要明顯往下拉、嘴角咧開，不要唸成較窄的 [ɛ]。字尾 [t] 只要舌尖頂住上排牙齦停住即可，不必用力放氣，更不要在後面加「特」的母音。也要注意不要多出一個 [k]：fat 和 fact 只差在 [k]。
fat.tip_en: For the vowel [æ], drop the jaw clearly and spread the corners of the mouth; don't make the narrower [ɛ]. For the final [t], just press the tongue tip on the upper gum ridge and stop; there's no need to push air out, and don't add a vowel after it. Also don't slip in a [k]: fat and fact differ only by the [k].

examples.en: Our cat is fat and lazy.
examples.zh: 我們的貓又胖又懶。

examples.en: The panda ate bamboo and got fat.
examples.zh: 那隻貓熊吃竹子吃得胖胖的。

father.tip_zh: father 中間的 th 是有聲的 [ð]，學生常唸成 [d] 或 [z]，聽起來像「fader」或「fazer」。發 [ð] 時舌尖輕輕夾在上下牙齒之間，喉嚨同時震動。前面的 [ɑ] 嘴巴張大、舌頭放低，從這個開口的位置把舌尖往前送到牙齒之間，再往後捲成字尾的 [ɚ]。
father.tip_en: The th in the middle of father is the voiced [ð]; students often say [d] or [z], so it sounds like 'fader' or 'fazer'. For [ð], hold the tongue tip lightly between the upper and lower teeth and voice it at the same time. The [ɑ] before it has the mouth wide open and the tongue low; from that open position, bring the tongue tip forward between the teeth, then curl it back for the final [ɚ].

examples.en: My father reads stories to me at night.
examples.zh: 我爸爸晚上會唸故事給我聽。

examples.en: My father and I play basketball on Sundays.
examples.zh: 我和爸爸星期天會一起打籃球。

favorite.tip_zh: favorite 結尾的 -ite 不唸 [aɪt]，跟 kite、bite 不一樣，這裡是短短的 [ɪt]。學生常照拼字把結尾唸成像 write 的音。重音在第一音節 [fe]，[e] 嘴角往兩邊拉。中間的 [və] 先用下唇碰上齒發 [v]，輕輕帶過再捲舌接 [rɪt]，說快時常合在一起。字尾 [t] 舌尖點一下就停，不要加母音。
favorite.tip_en: The -ite at the end of favorite is not [aɪt] as in kite and bite; here it is a short [ɪt]. Students often follow the spelling and make the ending sound like write. The stress is on the first syllable [fe], with the mouth corners spread for [e]. For the middle [və], touch the lower lip to the upper teeth for [v], pass over it lightly, then curl the tongue for [rɪt]; in fast speech they often blend together. For the final [t], tap the tongue tip once and stop; don't add a vowel.

examples.en: Blue is my favorite color.
examples.zh: 藍色是我最喜歡的顏色。

examples.en: What is your favorite animal?
examples.zh: 你最喜歡的動物是什麼？

favorite.spelling_zh: 結尾 -ite 唸 [ɪt]，不是 kite 的 [aɪt]。
favorite.spelling_en: The final -ite is [ɪt], not the [aɪt] of kite.

february.tip_zh: February 重音在第一音節 [fɛb]。學生常被拼字裡的兩個 r 困住，硬要把第一個 r 捲出來，結果舌頭打結。常見的美式唸法第一個 r 不發音，b 後面接輕輕的 [jə]，再接 [wɛrɪ]，這一段有次重音。結尾的 [ɛrɪ] 跟 very 的 [ɛrɪ] 一樣，January 的結尾也是這個音，可以一起練。
february.tip_en: February is stressed on the first syllable [fɛb]. Students often get stuck on the two r's in the spelling and force out the first r, which ties the tongue in a knot. In the common American pronunciation the first r is silent: after b comes a light [jə], then [wɛrɪ], which has secondary stress. The ending [ɛrɪ] is the same as the [ɛrɪ] of very, and January ends with the same sound, so practice them together.

examples.en: My birthday is in February.
examples.zh: 我的生日在二月。

examples.en: February is the shortest month of the year.
examples.zh: 二月是一年中最短的月份。

february.variant_zh: 也可以把第一個 r 唸出來：[ˈfɛbruˌɛrɪ]。
february.variant_en: Also correct with the first r: [ˈfɛbruˌɛrɪ].
february.spelling_zh: 常見的美式唸法中，第一個 r 不發音。
february.spelling_en: In the common American pronunciation, the first r is silent.

feed.tip_zh: [i] 是長母音，嘴角往兩邊拉開、舌頭前面抬高。字尾 [d] 是有聲的，喉嚨要震動，舌尖頂住牙齦收尾。常見的錯誤是唸成無聲的 [t]，聽起來像 feet；或把 [d] 吞掉。在 [d] 前面，[i] 會比在 feet 裡稍微長一點，這也能幫助對方聽出差別。
feed.tip_en: [i] is a long vowel: pull the corners of the mouth wide and raise the front of the tongue. The final [d] is voiced: the throat buzzes and the tongue tip finishes on the gum ridge. Common mistakes are saying a voiceless [t], which sounds like feet, or swallowing the [d]. Before [d], the [i] is a little longer than in feet, which also helps listeners hear the difference.

examples.en: It's my turn to feed the fish today.
examples.zh: 今天輪到我餵魚。

examples.en: We feed the dog twice a day.
examples.zh: 我們一天餵狗兩次。

feel.tip_zh: 長母音 [i] 嘴角要往兩邊拉，不要唸成短而放鬆的 [ɪ]，否則會變成 fill。字尾的 [l] 一定要發：從 [i] 移到 [l] 時舌尖抬到上排牙齦，舌根往後壓。常見的錯誤是把 [l] 省掉，只剩 [fi]，聽起來像沒說完；說 I feel 時尤其要把 [l] 收好。
feel.tip_en: For the long [i], pull the corners of the mouth wide; don't say the short, relaxed [ɪ], or it becomes fill. You must sound the final [l]: as you move from [i] to [l], lift the tongue tip to the upper gum ridge and press the back of the tongue back. A common mistake is dropping the [l] so only [fi] is left, which sounds unfinished; finish the [l] carefully especially in I feel.

examples.en: I feel happy when I play with my friends.
examples.zh: 跟朋友一起玩的時候我覺得很開心。

examples.en: How do you feel today?
examples.zh: 你今天覺得怎麼樣？

festival.tip_zh: festival 重音在第一音節 [fɛs]，後面兩拍都很輕。學生常在 [s] 和 [t] 中間加母音，唸成「fe-si-ti-val」，或把重音放到中間。[st] 要連在一起：先發 [s]，舌尖直接頂上牙齦放出 [t]。結尾 [vḷ] 下唇碰上齒發 [v]，接著把舌尖抬到上牙齦發暗 L，不要收成 [vo]。
festival.tip_en: Festival is stressed on the first syllable [fɛs], and the two beats after it are light. Students often add a vowel between [s] and [t], saying 'fe-si-ti-val', or put the stress in the middle. [st] must stay together: say [s], then press the tongue tip straight onto the upper gum ridge to release [t]. For the final [vḷ], touch the lower lip to the upper teeth for [v], then lift the tongue tip to the upper gum ridge for a dark L; don't end it as [vo].

examples.en: The Dragon Boat Festival is in early summer.
examples.zh: 端午節在初夏。

examples.en: Our school has a music festival every spring.
examples.zh: 我們學校每年春天都有音樂節。

fever.tip_zh: fever 的兩個子音 [f] 和 [v] 嘴型完全一樣，都是下唇輕碰上排牙齒，差別只在 [v] 要讓喉嚨震動。學生常把 [v] 也唸成無聲的 [f]，或換成 [w]。練習時把手放在喉嚨上：發 [f] 不會震，發 [v] 會震。開頭的 [i] 是長音、嘴角往兩邊拉，結尾的 [ɚ] 舌尖往後捲。
fever.tip_en: The two consonants in fever, [f] and [v], use exactly the same mouth shape: the lower lip lightly touching the upper teeth. The only difference is that [v] makes the throat vibrate. Students often say [v] as a voiceless [f] too, or swap it for [w]. To practice, put a hand on your throat: [f] doesn't buzz, [v] does. The [i] at the start is long, with the mouth corners spread, and for the final [ɚ] the tongue tip curls back.

examples.en: I stayed home because I had a fever.
examples.zh: 我因為發燒待在家裡。

examples.en: Drink lots of water when you have a fever.
examples.zh: 發燒的時候要多喝水。

few.tip_zh: few 唸 [fju]，[f] 和 [u] 中間有一個 [j] 的滑音，就像 you 的開頭。常見的錯誤是把 [j] 省掉，唸成 [fu]，聽起來不像 few。練法：上排牙齒輕碰下唇發 [f]，舌頭中間馬上往上抬發 [j]，最後嘴唇圓起來發長的 [u]。ew 兩個字母合起來就是 [ju]。
few.tip_en: few is [fju]: between [f] and [u] there is a [j] glide, just like the start of you. A common mistake is dropping the [j] and saying [fu], which doesn't sound like few. Practice: touch the upper teeth to the lower lip for [f], raise the middle of the tongue right away for [j], and finally round the lips for a long [u]. The two letters ew together make [ju].

examples.en: I have a few questions about the homework.
examples.zh: 我對功課有幾個問題。

examples.en: Only a few students were late today.
examples.zh: 今天只有少數幾個學生遲到。

fifteen.tip_zh: 重音在第二音節 [tin]：[i] 要拉長、嘴角往兩邊拉，字尾的 [n] 用舌尖收得清楚。常見的錯誤是把重音放在第一音節，聽起來就像 fifty。第一音節 [fɪf] 短而輕，兩個 [f] 中間是短的 [ɪ]，不要照 five 唸成 [faɪ]。
fifteen.tip_en: Stress the second syllable [tin]: stretch the [i] with the mouth corners pulled wide, and finish the [n] clearly with the tongue tip. A common mistake is stressing the first syllable, which makes it sound like fifty. The first syllable [fɪf] is short and light, with a short [ɪ] between the two [f]s; don't say [faɪ] as in five.

examples.en: My sister is fifteen years old.
examples.zh: 我姊姊十五歲。

examples.en: The bus comes every fifteen minutes.
examples.zh: 公車每十五分鐘來一班。

fifty.tip_zh: 重音在第一音節 [fɪf]，第二音節 [tɪ] 短而輕，結尾是短的 [ɪ]，不能拉長成 [tin]，否則就變成 fifteen。數數時也常有人唸成 five 加 ty，但第一音節是短的 [fɪf]，不是 [faɪv]。[f] 和 [t] 之間不加母音，牙齒離開下唇時舌尖已經頂好牙齦。
fifty.tip_en: Stress the first syllable [fɪf]; the second syllable [tɪ] is short and light and ends in a short [ɪ]. Don't stretch it into [tin], or it becomes fifteen. When counting, some learners say five plus ty, but the first syllable is a short [fɪf], not [faɪv]. Put no vowel between [f] and [t]: as the teeth leave the lower lip, the tongue tip is already on the gum ridge.

examples.en: There are fifty pages in this book.
examples.zh: 這本書有五十頁。

examples.en: I saved fifty dollars this month.
examples.zh: 我這個月存了五十元。

fight.tip_zh: igh 唸 [aɪ]，gh 完全不發音，嘴巴從張大的 [a] 滑到 [ɪ]。字尾 [t] 舌尖頂住上排牙齦停住即可，不要在後面多加母音變成兩拍。也不要把 [t] 完全省掉，否則字尾聽起來沒有收住。開頭 [f] 是上排牙齒輕碰下唇送氣，不要唸成 [h]。
fight.tip_en: igh is [aɪ] and the gh is completely silent; slide from an open [a] to [ɪ]. For the final [t], just press the tongue tip on the upper gum ridge and stop; don't add a vowel to make two beats. Don't drop the [t] entirely either, or the word won't sound finished. The opening [f] is the upper teeth lightly touching the lower lip as you blow; don't say [h].

examples.en: My brother and I sometimes fight over the TV.
examples.zh: 我和哥哥有時會為了電視吵架。

examples.en: Please don't fight. Let's share the toys.
examples.zh: 請不要吵架，我們一起分享玩具吧。

fight.spelling_en: igh says [aɪ]; the gh is silent.

file.tip_zh: [aɪ] 之後要接字尾的 [l]：舌尖抬到上排牙齦，舌根往後壓，發出暗 L。常見的錯誤是把 [l] 省掉，只剩 [faɪ]；或在最後多加一個「歐」的母音。從 [aɪ] 到 [l] 中間會自然帶出一點 [ə] 的滑音，聽起來有點像兩拍，這是正常的。字尾 e 不發音。
file.tip_en: After [aɪ], add the final [l]: lift the tongue tip to the upper gum ridge and pull the back of the tongue back for a dark L. Common mistakes are dropping the [l] so only [faɪ] is left, or adding an "o" vowel at the end. A slight [ə] glide naturally appears between [aɪ] and [l], so it can sound a little like two beats; that is normal. The final e is silent.

examples.en: Save the file before you close the computer.
examples.zh: 關電腦前要先存檔。

examples.en: The teacher put our tests in a blue file.
examples.zh: 老師把我們的考卷放進一個藍色資料夾。

fill.tip_zh: fill 的 [ɪ] 短而放鬆，常被拉長成 [i]，聽起來就變成 feel（感覺）。嘴角不要往兩旁拉，下巴稍微放低，母音快速帶過。字尾 [l] 也常被吞掉，只剩下母音；收尾時舌尖要確實貼住上排牙齒後面的牙齦，停一下再結束，可以跟 hill、will 一起練。
fill.tip_en: The [ɪ] in fill is short and relaxed, but it often gets stretched into [i], which makes it sound like feel. Don't pull the corners of your mouth back; drop the jaw slightly and say the vowel quickly. The final [l] is also often swallowed, leaving only the vowel; to finish, press the tongue tip firmly on the gum ridge behind the upper teeth and hold it a moment. You can practice it together with hill and will.

examples.en: Please fill your water bottle before class.
examples.zh: 請在上課前把你的水壺裝滿。

examples.en: Can you fill the cup with milk?
examples.zh: 你可以把杯子裝滿牛奶嗎？

finally.tip_zh: finally 的重音在第一音節 [faɪ]，中間的 [nə] 要又輕又短。常見錯誤是照 final 的拼字把中間的 a 唸成響亮的 [æ]，或三個音節一樣重。先把 [faɪ] 唸得長而有力，從 [a] 滑到 [ɪ]，接著 [nə] 一帶而過，最後 [lɪ] 舌尖碰一下上牙齦就放開，輕輕收尾。
finally.tip_en: The stress in finally is on the first syllable [faɪ]; the middle [nə] must be light and short. A common mistake is following the spelling of final and saying the middle a as a loud [æ], or giving all three syllables equal weight. Make [faɪ] long and strong, gliding from [a] to [ɪ], then pass quickly over [nə], and finish lightly with [lɪ]: the tongue tip touches the gum ridge once and lets go.

examples.en: We finally got home after a long drive.
examples.zh: 開了很久的車，我們終於到家了。

examples.en: Finally, it's time for lunch!
examples.zh: 終於到午餐時間了！

finally.spelling_zh: 兩個 l 只唸一個 [l]
finally.spelling_en: The double l is said as a single [l].

find.tip_zh: 字尾 [nd] 是重點：舌尖頂住上排牙齦發 [n]，不要離開，接著輕輕放開成有聲的 [d]。如果把 [d] 吞掉，find 就會變成 fine；如果多加母音，又會多出一拍。i 在這裡唸 [aɪ]，要從張大嘴的 [a] 滑向 [ɪ]，不是短的 [ɪ]。
find.tip_en: The final [nd] is the key: press the tongue tip on the upper gum ridge for [n], keep it there, then gently release it into a voiced [d]. If you swallow the [d], find turns into fine; if you add a vowel, you get an extra beat. The i here is [aɪ], sliding from an open [a] toward [ɪ], not a short [ɪ].

examples.en: I can't find my pencil case.
examples.zh: 我找不到我的鉛筆盒。

examples.en: Let's find a seat near the window.
examples.zh: 我們找個靠窗的位子吧。

fine.tip_zh: fine 只有 [faɪn] 一個音節，字尾的 e 不發音，所以 [n] 後面不要再多唸一個母音。[aɪ] 嘴巴先張大再收向 [ɪ]，要滑得完整。字尾是舌尖的 [n]：舌尖頂住上排牙齦，聲音從鼻子出來，不要讓舌根抬起變成 [ŋ]，也不要多加 [d] 變成 find。
fine.tip_en: fine is one syllable, [faɪn]; the final e is silent, so don't say another vowel after [n]. Open the mouth wide first and then close toward [ɪ], making the [aɪ] glide complete. The final sound is tongue-tip [n]: press the tip on the upper gum ridge and let the sound come out through the nose; don't raise the back of the tongue into [ŋ], and don't add a [d], which would make find.

examples.en: I'm fine, thank you.
examples.zh: 我很好，謝謝你。

examples.en: The weather is fine for a picnic today.
examples.zh: 今天天氣很適合野餐。

finger.tip_zh: finger 第一音節結尾是後鼻音 [ŋ]，舌根抬起碰軟顎，不是舌尖的 [n]。接著舌根放開就是 [g]，所以 [ŋ] 和 [g] 兩個都要有；學生常照 singer 的方式把 [g] 省掉。字尾 [ɚ] 要把舌頭往後捲，不要唸成平平的「格」。
finger.tip_en: The first syllable of finger ends in the back nasal [ŋ]: the back of the tongue rises to touch the soft palate — it is not a tongue-tip [n]. Releasing the back of the tongue then gives [g], so both [ŋ] and [g] must be heard; students often drop the [g] the way singer does. For the final [ɚ], curl the tongue back — don't say a flat 「格」 (ge).

examples.en: Point your finger at the right picture.
examples.zh: 用手指指出正確的圖片。

examples.en: She has a pretty ring on her finger.
examples.zh: 她的手指上戴著一枚漂亮的戒指。

finger.spelling_zh: ng 在這裡唸 [ŋg]，g 要發出來（singer 的 g 則不發）
finger.spelling_en: Here ng is [ŋg] — the g is pronounced (unlike in singer).

finish.tip_zh: 重音在第一音節 [fɪ]，兩個 i 都是短的 [ɪ]，不要拉長成 [i]。字尾 [ʃ] 嘴唇要往前嘟、舌頭稍微往後，不是注音的ㄒ，也不要在後面加母音。常見的錯誤是把重音放到第二音節，或把結尾的 [ʃ] 唸成扁扁的 [s]。
finish.tip_en: Stress the first syllable [fɪ]; both i's are a short [ɪ], not stretched to [i]. For the final [ʃ], push the lips forward and pull the tongue back a little; it is not Mandarin ㄒ, and don't add a vowel after it. Common mistakes are stressing the second syllable, or flattening the final [ʃ] into [s].

examples.en: Finish your homework before you watch TV.
examples.zh: 看電視前先把功課寫完。

examples.en: We will finish the puzzle tomorrow.
examples.zh: 我們明天會把拼圖拼完。

fire.tip_zh: [aɪ] 要從張大嘴的 [a] 滑向 [ɪ]，接著舌尖往後捲成 [r]。常見的錯誤是沒有捲舌，只剩 [faɪ]；或在 [aɪ] 後面插入一個「呀」的音再收尾。字尾的 e 不發音；唸完 [aɪ] 後舌頭直接往後捲，讓捲舌音一路持續到最後。
fire.tip_en: Slide [aɪ] from an open [a] toward [ɪ], then curl the tongue tip back into [r]. Common mistakes are skipping the curl so only [faɪ] is left, or inserting a "ya" sound after [aɪ] before finishing. The final e is silent; after [aɪ], curl the tongue back right away and keep the r-color going to the end.

examples.en: We sat by the fire and sang songs.
examples.zh: 我們坐在火堆旁唱歌。

examples.en: The firefighters practiced a fire drill at our school.
examples.zh: 消防員在我們學校進行消防演習。

first.tip_zh: ir 唸捲舌的 [ɝ]，和 bird、girl 的母音一樣：舌尖往後捲、嘴唇稍圓，整個母音都帶著捲舌。常見的錯誤是唸成沒有捲舌的 [ɛ]，聽起來像 fest，或和 fast 搞混。字尾 [st] 兩個子音都要發，不要把 [t] 吞掉，也不要多加母音。
first.tip_en: ir is the r-colored [ɝ], the same vowel as in bird and girl: curl the tongue tip back, round the lips slightly, and keep the r-color through the whole vowel. A common mistake is an uncurled [ɛ], which sounds like fest, or mixing it up with fast. Pronounce both consonants of the final [st]; don't swallow the [t] or add a vowel.

examples.en: I was the first one to get to school.
examples.zh: 我是第一個到學校的人。

examples.en: Wash your hands first, then eat.
examples.zh: 先洗手，再吃東西。

fish.tip_zh: i 是短的 [ɪ]，舌頭放鬆、嘴巴微開，不要拉長成 [i]。sh 兩個字母只發一個 [ʃ]：嘴唇往前嘟、只送氣不出聲，不是注音的ㄒ，也不要唸成扁扁的 [s]。最常見的錯誤是在 [ʃ] 後面多加一個母音，唸成兩拍；氣送完就停。
fish.tip_en: The i is a short [ɪ]: relax the tongue and open the mouth slightly; don't stretch it into [i]. The two letters sh make one sound, [ʃ]: push the lips forward and only blow, without voice. It is not Mandarin ㄒ, and not a flat [s]. The most common mistake is adding a vowel after [ʃ] to make two beats; when the air is out, stop.

examples.en: We saw many colorful fish at the aquarium.
examples.zh: 我們在水族館看到很多彩色的魚。

examples.en: My grandma cooks fish for dinner on Sundays.
examples.zh: 奶奶星期天晚餐會煮魚。

fisherman.tip_zh: 重音在第一音節 [fɪ]。中間的 [ʃɚ] 常被唸成 [s]，或用中文的「西」代替；英文 [ʃ] 要把嘴唇嘟起往前推，舌面靠近上顎但不碰到，送出氣流，然後馬上捲舌接 [ɚ]。最後的 [mæn] 是次重音，比第一音節輕，不要三個音節一樣重。
fisherman.tip_en: The stress is on the first syllable [fɪ]. The middle [ʃɚ] is often said with [s], or replaced by the Mandarin 「西」 (xi) sound; English [ʃ] needs the lips rounded and pushed forward, with the tongue close to the roof of the mouth but not touching it, pushing air out — then curl the tongue straight into [ɚ]. The final [mæn] has secondary stress and is lighter than the first syllable; don't give all three syllables equal weight.

examples.en: The fisherman caught a big fish this morning.
examples.zh: 那位漁夫今天早上抓到一條大魚。

examples.en: My uncle is a fisherman in Keelung.
examples.zh: 我叔叔是基隆的漁夫。

fisherman.variant_en: The last syllable is often reduced to [mən]: [ˈfɪʃɚmən].

five.tip_zh: 字尾 [v] 是有聲的：上排牙齒輕碰下唇，喉嚨要震動。常見的錯誤是唸成無聲的 [f]，或把 [v] 省掉只剩 [faɪ]；數數唸得快時更容易漏掉。開頭的 [f] 和結尾的 [v] 嘴形一樣，差別只在喉嚨震不震動，可以把手放在喉嚨上感覺。字尾 e 不發音。
five.tip_en: The final [v] is voiced: touch the upper teeth to the lower lip and make the throat buzz. Common mistakes are saying a voiceless [f], or dropping the [v] so only [faɪ] is left; it gets skipped even more when counting fast. The opening [f] and the final [v] use the same mouth shape and differ only in whether the throat vibrates; put a hand on your throat to feel it. The final e is silent.

examples.en: I have five color pencils in my bag.
examples.zh: 我書包裡有五枝色鉛筆。

examples.en: School starts in five minutes.
examples.zh: 再五分鐘就要上課了。

fix.tip_zh: x 一個字母代表 [ks] 兩個音：舌根頂一下發 [k]，接著送氣發 [s]。常見的錯誤是只唸出 [k] 或只剩 [s]，或在最後多加母音唸成兩拍。i 是短的 [ɪ]，舌頭放鬆，不要拉長成 [i]；整個字短短一拍就結束。
fix.tip_en: The single letter x stands for two sounds, [ks]: tap the back of the tongue for [k], then blow out [s]. Common mistakes are saying only [k] or only [s], or adding a vowel at the end to make two beats. The i is a short [ɪ] with a relaxed tongue; don't stretch it into [i]. The whole word is one short beat.

examples.en: Dad can fix my bike this weekend.
examples.zh: 爸爸這個週末可以修我的腳踏車。

examples.en: Can you help me fix this toy car?
examples.zh: 你可以幫我修這台玩具車嗎？

floor.tip_zh: oo 在這裡唸 [ɔ]，接著捲舌成 [r]，不是 food 的 [u]，也不是 book 的 [ʊ]。開頭 [fl] 兩個子音要連著發，[f] 和 [l] 中間不加母音：上排牙齒離開下唇時，舌尖已經抬到牙齦。最後舌頭往後捲成 [r]，不要只停在圓唇的 [ɔ]。
floor.tip_en: The oo here is [ɔ] followed by a curled [r]; it is not the [u] of food or the [ʊ] of book. Join the opening [fl] with no vowel between [f] and [l]: as the upper teeth leave the lower lip, the tongue tip is already up on the gum ridge. Finally curl the tongue back into [r]; don't stop at a round [ɔ].

examples.en: Please put your bag on the floor.
examples.zh: 請把你的書包放在地上。

examples.en: Our classroom is on the third floor.
examples.zh: 我們的教室在三樓。

flower.tip_zh: ow 在這裡唸 [aʊ]，嘴巴先張大再收圓，和 how、cow 一樣，不要照 flow 唸成 [o]。[aʊ] 之後舌頭要往後捲成 [r]，不要省略，否則聽起來只剩 [flaʊ]。開頭 [fl] 和 fly 的開頭一樣，[f] 和 [l] 中間不插入母音。練習時可以先說 how，再加上開頭的 [fl] 和結尾的捲舌。
flower.tip_en: The ow here is [aʊ]: open the mouth wide, then round it, as in how and cow; don't read it like flow with [o]. After [aʊ], curl the tongue back into [r]; don't drop it, or only [flaʊ] is left. The opening [fl] is the same as at the start of fly, with no vowel inserted between [f] and [l]. To practice, say how first, then add the opening [fl] and the final curl.

examples.en: She gave her mom a red flower.
examples.zh: 她送媽媽一朵紅花。

examples.en: This flower smells very sweet.
examples.zh: 這朵花聞起來很香。

flower.spelling_zh: ow 唸 [aʊ]，不是 flow 的 [o]。
flower.spelling_en: ow says [aʊ], not the [o] of flow.
flower.kk_flag: Taiwan dictionaries and most US references show two syllables, [ˈflaʊɚ]; the one-syllable [flaʊr] is a fast-speech form. Consider [ˈflaʊɚ] (sylls flaʊ·ɚ).

fly.tip_zh: 開頭 [fl] 是兩個子音連在一起，中間不能有母音，否則會唸成兩拍。這裡的 [l] 在母音前，是清楚的亮 L：舌尖輕碰上排牙齦後馬上放開。字尾 y 唸 [aɪ]，嘴巴從張大的 [a] 滑到 [ɪ]。也要注意 [l] 不要唸成 [r]，否則變成 fry。
fly.tip_en: The opening [fl] is two consonants together with no vowel between them; otherwise it becomes two beats. The [l] here comes before a vowel, so it is a clear, light L: touch the tongue tip to the upper gum ridge and release it right away. The final y is [aɪ], sliding from an open [a] to [ɪ]. Also keep [l] from turning into [r], or it becomes fry.

examples.en: Birds fly south in the winter.
examples.zh: 鳥兒冬天會飛到南方。

examples.en: Let's fly a kite at the beach.
examples.zh: 我們去海邊放風箏吧。

follow.tip_zh: 重音在第一音節 [fɑ]，o 在這裡唸張大嘴的 [ɑ]，不要唸成圓唇的 [o]。雙寫的 ll 只發一個 [l]，不要拆成兩個。字尾 ow 唸 [o]，嘴唇從圓到更圓、往 [ʊ] 的方向滑，不要唸成 how 的 [aʊ]。第二音節輕一點，兩拍不要一樣重。
follow.tip_en: Stress the first syllable [fɑ]; the o here is an open-mouthed [ɑ], not a round-lipped [o]. The double ll is a single [l]; don't split it in two. The final ow is [o], with the lips rounding further toward [ʊ]; don't say the [aʊ] of how. Make the second syllable lighter; the two beats aren't equal.

examples.en: Please follow me to the library.
examples.zh: 請跟我到圖書館。

examples.en: We must follow the rules in class.
examples.zh: 上課時我們必須遵守規則。

food.tip_zh: food 的 [u] 是長音，嘴唇要圓、往前嘟緊，比 good、foot 的 [ʊ] 更緊更長。字尾 [d] 常被省略，聽起來只剩 foo，或多加一個母音變成兩個音節。舌尖頂住上牙齦，喉嚨保持震動，輕輕放開就結束；如果把 [d] 換成 [l]，就成了 fool（傻瓜）。
food.tip_en: The [u] in food is long: round the lips and push them forward tightly — tighter and longer than the [ʊ] in good or foot. The final [d] is often dropped, leaving just "foo", or an extra vowel is added, making two syllables. Press the tongue tip on the gum ridge, keep the voice on, and release lightly to finish; if [d] turns into [l], it becomes fool.

examples.en: What's your favorite food?
examples.zh: 你最喜歡的食物是什麼？

examples.en: Let's buy some food for the picnic.
examples.zh: 我們去買一些野餐要吃的食物吧。

fool.tip_zh: oo 唸長的 [u]，嘴唇要用力嘟圓、往前推，不要唸成短而放鬆的 [ʊ]，否則會變成 full。字尾 [l] 要發出來：舌尖抬到上排牙齦，舌根往後壓。常見的錯誤是 [l] 沒發，只剩 [fu]；從 [u] 到 [l] 舌尖要確實碰到牙齦。
fool.tip_en: oo is a long [u]: round the lips firmly and push them forward; don't say the short, relaxed [ʊ], or it becomes full. You must sound the final [l]: lift the tongue tip to the upper gum ridge and press the back of the tongue back. A common mistake is skipping the [l] so only [fu] is left; going from [u] to [l], make sure the tongue tip really touches the gum ridge.

examples.en: The clown acted like a fool to make us laugh.
examples.zh: 小丑故意裝傻逗我們笑。

examples.en: Don't try to fool me with that story.
examples.zh: 別想用那個故事騙我。

foot.tip_zh: 雖然拼成 oo，foot 的母音是短而放鬆的 [ʊ]，不是 food 的長 [u]。嘴唇只要微微圓起、不要用力往前嘟，聲音短促。常見的錯誤是把它唸成拉長的 [u]，foot 和 food 就分不清。字尾 [t] 舌尖頂住牙齦停住即可，不要多加母音。
foot.tip_en: Even though it's spelled oo, the vowel in foot is a short, relaxed [ʊ], not the long [u] of food. Round the lips only slightly, without pushing them forward, and keep the sound short. A common mistake is stretching it into [u], so foot and food can't be told apart. For the final [t], press the tongue tip on the gum ridge and stop; don't add a vowel.

examples.en: My left foot hurts a little.
examples.zh: 我的左腳有點痛。

examples.en: We went to the park on foot.
examples.zh: 我們走路去公園。

foot.spelling_en: The oo here says a short [ʊ].

for.tip_zh: for 和 four 唸法相同，都是 [fɔr]：嘴巴張開、嘴唇稍圓發 [ɔ]，接著舌尖往後捲成 [r]。常見的錯誤是沒有捲舌，只剩圓唇的 [ɔ] 或 [o]。在句子裡 for 通常唸得又輕又快，母音會變弱（見下方），不需要每次都唸得很重。
for.tip_en: for and four sound the same, [fɔr]: open the mouth with slightly rounded lips for [ɔ], then curl the tongue tip back into [r]. A common mistake is leaving out the curl so only a round [ɔ] or [o] is left. Inside a sentence, for is usually light and quick and the vowel weakens (see below), so it doesn't need to be stressed every time.

examples.en: This gift is for you.
examples.zh: 這份禮物是給你的。

examples.en: We waited for the bus for ten minutes.
examples.zh: 我們等公車等了十分鐘。

for.variant_zh: 在句子裡常弱讀成 [fɚ]，例如 for you。
for.variant_en: In sentences it is often weakened to [fɚ], as in for you.

foreign.tip_zh: foreign 的第二音節是很輕的 [rən]，不是 rain 的 [en]；常見錯誤是看到 eign 就唸成「雷恩」，或把 g 也唸出來。重音在第一音節 [fɔ]，嘴唇微圓發 [ɔ]，再捲舌接到 [r]，後面的 [ən] 輕而短，舌尖頂住上牙齦收在 [n]。
foreign.tip_en: The second syllable of foreign is a very light [rən], not the [en] of rain; a common mistake is to see eign and say it like 「雷恩」 (lei-en, like rain), or to pronounce the g as well. Stress the first syllable [fɔ]: round the lips slightly for [ɔ], then curl the tongue into [r]; the [ən] after it is light and short, ending with the tongue tip on the gum ridge for [n].

examples.en: Do you speak any foreign languages?
examples.zh: 你會說任何外語嗎？

examples.en: We met a foreign student at the museum.
examples.zh: 我們在博物館遇到一位外國學生。

foreign.variant_zh: 也常唸成 [ˈfɑrən]，第一個母音嘴巴較開
foreign.variant_en: Also often [ˈfɑrən], with a more open first vowel.
foreign.spelling_zh: eign 的 g 不發音，結尾只唸 [ən]
foreign.spelling_en: The g in eign is silent; the ending is just [ən].

foreigner.tip_zh: foreigner 有兩個捲舌音：第二音節開頭的 [r] 和字尾的 [ɚ]。學生常把 eign 唸成 rain 的 [en]，重音也跟著跑到第二音節。重音只放在第一音節 [fɔ]，中間 [rə] 又輕又快；最後 [nɚ] 舌尖先碰上牙齦發 [n]，再把舌頭往後捲，不要唸成平平的「那」。
foreigner.tip_en: foreigner has two r-sounds: the [r] that opens the second syllable and the final [ɚ]. Students often say eign as the [en] of rain, and the stress moves to the second syllable along with it. Put the stress only on the first syllable [fɔ] and keep the middle [rə] light and quick; for the last [nɚ], touch the tongue tip to the gum ridge for [n], then curl the tongue back — don't say a flat 「那」 (na).

examples.en: A friendly foreigner asked us for directions.
examples.zh: 一位友善的外國人向我們問路。

examples.en: The foreigner at the night market loved the bubble tea.
examples.zh: 夜市裡的那位外國人很喜歡珍珠奶茶。

foreigner.variant_zh: 說快時中間的 [ə] 常省略：[ˈfɔrnɚ] 或 [ˈfɑrnɚ]
foreigner.variant_en: In fast speech the middle [ə] often drops: [ˈfɔrnɚ] or [ˈfɑrnɚ].
foreigner.spelling_zh: 跟 foreign 一樣，g 不發音
foreigner.spelling_en: As in foreign, the g is silent.

forget.tip_zh: 重音在第二音節 [gɛt]，第一音節 for- 只是很輕的 [fɚ]，不要唸成重重的 four。[g] 是有聲的，喉嚨要震動，不要唸成 [k]。[ɛ] 嘴巴半開、不滑動。字尾 [t] 舌尖頂住牙齦停住即可，不要多加母音。
forget.tip_en: Stress the second syllable [gɛt]; the first syllable for- is only a light [fɚ], not a heavy four. [g] is voiced, so the throat buzzes; don't say [k]. Keep [ɛ] half open with no glide. For the final [t], just press the tongue tip on the gum ridge and stop; don't add a vowel.

examples.en: Don't forget to bring your umbrella.
examples.zh: 別忘了帶雨傘。

examples.en: I always forget my friend's phone number.
examples.zh: 我老是忘記朋友的電話號碼。

forget.variant_zh: 也常唸成 [fɔrˈgɛt]，第一音節母音較清楚。
forget.variant_en: Also often [fɔrˈgɛt], with a clearer first vowel.

fork.tip_zh: [ɔ] 之後要先捲舌發 [r]，再用舌根頂住上顎發 [k]。常見的錯誤是把 [r] 省掉，變成 [fɔk]，聽起來接近 folk；或在 [k] 後面多加母音。練法：先說 for，舌頭保持捲起，再直接加上 [k] 收尾。字尾的 [k] 不必用力放氣，舌根頂住上顎就好。
fork.tip_en: After [ɔ], curl the tongue for [r] first, then press the back of the tongue against the roof of the mouth for [k]. Common mistakes are dropping the [r] so it becomes [fɔk], close to folk, or adding a vowel after [k]. Practice: say for first, keep the tongue curled, then add [k] directly to finish. The final [k] needs no strong burst of air; just press the back of the tongue up against the roof of the mouth.

examples.en: Can I have a fork, please?
examples.zh: 可以給我一支叉子嗎？

examples.en: I eat noodles with a fork, not chopsticks.
examples.zh: 我用叉子吃麵，不用筷子。

forty.tip_zh: 拼字要注意：four 變成 forty 時沒有 u，但發音一樣是捲舌的 [fɔr]。重音在第一音節，第二音節 [tɪ] 短而輕，結尾是短的 [ɪ]，不要拉長成 [tin]，否則像 fourteen。美國人說快時，[r] 後面的 [t] 常輕得像很快的 d。
forty.tip_en: Watch the spelling: four loses its u in forty, but the sound is still the curled [fɔr]. Stress the first syllable; the second syllable [tɪ] is short and light and ends in a short [ɪ]. Don't stretch it into [tin], or it sounds like fourteen. In fast American speech, the [t] after [r] is often light, like a quick d.

examples.en: There are forty kids in the gym.
examples.zh: 體育館裡有四十個小朋友。

examples.en: My dad is forty years old.
examples.zh: 我爸爸四十歲。

forty.spelling_zh: forty 沒有 u（不是 fourty）。

four.tip_zh: 拼字有 ou，但這裡不唸 our 的 [aʊ]，而是 [ɔr]：嘴巴張開、嘴唇稍微圓起發 [ɔ]，接著舌尖往後捲成 [r]。常見的錯誤是捲舌不夠，只剩接近「佛」的圓唇母音。four 和 for 唸法相同，要靠上下文分辨。
four.tip_en: It's spelled with ou, but it isn't the [aʊ] of our; it's [ɔr]: open the mouth with slightly rounded lips for [ɔ], then curl the tongue tip back into [r]. A common mistake is not curling enough, leaving only a round-lipped vowel. four and for sound the same; context tells them apart.

examples.en: A dog has four legs.
examples.zh: 狗有四條腿。

examples.en: We have four classes this morning.
examples.zh: 我們今天早上有四堂課。

fourteen.tip_zh: 重音在第二音節 [tin]，[i] 要拉長，最後用舌尖收清楚的 [n]。常見的錯誤是把重音放在 four，聽起來就像 forty。第一音節 [fɔr] 仍然要捲舌，但唸得比較輕。說 fourteen years old 時，teen 要清楚有力。和 forty 不同，這裡的 [t] 在重音音節開頭，說快時也要清楚送氣。
fourteen.tip_en: Stress the second syllable [tin]: stretch the [i] and finish with a clear tongue-tip [n]. A common mistake is stressing four, which makes it sound like forty. The first syllable [fɔr] still needs the curled r but is lighter. When saying fourteen years old, make the teen clear and strong. Unlike forty, the [t] here starts the stressed syllable, so it stays clear and puffed even in fast speech.

examples.en: My cousin is fourteen years old.
examples.zh: 我表哥十四歲。

examples.en: There are fourteen apples in the box.
examples.zh: 盒子裡有十四顆蘋果。

fox.tip_zh: o 在這裡唸 [ɑ]，嘴巴要張大、舌頭放低，嘴唇不要圓，不要唸成 [o] 或 [ɔ]。x 代表 [ks] 兩個音：舌根頂一下發 [k]，再送氣發 [s]，中間不加母音，也不要漏掉 [k] 只剩 [s]。可以先說 rocks 的結尾來練 [ks]。
fox.tip_en: The o here is [ɑ]: open the mouth wide with the tongue low and the lips unrounded; don't say [o] or [ɔ]. x stands for two sounds, [ks]: tap the back of the tongue for [k], then blow out [s], with no vowel between and without dropping the [k]. Practice the [ks] with the ending of rocks first.

examples.en: The fox has a long, bushy tail.
examples.zh: 狐狸有一條又長又蓬的尾巴。

examples.en: We read a story about a clever fox.
examples.zh: 我們讀了一個聰明狐狸的故事。

free.tip_zh: 開頭 [fr] 兩個子音要連在一起：上排牙齒碰下唇時，舌頭就已經往後捲好準備 [r]，中間不要插入母音唸成兩拍。ee 唸長的 [i]，嘴角往兩邊拉開、舌頭前面抬高，不要唸成短的 [ɪ]。[r] 也不能太弱，否則聽不出捲舌。
free.tip_en: Join the opening [fr]: as the upper teeth touch the lower lip, the tongue is already curled back ready for [r]; don't put a vowel in between to make two beats. ee is a long [i]: pull the mouth corners wide and raise the front of the tongue; don't say a short [ɪ]. The [r] can't be too weak either, or the curl won't be heard.

examples.en: Are you free this Saturday?
examples.zh: 你這個星期六有空嗎？

examples.en: The museum is free for children.
examples.zh: 博物館對兒童免費。

fresh.tip_zh: e 唸短的 [ɛ]，嘴巴半開、不滑動，不要唸成 [e]。開頭 [fr] 連著發，[r] 要捲舌，中間不加母音。字尾 [ʃ] 嘴唇往前嘟、只送氣不出聲，不要在最後多加母音。常見的錯誤是把 [ʃ] 唸成扁扁的 [s]，嘴唇沒有往前。
fresh.tip_en: e is a short [ɛ], half open with no glide; don't say [e]. Join the opening [fr] with a curled [r] and no vowel in between. For the final [ʃ], push the lips forward and only blow, without voice; don't add a vowel at the end. A common mistake is flattening [ʃ] into [s] without pushing the lips forward.

examples.en: These strawberries are very fresh.
examples.zh: 這些草莓很新鮮。

examples.en: Let's open the window for some fresh air.
examples.zh: 我們打開窗戶透透新鮮空氣吧。

friday.tip_zh: i 在這裡唸 [aɪ]，嘴巴從張大的 [a] 滑到 [ɪ]，不要唸成 free 的 [i]。重音在第一音節 [fraɪ]，第二音節 [dɪ] 輕而短，不要兩拍一樣重。開頭 [fr] 中間不加母音。星期名稱要大寫：Friday。[d] 是有聲的，舌尖輕碰牙齦就放開，不要唸成 [t]。
friday.tip_en: The i here is [aɪ], sliding from an open [a] to [ɪ]; don't say the [i] of free. Stress the first syllable [fraɪ]; the second syllable [dɪ] is light and short, so the two beats aren't equal. Put no vowel inside the opening [fr]. Days of the week are capitalized: Friday. [d] is voiced: tap the tongue tip on the gum ridge and let go; don't say [t].

examples.en: We have art class on Friday.
examples.zh: 我們星期五有美術課。

examples.en: Friday is my favorite day of the week.
examples.zh: 星期五是我一週中最喜歡的一天。

friday.variant_en: The second syllable is also often [de]: [ˈfraɪˌde].

friend.tip_zh: 拼字有 ie，但 friend 的母音是短的 [ɛ]，i 不發音，不要唸成 [i] 或 [aɪ]。字尾 [nd] 兩個子音都要有：舌尖頂住牙齦發 [n]，不移開直接放成 [d]。常見的錯誤是把 [d] 省掉，只剩 [frɛn]，或在最後多加母音。
friend.tip_en: It's spelled ie, but the vowel in friend is a short [ɛ]; the i is silent, so don't say [i] or [aɪ]. Both consonants of the final [nd] must be there: press the tongue tip on the gum ridge for [n], then release straight into [d] without moving it. Common mistakes are dropping the [d] so only [frɛn] is left, or adding a vowel at the end.

examples.en: Amy is my best friend.
examples.zh: 艾美是我最好的朋友。

examples.en: I made a new friend at school today.
examples.zh: 我今天在學校交了一個新朋友。

friend.spelling_en: ie says just [ɛ]; the i is silent.

friendly.tip_zh: 中間 [ndl] 三個子音連在一起：舌尖頂住上排牙齦發 [n]、[d]，舌尖不離開，讓氣流從舌頭兩側出來就變成 [l]。不要在 [d] 和 [l] 中間加母音，唸成三拍。重音在第一音節 [frɛnd]，ie 唸 [ɛ]，結尾是短的 [ɪ]。
friendly.tip_en: The middle [ndl] is three consonants together: press the tongue tip on the upper gum ridge for [n] and [d], keep it there, and let air flow out over the sides of the tongue to make [l]. Don't put a vowel between [d] and [l] to make three beats. Stress the first syllable [frɛnd]; ie is [ɛ], and the word ends in a short [ɪ].

examples.en: Our new neighbor is very friendly.
examples.zh: 我們的新鄰居很友善。

examples.en: The dog is friendly to everyone.
examples.zh: 這隻狗對每個人都很友善。

friendly.variant_en: In fast speech the [d] is often dropped: [ˈfrɛnlɪ].

fries.tip_zh: 字尾的 s 在這裡唸有聲的 [z]，喉嚨要震動，不要唸成無聲的 [s]。ie 唸 [aɪ]，嘴巴從張大的 [a] 滑向 [ɪ]，和 fry 的母音一樣。[aɪ] 唸完直接接 [z]，不要多加母音，也不要把 [z] 唸成注音ㄗ那樣先頓一下。
fries.tip_en: The final s here is a voiced [z], with the throat buzzing; don't say a voiceless [s]. ie is [aɪ], sliding from an open [a] toward [ɪ], the same vowel as in fry. Go straight from [aɪ] into [z] with no added vowel, and don't make the [z] start with a stop like Mandarin ㄗ.

examples.en: Can I have some fries with my burger?
examples.zh: 我的漢堡可以配一些薯條嗎？

examples.en: These fries are hot and crispy.
examples.zh: 這些薯條又熱又酥脆。

frog.tip_zh: o 在這裡唸張大嘴的 [ɑ]，嘴唇不要圓，不要唸成 [o]。字尾 [g] 是有聲的：舌根頂住上顎時喉嚨要震動，不要唸成無聲的 [k]，也不要在後面加母音。開頭 [fr] 中間不加母音，[r] 也不要唸成 [l]。
frog.tip_en: The o here is an open-mouthed [ɑ] with unrounded lips; don't say [o]. The final [g] is voiced: the throat buzzes as the back of the tongue presses the roof of the mouth; don't say a voiceless [k], and don't add a vowel after it. No vowel inside the opening [fr], and don't turn [r] into [l].

examples.en: A green frog jumped into the pond.
examples.zh: 一隻綠色的青蛙跳進池塘。

examples.en: The frog sat on a big leaf.
examples.zh: 青蛙坐在一片大葉子上。

frog.variant_en: [frɔg], with slightly rounded lips, is also common.

from.tip_zh: o 在這裡唸短而放鬆的 [ʌ]，像 up 的開頭，不要照拼字唸成 [ɑ] 或 [o]。字尾 [m] 雙唇要閉起來，不要唸成舌尖的 [n]。開頭 [fr] 中間不加母音。在句子裡 from 通常輕讀，母音更弱。from 和 front 的母音相同，可以兩個字一起練。
from.tip_en: The o here is a short, relaxed [ʌ], like the start of up; don't read it from the spelling as [ɑ] or [o]. Close the lips for the final [m]; don't say a tongue-tip [n]. No vowel inside the opening [fr]. In sentences, from is usually unstressed and its vowel weaker still. from and front share the same vowel, so practice the two words together.

examples.en: My new classmate is from Japan.
examples.zh: 我的新同學來自日本。

examples.en: We walked home from school together.
examples.zh: 我們一起從學校走路回家。

from.variant_en: In sentences it is often weakened to [frəm].

front.tip_zh: o 在這裡唸 [ʌ]，嘴巴放鬆微開，和 fun 的母音一樣，不要唸成 [ɑ] 或 [o]。字尾 [nt]：舌尖頂住上排牙齦發 [n]，不移開直接收成 [t]。常見的錯誤是把 [t] 省掉，或多加母音。[fr] 中間也不要插入母音。
front.tip_en: The o here is [ʌ], mouth relaxed and slightly open, the same vowel as in fun; don't say [ɑ] or [o]. For the final [nt], press the tongue tip on the upper gum ridge for [n], then stop it straight into [t] without moving. Common mistakes are dropping the [t] or adding a vowel. Don't insert a vowel inside [fr] either.

examples.en: Let's meet in front of the school.
examples.zh: 我們在學校前面見。

examples.en: I sit in the front of the classroom.
examples.zh: 我坐在教室的前面。

fruit.tip_zh: fruit 只有一個音節 [frut]，ui 只唸一個長的 [u]，i 不發音。常見的錯誤是照拼字唸成兩拍，好像 [fru] 再加 [ɪt]。[u] 嘴唇要嘟圓、往前推；字尾 [t] 舌尖頂住牙齦停住，不要多加母音。開頭 [fr] 中間也不要加母音，捲舌要提早準備好。
fruit.tip_en: fruit is one syllable, [frut]: ui is just one long [u], and the i is silent. A common mistake is reading the spelling as two beats, like [fru] plus [ɪt]. Round the lips and push them forward for [u]; for the final [t], press the tongue tip on the gum ridge and stop without adding a vowel. Don't put a vowel inside the opening [fr] either; get the tongue curled early.

examples.en: I eat fruit every morning.
examples.zh: 我每天早上吃水果。

examples.en: Bananas are my favorite fruit.
examples.zh: 香蕉是我最喜歡的水果。

fruit.spelling_en: ui says just [u]; the i is silent.

fry.tip_zh: fry 的開頭是 [fr]，舌尖要往後捲、不碰任何地方；fly 的 [fl] 則是舌尖碰上排牙齦。這兩個字只差在 [r] 和 [l]，常見的錯誤是把 [r] 唸成 [l]，fry 就變成 fly。y 唸 [aɪ]，嘴巴從張大的 [a] 滑向 [ɪ]。練習時把 fry、fly 輪流唸，注意舌尖的位置。
fry.tip_en: fry starts with [fr]: the tongue tip curls back and touches nothing, while the [fl] in fly has the tongue tip touching the upper gum ridge. These two words differ only in [r] and [l]; a common mistake is turning [r] into [l], which changes fry into fly. y is [aɪ], sliding from an open [a] toward [ɪ]. Practice by saying fry and fly in turn, paying attention to where the tongue tip is.

examples.en: Mom will fry some eggs for breakfast.
examples.zh: 媽媽早餐會煎幾顆蛋。

examples.en: We fry the dumplings until they are golden.
examples.zh: 我們把餃子煎到金黃色。

full.tip_zh: full 的 [ʊ] 短而放鬆，嘴唇只微微圓起；如果嘟緊拉長成 [u]，就變成 fool（傻瓜）。也別把嘴角拉開唸成 [ɪ]，那會變成 fill。字尾暗 L 常被吞掉只剩「福」，收尾時舌尖要碰到上牙齦，同時舌根稍微往後抬，聲音才會厚實。
full.tip_en: The [ʊ] in full is short and relaxed, with the lips only slightly rounded; if you tighten and stretch it into [u], it becomes fool. Don't spread the lips into [ɪ] either — that turns it into fill. The final dark L is often swallowed, leaving just 「福」 (fu); at the end, touch the tongue tip to the gum ridge while raising the back of the tongue slightly, so the sound comes out thick and full.

examples.en: My backpack is full of books.
examples.zh: 我的背包裝滿了書。

examples.en: I'm full, thank you!
examples.zh: 我吃飽了，謝謝！

fun.tip_zh: u 唸 [ʌ]，嘴巴放鬆微開、舌頭平放，聲音短，不要唸成圓唇的 [u] 或 [o]。字尾是舌尖的 [n]：舌尖頂住上排牙齦，不要讓舌根抬起變成 [ŋ]，否則字尾聽起來像注音ㄥ的鼻音。可以拿 sun、run 一起練，它們的結尾都一樣。
fun.tip_en: u is [ʌ]: relax the mouth slightly open, keep the tongue flat, and keep it short; don't say a round [u] or [o]. The end is tongue-tip [n]: press the tip on the upper gum ridge; don't raise the back of the tongue into [ŋ], or the ending sounds like the Mandarin ㄥ nasal. Practice it together with sun and run, which end the same way.

examples.en: We had so much fun at the zoo.
examples.zh: 我們在動物園玩得好開心。

examples.en: Learning English can be fun.
examples.zh: 學英文可以很有趣。

funny.tip_zh: 重音在第一音節 [fʌ]，u 唸放鬆的 [ʌ]。雖然拼成 nn，只發一個 [n]，不要把兩個 n 分開唸。結尾 y 是短的 [ɪ]，輕輕收掉即可，不要拉長或加重。常見的錯誤是兩個音節唸得一樣重，或第一音節唸成圓唇的 [o]。
funny.tip_en: Stress the first syllable [fʌ]; u is a relaxed [ʌ]. Although it's spelled nn, only one [n] is pronounced; don't split the two n's. The final y is a short [ɪ]; just let it go lightly without stretching or stressing it. Common mistakes are giving both syllables equal weight or saying a round [o] in the first.

examples.en: My uncle tells funny jokes.
examples.zh: 我叔叔會講好笑的笑話。

examples.en: The monkey made a funny face.
examples.zh: 那隻猴子做了一個好笑的鬼臉。

future.tip_zh: 第一音節 [fju] 有 [j] 的滑音，像 few 一樣，不要唸成 [fu]。t 在這裡唸 [tʃ]，嘴唇往前嘟，不是單純的 [t]。結尾 -ure 唸捲舌的 [ɚ]，舌頭往後捲，不要唸成 [ʊr] 或平平的 [ə]。重音在第一音節，第二音節 [tʃɚ] 輕輕帶過，不要兩拍一樣重。
future.tip_en: The first syllable [fju] has a [j] glide, like few; don't say [fu]. The t here is [tʃ], with the lips pushed forward, not a plain [t]. The final -ure is an r-colored [ɚ]: curl the tongue back; don't say [ʊr] or a flat [ə]. Stress the first syllable and pass lightly over the second syllable [tʃɚ]; the two beats aren't equal.

examples.en: I want to be a doctor in the future.
examples.zh: 我未來想當醫生。

examples.en: Let's plant trees for our future.
examples.zh: 我們為了未來來種樹吧。

game.tip_zh: a 唸 [e]，要從 [e] 滑向 [ɪ]，唸得飽滿，不要縮成短的 [ɛ]。字尾 [m] 雙唇要閉起來，不要唸成舌尖的 [n]；最後的 e 不發音，閉唇後不要再加母音。開頭的 [g] 喉嚨要震動，不要唸成送氣的 [k]，否則聽起來像 came。
game.tip_en: a is [e], gliding fully from [e] toward [ɪ]; don't shrink it to a short [ɛ]. Close the lips for the final [m]; don't say a tongue-tip [n]. The final e is silent, so add no vowel after the lips close. The opening [g] is voiced; don't say an aspirated [k], or it sounds like came.

examples.en: Let's play a card game after lunch.
examples.zh: 午餐後我們來玩紙牌遊戲吧。

examples.en: Our team won the basketball game.
examples.zh: 我們隊贏了籃球比賽。

garbage.tip_zh: 字尾 -age 唸短的 [ɪdʒ]，不要照 age 唸成 [edʒ]。[dʒ] 嘴唇往前嘟，收尾時不要多加母音。重音在第一音節 [gɑr]：嘴巴張大發 [ɑ]，捲舌發 [r]，再閉上雙唇發 [b]，不要把 [r] 省掉。第二音節 [bɪdʒ] 輕而短，兩拍不要一樣重。
garbage.tip_en: The final -age is a short [ɪdʒ]; don't read it like age, [edʒ]. Push the lips forward for [dʒ], and don't add a vowel at the end. Stress the first syllable [gɑr]: open wide for [ɑ], curl the tongue for [r], then close the lips for [b]; don't drop the [r]. The second syllable [bɪdʒ] is light and short; the two beats aren't equal.

examples.en: Please take out the garbage after dinner.
examples.zh: 晚餐後請把垃圾拿出去倒。

examples.en: The garbage truck plays music in Taiwan.
examples.zh: 台灣的垃圾車會播放音樂。

garden.tip_zh: 重音在第一音節 [gɑr]，嘴巴張大後要捲舌。第二音節 [dṇ] 沒有完整的母音：舌尖頂住牙齦發 [d] 後不放開，讓氣流直接從鼻子出來變成 [ṇ]。常見的錯誤是照拼字唸成清楚的 [dɛn]，或把 [r] 省掉。
garden.tip_en: Stress the first syllable [gɑr]: open the mouth wide and then curl the tongue. The second syllable [dṇ] has no full vowel: press the tongue tip on the gum ridge for [d], keep it there, and let the air go straight out through the nose for [ṇ]. Common mistakes are reading the spelling as a clear [dɛn], or dropping the [r].

examples.en: Grandma grows tomatoes in her garden.
examples.zh: 奶奶在她的花園裡種番茄。

examples.en: We had a picnic in the garden.
examples.zh: 我們在花園裡野餐。

gas.tip_zh: [æ] 下巴要往下拉、嘴角往兩邊開，不要唸成 [ɛ]，否則聽起來像 guess [gɛs]。字尾 [s] 是無聲的，只送氣，不要唸成 [z]，也不要多加母音。開頭 [g] 喉嚨震動，不要送氣唸成 [k]。可以把 gas、guess 輪流唸，感覺下巴高低的差別。
gas.tip_en: For [æ], drop the jaw and spread the mouth corners; don't say [ɛ], or it sounds like guess [gɛs]. The final [s] is voiceless, just air; don't say [z] or add a vowel. The opening [g] is voiced; don't aspirate it into [k]. Say gas and guess in turn and feel the difference in how low the jaw drops.

examples.en: Mom cooks with gas in the kitchen.
examples.zh: 媽媽在廚房用瓦斯煮飯。

examples.en: Turn off the gas after cooking.
examples.zh: 煮完飯要關掉瓦斯。

gate.tip_zh: a 唸 [e]，要從 [e] 滑向 [ɪ]。如果縮成短的 [ɛ]，gate 就會變成 get。字尾 [t] 舌尖頂住上排牙齦停住即可；最後的 e 不發音，不要在 [t] 後面多唸一個母音。說 school gate 時，[t] 常輕輕停住、不放氣。可以把 gate、get 輪流唸，聽出 [e] 和 [ɛ] 的差別。
gate.tip_en: a is [e], gliding from [e] toward [ɪ]. If you shrink it to a short [ɛ], gate turns into get. For the final [t], just press the tongue tip on the upper gum ridge and stop; the final e is silent, so don't say a vowel after [t]. In school gate, the [t] is often held without releasing air. Say gate and get in turn to hear the difference between [e] and [ɛ].

examples.en: I'll wait for you at the school gate.
examples.zh: 我會在校門口等你。

examples.en: Please close the gate behind you.
examples.zh: 進來後請把門關上。

get.tip_zh: e 唸短的 [ɛ]，嘴巴半開、不滑動，不要唸成 [e]，否則會變成 gate。字尾 [t] 常不放氣，舌尖頂住牙齦停住即可；在 get up 這種接母音的情況，美國人常把 [t] 彈成很快的 d。開頭 [g] 喉嚨要震動，不要唸成 [k]。
get.tip_en: e is a short [ɛ], mouth half open with no glide; don't say [e], or it becomes gate. The final [t] is often unreleased: just press the tongue tip on the gum ridge and stop. Before a vowel, as in get up, Americans often tap the [t] like a quick d. The opening [g] is voiced; don't say [k].

examples.en: What time do you get up?
examples.zh: 你幾點起床？

examples.en: I get good grades in English.
examples.zh: 我英文成績很好。

ghost.tip_zh: gh 在字首只唸 [g]，h 不發音。o 唸 [o]，嘴唇從圓到更圓、往 [ʊ] 滑，不要唸成張大嘴的 [ɑ] 或 [ɔ]。字尾 [st] 兩個子音都要發：送氣發 [s] 後舌尖頂住牙齦發 [t]。不要把 [t] 吞掉，也不要多加母音唸成「狗斯特」。
ghost.tip_en: At the start, gh is just [g]; the h is silent. o is [o], with the lips rounding further toward [ʊ]; don't say an open [ɑ] or [ɔ]. Pronounce both consonants of the final [st]: blow out [s], then press the tongue tip on the gum ridge for [t]. Don't swallow the [t], and don't add vowels to make extra beats.

examples.en: My little brother dressed up as a ghost.
examples.zh: 我弟弟打扮成一個鬼。

examples.en: We read a funny ghost story at camp.
examples.zh: 我們在營隊讀了一個好笑的鬼故事。

ghost.spelling_en: The h is silent; gh says just [g].

giant.tip_zh: g 在這裡唸 [dʒ]，嘴唇往前嘟，和 jump 的開頭一樣，不是 [g]。重音在第一音節 [dʒaɪ]，第二音節 [ənt] 只有很輕的 [ə]，不要唸成清楚的 [æ] 或 [ɛ]。字尾 [nt]：舌尖頂住牙齦發 [n]，再收成 [t]，不要漏掉 [t]。也不要在字尾多加母音，整個字只有兩拍。
giant.tip_en: The g here is [dʒ], with the lips pushed forward, like the start of jump, not [g]. Stress the first syllable [dʒaɪ]; the second syllable [ənt] has only a light [ə]; don't make it a clear [æ] or [ɛ]. For the final [nt], press the tongue tip on the gum ridge for [n], then stop it into [t]; don't drop the [t]. Don't add a vowel at the end either; the whole word has just two beats.

examples.en: We saw a giant panda at the zoo.
examples.zh: 我們在動物園看到一隻大貓熊。

examples.en: The giant in the story was very kind.
examples.zh: 故事裡的巨人非常善良。

gift.tip_zh: g 在這裡唸硬的 [g]，不是 giant 的 [dʒ]。i 是短的 [ɪ]，不要拉長成 [i]。字尾 [ft] 兩個子音連著：上排牙齒碰下唇送氣發 [f]，接著舌尖頂住牙齦收成 [t]，中間不加母音，也不要漏掉 [t]。字尾 [ft] 和 left、lift 的結尾一樣，可以一起練。
gift.tip_en: The g here is a hard [g], not the [dʒ] of giant. i is a short [ɪ]; don't stretch it into [i]. Join the final [ft]: blow out [f] with the upper teeth on the lower lip, then stop with the tongue tip on the gum ridge for [t], with no vowel in between and without dropping the [t]. The final [ft] is the same as the ending of left and lift, so practice them together.

examples.en: I made a birthday gift for my mom.
examples.zh: 我做了一份生日禮物給媽媽。

examples.en: Thank you for the lovely gift.
examples.zh: 謝謝你送的可愛禮物。

girl.tip_zh: girl 只有一個音節，但 [ɝ] 和 [l] 緊緊連在一起。常見錯誤是捲舌後把 l 吞掉，或在 [ɝ] 和 [l] 之間多加一個母音，變成兩個音節。先把舌頭往後捲，發 her、bird 裡的 [ɝ]，保持捲舌，再把舌尖往上抬碰上牙齦收在 [l]，中間不停頓。
girl.tip_en: girl has only one syllable, but [ɝ] and [l] are packed tightly together. Common mistakes are dropping the l after the curled vowel, or adding an extra vowel between [ɝ] and [l], which makes two syllables. First curl the tongue back for the [ɝ] in her and bird, hold the curl, then lift the tongue tip to the gum ridge to finish on [l], with no pause in between.

examples.en: The girl next to me likes drawing.
examples.zh: 坐我旁邊的女孩喜歡畫畫。

examples.en: That girl is my best friend.
examples.zh: 那個女孩是我最好的朋友。

give.tip_zh: give 的 [ɪ] 要短，不要拉成 [i]。字尾 [v] 是有聲音：上排牙齒輕碰下唇，喉嚨要震動。常見錯誤是唸成無聲的 [f]，聽起來像 gif，或在後面多加母音變成「給夫」。把手放在喉嚨上，確認 [v] 有震動，然後直接停住，不加尾音。
give.tip_en: The [ɪ] in give is short — don't stretch it into [i]. The final [v] is voiced: the upper teeth lightly touch the lower lip and the throat vibrates. A common mistake is saying a voiceless [f], so it sounds like gif, or adding a vowel at the end, like 「給夫」 (gei-fu). Put your hand on your throat to check that [v] vibrates, then stop right there with no extra sound.

examples.en: Can you give me a pencil, please?
examples.zh: 可以給我一支鉛筆嗎？

examples.en: I want to give my mom a card.
examples.zh: 我想送媽媽一張卡片。

give.spelling_zh: 字尾 e 不發音，i 唸短的 [ɪ]，不是 five 的 [aɪ]
give.spelling_en: The final e is silent, and i is a short [ɪ], not the [aɪ] of five.

glad.tip_zh: 開頭 [gl] 兩個子音連著唸：舌根頂住上顎發 [g] 時，舌尖已經抬到上排牙齦準備 [l]，中間不加母音。[æ] 嘴巴要張大，不要唸成 [ɛ]。字尾 [d] 有聲，喉嚨要震動，不要唸成無聲的 [t]，也不要多加母音。
glad.tip_en: Join the opening [gl]: while the back of the tongue presses the roof of the mouth for [g], the tongue tip is already up on the upper gum ridge ready for [l], with no vowel in between. Open the mouth wide for [æ]; don't say [ɛ]. The final [d] is voiced, with the throat buzzing; don't say a voiceless [t] or add a vowel.

examples.en: I'm glad you came to my party.
examples.zh: 我很高興你來參加我的派對。

examples.en: We were glad to see the sun again.
examples.zh: 再次看到太陽我們很高興。

glass.tip_zh: glass 和 grass 只差在第二個音：[l] 是舌尖碰上排牙齦，[r] 是舌尖往後捲、不碰任何地方，常見的錯誤是把兩個字唸成一樣。[æ] 下巴往下拉、嘴角往兩邊開；雙寫的 ss 只唸一個無聲的 [s]，不要唸成 [z]。
glass.tip_en: glass and grass differ only in the second sound: for [l] the tongue tip touches the upper gum ridge; for [r] it curls back and touches nothing. A common mistake is saying the two words the same. For [æ], drop the jaw and spread the mouth corners; the double ss is a single voiceless [s], not [z].

examples.en: Can I have a glass of water?
examples.zh: 可以給我一杯水嗎？

examples.en: The window is made of glass.
examples.zh: 這扇窗戶是玻璃做的。

glasses.tip_zh: 開頭 [gl] 是兩個子音連在一起，不要在 g 和 l 之間加母音唸成「格拉」。[æ] 要把嘴巴張大、嘴角往兩旁拉，像 cat 的母音，不是中文的「啊」。字尾 [əz] 的 [z] 是有聲音，喉嚨要震動，學生常唸成無聲的 [s]；想像蜜蜂嗡嗡叫，讓聲音持續震動。
glasses.tip_en: The opening [gl] is two consonants together — don't put a vowel between g and l, as in 「格拉」 (ge-la). For [æ], open the mouth wide and pull the corners back, like the vowel in cat, not Mandarin 「啊」 (a). The [z] in the final [əz] is voiced and the throat must vibrate; students often say a voiceless [s] — imagine a buzzing bee and keep the sound vibrating.

examples.en: My dad wears glasses when he reads.
examples.zh: 我爸爸看書時會戴眼鏡。

examples.en: I can't find my glasses anywhere!
examples.zh: 我到處都找不到我的眼鏡！

glove.tip_zh: glove 有三個地方容易錯：開頭 [gl] 兩個子音要連在一起，不要在中間多塞母音唸成「葛拉」；母音是短的 [ʌ]，跟 love 押韻，不是 go 的 [o]；字尾 [v] 要上齒輕咬下唇、喉嚨震動，不要換成 [f] 或 [b]，也不要在後面多加一個母音。
glove.tip_en: glove has three trouble spots: the opening [gl] must be joined, with no vowel squeezed in between (not "ge-la"); the vowel is short [ʌ], rhyming with love, not the [o] of go; the final [v] needs the upper teeth lightly on the lower lip with the throat buzzing — don't swap it for [f] or [b], and don't add a vowel after it.

examples.en: I lost my left glove at the park.
examples.zh: 我在公園弄丟了左手的手套。

examples.en: Put a glove on each hand before you go out.
examples.zh: 出門前每隻手都要戴上手套。

glove.spelling_zh: o 唸 [ʌ]，像 love，不像 stove 的 [o]。
glove.spelling_en: The o says [ʌ] as in love, not [o] as in stove.

glue.tip_zh: glue 的開頭是 [gl]：舌根頂住軟顎發 [g] 的同時，舌尖已經貼在上排牙齦準備發 [l]，一口氣滑過去，不要唸成兩拍的「咕嚕」。後面的 [u] 嘴唇要嘟圓、拉長。它跟 blue 只差第一個音：[g] 從嘴巴後面出來，[b] 是雙唇合起來再打開。
glue.tip_en: glue starts with [gl]: while the back of the tongue presses the soft palate for [g], the tongue tip is already on the ridge behind the upper teeth ready for [l] — glide through in one go, not a two-beat "gu-lu". The [u] after it needs rounded, pushed-out lips held long. It differs from blue only in the first sound: [g] comes from the back of the mouth, [b] from the lips closing and opening.

examples.en: Can I borrow your glue for my art project?
examples.zh: 我可以借你的膠水做美勞作業嗎？

examples.en: Use a little glue to stick the paper stars on.
examples.zh: 用一點膠水把紙星星黏上去。

go.tip_zh: 美式英語 go 的 [o] 其實會滑動：嘴唇從半圓開始，越唸越收圓，像要接著發 [ʊ]。台灣學生常唸得又短又平，嘴型不動，聽起來不夠道地。喊 Let's go! 時要把 [o] 唸滿、拉長。加了 -es 的 goes 唸 [goz]，字尾是有聲的 [z]，不是 [s]。
go.tip_en: In American English the [o] of go actually glides: the lips start half-round and round more as you go, as if heading to [ʊ]. Taiwanese learners often make it short and flat with a still mouth, which sounds off. When you shout Let's go!, give the [o] its full length. goes is [goz] — the ending is a voiced [z], not [s].

examples.en: Let's go to the library after lunch.
examples.zh: 午餐後我們去圖書館吧。

examples.en: I go to school by bus every day.
examples.zh: 我每天搭公車上學。

goat.tip_zh: goat 和 go 只差字尾的 [t]。台灣學生常把 [t] 省掉，聽起來就變成 go，或是在後面多加一個母音唸成「勾特」。[o] 唸完後，舌尖頂住上排牙齦停住，輕輕放氣或不放氣都可以，但一定要有「卡住」的感覺。也要跟 gate [get] 分清楚：goat 的嘴唇是圓的。
goat.tip_en: goat differs from go only by the final [t]. Taiwanese learners often drop the [t], so it sounds like go, or add a vowel after it ("gou-te"). After the [o], press the tongue tip on the ridge behind the upper teeth and stop — a light release or none is fine, but there must be a clear stop. Also keep it apart from gate [get]: goat has rounded lips.

examples.en: The goat on the farm likes to eat grass.
examples.zh: 農場上的山羊喜歡吃草。

examples.en: A baby goat jumped onto the big rock.
examples.zh: 一隻小山羊跳上了大石頭。

god.tip_zh: god 的母音是 [ɑ]：嘴巴張大、下巴往下掉，像看醫生時說「啊」，不要把嘴唇嘟圓唸成 [o] 或 [ɔ]。它和 good [gʊd] 只差母音，good 的嘴巴幾乎不張開，兩個字常被學生唸混。字尾 [d] 要讓喉嚨震動；如果唸成無聲的 [t]，就變成 got 了。
god.tip_en: The vowel in god is [ɑ]: open the mouth wide and drop the jaw, like saying "ah" at the doctor — don't round the lips into [o] or [ɔ]. It differs from good [gʊd] only in the vowel; good barely opens the mouth, and learners often mix the two. The final [d] must buzz in the throat; a voiceless [t] turns it into got.

examples.en: In the old story, the god of the sea was very strong.
examples.zh: 在古老的故事裡，海神非常強壯。

examples.en: We read a Greek myth about the god of the sun.
examples.zh: 我們讀了一則關於太陽神的希臘神話。

good.tip_zh: good 的 [ʊ] 是短而放鬆的音，嘴唇只微微圓起，不要像 food 的 [u] 那樣嘟起來拉長；台灣學生常唸成拉長的 goo，再補一點 [d]。字尾 [d] 舌尖要碰上排牙齦。說 Good morning 時 [d] 可以只碰不放氣，但不能完全消失。它跟 could、should 押韻。
good.tip_en: The [ʊ] in good is short and relaxed, with only slightly rounded lips — don't push the lips out and stretch it like the [u] in food; Taiwanese learners often say a long "goo" plus a bit of [d]. For the final [d], the tongue tip touches the ridge behind the upper teeth. In Good morning the [d] can be touched without a release, but it can't vanish. It rhymes with could and should.

examples.en: You did a good job on your test.
examples.zh: 你這次考試考得很好。

examples.en: This apple pie smells really good.
examples.zh: 這個蘋果派聞起來好香。

goose.tip_zh: goose 雖然拼成 -se，字尾卻是無聲的 [s]，像蛇的嘶嘶聲，不是 choose 的 [z]。中間的 [u] 要嘟嘴、拉長，嘴型太鬆就會變成 guess [gɛs] 或 gas [gæs]。另外複數是 geese [gis]，母音換成 [i]，不是在字尾加 s。
goose.tip_en: Although goose is spelled -se, it ends in a voiceless [s], like a hissing snake, not the [z] of choose. The [u] in the middle needs pushed-out lips held long; with a loose mouth it turns into guess [gɛs] or gas [gæs]. Also, the plural is geese [gis] — the vowel changes to [i] instead of adding s.

examples.en: A white goose is swimming in the pond.
examples.zh: 一隻白色的鵝在池塘裡游泳。

examples.en: The goose followed the farmer across the yard.
examples.zh: 那隻鵝跟著農夫走過院子。

grade.tip_zh: grade 和 great 只差最後一個音：grade 是有聲的 [d]，great 是無聲的 [t]。台灣學生常把字尾吞掉，兩個字就分不出來。唸 [d] 時，前面的 [e] 可以稍微拉長，再讓舌尖碰上排牙齦、喉嚨保持震動。開頭 [gr] 之間不要多加母音唸成「格雷」。
grade.tip_en: grade and great differ only in the last sound: grade ends in voiced [d], great in voiceless [t]. Taiwanese learners often swallow the ending, and the two words become the same. For [d], let the [e] before it run a little longer, then touch the tongue tip to the ridge behind the upper teeth with the throat still buzzing. Don't add a vowel inside the opening [gr] ("ge-lei").

examples.en: My brother is in fifth grade this year.
examples.zh: 我弟弟今年五年級。

examples.en: She got a good grade on her English test.
examples.zh: 她英文考試拿到好成績。

gram.tip_zh: gram 的 [æ] 要嘴角往兩旁拉開、下巴放低，介於 [ɛ] 和 [ɑ] 之間，不要唸成偏 [ɑ] 的「格蘭」。字尾 [m] 雙唇一定要閉起來，台灣學生常唸成 [n] 或嘴巴沒合上。開頭 [gr] 舌頭往後捲，中間不加母音，跟 grass 的開頭一樣。
gram.tip_en: The [æ] in gram needs the mouth corners pulled wide and the jaw lowered — between [ɛ] and [ɑ] — not an [ɑ]-like "ge-lan". For the final [m] the lips must close; Taiwanese learners often say [n] or leave the lips open. The opening [gr] curls the tongue back with no vowel in between, the same start as grass.

examples.en: A paper clip weighs about one gram.
examples.zh: 一個迴紋針大約重一公克。

examples.en: Add one gram of salt to the soup.
examples.zh: 在湯裡加一公克的鹽。

grandfather.tip_zh: grandfather 的重點在第三音節開頭的 [ð]：[fɑ] 後面不是 [d] 或 [z]，要把舌尖輕輕放在上下排牙齒之間，喉嚨震動往外送氣。開頭 [gr] 之間不要加母音，[æ] 嘴巴張大。重音在 grand，father 部分稍輕，最後的 [ɚ] 捲舌收尾。
grandfather.tip_en: The key to grandfather is the [ð] that starts the third syllable: what follows [fɑ] is not [d] or [z] — rest the tongue tip lightly between the upper and lower teeth and push air out with the throat vibrating. Don't put a vowel between [g] and [r] at the start, and open the mouth wide for [æ]. The stress is on grand; the father part is a little lighter, ending with a curled [ɚ].

examples.en: My grandfather likes to go fishing on Sundays.
examples.zh: 我爺爺星期天喜歡去釣魚。

examples.en: Grandfather told us a funny story.
examples.zh: 爺爺跟我們講了一個好笑的故事。

grandfather.variant_zh: 口語中 d 常省略：[ˈgrænˌfɑðɚ]
grandfather.variant_en: In everyday speech the d is often dropped: [ˈgrænˌfɑðɚ].

grandmother.tip_zh: mother 部分的 o 唸 [ʌ]，像 cup 的母音，嘴巴輕鬆半開，不要照拼字唸成 [o]。接著的 [ð] 舌尖放在牙齒之間並帶震動，不能換成 [z] 或 [d]。前面 grand 的 [nd] 碰到 [m] 時，d 幾乎不爆開，舌尖一碰到牙齦就閉上嘴唇發 [m]。
grandmother.tip_en: The o in the mother part is [ʌ], like the vowel in cup — mouth relaxed and half open; don't follow the spelling and say [o]. The [ð] after it has the tongue tip between the teeth, with voicing; it can't become [z] or [d]. Where the [nd] of grand meets [m], the d is barely released: the tongue tip just touches the gum ridge and the lips close for [m].

examples.en: My grandmother makes dumplings every New Year.
examples.zh: 我奶奶每年過年都會包水餃。

examples.en: We visit my grandmother every weekend.
examples.zh: 我們每個週末都去看奶奶。

grandmother.spelling_zh: mother 的 o 唸 [ʌ]，不唸 [o]
grandmother.spelling_en: The o in mother is [ʌ], not [o].

grape.tip_zh: grape 字尾的 [p] 是雙唇合起來再輕輕放氣，台灣學生常把它省略，聽起來像 gray，或多加母音變成三拍。母音 [e] 要從 [e] 滑向 [ɪ]，嘴角往兩邊拉，不要唸成 group [grup] 的圓唇 [u]。說複數 grapes 時，[p] 和 [s] 要緊緊接在一起。
grape.tip_en: The final [p] of grape is the lips closing and then releasing a little air; Taiwanese learners often drop it, so it sounds like gray, or add a vowel and make it three beats. The [e] glides from [e] toward [ɪ] with the mouth corners pulled wide — not the rounded [u] of group [grup]. In the plural grapes, [p] and [s] must be tightly joined.

examples.en: This grape is small but very sweet.
examples.zh: 這顆葡萄很小，但是非常甜。

examples.en: Mom put a grape in my lunch box.
examples.zh: 媽媽在我的便當盒裡放了一顆葡萄。

grass.tip_zh: grass 和 glass 只差第二個音：grass 的 [r] 舌尖往後捲、不碰任何地方；glass 的 [l] 舌尖要貼住上排牙齦。台灣學生常把這兩個字唸成同一個。母音是大嘴的 [æ]，嘴角往兩旁拉開，不是 [ɛ]。字尾 [s] 要清楚地嘶出來，不要在後面多加母音。
grass.tip_en: grass and glass differ only in the second sound: for [r] in grass the tongue tip curls back and touches nothing; for [l] in glass the tip presses the ridge behind the upper teeth. Taiwanese learners often say both the same way. The vowel is the wide-mouth [æ], corners pulled apart, not [ɛ]. Hiss the final [s] clearly with no vowel after it.

examples.en: Please don't walk on the grass.
examples.zh: 請不要踩草地。

examples.en: The children sat on the grass to eat lunch.
examples.zh: 孩子們坐在草地上吃午餐。

gray.tip_zh: gray 只有一個音節，但台灣學生常在 [g] 和 [r] 之間多加母音，唸成兩拍的「格雷」。練習時先把舌頭往後捲好，再從 [g] 直接滑進 [r]，接著唸 [e]，嘴角往兩旁拉開收尾。也要跟 grow [gro] 分清楚：grow 的結尾嘴唇是圓的，gray 是扁的。
gray.tip_en: gray has only one syllable, but Taiwanese learners often insert a vowel between [g] and [r], making a two-beat "ge-lei". To practice, curl the tongue back first, slide straight from [g] into [r], then say [e], finishing with the mouth corners pulled wide. Keep it apart from grow [gro]: grow ends with round lips, gray with spread lips.

examples.en: My grandpa has gray hair.
examples.zh: 我爺爺頭髮是灰色的。

examples.en: It's a gray and cloudy day today.
examples.zh: 今天是灰濛濛的陰天。

great.tip_zh: great 拼字有 ea，學生常照著 eat、meat 唸成 [grit]，但它的母音其實是 [e]，跟 eight、late 押韻。字尾 [t] 要收住，不然會變成 gray。它和 grade 只差最後一個音：great 是無聲的 [t]，所以前面的 [e] 比 grade 短一點、乾脆一點。
great.tip_en: great is spelled with ea, so learners often read it like eat or meat as [grit], but its vowel is [e], rhyming with eight and late. Close the final [t], or it becomes gray. It differs from grade only in the last sound: great ends in voiceless [t], so its [e] is a bit shorter and crisper than in grade.

examples.en: We had a great time at the zoo.
examples.zh: 我們在動物園玩得很開心。

examples.en: That's a great idea!
examples.zh: 那是個很棒的點子！

great.spelling_zh: ea 唸 [e]，不是 eat 的 [i]。
great.spelling_en: The ea says [e], not the [i] of eat.

green.tip_zh: green 的字尾是 [n]，舌尖要頂住上排牙齦停住；台灣學生常把舌頭往後縮，唸成 [ŋ]，聽起來像 greeng。[i] 要嘴角往兩邊拉、拉長。檢查方法：唸完時舌尖應該還貼在牙齦上，如果舌尖放下、舌根抬起，就變成 [ŋ] 了。
green.tip_en: green ends in [n]: the tongue tip presses the ridge behind the upper teeth and stays there. Taiwanese learners often pull the tongue back and say [ŋ], so it sounds like "greeng". Stretch the [i] with the mouth corners pulled wide. To check: when you finish, the tongue tip should still be on the ridge — if the tip has dropped and the back of the tongue is raised, you've made [ŋ].

examples.en: My favorite color is green.
examples.zh: 我最喜歡的顏色是綠色。

examples.en: The leaves turn green in spring.
examples.zh: 春天時葉子會變綠。

ground.tip_zh: ground 字尾有 [n] 和 [d] 兩個子音，台灣學生常只唸到 [n] 就停，或把 [d] 加上母音唸成「德」。舌尖頂住上排牙齦發 [n]，舌頭不要離開，直接讓氣在原位爆出 [d]。前面的 [aʊ] 從大嘴的 [a] 滑到圓唇，跟 around、sound 的韻腳一樣。
ground.tip_en: ground ends in two consonants, [n] and [d]. Taiwanese learners often stop at [n], or add a vowel to [d] ("de"). Press the tongue tip on the ridge behind the upper teeth for [n], keep it there, and release [d] from the same spot. The [aʊ] before it slides from a wide [a] to rounded lips, the same rhyme as around and sound.

examples.en: The ground is wet after the rain.
examples.zh: 下過雨後地面是濕的。

examples.en: Please sit on the ground and listen.
examples.zh: 請坐在地上聽。

group.tip_zh: group 拼字有 ou，學生容易照 ground、house 的規則唸成 [aʊ]，但這裡是 [u]，跟 soup 押韻。嘴唇要嘟圓、拉長，最後雙唇閉上發 [p]，不要多加母音唸成「格魯普」。也別和 grape [grep] 搞混：grape 的嘴角往兩邊拉，group 嘴唇往前嘟。
group.tip_en: group is spelled with ou, so learners tend to follow ground or house and say [aʊ], but here it is [u], rhyming with soup. Push the lips round and hold it, then close the lips for [p] — no extra vowel ("ge-lu-pu"). Don't confuse it with grape [grep]: grape pulls the mouth corners wide, group pushes the lips forward.

examples.en: We worked in a group of four.
examples.zh: 我們四個人一組合作。

examples.en: Our group made a poster about the ocean.
examples.zh: 我們這組做了一張關於海洋的海報。

group.spelling_zh: ou 在這裡唸 [u]，不是 house 的 [aʊ]。
group.spelling_en: Here ou says [u], not the [aʊ] of house.

grow.tip_zh: grow 的 [r] 和 glow 的 [l] 是台灣學生最難分的一組：[r] 舌尖往後捲、嘴唇微微嘟起，舌頭不碰牙齦；[l] 則是舌尖貼住上排牙齦。唸 grow 時 [o] 要收圓唇並拉長。拼字的 ow 在這裡唸 [o]，不是 how 的 [aʊ]。
grow.tip_en: The [r] of grow versus the [l] of glow is a pair Taiwanese learners find very hard to separate: for [r] the tongue tip curls back, the lips round slightly, and the tongue touches nothing; for [l] the tip presses the ridge behind the upper teeth. In grow, round the lips for [o] and hold it. The ow here says [o], not the [aʊ] of how.

examples.en: We grow tomatoes in our garden.
examples.zh: 我們在花園裡種番茄。

examples.en: Drink milk and you will grow tall.
examples.zh: 多喝牛奶，你就會長高。

grow.spelling_zh: ow 唸 [o]，不是 how 的 [aʊ]。
grow.spelling_en: The ow says [o], not the [aʊ] of how.

guava.tip_zh: guava 只有兩個音節。開頭的 gu 要一口氣唸成 [gw]：嘴唇先嘟圓，再迅速打開到大嘴的 [ɑ]，不要拆成「古、阿」兩拍，變成三個音節。重音在第一音節。第二音節的 [v] 要上齒輕咬下唇、喉嚨震動，不要唸成 [b]，最後的 [ə] 輕輕帶過。
guava.tip_en: guava has only two syllables. The opening gu is said in one go as [gw]: round the lips, then open quickly to the wide [ɑ] — don't split it into two beats ("gu, a") and make three syllables. The stress is on the first syllable. In the second syllable, the [v] needs the upper teeth lightly on the lower lip with the throat buzzing — not [b] — and the final [ə] is just a light touch.

examples.en: Taiwan has very sweet guava.
examples.zh: 台灣的芭樂非常甜。

examples.en: Would you like a slice of guava?
examples.zh: 你要不要吃一片芭樂？

guava.spelling_en: The gu says [gw]; the u is pronounced here.

guess.tip_zh: guess 的 u 不發音，開頭就是 [g]，不要唸成 [gw]。母音是 [ɛ]，嘴巴半開，比 gas 的 [æ] 小；字尾是無聲的 [s]，不是 [z]，台灣學生也常在 [s] 後面多加母音。可以用押韻的 yes 來練：把開頭的 [j] 換成 [g] 就對了。
guess.tip_en: In guess the u is silent; it starts with plain [g], not [gw]. The vowel is [ɛ], mouth half open, smaller than the [æ] of gas. It ends in voiceless [s], not [z], and Taiwanese learners often add a vowel after the [s]. Practice with the rhyme yes: swap the opening [j] for [g] and you have it.

examples.en: Can you guess what is in the box?
examples.zh: 你猜得到盒子裡是什麼嗎？

examples.en: I guess it will rain this afternoon.
examples.zh: 我猜今天下午會下雨。

guess.spelling_en: The u is silent; gu is just [g].

guitar.tip_zh: guitar 的重音在第二音節 [tɑr]，學生常受中文「吉他」影響，把重音放在第一音節。第一音節 [gɪ] 要短而輕；第二音節拉長、音調提高，[t] 用力送氣，[ɑ] 嘴巴張大，最後舌頭往後捲收在 [r]，不要停在「他」就結束。
guitar.tip_en: The stress in guitar is on the second syllable [tɑr]; influenced by the Mandarin 「吉他」 (jita), students often stress the first syllable. Keep the first syllable [gɪ] short and light; make the second syllable longer and higher, with a strongly aspirated [t] and a wide-open [ɑ], and finish by curling the tongue back into [r] — don't stop at 「他」 (ta).

examples.en: My brother is learning to play the guitar.
examples.zh: 我哥哥正在學彈吉他。

examples.en: She played the guitar at the school concert.
examples.zh: 她在學校音樂會上彈吉他。

guitar.spelling_zh: gu 的 u 不發音，只唸 [g]
guitar.spelling_en: The u in gu is silent; it's just [g].

guy.tip_zh: guy 的 u 不發音，整個字就是 [g] 加上 [aɪ]，跟 buy、my 押韻。[aɪ] 要從大嘴的 [a] 滑到 [ɪ]；台灣學生常滑得不夠，只唸前半，聽起來接近「嘎」。練習時讓下巴從張開慢慢往上收，最後嘴角微微往兩邊拉。
guy.tip_en: In guy the u is silent: the whole word is [g] plus [aɪ], rhyming with buy and my. The [aɪ] must slide from a wide [a] to [ɪ]; Taiwanese learners often don't finish the glide and say only the first half, so it sounds like "ga". Practice by letting the jaw rise slowly from open, ending with the mouth corners slightly spread.

examples.en: The new guy in our class is very friendly.
examples.zh: 我們班上的新同學很友善。

examples.en: That guy at the store helped us find the milk.
examples.zh: 店裡那個人幫我們找到了牛奶。

guy.spelling_en: The u is silent; gu is just [g].

gym.tip_zh: gym 的 g 唸 [dʒ]，跟 jump 的開頭一樣，不是 [g]；y 在這裡是短的 [ɪ]，嘴巴放鬆，不要拉長成 [i]。其實 gym 和人名 Jim 發音完全相同。字尾 [m] 雙唇一定要閉上，台灣學生常唸成 [n]，或嘴巴沒合起來。
gym.tip_en: In gym the g says [dʒ], like the start of jump, not [g]; the y here is a short, relaxed [ɪ] — don't stretch it to [i]. In fact gym sounds exactly like the name Jim. For the final [m] the lips must close; Taiwanese learners often say [n] or leave the lips apart.

examples.en: We play basketball in the gym on Fridays.
examples.zh: 我們每週五在體育館打籃球。

examples.en: My dad goes to the gym after work.
examples.zh: 我爸爸下班後去健身房。

gym.spelling_zh: g 唸 [dʒ]，y 唸 [ɪ]，和 Jim 同音。
gym.spelling_en: The g says [dʒ] and the y says [ɪ]; it sounds like Jim.

habit.tip_zh: habit 重音在第一音節 ha，母音是大嘴的 [æ]，嘴角往兩邊拉開；第二音節 [bət] 要唸得又輕又短，母音弱化成 [ə]。台灣學生常兩個音節唸得一樣重，或把字尾 [t] 吞掉。它跟 rabbit 押韻，可以先唸 rabbit，再把開頭的 [r] 換成輕輕吐氣的 [h]。
habit.tip_en: habit is stressed on the first syllable, ha, with the wide-mouth [æ], corners pulled apart; the second syllable [bət] is light and short, its vowel reduced to [ə]. Taiwanese learners often give both syllables equal weight or swallow the final [t]. It rhymes with rabbit: say rabbit first, then swap the opening [r] for a soft breathy [h].

examples.en: Brushing your teeth every night is a good habit.
examples.zh: 每天晚上刷牙是個好習慣。

examples.en: Reading before bed is my favorite habit.
examples.zh: 睡前閱讀是我最喜歡的習慣。

hair.tip_zh: hair 的母音是 [ɛ]，嘴巴半開，像 bed 的母音，再把舌頭往後捲到 [r]。常見錯誤是嘴巴太扁，唸得像 here、hear 的 [ɪr]，意思就變了。開頭 [h] 只是輕輕吐氣，不要像中文「喝」那樣在舌根摩擦。可以用同韻的 chair、bear 一起練。
hair.tip_en: The vowel in hair is [ɛ]: mouth half open, like the vowel in bed, then curl the tongue back into [r]. A common mistake is keeping the mouth too flat, so it sounds like the [ɪr] of here or hear, which changes the meaning. The opening [h] is just a light breath — don't make friction at the back of the tongue like Mandarin 「喝」 (he). Practice with the rhyming words chair and bear.

examples.en: My sister has long black hair.
examples.zh: 我姊姊有一頭黑色長髮。

examples.en: Don't forget to brush your hair.
examples.zh: 別忘了梳頭髮。

half.tip_zh: half 的 l 不發音，學生常照拼字唸出 [l]。母音是 [æ]，下巴往下、嘴巴張大，跟 laugh 同韻。字尾 [f] 是無聲音，上排牙齒輕碰下唇吹氣就好，喉嚨不震動，否則會變成 have；也不要多加母音唸成「哈夫」。
half.tip_en: The l in half is silent, but students often follow the spelling and say [l]. The vowel is [æ]: drop the jaw and open the mouth wide; it rhymes with laugh. The final [f] is voiceless: the upper teeth lightly touch the lower lip and you just blow air, with no throat vibration — otherwise it becomes have. Don't add a vowel either, as in 「哈夫」 (ha-fu).

examples.en: I ate half of the pizza.
examples.zh: 我吃了半個披薩。

examples.en: Let's meet at half past three.
examples.zh: 我們三點半見吧。

half.spelling_zh: alf 的 l 不發音，只唸 [æf]
half.spelling_en: The l in -alf is silent; say only [æf].

halloween.tip_zh: Halloween 的重音在最後一個音節 [win]，不在開頭。常見錯誤是受 hello 影響唸成「哈囉溫」，三個音一樣重或重音在前。開頭 [hæ] 嘴巴張大，中間 [lə] 很輕很短，最後 [win] 拉長、音調提高，[i] 是長音，收尾時舌尖頂住上牙齦發 [n]。
halloween.tip_en: The stress in Halloween is on the last syllable [win], not at the start. A common mistake, influenced by hello, is saying 「哈囉溫」 (ha-luo-wen) with all three syllables equal or the stress up front. Open the mouth wide for [hæ], keep the middle [lə] very light and short, and make [win] long and higher in pitch; the [i] is long, and you finish with the tongue tip on the gum ridge for [n].

examples.en: We wear costumes on Halloween.
examples.zh: 我們在萬聖節穿上變裝服。

examples.en: What are you going to be for Halloween?
examples.zh: 萬聖節你要裝扮成什麼？

ham.tip_zh: ham 跟 home 只差母音：ham 是 [æ]，嘴巴往兩邊拉開、下巴放低；home 是 [o]，嘴唇收圓。字尾 [m] 雙唇一定要閉上，否則會聽起來像 [n]，或變成 hang 的 [ŋ]。開頭 [h] 只是輕輕吐氣，不要像中文那樣用舌根摩擦出很粗的聲音。
ham.tip_en: ham differs from home only in the vowel: ham has [æ], mouth spread wide and jaw lowered; home has [o], lips rounded. For the final [m] the lips must close, or it sounds like [n] or turns into the [ŋ] of hang. The opening [h] is just a soft breath — don't make the rough, tongue-back friction of the Mandarin h.

examples.en: I had a ham sandwich for lunch.
examples.zh: 我午餐吃了火腿三明治。

examples.en: Mom cut the ham into small pieces.
examples.zh: 媽媽把火腿切成小塊。

hamburger.tip_zh: hamburger 重音在第一音節 [hæm]，[æ] 嘴巴張大。學生常被中文「漢堡」帶著把 [m] 唸成舌尖的 [n]；其實發 [m] 時雙唇閉上，直接接 [b] 最順。後面兩個音節 [bɚ]、[gɚ] 都是輕的捲舌音，子音一出來舌頭就要捲，不要唸成「堡」或「格」。
hamburger.tip_en: The stress in hamburger is on the first syllable [hæm], with a wide-open [æ]. Led by the Mandarin 「漢堡」 (hanbao), students often turn [m] into a tongue-tip [n]; in fact, the lips close for [m], which leads most smoothly into [b]. The next two syllables, [bɚ] and [gɚ], are both light r-colored sounds — curl the tongue as soon as each consonant comes out, and don't say 「堡」 (bao) or 「格」 (ge).

examples.en: I'd like a hamburger and a glass of juice.
examples.zh: 我想要一個漢堡和一杯果汁。

examples.en: This hamburger is too big for me!
examples.zh: 這個漢堡對我來說太大了！

hand.tip_zh: hand 的母音是 [æ]，嘴角往兩旁拉開、下巴放低，不要縮成 [ɛ]，否則聽起來像 hen 後面加 [d]。字尾 [nd] 是另一個陷阱：台灣學生常只唸到 [n] 就停。舌尖頂在上排牙齦發 [n] 後不要移開，直接在原位放出 [d]。它跟 band、land、stand 押韻。
hand.tip_en: The vowel in hand is [æ]: mouth corners pulled apart, jaw lowered — don't shrink it to [ɛ], or it sounds like hen plus [d]. The final [nd] is the second trap: Taiwanese learners often stop at [n]. After pressing the tongue tip on the ridge behind the upper teeth for [n], don't move it; release [d] from the same spot. It rhymes with band, land and stand.

examples.en: Raise your hand if you know the answer.
examples.zh: 知道答案的人請舉手。

examples.en: Hold my hand when we cross the street.
examples.zh: 過馬路時要牽著我的手。

handsome.tip_zh: handsome 拼字裡的 d 不發音，KK 是 [ˈhænsəm]；台灣學生常照拼字把 [d] 唸出來，讓三個子音擠在一起。重音在第一音節 [hæn]，母音是大嘴的 [æ]；後面的 some 要弱化成輕短的 [səm]，不要唸成單字 some [sʌm] 那麼重。字尾 [m] 雙唇要閉起來。
handsome.tip_en: The d in handsome is silent; the KK is [ˈhænsəm]. Taiwanese learners often follow the spelling and pronounce the [d], cramming three consonants together. The stress is on the first syllable [hæn] with the wide-mouth [æ]; the some part reduces to a light, short [səm] — not as heavy as the word some [sʌm]. Close the lips for the final [m].

examples.en: The prince in the story is tall and handsome.
examples.zh: 故事裡的王子又高又英俊。

examples.en: You look so handsome in that new shirt!
examples.zh: 你穿那件新襯衫好帥！

hang.tip_zh: hang 的字尾是 [ŋ]：舌根往上抬、頂住軟顎，聲音從鼻子出來，跟 sing 的結尾一樣。不要唸成舌尖音 [n]，那會變成 [hæn]；也不要在後面多發一個 [g]，拼字的 ng 在這裡只是一個音。母音是 [æ]，嘴巴要張開，不要縮成 [ɛ]。
hang.tip_en: hang ends in [ŋ]: raise the back of the tongue against the soft palate and let the sound come out through the nose, like the end of sing. Don't make a tongue-tip [n], which gives [hæn]; and don't add a [g] after it — the spelling ng is a single sound here. The vowel is [æ], so open the mouth; don't shrink it to [ɛ].

examples.en: Please hang your coat on the hook.
examples.zh: 請把外套掛在掛鉤上。

examples.en: Let's hang the picture on the wall.
examples.zh: 我們把這幅畫掛在牆上吧。

hang.spelling_zh: ng 是一個音 [ŋ]，不要唸成 [n] 加 [g]。
hang.spelling_en: The ng is one sound, [ŋ] — not [n] plus [g].

happen.tip_zh: happen 的第一音節 [hæ] 要重、嘴巴張大；第二音節 [pən] 很輕，[p] 送氣後 [ə] 幾乎一帶而過。常見錯誤是兩個音節一樣重，把 en 唸得很清楚。結尾 [n] 要用舌尖頂住上牙齦，不要變成後鼻音 [ŋ]。拼字有兩個 p，但只唸一個 [p]。
happen.tip_en: The first syllable of happen, [hæ], is strong with the mouth wide open; the second syllable [pən] is very light — after the aspirated [p], the [ə] passes almost instantly. A common mistake is giving both syllables equal weight and saying en very clearly. The final [n] uses the tongue tip on the gum ridge — don't let it become the back nasal [ŋ]. The spelling has two p's, but you say only one [p].

examples.en: What will happen next in the story?
examples.zh: 故事接下來會發生什麼事？

examples.en: Good things happen when we work together.
examples.zh: 我們一起努力時，好事就會發生。

happy.tip_zh: happy 的 [æ] 是關鍵：學生常唸成「黑皮」，嘴巴開得不夠，母音變成 [ɛ]。下巴要往下放、嘴角往兩旁拉，像要說 cat。重音在第一音節，第二音節 [pɪ] 短而輕，[p] 送出一點氣。可以先慢慢唸 [hæ]，確認嘴巴張開，再快速接上 [pɪ]。
happy.tip_en: The key in happy is [æ]: students often say 「黑皮」 (hei-pi), with the mouth not open enough, so the vowel becomes [ɛ]. Drop the jaw and pull the corners of the mouth back, as if saying cat. The stress is on the first syllable; the second syllable [pɪ] is short and light, with a little puff of air on [p]. Say [hæ] slowly first to check that the mouth is open, then add [pɪ] quickly.

examples.en: I'm so happy to see you!
examples.zh: 看到你我好開心！

examples.en: We sang Happy Birthday to Grandma.
examples.zh: 我們唱生日快樂歌給奶奶聽。

hard.tip_zh: hard 的 [ɑr] 要先張大嘴唸 [ɑ]，再把舌頭往後捲出 [r]；台灣學生常唸成沒有捲舌的「哈」，或捲舌捲得太晚、太短。字尾 [d] 要讓喉嚨震動，唸成無聲的 [t] 就變成 heart [hɑrt] 了。練習時把 hard 和 heart 輪流唸，hard 的母音比較長。
hard.tip_en: In hard, open the mouth wide for [ɑ] first, then curl the tongue back for [r]. Taiwanese learners often say a flat "ha" with no r, or curl too late and too briefly. The final [d] must buzz in the throat; a voiceless [t] turns it into heart [hɑrt]. Practice by alternating hard and heart — the vowel in hard is longer.

examples.en: This math problem is really hard.
examples.zh: 這道數學題真的很難。

examples.en: The bread is too hard to eat.
examples.zh: 這個麵包硬得咬不動。

hat.tip_zh: hat 的 [æ] 舌頭在前、嘴角往兩旁拉開：嘴巴太扁會聽成 [ɛ]；舌頭往後縮又會變成 hot（熱的）的 [ɑ]。字尾 [t] 輕輕停住就好，舌尖頂住上牙齦，美式口語常常不爆出氣，但絕不能多加母音變成兩個音節。可以跟同韻的 cat、bat 一起練。
hat.tip_en: For the [æ] in hat, keep the tongue forward and spread the corners of the mouth: too flat a mouth and it's heard as [ɛ]; pull the tongue back and it becomes the [ɑ] of hot. Just stop gently on the final [t] with the tongue tip on the gum ridge — in casual American speech it often isn't released with a puff of air — but never add a vowel and make it two syllables. Practice with the rhyming words cat and bat.

examples.en: Wear a hat when it's sunny.
examples.zh: 天氣晴朗時要戴帽子。

examples.en: I like your red hat!
examples.zh: 我喜歡你的紅色帽子！

hate.tip_zh: hate 的母音是 [e]，嘴角往兩邊拉，並從 [e] 滑向 [ɪ]，跟 late、eight 押韻；台灣學生常唸得太短、嘴巴太開，聽起來像 hat [hæt]。字尾的 e 不發音，只是讓 a 唸成 [e]。最後的 [t] 舌尖頂住上排牙齦收住，不要多加母音唸成「黑特」。
hate.tip_en: The vowel in hate is [e]: mouth corners pulled wide, gliding from [e] toward [ɪ], rhyming with late and eight.
