Taiwanese learners often make it too short and too open, so it sounds like hat [hæt]. The final e is silent; it only makes the a say [e]. Close the final [t] with the tongue tip on the ridge behind the upper teeth — no extra vowel ("hei-te").

examples.en: I hate waiting in long lines.
examples.zh: 我討厭排很長的隊。

examples.en: My cat and I both hate loud noises.
examples.zh: 我和我的貓都討厭很吵的聲音。

have.tip_zh: have 的字尾 [v] 有聲：上排牙齒輕碰下唇，喉嚨震動。學生常唸成無聲的 [f]，聽起來像 half，或乾脆把尾音省掉。比較 half [hæf] 和 have [hæv]：母音相同，差別在最後喉嚨有沒有震動，而且 have 的 [æ] 會稍微拉長一點。
have.tip_en: The final [v] in have is voiced: the upper teeth lightly touch the lower lip and the throat vibrates. Students often say a voiceless [f], so it sounds like half, or simply drop the ending. Compare half [hæf] and have [hæv]: the vowel is the same; the difference is whether the throat vibrates at the end, and the [æ] in have is held a little longer.

examples.en: I have two brothers and one sister.
examples.zh: 我有兩個哥哥和一個妹妹。

examples.en: Do you have a pencil?
examples.zh: 你有鉛筆嗎？

have.spelling_zh: 字尾 e 不發音，a 唸 [æ]，不像 save 唸 [e]
have.spelling_en: The final e is silent, and a is [æ], not [e] as in save.

he.tip_zh: he 的 [h] 只是一口輕輕的氣，像對著鏡子哈氣，不要用中文那種舌根摩擦的粗聲音。[i] 要嘴角往兩邊拉開、拉長。句子裡沒有強調時，he 常唸得很輕，例如 Is he here? 裡的 [h] 幾乎聽不到，聽力測驗時要特別留意。
he.tip_en: The [h] in he is just a soft breath, like fogging a mirror — not the rough, tongue-back friction of Mandarin. Spread the mouth corners for [i] and hold it. When it isn't stressed in a sentence, he is often very light — in Is he here? the [h] is barely heard, so listen for it carefully on listening tests.

examples.en: He is my best friend.
examples.zh: 他是我最好的朋友。

examples.en: Where does he live?
examples.zh: 他住在哪裡？

head.tip_zh: head 拼字有 ea，但這裡唸短的 [ɛ]，跟 bed、red 押韻，不是 eat 的 [i]，也不是 hide 的 [aɪ]。唸 [ɛ] 時嘴巴半開、舌頭放平；接著舌尖碰上排牙齦，喉嚨震動發 [d]。台灣學生常把字尾 [d] 吞掉或唸成無聲的 [t]。
head.tip_en: head is spelled with ea, but here it is the short [ɛ], rhyming with bed and red — not the [i] of eat, nor the [aɪ] of hide. For [ɛ], open the mouth halfway with the tongue flat; then touch the tongue tip to the ridge behind the upper teeth and buzz for [d]. Taiwanese learners often swallow the final [d] or turn it into a voiceless [t].

examples.en: Put your hat on your head.
examples.zh: 把帽子戴在頭上。

examples.en: She nodded her head and smiled.
examples.zh: 她點點頭笑了。

headache.tip_zh: headache 的後半 ache 唸 [ek]，ch 發 [k]，不是 [tʃ]；台灣學生常照拼字唸成類似 aitch 的音。重音在 head，ache 是次重音。head 的 [d] 直接連到 ache，唸起來像 [hɛ dek]，中間不要停頓，也不要在 [d] 後面多加母音。
headache.tip_en: The second half of headache, ache, is [ek] — the ch says [k], not [tʃ]; Taiwanese learners often follow the spelling and say something like "aitch". The main stress is on head, with secondary stress on ache. The [d] of head links straight into ache, so it sounds like [hɛ dek] — no pause in the middle and no vowel after the [d].

examples.en: I have a headache, so I want to rest.
examples.zh: 我頭痛，想休息一下。

examples.en: Drink some water if you have a headache.
examples.zh: 如果頭痛就喝點水。

health.tip_zh: health 字尾是 [lθ] 兩個子音：先把舌尖貼住上排牙齦發 [l]，再把舌尖往前伸到上下齒之間吹氣發 [θ]。台灣學生常把 [l] 省掉，或把 [θ] 唸成 [s]，聽起來像 hel-s。拼字的 ea 在這裡唸 [ɛ]，和 help 的母音一樣。
health.tip_en: health ends in two consonants, [lθ]: first press the tongue tip on the ridge behind the upper teeth for [l], then slide the tip forward between the teeth and blow for [θ]. Taiwanese learners often drop the [l] or turn [θ] into [s], so it sounds like "hel-s". The ea here says [ɛ], the same vowel as in help.

examples.en: Fruit and vegetables are good for your health.
examples.zh: 水果和蔬菜對健康有益。

examples.en: Sleep is important for your health.
examples.zh: 睡眠對你的健康很重要。

healthy.tip_zh: healthy 重音在第一音節 [hɛl]，裡面的 [l] 要確實發出來，舌尖貼在上排牙齦；接著把舌尖往前移到上下齒之間發 [θ]，再接輕短的 [ɪ]。台灣學生常把 [θ] 唸成 [s] 或 [ʃ]，變成 hel-see。可以分兩步練：先唸 [hɛl]，再讓舌尖往前滑出 [θɪ]。
healthy.tip_en: healthy is stressed on the first syllable [hɛl], and its [l] must really be made, tongue tip on the ridge behind the upper teeth; then move the tip forward between the teeth for [θ], followed by a short, light [ɪ]. Taiwanese learners often turn [θ] into [s] or [ʃ], giving "hel-see". Practice in two steps: say [hɛl], then slide the tongue tip forward into [θɪ].

examples.en: Eating breakfast helps you stay healthy.
examples.zh: 吃早餐能幫助你保持健康。

examples.en: Our teacher brought a healthy snack to class.
examples.zh: 老師帶了健康的點心到班上。

hear.tip_zh: hear 和 here 發音完全一樣，都是 [hɪr]，要分的是 hair [hɛr]：hear 的母音是較高、較緊的 [ɪ]，嘴巴微開；hair 嘴巴張得比較開。台灣學生常把結尾的 [r] 唸成拖長的「爾」，變成兩個音節。[ɪ] 唸完直接把舌頭往後捲，一拍就結束。
hear.tip_en: hear sounds exactly like here — both are [hɪr]. The word to keep apart is hair [hɛr]: hear has the higher, tighter [ɪ] with the mouth slightly open, while hair opens wider. Taiwanese learners often drag the final [r] into a separate "er", making two syllables. After [ɪ], curl the tongue back straight away and finish in one beat.

examples.en: Can you hear the birds singing?
examples.zh: 你聽得到鳥在唱歌嗎？

examples.en: I can't hear you. Please speak louder.
examples.zh: 我聽不到你說話，請大聲一點。

heart.tip_zh: heart 拼字有 ea，卻唸 [ɑr]，跟 art、part 押韻。因為字裡藏著 hear，學生常唸成 [hɪrt]。正確是嘴巴張大唸 [ɑ]，舌頭再往後捲成 [r]，最後舌尖頂住上排牙齦收 [t]。和 hard 對照：heart 結尾是無聲的 [t]，母音稍短。
heart.tip_en: heart is spelled with ea yet says [ɑr], rhyming with art and part. Because the word hear is hiding inside it, learners often say [hɪrt]. The right way: open the mouth wide for [ɑ], curl the tongue back for [r], and close with the tongue tip on the ridge behind the upper teeth for [t]. Compared with hard, heart ends in voiceless [t] and its vowel is a little shorter.

examples.en: She drew a big red heart on the card.
examples.zh: 她在卡片上畫了一個大紅心。

examples.en: My heart beats fast after running.
examples.zh: 跑步後我的心跳很快。

heart.spelling_zh: ea 唸 [ɑr]，不要被裡面的 hear 騙了。
heart.spelling_en: The ea here says [ɑr] — don't be fooled by the hear inside.

heat.tip_zh: heat 的 [i] 要嘴角往兩邊拉、拉長，才能跟 hit [hɪt] 分開；hit 的 [ɪ] 短而放鬆。台灣學生常把兩個字都唸成中間值，老師聽不出是哪一個。字尾 [t] 也要收住：舌尖頂住上排牙齦停住，不要多加母音，也不要省掉，否則就變成 he 了。
heat.tip_en: The [i] in heat needs the mouth corners pulled wide and held long, to keep it apart from hit [hɪt], whose [ɪ] is short and relaxed. Taiwanese learners often say both with an in-between vowel, so a listener can't tell which word it is. Close the final [t] too: tongue tip on the ridge behind the upper teeth, then stop — no extra vowel, and don't drop it, or it becomes he.

examples.en: Please heat the milk for the baby.
examples.zh: 請把寶寶的牛奶熱一下。

examples.en: The heat of the sun makes the sand hot.
examples.zh: 太陽的熱度讓沙子變得很燙。

heavy.tip_zh: heavy 中間的 [v] 最常出錯，台灣學生常唸成 [b]，聽起來像 heby，或唸成 [w]。正確做法是上排牙齒輕放在下唇上，喉嚨震動、讓氣從縫裡擠出來。拼字的 ea 唸短的 [ɛ]，不是 [i]。重音在第一音節，最後的 [ɪ] 輕而短。
heavy.tip_en: The [v] in the middle of heavy is where it usually goes wrong: Taiwanese learners often say [b], giving "heby", or [w]. Rest the upper teeth lightly on the lower lip, buzz the throat, and squeeze air through the gap. The ea is short [ɛ], not [i]. Stress the first syllable; the final [ɪ] is light and short.

examples.en: This box is too heavy for me to carry.
examples.zh: 這個箱子太重了，我搬不動。

examples.en: My school bag is heavy today.
examples.zh: 我今天的書包很重。

height.tip_zh: height 的字尾是 [t]，不是 [θ]！因為 width、length 都以 th 結尾，學生常順口把 height 唸成 [haɪθ]。正確是 [aɪ] 之後舌尖頂住上排牙齦收 [t]，舌頭不要伸出來。拼字的 ei 在這裡唸 [aɪ]，gh 不發音，所以它跟 light、night 押韻。
height.tip_en: height ends in [t], not [θ]! Because width and length both end in th, learners often slip and say [haɪθ]. The right way: after [aɪ], close with the tongue tip on the ridge behind the upper teeth for [t] — the tongue doesn't come out between the teeth. The ei here says [aɪ] and the gh is silent, so it rhymes with light and night.

examples.en: The nurse checked my height and weight.
examples.zh: 護理師幫我量身高和體重。

examples.en: What is the height of that tree?
examples.zh: 那棵樹有多高？

height.spelling_zh: ei 唸 [aɪ]，gh 不發音，結尾是 [t] 不是 th。
height.spelling_en: The ei says [aɪ], the gh is silent, and it ends in [t], not th.

hello.tip_zh: hello 重音在第二音節 lo，第一音節 [hə] 要又輕又短。台灣學生習慣說「哈囉」，把重音放在前面，母音也唸成大嘴的 [a]。正確是輕輕帶過 [hə]，再把 lo 唸得響亮、拉長，[o] 嘴唇收圓。中間的 [l] 舌尖要碰上排牙齦，不要變成 [n]。
hello.tip_en: hello is stressed on the second syllable, lo; the first syllable [hə] is light and short. Taiwanese learners tend to say "ha-lo" with the stress at the front and an open [a] vowel. Instead, touch [hə] lightly, then make lo loud and long with rounded lips for [o]. For the [l] in the middle, the tongue tip touches the ridge behind the upper teeth — don't let it become [n].

examples.en: Say hello to your new classmates.
examples.zh: 跟你的新同學打聲招呼。

examples.en: Hello, this is Amy. Can I talk to Ben?
examples.zh: 喂，我是 Amy，請問 Ben 在嗎？

hello.variant_en: The first syllable is also often [hɛ]: [hɛˈlo].

help.tip_zh: help 的字尾有 [l] 和 [p] 兩個子音：[ɛ] 之後舌尖要往上貼住牙齦發 [l]，再閉上雙唇收 [p]。台灣學生常省掉 [l]，唸成 [hɛp]，或在 [p] 後面多加一個母音。先慢慢唸 hel-，確認舌尖真的碰到牙齦，再接上 [p]；喊 Help! 時 [p] 也只是雙唇閉合後輕輕放氣。
help.tip_en: help ends in two consonants, [l] and [p]: after [ɛ], raise the tongue tip to the ridge for [l], then close the lips for [p]. Taiwanese learners often drop the [l] and say [hɛp], or add a vowel after the [p]. Say hel- slowly first and make sure the tongue tip really touches the ridge, then add [p]; even when you shout Help!, the [p] is just the lips closing and letting out a little air.

examples.en: Can you help me with my homework?
examples.zh: 你可以幫我寫作業嗎？

examples.en: Thank you for your help!
examples.zh: 謝謝你的幫忙！

helpful.tip_zh: helpful 中間是 [lpf] 三個子音連在一起：舌尖貼牙齦發 [l]，雙唇閉合發 [p]，接著上齒碰下唇發 [f]，中間不要加母音。字尾 ful 輕讀成 [ḷ]，舌尖碰上排牙齦結束，不要唸成單字 full 那麼重，也不要把最後的 [l] 唸成「歐」。重音在 help。
helpful.tip_en: The middle of helpful is three consonants in a row, [lpf]: tongue tip on the ridge for [l], lips closed for [p], then upper teeth on the lower lip for [f] — no vowels in between. The ending ful is read lightly as [ḷ], finishing with the tongue tip on the ridge behind the upper teeth; don't make it as heavy as the word full, and don't turn the final [l] into an "o" sound. The stress is on help.

examples.en: Thanks, that map was very helpful.
examples.zh: 謝謝，那張地圖很有幫助。

examples.en: Ben is always helpful in class.
examples.zh: Ben 在班上總是很樂於幫忙。

hen.tip_zh: hen 字尾是 [n]，舌尖要頂在上排牙齦後面停住；台灣學生常把舌頭往後縮，唸成 [hɛŋ]。母音是 [ɛ]，嘴巴半開就好，如果張得太大變成 [æ]，再加上字尾錯成 [ŋ]，就變成 hang 了。可以拿押韻的 ten、pen 來練，只要換掉第一個音。
hen.tip_en: hen ends in [n]: the tongue tip presses the ridge behind the upper teeth and stays there. Taiwanese learners often pull the tongue back and say [hɛŋ]. The vowel is [ɛ], with the mouth only half open; open it too wide into [æ], add a wrong [ŋ] ending, and you get hang. Practice with the rhymes ten and pen — just change the first sound.

examples.en: The hen laid three eggs this morning.
examples.zh: 母雞今天早上下了三顆蛋。

examples.en: A brown hen is walking around the farm.
examples.zh: 一隻棕色的母雞在農場裡走來走去。

here.tip_zh: here 跟 there、where 拼法很像，但 there、where 唸 [ɛr]，here 卻是 [ɪr]，和 hear 同音。台灣學生常被拼字帶跑，把 here 唸成 hair [hɛr] 的音。唸 [ɪ] 時嘴巴不要張太開，接著舌頭往後捲成 [r]，一口氣結束，不要拖成兩個音節。
here.tip_en: here is spelled much like there and where, but those say [ɛr] while here says [ɪr], the same as hear. Taiwanese learners are often misled by the spelling and say here like hair [hɛr]. Keep the mouth fairly closed for [ɪ], then curl the tongue back for [r] and finish in one breath — don't drag it into two syllables.

examples.en: Come here and look at this!
examples.zh: 過來看看這個！

examples.en: My house is not far from here.
examples.zh: 我家離這裡不遠。

here.spelling_zh: ere 唸 [ɪr]，和 there、where 的 [ɛr] 不同。
here.spelling_en: The ere says [ɪr], unlike the [ɛr] of there and where.

hey.tip_zh: hey 拼字的 ey 唸 [e]，跟 day、say 押韻，不是 key 的 [i]，所以不要和 he [hi] 混在一起。[e] 要從 [e] 滑向 [ɪ]，嘴角往兩邊拉。和 hi [haɪ] 相比，hey 一開始嘴巴不用張那麼大。開頭的 [h] 只是輕輕吐氣，不要喉嚨用力。
hey.tip_en: The ey in hey says [e], rhyming with day and say — not the [i] of key — so don't mix it up with he [hi]. Glide the [e] toward [ɪ] with the mouth corners pulled wide. Compared with hi [haɪ], hey starts with the mouth less open. The opening [h] is only a soft breath, with no strain in the throat.

examples.en: Hey, wait for me!
examples.zh: 嘿，等等我！

examples.en: Hey, do you want to play tag?
examples.zh: 嘿，你想玩鬼抓人嗎？

hey.spelling_zh: ey 唸 [e]，不是 key 的 [i]。
hey.spelling_en: The ey says [e], not the [i] of key.

hi.tip_zh: hi 最常見的問題是學生直接用中文的「嗨」來代替：中文的 h 舌根會摩擦，聲音比較粗；英文 [h] 只是喉嚨打開，輕輕吐一口氣。打招呼時把氣放輕，[aɪ] 從大嘴的 [a] 滑到 [ɪ]，下巴慢慢往上收。另外 hi 和 high 發音一模一樣。
hi.tip_en: The most common problem with hi is that learners simply use the Mandarin greeting instead: the Mandarin h has friction at the back of the tongue and sounds rougher, while English [h] is just an open throat and a soft breath. Keep the breath light, and slide [aɪ] from a wide [a] to [ɪ], raising the jaw gradually. Also, hi sounds exactly like high.

examples.en: Hi, my name is Lily.
examples.zh: 嗨，我的名字是 Lily。

examples.en: Say hi to your grandma for me.
examples.zh: 幫我跟你奶奶問好。

hide.tip_zh: hide 和 height 只差最後一個音：hide 是有聲的 [d]，height 是無聲的 [t]。台灣學生常把字尾 [d] 吞掉，聽起來就只剩 hi。唸 [d] 之前，[aɪ] 可以稍微拉長，然後舌尖碰上排牙齦、喉嚨保持震動。字尾的 e 不發音，只是讓 i 唸成 [aɪ]。
hide.tip_en: hide and height differ only in the last sound: hide ends in voiced [d], height in voiceless [t]. Taiwanese learners often swallow the final [d], so only hi is left. Before the [d], let [aɪ] run a little longer, then touch the tongue tip to the ridge behind the upper teeth with the throat still buzzing. The final e is silent; it only makes the i say [aɪ].

examples.en: Let's play hide and seek!
examples.zh: 我們來玩捉迷藏吧！

examples.en: The cat likes to hide under the bed.
examples.zh: 貓咪喜歡躲在床底下。

high.tip_zh: high 的 gh 完全不發音，整個字就是 [haɪ]，和 hi 同音。學生看到 gh，有時會在結尾多加 [g] 或 [f] 的音，兩種都不對。重點在 [aɪ]：從張大嘴的 [a] 滑到 [ɪ]，滑動要完整，不要只停在 [a]。強調「很高」時可以把 [aɪ] 拉長，例如 Jump high!
high.tip_en: The gh in high is completely silent; the whole word is [haɪ], the same as hi. Seeing gh, learners sometimes add a [g] or [f] at the end — both are wrong. The key is [aɪ]: slide from a wide [a] all the way to [ɪ], not stopping at [a]. To stress "very high", you can stretch the [aɪ], as in Jump high!

examples.en: The kite is flying high in the sky.
examples.zh: 風箏在天上飛得很高。

examples.en: That mountain is very high.
examples.zh: 那座山非常高。

high.spelling_zh: gh 不發音，和 hi 同音。
high.spelling_en: The gh is silent; it sounds like hi.

hike.tip_zh: hike 字尾是 [k]：舌根抬起頂住軟顎，再輕輕放開，台灣學生常省略不唸，或多加母音變成兩拍。和 hide [haɪd] 相比，[k] 是無聲的，所以前面的 [aɪ] 比較短、比較乾脆。可以先唸押韻的 like，再把 [l] 換成輕輕吐氣的 [h]。
hike.tip_en: hike ends in [k]: raise the back of the tongue against the soft palate, then release lightly. Taiwanese learners often leave it out or add a vowel and make two beats. Compared with hide [haɪd], [k] is voiceless, so the [aɪ] before it is shorter and crisper. Say the rhyme like first, then swap the [l] for a soft breathy [h].

examples.en: We hike up the mountain every Sunday.
examples.zh: 我們每個星期天去爬山。

examples.en: Let's go for a hike in the park.
examples.zh: 我們去公園健行吧。

hill.tip_zh: hill 跟 heel（腳跟）只差在母音：hill 的 [ɪ] 短而鬆，舌頭稍低；heel 的 [i] 長而緊、嘴角拉開。母音後面接暗 L 時，會有一點往 [l] 滑過去的感覺，但最後舌尖一定要碰到上牙齦，不能只剩「嘿喔」。可以拿同韻的 will、still 一起練。
hill.tip_en: hill and heel differ only in the vowel: the [ɪ] in hill is short and loose, with the tongue a bit lower; the [i] in heel is long and tense, with the lips spread. Before the dark L, the vowel glides a little toward [l], but at the end the tongue tip must touch the gum ridge — don't leave only 「嘿喔」 (hei-o). Practice with the rhyming words will and still.

examples.en: We walked up the hill to see the sunset.
examples.zh: 我們走上山丘看夕陽。

examples.en: Our school is on a small hill.
examples.zh: 我們學校在一座小山丘上。

history.tip_zh: history 重音在第一音節 [hɪs]，後面都要輕。學生常三個音節一樣重，或把 to 唸成清楚的 [o]。中間的 [tə] 只是很輕的音，美國人說快時常幾乎消失，變成 [ˈhɪstrɪ]。[s] 後面的 [t] 不送氣，兩個子音之間也不要加母音。
history.tip_en: The stress in history is on the first syllable [hɪs]; everything after it is light. Students often give all three syllables equal weight, or say to with a clear [o]. The middle [tə] is just a very light sound, and in fast American speech it often almost disappears, giving [ˈhɪstrɪ]. The [t] after [s] is not aspirated, and no vowel goes between those two consonants either.

examples.en: History is my favorite subject.
examples.zh: 歷史是我最喜歡的科目。

examples.en: We learned about Taiwan's history today.
examples.zh: 我們今天學了台灣的歷史。

history.variant_en: In everyday speech it often shrinks to two syllables: [ˈhɪstrɪ].
history.kk_flag: Taiwan KK dictionaries write [ˈhɪstərɪ] (or [ˈhɪstrɪ]); [ˈhɪstɚɪ] looks like a CMU conversion artifact (ER0 + IY0) and forces the odd syllable split hɪs·tɚ·ɪ. Suggest [ˈhɪstərɪ] → hɪs·tə·rɪ.

hit.tip_zh: hit 的 [ɪ] 是短而放鬆的音：嘴巴不要拉開，舌頭比 [i] 低一點；唸得太長、太緊，就變成 heat [hit]。台灣學生也常把字尾 [t] 省掉。練習時先唸押韻的 it、sit，再加上輕輕吐氣的 [h]。過去式也還是 hit，發音不變。
hit.tip_en: The [ɪ] in hit is short and relaxed: don't spread the mouth, and keep the tongue a little lower than for [i]; make it long and tense and it becomes heat [hit]. Taiwanese learners also often drop the final [t]. Practice with the rhymes it and sit, then add a soft breathy [h]. The past tense is also hit, pronounced the same.

examples.en: Try to hit the ball with the bat.
examples.zh: 試著用球棒打到球。

examples.en: Be careful not to hit your head.
examples.zh: 小心別撞到頭。

hobby.tip_zh: hobby 第一音節的 o 唸 [ɑ]，嘴巴張大、下巴放低，跟 hot 的母音一樣；台灣學生常唸成圓唇的 [o]，聽起來像「豪比」。重音在第一音節，拼字的 bb 只唸一個 [b]，不要停頓兩次。最後的 [ɪ] 短而輕，不要拉成 [i]。
hobby.tip_en: The o in the first syllable of hobby says [ɑ]: open the mouth wide and drop the jaw, the same vowel as hot. Taiwanese learners often use a rounded [o], so it sounds like "hao-bi". Stress the first syllable; the double bb is a single [b], with no double stop. The final [ɪ] is short and light — don't stretch it to [i].

examples.en: My hobby is drawing animals.
examples.zh: 我的嗜好是畫動物。

examples.en: What is your favorite hobby?
examples.zh: 你最喜歡的嗜好是什麼？

hobby.spelling_en: The o says [ɑ]; the bb is one [b].

hold.tip_zh: hold 字尾是 [ld]：[o] 之後舌尖往上貼住牙齦發 [l]，舌頭不要放開，直接接著發 [d]。台灣學生常把 [l] 唸成「歐」或乾脆省掉，變成 [hod]，聽起來不像 hold。它和 cold、old 押韻，可以先唸熟 old，再在前面加上輕輕的 [h]。
hold.tip_en: hold ends in [ld]: after [o], raise the tongue tip to the ridge for [l] and, without letting go, go straight into [d]. Taiwanese learners often turn the [l] into an "o" sound or drop it, giving [hod], which doesn't sound like hold. It rhymes with cold and old: get old smooth first, then add a soft [h] in front.

examples.en: Please hold my bag for a minute.
examples.zh: 請幫我拿一下包包。

examples.en: Hold the baby rabbit gently.
examples.zh: 輕輕地抱著小兔子。

holiday.tip_zh: holiday 的 o 唸 [ɑ]，嘴巴張大，像 hot 的母音，不是 [o]。重音在第一音節，中間 [lə] 輕輕帶過；最後 [de] 有次重音，要唸出跟 day 一樣從 [e] 往上滑的感覺，不要唸成短促平板的「得」。三個音節的輕重是：重、輕、中。
holiday.tip_en: The o in holiday is [ɑ]: open the mouth wide, as for the vowel in hot — not [o]. The stress is on the first syllable and the middle [lə] passes lightly; the final [de] has secondary stress and should have the same upward glide from [e] as day — don't make it a short, flat 「得」 (de). The three syllables go: strong, light, medium.

examples.en: What do you want to do this holiday?
examples.zh: 這次放假你想做什麼？

examples.en: Christmas is my favorite holiday.
examples.zh: 聖誕節是我最喜歡的節日。

holiday.spelling_zh: o 唸 [ɑ]，不像 holy 唸 [o]
holiday.spelling_en: The o is [ɑ], not the [o] of holy.

home.tip_zh: home 的字尾 [m] 雙唇一定要閉起來，台灣學生常唸成 [n]，或是嘴巴沒合上就結束。母音 [o] 要嘴唇收圓並稍微滑動；字尾的 e 不發音，只是讓 o 唸 [o]。它和 hope [hop] 只差最後一個音：home 雙唇閉著、讓聲音從鼻子出來，hope 雙唇閉合後放氣。
home.tip_en: For the final [m] in home, the lips must close; Taiwanese learners often say [n] or finish without closing the lips. The [o] rounds the lips with a slight glide; the final e is silent and only makes the o say [o]. home differs from hope [hop] only in the last sound: for home the lips stay closed and the sound goes through the nose, for hope the lips close and then release air.

examples.en: I go home at four o'clock.
examples.zh: 我四點回家。

examples.en: There's no place like home.
examples.zh: 哪裡都比不上家。

homework.tip_zh: homework 的後半 work 唸 [wɝk]，舌頭要捲起來，跟 bird 的母音一樣；台灣學生常唸成 walk [wɔk]，那是完全不同的字。重音在 home，work 是次重音。home 的 [m] 雙唇閉上後，直接嘟圓嘴唇接 [w]，中間不要停頓，也不要加母音。
homework.tip_en: The second half of homework, work, is [wɝk], with the tongue curled back — the same vowel as bird. Taiwanese learners often say walk [wɔk], which is a completely different word. The main stress is on home, with secondary stress on work. After the lips close for the [m] of home, round them straight into [w] — no pause and no vowel in between.

examples.en: I finish my homework before dinner.
examples.zh: 我在晚餐前寫完作業。

examples.en: Our teacher gave us a lot of homework today.
examples.zh: 老師今天給我們很多作業。

honest.tip_zh: honest 開頭的 h 不發音，第一個音就是嘴巴張大的 [ɑ]，所以要說 an honest boy，不是 a honest boy。常見錯誤是照拼字發出 [h]，或把字尾 [st] 唸成「斯特」，多加一個母音。第二音節的 [ə] 輕輕帶過，[s] 之後舌尖頂住上齒齦發 [t]，收在那裡就好。
honest.tip_en: The h at the start of honest is silent; the first sound is the open-mouthed [ɑ], so we say an honest boy, not a honest boy. A common mistake is pronouncing the [h] because of the spelling, or turning the final [st] into something like 'si-te' with an extra vowel. Pass lightly over the [ə] in the second syllable; after [s], press the tongue tip to the gum ridge for [t] and simply stop there.

examples.en: Tom is an honest boy.
examples.zh: 湯姆是個誠實的男孩。

examples.en: Please give me an honest answer.
examples.zh: 請給我一個誠實的回答。

honest.spelling_zh: 開頭的 h 不發音，和 hour 一樣。
honest.spelling_en: The h at the start is silent, just like in hour.

honey.tip_zh: honey 的 o 唸 [ʌ]，跟 money、funny 押韻，不是 home 的 [o]；台灣學生常照拼字唸成 [ˈhonɪ]。[ʌ] 是嘴巴微開、短促的音，下巴放鬆，嘴唇不要圓。重音在第一音節，拼字的 ey 唸輕短的 [ɪ]。叫家人 honey 時也是同樣的發音。
honey.tip_en: The o in honey says [ʌ], rhyming with money and funny — not the [o] of home; Taiwanese learners often follow the spelling and say [ˈhonɪ]. [ʌ] is a short sound with the mouth slightly open, jaw relaxed and lips unrounded. Stress the first syllable; the ey is a light, short [ɪ]. It's the same pronunciation when family members call each other honey.

examples.en: Bees make honey from flowers.
examples.zh: 蜜蜂用花朵做蜂蜜。

examples.en: I put some honey in my tea.
examples.zh: 我在茶裡加了一點蜂蜜。

honey.spelling_en: The o says [ʌ], as in money.

hope.tip_zh: hope 和 hop 只差母音：hope 是圓唇、會滑動的 [o]，hop 是張大嘴的 [ɑ]。字尾的 e 不發音，它的作用是提醒你 o 要唸 [o]。最後的 [p] 雙唇閉合、輕輕放氣；台灣學生常把 [p] 省掉，只剩下 hoe，或在後面多加一個母音。
hope.tip_en: hope and hop differ only in the vowel: hope has a rounded, gliding [o], hop has a wide-mouth [ɑ]. The final e is silent; its job is to tell you the o says [o]. Close the lips for the final [p] and release a little air; Taiwanese learners often drop the [p], leaving only "hoe", or add a vowel after it.

examples.en: I hope it will be sunny tomorrow.
examples.zh: 我希望明天是晴天。

examples.en: We hope you can come to our party.
examples.zh: 我們希望你能來參加我們的派對。

horse.tip_zh: horse 的 [ɔr] 要嘴唇先收成半圓唸 [ɔ]，再把舌頭往後捲；字尾是無聲的 [s]，不是 [z]。台灣學生常把它和 house [haʊs] 混在一起，或把 [r] 省掉。它和 course 押韻。複數 horses 會多一個音節，唸 [ˈhɔrsɪz]。
horse.tip_en: For [ɔr] in horse, first make the lips half round for [ɔ], then curl the tongue back; the ending is a voiceless [s], not [z]. Taiwanese learners often mix it up with house [haʊs] or leave out the [r]. It rhymes with course. The plural horses gains a syllable: [ˈhɔrsɪz].

examples.en: I rode a horse at my uncle's farm.
examples.zh: 我在叔叔的農場騎了馬。

examples.en: The white horse runs very fast.
examples.zh: 那匹白馬跑得很快。

hospital.tip_zh: 重音在第一音節 [ˈhɑs]，母音是嘴巴張大的 [ɑ]，學生常看到字母 o 就唸成圓唇的 [o]。字尾 -tal 也不要唸成 [tæl] 或加上清楚的母音；[tḷ] 是舌尖頂住上齒齦發完 [t] 後不放開，直接讓舌根往後抬，發出暗 L。中間的 [pɪ] 短而輕。
hospital.tip_en: The stress is on the first syllable [ˈhɑs], and its vowel is the open-mouthed [ɑ]; learners often see the letter o and say a rounded [o]. Don't say the ending -tal as [tæl] or with a clear vowel either: for [tḷ], press the tongue tip to the gum ridge for [t], keep it there, and raise the back of the tongue to make a dark L. The middle [pɪ] is short and light.

examples.en: My mom works at the hospital as a nurse.
examples.zh: 我媽媽在醫院當護士。

examples.en: The hospital is across from our school.
examples.zh: 醫院就在我們學校對面。

hospital.kk_flag: The secondary stress mark on the 2nd syllable (ˌspɪ) is a CMU artifact; standard GA/KK is [ˈhɑspɪtḷ] with no secondary stress.

hot.tip_zh: hot 的母音是 [ɑ]：下巴往下、嘴巴張大，舌頭放低，像看醫生時說「啊」。學生常照字母 o 唸成圓唇的 [o]，聽起來不像 hot。也要跟 hat 的 [æ] 分開：[æ] 嘴角往兩邊拉，[ɑ] 嘴巴上下拉開、嘴角不往旁邊拉。字尾 [t] 舌尖頂住上齒齦就停，不要加母音。
hot.tip_en: The vowel in hot is [ɑ]: drop the jaw, open the mouth wide and keep the tongue low, like saying 'ah' for the doctor. Learners often follow the letter o and use a rounded [o], which doesn't sound like hot. Also keep it apart from the [æ] in hat: for [æ] the corners of the mouth spread sideways; for [ɑ] the mouth opens up and down without spreading. For the final [t], touch the tongue tip to the gum ridge and stop; don't add a vowel.

examples.en: It is very hot today.
examples.zh: 今天非常熱。

examples.en: Be careful, the soup is hot!
examples.zh: 小心，湯很燙！

hotel.tip_zh: hotel 的重音在第二音節 [ˈtɛl]，學生常把重音放在第一音節，唸成 HO-tel。第一音節 [ho] 短而輕，第二音節拉長、音調升高。後半其實就是 tell：先說 tell，再在前面輕輕加上 [ho]。字尾的 l 是暗 L，舌尖頂上齒齦、舌根抬起，不要省略或唸成「喔」。
hotel.tip_en: The stress in hotel is on the second syllable [ˈtɛl]; learners often stress the first syllable and say HO-tel. The first syllable [ho] is short and light; the second is longer and higher in pitch. The second half is really just tell: say tell first, then add a light [ho] in front. The final l is a dark L: tongue tip on the gum ridge, back of the tongue raised; don't drop it or turn it into an 'o' sound.

examples.en: We stayed at a hotel near the beach.
examples.zh: 我們住在海灘附近的一家旅館。

examples.en: Our hotel room has a big window.
examples.zh: 我們的飯店房間有一扇大窗戶。

hour.tip_zh: hour 的 h 不發音，唸起來跟 our 一樣，所以要說 an hour。學生常照拼字在開頭加上 [h]，或只唸出 [aʊ] 就停，漏掉最後的 [r]。做法：嘴巴先張大發 [a]，再收圓滑到 [ʊ]，最後舌尖往後捲、不碰到任何地方，讓聲音帶出捲舌的 [r]。
hour.tip_en: The h in hour is silent; it sounds the same as our, so we say an hour. Learners often add an [h] because of the spelling, or stop at [aʊ] and leave out the final [r]. How to do it: open the mouth wide for [a], round it as you glide to [ʊ], and finally curl the tongue tip back without touching anything to add the r-colored [r].

examples.en: I read for an hour every night.
examples.zh: 我每天晚上閱讀一個小時。

examples.en: The bus comes once an hour.
examples.zh: 公車每小時來一班。

hour.spelling_zh: h 不發音，hour 與 our 同音。
hour.spelling_en: The h is silent; hour sounds the same as our.

house.tip_zh: house 當名詞時字尾是無聲的 [s]，跟 mouse 押韻；[aʊ] 要從大嘴的 [a] 滑到圓唇的 [ʊ]，台灣學生常滑得不夠，嘴唇沒收圓。要特別注意複數 houses：s 會變成有聲的 [z]，唸 [ˈhaʊzɪz]，不是 [ˈhaʊsɪz]。
house.tip_en: As a noun, house ends in a voiceless [s], rhyming with mouse. The [aʊ] slides from a wide [a] to rounded [ʊ]; Taiwanese learners often don't glide far enough and never round the lips. Watch the plural houses: the s becomes a voiced [z], so it's [ˈhaʊzɪz], not [ˈhaʊsɪz].

examples.en: My house has a small garden.
examples.zh: 我家有一個小花園。

examples.en: Let's draw a house with a red door.
examples.zh: 我們來畫一間有紅色門的房子。

housewife.tip_zh: housewife 是 house 加 wife，重音在 house，wife 是次重音。中間的 [s] 和 [w] 要接得順：[s] 嘶完，雙唇立刻嘟圓發 [w]，中間不要加母音。字尾 [f] 是上齒輕碰下唇吹氣，不要唸成 [v]，也不要多加母音。複數是 housewives。
housewife.tip_en: housewife is house plus wife, with the main stress on house and secondary stress on wife. The [s] and [w] in the middle must join smoothly: as the [s] hiss ends, round the lips straight into [w], with no vowel in between. The final [f] is the upper teeth lightly on the lower lip with air blowing — not [v], and no extra vowel. The plural is housewives.

examples.en: My aunt is a housewife with three kids.
examples.zh: 我阿姨是家庭主婦，有三個小孩。

examples.en: The housewife in the story bakes bread every morning.
examples.zh: 故事裡的家庭主婦每天早上烤麵包。

how.tip_zh: how 的 [aʊ] 要從張大嘴的 [a] 開始，最後收成圓唇；台灣學生常只唸到一半，聽起來像 ha。也有人嘴巴一開始就是圓的，結果和 who [hu] 分不清。拼字的 ow 在這裡跟 cow、now 一樣唸 [aʊ]，不是 grow 的 [o]。
how.tip_en: The [aʊ] in how starts from a wide-open [a] and ends with rounded lips; Taiwanese learners often say only half of it, so it sounds like "ha". Others start with rounded lips and it gets confused with who [hu]. The ow here says [aʊ], as in cow and now — not the [o] of grow.

examples.en: How are you today?
examples.zh: 你今天好嗎？

examples.en: How do you spell your name?
examples.zh: 你的名字怎麼拼？

how.spelling_zh: ow 唸 [aʊ]，不是 grow 的 [o]。
how.spelling_en: The ow says [aʊ], not the [o] of grow.

however.tip_zh: however 的重音在第二音節 [ˈɛ]，不是 how。學生常把 how 和 ever 拆開、中間停頓，或把 how 唸得最重。要連成一口氣：[haʊ] 的尾音自然滑進 [ɛ]。[v] 要上齒輕咬下唇並震動，不要唸成 [w] 或 [b]；結尾 [vɚ] 捲舌。練習時先說 ever，再在前面輕輕加上 how。
however.tip_en: The stress in however is on the second syllable [ˈɛ], not on how. Learners often split how and ever with a pause, or say how the loudest. Say it in one breath: the end of [haʊ] glides naturally into [ɛ]. For [v], lightly bite the lower lip with the upper teeth and let it buzz; don't turn it into [w] or [b]; the ending [vɚ] is r-colored. To practice, say ever first, then add a light how in front.

examples.en: I like apples. However, I don't like apple juice.
examples.zh: 我喜歡蘋果，不過我不喜歡蘋果汁。

examples.en: It was raining. However, we still played outside.
examples.zh: 當時在下雨，然而我們還是在外面玩。

hundred.tip_zh: hundred 重音在第一音節 [hʌn]，母音是短的 [ʌ]，後面的 [drəd] 要輕輕帶過。中間 [n]、[d]、[r] 三個子音連在一起，台灣學生常在 [d] 和 [r] 之間加母音，唸成三個音節，或把最後的 [d] 吞掉。舌尖頂牙齦發完 [nd] 後，立刻往後捲進 [r]。
hundred.tip_en: hundred is stressed on the first syllable [hʌn], with the short [ʌ]; the following [drəd] is touched lightly. Three consonants, [n], [d] and [r], run together in the middle; Taiwanese learners often add a vowel between [d] and [r], making three syllables, or swallow the final [d]. After the tongue tip finishes [nd] on the ridge, curl it straight back into [r].

examples.en: There are one hundred students in our grade.
examples.zh: 我們年級有一百個學生。

examples.en: My grandma is almost one hundred years old.
examples.zh: 我奶奶快一百歲了。

hundred.variant_en: In casual speech [ˈhʌndɚd] is also common.

hungry.tip_zh: hungry 中間是 [ŋg]：舌根抬起頂住軟顎發鼻音 [ŋ]，再在同一個位置放出 [g]，接著捲舌發 [r]。台灣學生常把 [ŋ] 唸成 [n]，或把 [g] 漏掉。第一音節的母音是短的 [ʌ]，不是 [ɑ]；別和 angry [ˈæŋgrɪ] 搞混，angry 開頭嘴巴張得比較大。
hungry.tip_en: The middle of hungry is [ŋg]: raise the back of the tongue to the soft palate for the nasal [ŋ], then release [g] from the same spot, followed by a curled [r]. Taiwanese learners often turn [ŋ] into [n] or leave out the [g]. The first vowel is the short [ʌ], not [ɑ]; don't confuse it with angry [ˈæŋgrɪ], which opens the mouth wider at the start.

examples.en: I'm hungry. Can we eat now?
examples.zh: 我肚子餓了，我們可以吃飯了嗎？

examples.en: The hungry puppy ate all its food.
examples.zh: 那隻餓壞的小狗把食物全吃光了。

hunt.tip_zh: hunt 字尾是 [nt]：舌尖頂住上排牙齦發 [n]，舌頭不要動，直接把氣擋住收 [t]。台灣學生常只唸到 [n]，變成 [hʌn]，或在最後多加母音。母音是短的 [ʌ]，跟 front 押韻。美式口語裡 [t] 有時很輕，但 [n] 結尾時舌尖停住的感覺一定要有。
hunt.tip_en: hunt ends in [nt]: press the tongue tip on the ridge behind the upper teeth for [n], keep the tongue still, and block the air for [t]. Taiwanese learners often stop at [n], giving [hʌn], or add a vowel at the end. The vowel is the short [ʌ], rhyming with front. In casual American speech the [t] can be very light, but the stop with the tongue tip held at the end of [n] must be there.

examples.en: We hunt for seashells on the beach.
examples.zh: 我們在沙灘上找貝殼。

examples.en: The kids hunt for eggs in the garden at Easter.
examples.zh: 復活節時孩子們在花園裡找彩蛋。

hurry.tip_zh: hurry 第一音節是捲舌的 [ɝ]，跟 bird、her 的母音一樣，嘴巴不用張大；台灣學生常唸成 [hʌ] 再加 [r]，聽起來像「哈瑞」。正確是一開口舌頭就捲好，保持捲舌，直接滑到輕短的 [ɪ]。拼字的 rr 只唸一次 [r]。它和 worry [ˈwɝɪ] 押韻。
hurry.tip_en: The first syllable of hurry is the r-colored [ɝ], the same vowel as bird and her, with no need to open the mouth wide. Taiwanese learners often say [hʌ] and then add [r], so it sounds like "ha-ree". Instead, have the tongue curled from the very start, keep it curled, and slide straight into a light, short [ɪ]. The double rr is said only once. It rhymes with worry [ˈwɝɪ].

examples.en: Hurry up, or we will miss the bus!
examples.zh: 快一點，不然我們會趕不上公車！

examples.en: There's no need to hurry. We have time.
examples.zh: 不用急，我們還有時間。

hurt.tip_zh: hurt 的 [ɝ] 嘴巴只微微打開、舌頭捲起來，跟 shirt、skirt 押韻；台灣學生常把嘴巴張太大，唸得像 heart [hɑrt]。兩個字對照：heart 先張大嘴唸 [ɑ] 才捲舌，hurt 一開始就捲舌。字尾 [t] 舌尖頂住牙齦收住，不要省掉。
hurt.tip_en: For the [ɝ] in hurt, the mouth opens only slightly and the tongue curls back, rhyming with shirt and skirt. Taiwanese learners often open the mouth too wide, so it sounds like heart [hɑrt]. Compare the two: heart opens wide for [ɑ] before curling, hurt is curled from the start. Close the final [t] with the tongue tip on the ridge — don't drop it.

examples.en: Does your arm still hurt?
examples.zh: 你的手臂還會痛嗎？

examples.en: Be careful, or you will hurt your hand.
examples.zh: 小心點，不然你會弄傷手。

husband.tip_zh: husband 的 s 唸有聲的 [z]，不是 [s]，台灣學生常照拼字唸成 [hʌs]。[z] 之後雙唇閉合發 [b]，兩個子音都要讓喉嚨震動。重音在第一音節，後面的 band 要弱化成 [bənd]，不要唸成單字 band [bænd]；字尾 [nd] 的 [d] 也別漏掉。
husband.tip_en: The s in husband is a voiced [z], not [s]; Taiwanese learners often follow the spelling and say [hʌs]. After [z], close the lips for [b] — both consonants buzz in the throat. Stress the first syllable; the band part reduces to [bənd], not the word band [bænd], and don't drop the [d] of the final [nd].

examples.en: Mrs. Lin and her husband run a bakery.
examples.zh: 林太太和她先生開了一家麵包店。

examples.en: Her husband cooks dinner on weekends.
examples.zh: 她先生週末會煮晚餐。

i.tip_zh: I 是雙母音 [aɪ]：從嘴巴張大的 [a] 滑到 [ɪ]，嘴角最後微微往兩邊拉。學生常把它唸成中文「愛」的第四聲，又短又重、音調往下掉，句子聽起來像在生氣。在句子裡 I 通常輕而平，重音放在後面的動詞：說 I like it 時，把 like 唸重，I 輕輕帶過，但滑音仍要做完整。
i.tip_en: I is the diphthong [aɪ]: glide from an open-mouthed [a] to [ɪ], with the corners of the mouth spreading slightly at the end. Learners often say it like the Mandarin 'ài' with a fourth tone—short, heavy and falling—which makes the sentence sound angry. In a sentence, I is usually light and level, and the stress goes on the verb after it: in I like it, stress like and pass lightly over I, but still finish the glide.

examples.en: I have a little brother.
examples.zh: 我有一個弟弟。

examples.en: I like to draw pictures after school.
examples.zh: 我喜歡放學後畫畫。

ice.tip_zh: ice 只有一個音節：[aɪ] 之後接 [s] 就結束，台灣學生常在 [s] 後面加母音，唸成兩拍。[aɪ] 要從大嘴的 [a] 滑向 [ɪ]，字尾的 e 不發音。特別注意 ice 和 eyes [aɪz] 只差字尾：ice 是無聲的 [s]，像漏氣聲；eyes 是有聲的 [z]，像蜜蜂嗡嗡聲。
ice.tip_en: ice has only one syllable: [aɪ] followed by [s], and that's it. Taiwanese learners often add a vowel after the [s], making two beats. Slide [aɪ] from a wide [a] toward [ɪ]; the final e is silent. Note that ice and eyes [aɪz] differ only at the end: ice has a voiceless [s], like air leaking; eyes has a voiced [z], like a buzzing bee.

examples.en: Do you want ice in your juice?
examples.zh: 你的果汁要加冰塊嗎？

examples.en: The ice on the lake is very thick.
examples.zh: 湖面上的冰很厚。

idea.tip_zh: idea 有三個音節 [aɪ]·[di]·[ə]，重音在第二音節 [ˈdi]。學生常把重音放在開頭的 [aɪ]，或漏掉最後的 [ə]，只唸兩個音節，聽起來像 I-dee。[di] 要拉長、音調拉高；結尾的 [ə] 嘴巴放鬆微張，輕輕發出來就好，不要捲舌加 [r]。
idea.tip_en: idea has three syllables, [aɪ]·[di]·[ə], with the stress on the second, [ˈdi]. Learners often stress the opening [aɪ], or drop the final [ə] and say only two syllables, which sounds like I-dee. Make [di] long and high in pitch; for the final [ə], relax the mouth, open it slightly and say it softly—don't curl the tongue and add an [r].

examples.en: That is a great idea!
examples.zh: 那是個很棒的主意！

examples.en: Who has an idea for the class party?
examples.zh: 誰對班級派對有想法？

if.tip_zh: if 的 [ɪ] 短而放鬆，嘴巴不要拉成 [i]，否則聽起來像 eef。字尾 [f] 要上排牙齒輕碰下唇、吹氣摩擦，台灣學生常在 [f] 後面多加母音，或把 [f] 唸得太弱，結果和 it、in 分不清。句子裡的 if 又輕又快，但 [f] 的摩擦聲仍然要留著。
if.tip_en: The [ɪ] in if is short and relaxed — don't spread the mouth into [i], or it sounds like "eef". For the final [f], the upper teeth touch the lower lip lightly and air rubs through; Taiwanese learners often add a vowel after the [f] or make it too weak, so it can't be told apart from it or in. In a sentence if is quick and light, but the friction of [f] must stay.

examples.en: If it rains, we will stay inside.
examples.zh: 如果下雨，我們就待在室內。

examples.en: Ask me if you need help.
examples.zh: 如果你需要幫忙就問我。

important.tip_zh: important 的重音在第二音節 [ˈpɔr]，[ɪm] 短而輕，[pɔr] 要捲舌。學生常把字尾 -tant 唸成「疼特」，多加一個完整的母音。[tṇt] 的做法：舌尖頂住上齒齦發 [t] 後不要放開，讓氣直接從鼻子出來變成 [ṇ]，最後再輕輕放出 [t]。整個字只有 [pɔr] 是重的。
important.tip_en: The stress in important is on the second syllable [ˈpɔr]; [ɪm] is short and light, and [pɔr] needs the curled r. Learners often say the ending -tant like 'teng-te', adding a full vowel. For [tṇt]: press the tongue tip on the gum ridge for [t] and don't let go; let the air go straight out through the nose to make [ṇ], and finally release a light [t]. Only [pɔr] is strong in the whole word.

examples.en: Breakfast is an important meal.
examples.zh: 早餐是很重要的一餐。

examples.en: It is important to wash your hands.
examples.zh: 洗手是很重要的。

in.tip_zh: in 的 [ɪ] 短而放鬆，舌頭比 [i] 低，嘴角不要拉開；字尾 [n] 舌尖頂住上排牙齦，不要往後縮成 [ŋ]。台灣學生常照中文「因」的感覺唸，母音太緊、太長。它和 win、pin 押韻；in 和 on 只差母音，on 要張大嘴唸 [ɑ]。
in.tip_en: The [ɪ] in in is short and relaxed, with the tongue lower than for [i] and the mouth corners not spread; for the final [n], the tongue tip presses the ridge behind the upper teeth — don't pull back into [ŋ]. Taiwanese learners often say it like a Mandarin syllable, with a vowel that is too tense and too long. It rhymes with win and pin; in and on differ only in the vowel — on opens wide for [ɑ].

examples.en: My pencil is in my bag.
examples.zh: 我的鉛筆在書包裡。

examples.en: We swim in the pool in summer.
examples.zh: 我們夏天在游泳池游泳。

inch.tip_zh: inch 字尾是 [ntʃ]：舌尖先頂住牙齦發 [n]，接著舌面往上抬、嘴唇微微嘟起，送出 [tʃ]。台灣學生常把 [n] 省掉，唸成 itch [ɪtʃ]，或在 [tʃ] 後面多加母音。開頭的 [ɪ] 要短而放鬆。複數 inches 唸 [ˈɪntʃɪz]，多一個音節。
inch.tip_en: inch ends in [ntʃ]: first the tongue tip presses the ridge for [n], then the front of the tongue rises and the lips push out slightly to release [tʃ]. Taiwanese learners often drop the [n] and say itch [ɪtʃ], or add a vowel after [tʃ]. The opening [ɪ] is short and relaxed. The plural inches is [ˈɪntʃɪz], one syllable longer.

examples.en: This line is one inch long.
examples.zh: 這條線長一英吋。

examples.en: The plant grew an inch this week.
examples.zh: 這株植物這星期長高了一英吋。

insect.tip_zh: insect 重音在第一音節 in，sect 是次重音。字尾是 [kt] 兩個子音：舌根頂住軟顎發 [k]，不要放出太多氣，緊接著舌尖頂住牙齦收 [t]。台灣學生常只唸 [k] 或只唸 [t]，或在中間加母音。第二音節的 [ɛ] 嘴巴半開，不要唸成 [æ]。
insect.tip_en: insect has its main stress on the first syllable, in, with secondary stress on sect. It ends in two consonants, [kt]: the back of the tongue presses the soft palate for [k], without much air released, and then the tongue tip closes on the ridge for [t]. Taiwanese learners often say only [k] or only [t], or put a vowel between them. The [ɛ] in the second syllable is half open — not [æ].

examples.en: An ant is a small insect.
examples.zh: 螞蟻是一種小昆蟲。

examples.en: We found an insect with six legs in the garden.
examples.zh: 我們在花園裡發現一隻六隻腳的昆蟲。

inside.tip_zh: 當「在…裡面」用時，inside 重音在第二音節 side：in 輕短，side 響亮、拉長。台灣學生常把兩個音節唸得一樣重，或把字尾 [d] 吞掉。[n] 舌尖頂住牙齦後，直接滑到 [s]，中間不要加母音。可以和 outside 一起練，兩個字重音位置相同。
inside.tip_en: Used as "inside of", inside is stressed on the second syllable, side: in is light and short, side is loud and long. Taiwanese learners often give both syllables equal weight or swallow the final [d]. After the tongue tip presses the ridge for [n], slide straight into [s] with no vowel in between. Practice it alongside outside — both words have the stress in the same place.

examples.en: The cat is sleeping inside the box.
examples.zh: 貓咪在箱子裡睡覺。

examples.en: It's cold, so let's play inside the house.
examples.zh: 外面很冷，我們在屋子裡玩吧。

inside.variant_zh: 當名詞或形容詞（the inside）時常唸 [ˈɪnˌsaɪd]，重音在前。
inside.variant_en: As a noun or adjective (the inside) it's often [ˈɪnˌsaɪd], stressed first.

interest.tip_zh: interest 拼字看起來有三個母音，但美式英語常唸成兩個音節 [ˈɪn·trəst]，中間的 e 幾乎消失。重音在第一音節 in；台灣學生常把重音放到中間，唸成 in-TER-est。字尾 [st] 兩個子音都要唸出來，[s] 之後舌尖頂住牙齦收 [t]，不要多加母音。
interest.tip_en: interest looks like it has three vowels, but American English often says it in two syllables, [ˈɪn·trəst], with the middle e nearly gone. The stress is on the first syllable, in; Taiwanese learners often move it to the middle, saying in-TER-est. Both consonants of the final [st] must be heard: after [s], close with the tongue tip on the ridge for [t], with no added vowel.

examples.en: Does this book interest you?
examples.zh: 這本書讓你感興趣嗎？

examples.en: Dinosaurs really interest my little brother.
examples.zh: 我弟弟對恐龍非常感興趣。

interest.variant_en: It can also be said in three syllables: [ˈɪntɚəst].
interest.spelling_zh: 中間的 e 常常不發音。
interest.spelling_en: The middle e is often not pronounced.

interested.tip_zh: interested 的重音在第一音節 [ˈɪn]。學生最常把重音移到中間的 rest，唸成 in-ter-REST-ed。美式口語常唸成三個音節，ter 的母音省掉，[t] 直接連 [r]，就像 tree 開頭的 [tr]。字尾 -ed 唸 [ɪd]，因為前面是 [t]，要多一個小音節，不能只加 [d]，也別和 interesting 搞混。
interested.tip_en: The stress in interested is on the first syllable [ˈɪn]. The most common mistake is moving it to rest in the middle: in-ter-REST-ed. In everyday American speech it is often three syllables: the vowel of ter drops out and [t] joins straight onto [r], like the [tr] at the start of tree. The ending -ed is [ɪd] because it follows [t], so it adds a small syllable—don't just add [d]—and don't mix it up with interesting.

examples.en: I am interested in dinosaurs.
examples.zh: 我對恐龍很有興趣。

examples.en: Are you interested in joining the art club?
examples.zh: 你有興趣參加美術社嗎？

interested.variant_zh: 也常聽到四個音節的 [ˈɪntɚɪstɪd]，兩種都正確。
interested.variant_en: A four-syllable [ˈɪntɚɪstɪd] is also common; both are correct.

interesting.tip_zh: interesting 只有開頭的 [ˈɪn] 是重的，後面全部輕輕帶過，不要把 rest 唸得最響。字尾 [ɪŋ] 是舌根往上頂住軟顎的鼻音，嘴巴保持微開，學生常把它唸成舌尖的 [n]，或在最後多發一個 [g]。可以想 sing 的結尾。分清 interesting 的 [ɪŋ] 和 interested 的 [ɪd]，意思才不會說錯。
interesting.tip_en: Only the opening [ˈɪn] in interesting is strong; everything after it is light—don't make rest the loudest part. The final [ɪŋ] is a nasal made by raising the back of the tongue against the soft palate with the mouth slightly open; learners often turn it into a tongue-tip [n] or add an extra [g] at the end. Think of the end of sing. Keep the [ɪŋ] of interesting apart from the [ɪd] of interested, so the meaning comes out right.

examples.en: This book is really interesting.
examples.zh: 這本書真的很有趣。

examples.en: We watched an interesting video about whales.
examples.zh: 我們看了一部關於鯨魚的有趣影片。

interesting.variant_zh: 也常聽到四個音節的 [ˈɪntɚɪstɪŋ]，兩種都對。
interesting.variant_en: A four-syllable [ˈɪntɚɪstɪŋ] is also common; both are fine.

internet.tip_zh: Internet 的重音在第一音節 [ˈɪn]，最後的 [nɛt] 只是次重音，不要唸得比開頭還重。中間的 [tɚ] 要捲舌：舌尖往後捲、不碰上顎，學生常唸成平平的「特」。字尾 [t] 舌尖頂住上齒齦就停，不要加母音變成「內特」。net 跟 get、pet 押韻，可以先練這幾個字。
internet.tip_en: The stress in Internet is on the first syllable [ˈɪn]; the final [nɛt] has only secondary stress, so don't make it stronger than the start. The middle [tɚ] needs the curled r: curl the tongue tip back without touching the roof of the mouth; learners often say a flat 'te'. For the final [t], put the tongue tip on the gum ridge and stop—don't add a vowel to make it 'nei-te'. net rhymes with get and pet, so practice those first.

examples.en: We use the Internet to do homework.
examples.zh: 我們用網路寫功課。

examples.en: My grandpa learned to use the Internet.
examples.zh: 我爺爺學會了用網路。

interview.tip_zh: view 的開頭是 [vj]：上齒輕咬下唇發出震動的 [v]，再滑進 [ju]。學生常把 [v] 唸成 [w]，或漏掉 [j]，只剩 [vu]。[vju] 跟 few 的 [fju] 嘴型一樣，只是喉嚨要震動。重音在第一音節 [ˈɪn]，中間 [tɚ] 捲舌，view 是次重音，不要唸成 in-ter-VIEW。
interview.tip_en: view starts with [vj]: lightly bite the lower lip with the upper teeth for a buzzing [v], then glide into [ju]. Learners often turn [v] into [w], or drop the [j] and say only [vu]. [vju] uses the same mouth shape as the [fju] in few—just add voice in the throat. The stress is on the first syllable [ˈɪn], the middle [tɚ] is r-colored, and view takes only secondary stress—don't say in-ter-VIEW.

examples.en: My sister has a job interview today.
examples.zh: 我姊姊今天有工作面試。

examples.en: Our class will interview the school principal.
examples.zh: 我們班要訪問校長。

into.tip_zh: into 重音在第一音節 in，to 要輕輕帶過；台灣學生常把 in 和 to 分開唸成兩個字，或把重音放在 to。[n] 和 [t] 都是舌尖頂在上排牙齦，可以在同一個位置連續完成，中間不要停頓。在句子裡 to 常弱化，例如 Come into the room。
into.tip_en: into is stressed on the first syllable, in, and to is touched lightly. Taiwanese learners often say in and to as two separate words, or stress to. Both [n] and [t] are made with the tongue tip on the ridge behind the upper teeth, so do them in one spot without a break. In a sentence the to often weakens, as in Come into the room.

examples.en: The frog jumped into the pond.
examples.zh: 青蛙跳進了池塘。

examples.en: Please put the toys into the box.
examples.zh: 請把玩具放進箱子裡。

into.variant_en: In sentences it's often weakened to [ˈɪntə].

invite.tip_zh: invite 重音在第二音節 vite，in 要輕；台灣學生常把重音放在 in。[n] 之後要馬上把上齒輕放在下唇上發 [v]，喉嚨震動，不要唸成 [b] 或 [w]。接著 [aɪ] 拉開，最後舌尖頂牙齦收 [t]，跟 kite、night 押韻。
invite.tip_en: invite is stressed on the second syllable, vite, and in is light; Taiwanese learners often stress in. Right after [n], rest the upper teeth lightly on the lower lip for [v] with the throat buzzing — not [b] or [w]. Then open into [aɪ] and close with the tongue tip on the ridge for [t], rhyming with kite and night.

examples.en: I want to invite Amy to my birthday party.
examples.zh: 我想邀請 Amy 來我的生日派對。

examples.en: Let's invite our neighbors for dinner.
examples.zh: 我們邀請鄰居來吃晚餐吧。

island.tip_zh: island 的 s 不發音，唸 [ˈaɪlənd]。學生常照拼字唸成 [ˈaɪslənd]，多出一個 [s]。前半其實就是 I [aɪ]，後面接一個很輕的 [lənd]，[ə] 短到幾乎聽不見。字尾 [nd] 兩個子音都要有：舌尖頂上齒齦發 [n]，再輕輕放出 [d]，不要加母音變成「的」。
island.tip_en: The s in island is silent: say [ˈaɪlənd]. Learners often follow the spelling and say [ˈaɪslənd] with an extra [s]. The first half is just I [aɪ], followed by a very light [lənd] whose [ə] is so short it is almost silent. Both consonants of the final [nd] are needed: tongue tip on the gum ridge for [n], then a light release for [d]—don't add a vowel like 'de'.

examples.en: Taiwan is a beautiful island.
examples.zh: 台灣是一座美麗的島嶼。

examples.en: We took a boat to a small island.
examples.zh: 我們搭船去一座小島。

island.spelling_zh: s 不發音，is- 唸起來跟 I 一樣。
island.spelling_en: The s is silent; is- sounds just like I.

it.tip_zh: it 和 eat 是一組：it 的 [ɪ] 短而放鬆，eat 的 [i] 嘴角拉開又長。台灣學生常把 it 唸得太緊太長，聽起來像 eat。句子裡的 it 通常很輕，字尾 [t] 常只閉住不放氣，例如 Is it fun? 的 [t]，但舌尖還是要碰到牙齦，不能整個消失。
it.tip_en: it and eat are a pair: the [ɪ] of it is short and relaxed, the [i] of eat is long with the mouth corners spread. Taiwanese learners often make it too tense and long, so it sounds like eat. In a sentence it is usually light, and the final [t] is often held without releasing air, as in Is it fun?, but the tongue tip must still touch the ridge — the [t] can't disappear completely.

examples.en: It is my turn to read.
examples.zh: 輪到我朗讀了。

examples.en: I found my ball. It was under the table.
examples.zh: 我找到我的球了，它在桌子底下。

item.tip_zh: 重音在第一音節 [aɪ]，要從張大嘴的 [a] 滑到 [ɪ]，不能只唸一個「啊」。第二音節 [təm] 很輕，母音弱化成 [ə]，容易照拼字唸成清楚的 [tɛm]。美式口語中 [t] 夾在兩個母音之間，會變成舌尖輕點一下的彈音，聽起來接近輕的 d。最後的 [m] 雙唇要閉上停住。
item.tip_en: Stress the first syllable [aɪ], gliding from an open [a] to [ɪ] — not just one 'ah'. The second syllable [təm] is light, with the vowel reduced to [ə]; learners tend to follow the spelling and say a clear [tɛm]. In everyday American speech, [t] between two vowels becomes a quick tap of the tongue tip that sounds close to a light d. Close the lips firmly on the final [m].

examples.en: Please check every item on the list.
examples.zh: 請檢查清單上的每一個項目。

examples.en: The first item in my bag is a water bottle.
examples.zh: 我包包裡的第一樣東西是水壺。

jacket.tip_zh: 第一音節 [æ] 要把下巴拉低、嘴角往兩旁咧開，和 cat 的母音一樣；容易唸成嘴巴較小的 [ɛ]，聽起來像 jecket。第二音節 [kət] 很輕，母音弱化成 [ə]，不要唸成清楚的 [kɛt]。字尾 [t] 舌尖頂住上齒齦就停，不要多加一個母音。
jacket.tip_en: The first syllable's [æ] needs the jaw dropped and the lip corners pulled wide, the same vowel as in cat; learners often use the smaller [ɛ], so it sounds like 'jecket'. The second syllable [kət] is light with a reduced [ə] — don't say a clear [kɛt]. For the final [t], press the tongue tip to the gum ridge and stop; don't add a vowel.

examples.en: Put on your jacket before you go outside.
examples.zh: 出門前先穿上你的夾克。

examples.en: My new jacket has two big pockets.
examples.zh: 我的新夾克有兩個大口袋。

january.tip_zh: January 的重音在第一音節 [ˈdʒæn]，[æ] 要下巴往下、嘴角往兩邊拉，學生常唸成比較窄的 [ɛ]。[dʒ] 嘴唇微微往前嘟，舌尖放在上齒齦後面。後半 -uary 是 [ju] 加上 [ˌɛrɪ]，[ɛrɪ] 跟 very 的後半一樣，帶次重音，不要把主要重音移到最後。
january.tip_en: The stress in January is on the first syllable [ˈdʒæn]; for [æ], drop the jaw and spread the corners of the mouth—learners often use the narrower [ɛ]. For [dʒ], push the lips slightly forward with the tongue tip just behind the gum ridge. The second half -uary is [ju] plus [ˌɛrɪ]; [ɛrɪ] is the same as the end of very and carries secondary stress—don't move the main stress to the end.

examples.en: My birthday is in January.
examples.zh: 我的生日在一月。

examples.en: It is very cold in January.
examples.zh: 一月非常冷。

jeans.tip_zh: 字尾是 [n] 和 [z] 兩個子音連在一起：舌尖先頂住上齒齦發 [n]，接著舌尖留在附近，讓喉嚨繼續振動擦出 [z]。容易把 [z] 漏掉，或唸成無聲的 [s]。前面的 [i] 是長而緊的母音，嘴角往兩邊拉開，和 see 的母音一樣，要唸得夠長。
jeans.tip_en: The word ends in two consonants, [n] then [z]: put the tongue tip on the gum ridge for [n], then keep it close by and let the voice keep buzzing into [z]. Learners often drop the [z] or turn it into a voiceless [s]. The [i] before it is long and tense — spread the lips like the vowel in see, and hold it long enough.

examples.en: I like to wear jeans on the weekend.
examples.zh: 我週末喜歡穿牛仔褲。

examples.en: These blue jeans are too long for me.
examples.zh: 這件藍色牛仔褲對我來說太長了。

job.tip_zh: 母音是 [ɑ]，下巴要張大、嘴唇不圓，像看醫生時張嘴說「啊」；容易受拼字 o 影響唸成圓唇的 [o]。字尾 [b] 雙唇閉上後輕輕放開即可，不要多加母音變成兩個音節。也要和 jog 分清楚：job 結尾是雙唇閉合的 [b]，jog 結尾是舌根頂住軟顎的 [g]。
job.tip_en: The vowel is [ɑ]: open the jaw wide with unrounded lips, like saying 'ah' for the doctor; the letter o tempts learners into a rounded [o]. For the final [b], close the lips and release gently — don't add a vowel that makes a second syllable. Keep it apart from jog: job ends with closed lips [b], jog ends with the back of the tongue against the soft palate [g].

examples.en: My dad's job is in Taipei.
examples.zh: 我爸爸的工作在台北。

examples.en: You did a great job on your poster!
examples.zh: 你的海報做得很棒！

jog.tip_zh: 字尾 [g] 是有聲子音，舌根抬起頂住軟顎，喉嚨要有振動；容易唸成無聲的 [k]，聽起來像 jock。前面的 [ɑ] 嘴巴張大、嘴唇不圓，和 frog 的母音一樣，可以先唸 frog 再換開頭。和 job 只差最後一個音：jog 結尾時嘴唇是張開的，不要閉上。
jog.tip_en: The final [g] is voiced: raise the back of the tongue to the soft palate and keep the throat buzzing; learners often make it a voiceless [k], so it sounds like 'jock'. The [ɑ] before it is wide open with unrounded lips, the same vowel as in frog — say frog first, then swap the beginning. It differs from job only in the last sound: for jog the lips stay open at the end.

examples.en: My mom and I jog in the park every morning.
examples.zh: 我媽媽和我每天早上在公園慢跑。

examples.en: Let's jog around the track two times.
examples.zh: 我們繞操場慢跑兩圈吧。

join.tip_zh: 母音 [ɔɪ] 是雙母音：先把嘴唇收圓發 [ɔ]，再滑向嘴角展開的 [ɪ]，嘴形要有明顯的變化，和 boy 的母音相同。字尾 [n] 要用舌尖頂住上齒齦收住；容易改用舌根收成 [ŋ]，聽起來像 joing。也別和 June [dʒun] 混淆，June 只有一個長 [u]，沒有滑動。
join.tip_en: [ɔɪ] is a two-part vowel: start with rounded lips for [ɔ], then glide to spread lips for [ɪ] — the mouth shape must clearly change, as in boy. End on [n] with the tongue tip on the gum ridge; learners often close with the back of the tongue instead, giving [ŋ] ('joing'). Don't mix it up with June [dʒun], which has a single long [u] and no glide.

examples.en: Do you want to join our team?
examples.zh: 你想加入我們的隊伍嗎？

examples.en: Ten new students will join the music club.
examples.zh: 會有十位新同學加入音樂社。

joke.tip_zh: 母音 [o] 嘴唇要收圓、聲音拉長，結尾嘴唇再稍微往內收一點，不要唸得又短又扁。拼字結尾的 e 不發音，它的作用是讓 o 唸成 [o]，所以 joke 和 smoke 押韻。字尾 [k] 舌根頂住軟顎就停，容易在後面多加一個母音，讓一個音節的字變成兩個音節。
joke.tip_en: For [o], round the lips and hold the sound, letting the lips close in a little at the end — don't make it short and flat. The final e is silent; it only tells you the o says [o], which is why joke rhymes with smoke. For the final [k], press the back of the tongue to the soft palate and stop; learners often add a vowel after it, turning a one-syllable word into two.

examples.en: My brother told a funny joke at dinner.
examples.zh: 我哥哥在晚餐時說了一個好笑的笑話。

examples.en: Do you know a good joke about cats?
examples.zh: 你知道關於貓的好笑話嗎？

joy.tip_zh: 開頭 [dʒ] 嘴唇要微微往前噘、舌面貼近上齒齦後方；容易直接用中文較扁的ㄐ代替，嘴唇沒有噘起，聲音聽起來太細。母音 [ɔɪ] 從圓唇的 [ɔ] 滑到 [ɪ]，和 boy、toy 押韻：可以先說 boy，再把開頭的 [b] 換成 [dʒ]。
joy.tip_en: For the opening [dʒ], push the lips slightly forward and raise the tongue toward the area just behind the gum ridge; learners often substitute the flatter Mandarin ㄐ without rounding the lips, which sounds too thin. The vowel [ɔɪ] glides from rounded [ɔ] to [ɪ] and rhymes with boy and toy: say boy first, then swap the opening [b] for [dʒ].

examples.en: The baby laughed with joy at the bubbles.
examples.zh: 小嬰兒看到泡泡開心地笑了。

examples.en: Reading gives my grandma a lot of joy.
examples.zh: 閱讀帶給我奶奶很多快樂。

juice.tip_zh: 拼字 ui 在這裡只唸一個長母音 [u]，嘴唇噘圓、往前推，不要唸成 [u] 再加 [ɪ] 的兩個音。字尾是無聲的 [s]，只有氣流、喉嚨不振動；容易唸成有聲的 [z]，或在後面多加母音。和 goose 押韻，可以用 goose 練同樣的 [us] 結尾。
juice.tip_en: The letters ui stand for just one long vowel here, [u]: round and push the lips forward — don't say [u] plus [ɪ] as two sounds. The ending is a voiceless [s], air only with no buzz in the throat; learners often voice it as [z] or add a vowel after it. It rhymes with goose, so practice the same [us] ending with goose.

examples.en: I drink orange juice with my breakfast.
examples.zh: 我早餐時喝柳橙汁。

examples.en: Can I have some apple juice, please?
examples.zh: 可以給我一些蘋果汁嗎？

juice.spelling_zh: ui 只唸一個 [u]；字尾 e 不發音。
juice.spelling_en: ui says one sound, [u]; the final e is silent.

july.tip_zh: 重音在第二音節 [laɪ]，第一音節 [dʒu] 要輕而短；若把重音放在前面，聽起來會像女生的名字 Julie。[laɪ] 要從張大嘴的 [a] 滑到 [ɪ]，和 fly、high 押韻。注意拼字雖然是 y 結尾，這裡唸的是 [aɪ]，不是 [ɪ]。
july.tip_en: The stress falls on the second syllable [laɪ]; the first syllable [dʒu] is short and light. Put the stress up front and it sounds like the girl's name Julie. [laɪ] glides from an open [a] to [ɪ] and rhymes with fly and high. Note that although the word ends in the letter y, it says [aɪ] here, not [ɪ].

examples.en: Summer vacation starts in July.
examples.zh: 暑假在七月開始。

examples.en: My birthday is on July tenth.
examples.zh: 我的生日是七月十日。

july.variant_zh: 口語快說時，第一音節常弱化成 [dʒəˈlaɪ]。
july.variant_en: In fast speech the first syllable often weakens: [dʒəˈlaɪ].

jump.tip_zh: 母音 [ʌ] 短而放鬆，嘴巴半開，和 cup 的母音一樣，不要唸成圓唇的 [u] 或 [o]。字尾 [mp] 兩個音都用嘴唇：雙唇閉上發 [m]，再在同一個位置憋住氣、輕輕放開成 [p]。容易唸到 [m] 就停，漏掉 [p]，或在 [p] 後面多加母音。
jump.tip_en: [ʌ] is short and relaxed with the mouth half open, the same vowel as in cup — don't round it into [u] or [o]. Both sounds of the final [mp] use the lips: close them for [m], then hold the air in the same spot and release it gently as [p]. Learners often stop at [m] and lose the [p], or add a vowel after [p].

examples.en: Can you jump over this rope?
examples.zh: 你可以跳過這條繩子嗎？

examples.en: The kids jump into the pool together.
examples.zh: 孩子們一起跳進游泳池。

june.tip_zh: 母音 [u] 要長、嘴唇噘圓往前推，和 moon、soon 押韻。字尾 [n] 用舌尖頂住上齒齦收尾，讓聲音從鼻子出來；容易改用舌根收成 [ŋ]，或舌尖還沒碰到就結束。也要和 join [dʒɔɪn] 分開：June 只有一個長母音 [u]，嘴形從頭到尾不變。
june.tip_en: Make [u] long, with the lips rounded and pushed forward; it rhymes with moon and soon. Finish [n] with the tongue tip on the gum ridge and the sound through the nose; learners often close with the back of the tongue ([ŋ]) or stop before the tongue tip touches. Keep it apart from join [dʒɔɪn]: June has one long vowel [u] and the mouth shape doesn't change.

examples.en: School ends in June this year.
examples.zh: 今年學校在六月結束。

examples.en: We will visit Grandpa in June.
examples.zh: 我們六月會去看爺爺。

just.tip_zh: 母音 [ʌ] 短而放鬆，和 must 押韻。重點在字尾 [st]：先送出只有氣流的 [s]，舌尖不要放鬆，直接往上頂住上齒齦，停成 [t]。容易漏掉 [t] 只剩 [s]，或在後面加母音變成兩個音節。把 must 和 just 一起練，結尾的動作完全相同。
just.tip_en: [ʌ] is short and relaxed; the word rhymes with must. The key is the final [st]: push out air-only [s], then without relaxing, raise the tongue tip to the gum ridge and stop on [t]. Learners often drop the [t] and leave only [s], or add a vowel that makes a second syllable. Practice must and just together — the ending movement is exactly the same.

examples.en: I just finished my homework.
examples.zh: 我剛剛寫完功課。

examples.en: Just a minute, I'm coming!
examples.zh: 等一下，我來了！

just.variant_zh: 口語快說時常弱化成 [dʒɪst] 或 [dʒəst]。
just.variant_en: In fast speech it often weakens to [dʒɪst] or [dʒəst].

keep.tip_zh: 母音 [i] 是長而緊的音，嘴角往兩旁拉開像微笑，並且拉長；唸得太短、太鬆就會偏向 [ɪ]。開頭 [k] 要送出一口明顯的氣，手放在嘴前應該感覺得到。字尾 [p] 雙唇閉上就停住，不要再張開嘴多加母音。和 sheep、deep 押韻，可以三個字一起練長 [i]。
keep.tip_en: [i] is long and tense: spread the lip corners as if smiling and hold it; too short or too lax and it drifts toward [ɪ]. The opening [k] needs a clear puff of air you can feel on your hand. For the final [p], close the lips and stop — don't open again and add a vowel. It rhymes with sheep and deep, so practice the long [i] with all three.

examples.en: Please keep your desk clean.
examples.zh: 請保持你的桌子乾淨。

examples.en: You can keep this book for a week.
examples.zh: 這本書你可以留一個星期。

key.tip_zh: 拼字是 ey，但這裡唸長的 [i]，和 see、tree 押韻；不要照 they、hey 的拼法唸成 [e]。開頭 [k] 是送氣音：舌根頂住軟顎，再用力放開，送出一口氣。[i] 嘴角往兩旁拉開，聲音拉長。key 和 knee 押韻，兩字只差開頭的 [k] 和 [n]。
key.tip_en: It's spelled ey, but here it says a long [i], rhyming with see and tree — don't follow they and hey and say [e]. The opening [k] is aspirated: press the back of the tongue to the soft palate, then release it with a puff of air. Spread the lips for [i] and hold it. Key rhymes with knee; the two differ only in the first sound, [k] versus [n].

examples.en: I can't find my house key.
examples.zh: 我找不到我家的鑰匙。

examples.en: Mom keeps the car key in her bag.
examples.zh: 媽媽把車鑰匙放在她的包包裡。

key.spelling_zh: ey 唸 [i]，不像 they 的 [e]。
key.spelling_en: ey says [i] here, not the [e] of they.

kick.tip_zh: 中間是短而鬆的 [ɪ]，嘴巴比 [i] 放鬆、下巴略低，時間要短；唸成長而緊的 [i] 會聽起來像 keek。頭尾都是 [k]：開頭的 [k] 送氣要明顯，字尾的 [k]（拼字 ck）舌根頂住軟顎就停，不要再放出母音。和 pick、sick 押韻。
kick.tip_en: The middle vowel is a short, lax [ɪ]: more relaxed than [i], jaw a little lower, and quick; a long tense [i] makes it sound like 'keek'. The word starts and ends with [k]: the first one has a strong puff of air, while the last one (spelled ck) just stops with the back of the tongue on the soft palate — no extra vowel. It rhymes with pick and sick.

examples.en: Kick the ball to me!
examples.zh: 把球踢給我！

examples.en: He can kick the ball very far.
examples.zh: 他可以把球踢得很遠。

kid.tip_zh: 字尾 [d] 是有聲子音，舌尖頂住上齒齦、喉嚨要振動；容易唸成無聲的 [t]，變成 kit（一套工具）。英語母音在有聲子音前會唸得稍長，所以 kid 的 [ɪ] 比 kit 的略長一點，這能幫對方聽出結尾是 [d]。[ɪ] 本身仍是短而鬆的音，不要唸成 [i]。
kid.tip_en: The final [d] is voiced: tongue tip on the gum ridge, throat buzzing; learners often devoice it to [t], which gives kit (a set of tools). English vowels are a bit longer before voiced consonants, so the [ɪ] in kid is slightly longer than in kit — that helps listeners hear the [d]. [ɪ] itself stays short and lax; don't turn it into [i].

examples.en: That kid is my little cousin.
examples.zh: 那個小孩是我的小表弟。

examples.en: Every kid in my class likes recess.
examples.zh: 我們班每個小孩都喜歡下課時間。

kilogram.tip_zh: kilogram 的重音在第一音節 [ˈkɪ]，母音是短而放鬆的 [ɪ]，不是長的 [i]。第二音節的 o 弱化成 [ə]，學生常照拼字唸成清楚的 [o]，聽起來每個音節一樣重。最後的 gram 帶次重音，[æ] 嘴巴張大、嘴角往兩邊拉，結尾 [m] 雙唇要閉上。gram 跟 ham 押韻。
kilogram.tip_en: The stress in kilogram is on the first syllable [ˈkɪ], with a short, relaxed [ɪ], not a long [i]. The o in the second syllable weakens to [ə]; learners often follow the spelling and say a clear [o], so every syllable sounds equally strong. The final gram has secondary stress: open the mouth wide for [æ] with the corners spread, and close the lips for the final [m]. gram rhymes with ham.

examples.en: I bought a kilogram of apples.
examples.zh: 我買了一公斤蘋果。

examples.en: The bag of rice weighs one kilogram.
examples.zh: 這袋米重一公斤。

kind.tip_zh: [aɪ] 從張大嘴的 [a] 滑到 [ɪ]，和 find、mind 押韻。字尾 [nd]：舌尖頂住上齒齦發 [n]，舌頭不離開，接著憋一下放出有聲的 [d]；兩個音位置相同，容易只唸到 [n] 就停。拼字雖然是 i，這裡不是短的 [ɪ]，不要唸成 kin 加 d。
kind.tip_en: [aɪ] glides from an open [a] to [ɪ]; it rhymes with find and mind. For the final [nd], put the tongue tip on the gum ridge for [n], keep it there, then hold briefly and release a voiced [d]; since both sounds use the same spot, learners often stop at [n]. Although the letter is i, it isn't a short [ɪ] here — don't say 'kin' plus d.

examples.en: What kind of music do you like?
examples.zh: 你喜歡哪一種音樂？

examples.en: This kind of apple is very sweet.
examples.zh: 這種蘋果很甜。

king.tip_zh: 字尾 [ŋ] 用舌根抬起頂住軟顎，聲音從鼻子出來，舌尖不碰上齒齦；若改用舌尖收尾，就變成 kin。[ŋ] 之後不要再補一個 [g] 的爆破音或母音。開頭 [k] 送氣，[ɪ] 短而鬆。和 sing、ring 押韻，可以拉長 [ŋ] 感覺鼻腔的振動。
king.tip_en: For the final [ŋ], raise the back of the tongue to the soft palate and let the sound out through the nose — the tongue tip doesn't touch the gum ridge; finish with the tongue tip and it becomes kin. Don't add a [g] burst or a vowel after [ŋ]. The opening [k] is aspirated and [ɪ] is short and lax. It rhymes with sing and ring; hold the [ŋ] to feel the buzz in your nose.

examples.en: The king lives in a big castle.
examples.zh: 國王住在一座大城堡裡。

examples.en: In the story, the king has three daughters.
examples.zh: 故事裡，國王有三個女兒。

kiss.tip_zh: [ɪ] 短而鬆，舌頭比 [i] 低一點，嘴角不用用力拉；拉長成 [i] 會變成另一個音。拼字 ss 只唸一個 [s]，氣流持續送出、喉嚨不振動；容易唸成有聲的 [z]，或在 [s] 後面加一個母音。和 miss、this 押韻，三個字都用無聲的 [s] 結尾。
kiss.tip_en: [ɪ] is short and lax, the tongue a little lower than for [i], lips not pulled hard; stretch it to [i] and it becomes a different sound. The double ss is one [s]: a steady stream of air with no buzz in the throat; learners often voice it as [z] or add a vowel after the [s]. It rhymes with miss and this, all three ending in a voiceless [s].

examples.en: Mom gives me a kiss every night.
examples.zh: 媽媽每天晚上都會親我一下。

examples.en: The baby likes to kiss her teddy bear.
examples.zh: 小嬰兒喜歡親她的泰迪熊。

kitchen.tip_zh: 重音在第一音節 [kɪ]，第二音節 [tʃən] 輕而短，母音弱化成 [ə]，不要唸成清楚的 [tʃɛn]。拼字 tch 只唸一個 [tʃ]，t 不另外發音。小心和 chicken 弄反：kitchen 是 [k] 開頭、[tʃ] 在中間；chicken 是 [tʃ] 開頭、[k] 在中間。
kitchen.tip_en: Stress the first syllable [kɪ]; the second syllable [tʃən] is short and light with the vowel reduced to [ə] — not a clear [tʃɛn]. The letters tch make one sound, [tʃ]; the t is not pronounced separately. Don't swap it with chicken: kitchen starts with [k] and has [tʃ] in the middle, while chicken starts with [tʃ] and has [k] in the middle.

examples.en: Dad is cooking noodles in the kitchen.
examples.zh: 爸爸正在廚房煮麵。

examples.en: Our kitchen has a big window.
examples.zh: 我們家的廚房有一扇大窗戶。

kitchen.spelling_zh: tch 只唸一個 [tʃ]，t 不另外發音。
kitchen.spelling_en: tch is one sound, [tʃ]; the t is not said separately.

kite.tip_zh: [aɪ] 要先張大嘴發 [a]，再收小滑到 [ɪ]；拼字 i 加結尾不發音的 e，讓 i 唸成 [aɪ]，和 night、light 押韻。字尾 [t] 舌尖頂住上齒齦就停，美式說話時常常不放氣，容易多加一個母音。也要和 cat [kæt] 分開：kite 的母音會滑動，cat 的 [æ] 不會。
kite.tip_en: For [aɪ], open wide for [a], then close toward [ɪ]; the letter i plus the silent final e makes the i say [aɪ], rhyming with night and light. For the final [t], press the tongue tip to the gum ridge and stop — Americans often don't release it — and don't add a vowel. Keep it apart from cat [kæt]: the vowel in kite glides, the [æ] in cat does not.

examples.en: We flew a kite at the beach.
examples.zh: 我們在海邊放風箏。

examples.en: My kite is shaped like a fish.
examples.zh: 我的風箏是魚的形狀。

knee.tip_zh: 開頭的 k 不發音，直接從 [n] 開始：舌尖頂住上齒齦，聲音從鼻子出來，再接長而緊的 [i]。容易照拼字在前面多唸一個 [k]，變成兩個子音。knee 和 key 押韻：key 開頭是送氣的 [k]，knee 開頭是鼻音 [n]，兩字只差這一個音。
knee.tip_en: The k at the start is silent, so begin directly with [n]: tongue tip on the gum ridge, sound through the nose, then a long tense [i]. Learners often follow the spelling and add a [k] in front. Knee rhymes with key: key starts with an aspirated [k], knee with a nasal [n] — that one sound is the only difference.

examples.en: I hurt my knee in P.E. class.
examples.zh: 我在體育課弄傷了膝蓋。

examples.en: The water came up to my knee.
examples.zh: 水淹到我的膝蓋。

knee.spelling_zh: 開頭的 k 不發音。
knee.spelling_en: The k at the start is silent.

knife.tip_zh: knife 的 k 不發音，開頭直接是 [n]，學生常照拼字在前面多加一個 [k]。中間 [aɪ] 從張大嘴滑到 [ɪ]。最重要的是字尾 [f]：上齒輕碰下唇吹氣，不要省略，也不要加母音變成「夫」。字尾發不清楚，就容易和只差最後一個音的 nice、night、nine 混淆。knife 跟 wife、life 押韻。
knife.tip_en: The k in knife is silent; it starts straight with [n]—learners often add a [k] in front because of the spelling. The middle [aɪ] glides from an open mouth to [ɪ]. The most important part is the final [f]: touch the upper teeth to the lower lip and blow—don't drop it, and don't add a vowel to make it 'fu'. If the ending is unclear, it is easily confused with nice, night and nine, which differ only in the last sound. knife rhymes with wife and life.

examples.en: Dad cuts the cake with a knife.
examples.zh: 爸爸用刀子切蛋糕。

examples.en: Please use a knife and fork.
examples.zh: 請用刀叉。

knife.spelling_zh: 開頭的 k 不發音，和 know、knee 一樣。
knife.spelling_en: The k at the start is silent, as in know and knee.

knock.tip_zh: 開頭 kn 的 k 不發音，從 [n] 開始。這個字頭尾都有 k 字母，只有結尾 ck 唸 [k]，舌根頂住軟顎停住。母音 [ɑ] 下巴張大、嘴唇不圓；容易照拼字 o 唸成圓唇的 [o]。和 clock、rock 押韻，可以先唸 rock 再把開頭換成 [n]。
knock.tip_en: In kn the k is silent, so start with [n]. The word has the letter k at both ends, but only the final ck is pronounced [k] — stop with the back of the tongue on the soft palate. The vowel [ɑ] needs a dropped jaw and unrounded lips; the letter o tempts learners into a rounded [o]. It rhymes with clock and rock: say rock, then change the start to [n].

examples.en: Please knock before you come in.
examples.zh: 進來之前請先敲門。

examples.en: I heard someone knock on the door.
examples.zh: 我聽到有人敲門。

knock.spelling_zh: 開頭的 k 不發音，結尾 ck 才唸 [k]。
knock.spelling_en: The first k is silent; only the final ck says [k].

know.tip_zh: know 的 k 不發音，唸起來和 no 完全一樣，都是 [no]。拼字的 -ow 在這裡唸 [o]，像 go，不是 now 的 [aʊ]，學生常因為拼字像 now 而唸錯。[o] 是圓唇音，嘴巴從圓形再收得更小一點，聲音拉長，不要唸得又短又扁。
know.tip_en: The k in know is silent; it sounds exactly like no—both are [no]. The -ow here is [o], as in go, not the [aʊ] of now; learners often get it wrong because the spelling looks like now. [o] is a rounded vowel: start with round lips and close them a little more, holding the sound—don't make it short and flat.

examples.en: I know the answer!
examples.zh: 我知道答案！

examples.en: Do you know my teacher?
examples.zh: 你認識我的老師嗎？

know.spelling_zh: k 不發音，know 和 no 同音。
know.spelling_en: The k is silent; know and no sound the same.

knowledge.tip_zh: 雖然這個字來自 know，但第一音節不是 know 的 [no]，而是嘴巴張大的 [nɑ]；開頭 k 不發音。重音在第一音節，第二音節 [lədʒ] 輕而短，拼字 -ledge 的母音弱化成 [ə]，不要唸成 ledge 的 [ɛ]。字尾 [dʒ] 嘴唇微噘，結尾不加母音。
knowledge.tip_en: Though it comes from know, the first syllable is not know's [no] but an open [nɑ]; the k is silent. Stress the first syllable. The second syllable [lədʒ] is short and light — the vowel in -ledge reduces to [ə], not the [ɛ] of ledge. For the final [dʒ], round the lips slightly and don't add a vowel after it.

examples.en: Books give us knowledge about the world.
examples.zh: 書本讓我們獲得關於世界的知識。

examples.en: She has a lot of knowledge about animals.
examples.zh: 她對動物有很多知識。

knowledge.spelling_zh: k 不發音；dg 合起來唸 [dʒ]。
knowledge.spelling_en: The k is silent; dg together say [dʒ].

lake.tip_zh: lake 和 like 只差母音：lake 的 [e] 嘴巴半開，再滑向 [ɪ]；like 的 [aɪ] 要從張大嘴的 [a] 開始。[e] 要唸夠長，不要唸成短而不滑動的 [ɛ]。拼字結尾 e 不發音，讓 a 唸 [e]，和 cake、make 押韻。字尾 [k] 舌根頂住軟顎停住。
lake.tip_en: Lake and like differ only in the vowel: lake's [e] starts half-open and glides to [ɪ], while like's [aɪ] starts from a wide-open [a]. Hold [e] long enough and don't make it a short, steady [ɛ]. The final e is silent and makes the a say [e], so it rhymes with cake and make. End by stopping the back of the tongue on the soft palate for [k].

examples.en: We had a picnic by the lake.
examples.zh: 我們在湖邊野餐。

examples.en: There are ducks swimming in the lake.
examples.zh: 湖裡有鴨子在游泳。

lamp.tip_zh: [æ] 下巴要大大拉低、嘴角往兩邊咧開，開口比 [ɛ] 大；容易唸成較小的 [ɛ]，聽起來像 lemp。字尾 [mp]：雙唇閉上發 [m]，再在原位輕輕放出 [p]，不要漏掉 [p]，也不要在後面加母音。和 camp、stamp 押韻，可以三個字連著練 [æmp]。
lamp.tip_en: For [æ], drop the jaw a lot and pull the lip corners wide — a bigger opening than [ɛ]; learners often use the smaller [ɛ], so it sounds like 'lemp'. For the final [mp], close the lips for [m], then release a soft [p] from the same spot; don't lose the [p] or add a vowel. It rhymes with camp and stamp — practice [æmp] across all three.

examples.en: Turn on the lamp so you can read.
examples.zh: 把檯燈打開，你才能看書。

examples.en: There is a small lamp on my desk.
examples.zh: 我的書桌上有一盞小檯燈。

land.tip_zh: land 和 lend 只差母音：land 的 [æ] 下巴拉低、嘴角咧開，lend 的 [ɛ] 嘴巴比較小；開口不夠就會被聽成 lend。字尾 [nd] 舌尖頂住上齒齦，先發鼻音 [n]，再接有聲的 [d]，不要只唸到 [n] 就停。和 hand、stand 押韻，可以先唸 hand 再換開頭。
land.tip_en: Land and lend differ only in the vowel: land's [æ] has a dropped jaw and wide lip corners, lend's [ɛ] is smaller; open too little and listeners hear lend. For the final [nd], keep the tongue tip on the gum ridge, make the nasal [n], then a voiced [d] — don't stop at [n]. It rhymes with hand and stand; say hand first and change the start.

examples.en: The plane will land in ten minutes.
examples.zh: 飛機十分鐘後會降落。

examples.en: Farmers grow rice on this land.
examples.zh: 農夫在這塊土地上種稻米。

language.tip_zh: language 第一音節 [læŋ] 的 n 其實是 [ŋ]：舌根抬起碰軟顎，像 long 的結尾，接著馬上發 [g]。學生常省略 [g]，唸成 lan-wage，或把 [æ] 唸得太窄。後半 -guage 不是 age 的 [e]，而是很輕的 [ə]，最後的 [dʒ] 嘴唇往前嘟，送出氣就停，不要加母音。重音在第一音節。
language.tip_en: In the first syllable of language, [læŋ], the n is really [ŋ]: raise the back of the tongue to the soft palate, as at the end of long, and go straight into [g]. Learners often drop the [g] and say lan-wage, or make the [æ] too narrow. The second half -guage doesn't have the [e] of age but a very light [ə]; for the final [dʒ], push the lips forward, release and stop—don't add a vowel. The stress is on the first syllable.

examples.en: English is a fun language to learn.
examples.zh: 英文是一種學起來很有趣的語言。

examples.en: What language do people speak in Japan?
examples.zh: 日本人說什麼語言？

language.spelling_zh: -guage 的 u 唸 [w]，a 弱化成 [ə]。
language.spelling_en: In -guage, the u sounds like [w] and the a weakens to [ə].

large.tip_zh: [ɑr] 要先張大嘴發 [ɑ]，再把舌尖往後捲起、不碰上顎，帶出 [r]；容易漏掉捲舌，只剩 [ɑ]。字尾 [dʒ] 嘴唇微微往前噘、聲帶振動，結尾不要加上 [i] 之類的母音變成兩個音節。拼字 ge 的 e 不發音，g 在這裡唸 [dʒ]。
large.tip_en: For [ɑr], open wide for [ɑ], then curl the tongue tip back without touching the roof of the mouth to add [r]; learners often skip the curl and leave just [ɑ]. For the final [dʒ], push the lips slightly forward with the voice on, and don't add a vowel like [i] that makes a second syllable. In ge the e is silent and the g says [dʒ].

examples.en: I would like a large cup of tea.
examples.zh: 我想要一大杯茶。

examples.en: An elephant is a very large animal.
examples.zh: 大象是非常大的動物。

last.tip_zh: last、least、list 只差中間的母音：last 是嘴巴張大、嘴角咧開的 [æ]，least 是長而緊的 [i]，list 是短而鬆的 [ɪ]。字尾 [st] 先送出無聲的 [s]，再讓舌尖頂住上齒齦停成 [t]；容易漏掉 [t] 只剩 [s]，或在後面加母音。和 fast、past 押韻。
last.tip_en: Last, least and list differ only in the middle vowel: last has the wide-open, spread [æ], least the long tense [i], list the short lax [ɪ]. For the final [st], push out a voiceless [s], then stop with the tongue tip on the gum ridge for [t]; learners often drop the [t] or add a vowel after it. It rhymes with fast and past.

examples.en: Friday is the last day of the school week.
examples.zh: 星期五是一週上學的最後一天。

examples.en: I ate the last cookie in the box.
examples.zh: 我吃掉了盒子裡最後一塊餅乾。

late.tip_zh: late [let] 和 let [lɛt] 只差母音：late 的 [e] 要拉長，並從 [e] 滑到 [ɪ]；let 的 [ɛ] 短而不滑動。拼字結尾 e 不發音，它讓 a 唸成 [e]。字尾 [t] 舌尖頂住上齒齦就停住，不要多加一個母音。和 date、gate 押韻。
late.tip_en: Late [let] and let [lɛt] differ only in the vowel: late's [e] is held longer and glides from [e] to [ɪ]; let's [ɛ] is short with no glide. The final e is silent — it makes the a say [e]. For the final [t], press the tongue tip to the gum ridge and stop; don't add a vowel. It rhymes with date and gate.

examples.en: Hurry up, or we will be late!
examples.zh: 快一點，不然我們會遲到！

examples.en: I stayed up late to finish my book.
examples.zh: 我熬夜把書看完。

later.tip_zh: 美式英語中，[t] 夾在重讀的 [e] 和 [ɚ] 之間，會變成舌尖輕點一下上齒齦的彈音，聽起來接近輕的 d，不要唸成用力送氣的 [t]。結尾 [ɚ] 舌尖往後捲、不碰上顎，不要唸成不捲舌的 [ə]。第一音節的 [e] 會滑動，letter 的 [ɛ] 不會，這是兩字的差別。
later.tip_en: In American English, [t] between the stressed [e] and [ɚ] becomes a quick tap of the tongue tip on the gum ridge, close to a light d — not a strong, breathy [t]. For the final [ɚ], curl the tongue tip back without touching the roof of the mouth; don't say an uncurled [ə]. The first syllable's [e] glides, while letter's [ɛ] does not — that's what separates the two words.

examples.en: See you later, I have to go home now!
examples.zh: 待會兒見，我現在得回家了！

examples.en: I will clean my room later.
examples.zh: 我等一下會打掃房間。

laugh.tip_zh: laugh 的拼字很容易騙人：au 唸 [æ]，gh 唸 [f]，整個字是 [læf]，跟 half 押韻。學生常把 au 唸成 [ɔ] 或 [ɑ]，或者看到 gh 就不發音，把字尾的 [f] 漏掉。做法：[l] 舌尖頂上齒齦，接著嘴巴張大、嘴角往兩邊拉發 [æ]，最後上齒輕碰下唇吹出 [f]。
laugh.tip_en: The spelling of laugh is easy to be fooled by: au is [æ], gh is [f], and the whole word is [læf], rhyming with half. Learners often say au as [ɔ] or [ɑ], or treat gh as silent and leave out the final [f]. How to do it: tongue tip on the gum ridge for [l], then open the mouth wide with the corners spread for [æ], and finally touch the upper teeth to the lower lip and blow out [f].

examples.en: My little brother likes to laugh.
examples.zh: 我弟弟很愛笑。

examples.en: Funny movies always make me laugh.
examples.zh: 搞笑電影總是讓我哈哈大笑。

laugh.spelling_zh: au 唸 [æ]，gh 唸 [f]，跟 half 押韻。
laugh.spelling_en: au sounds like [æ] and gh like [f]; it rhymes with half.

lawyer.tip_zh: 重音在第一音節 [lɔ]：嘴巴張開、嘴唇稍圓，拼字 aw 和 saw、draw 一樣唸 [ɔ]，不要唸成較閉的 [o]。第二音節 [jɚ]：舌面先往上靠近硬顎滑出 [j]，緊接著捲舌成 [ɚ]；容易省略捲舌，或把 [j] 漏掉，讓兩個音節黏不起來。
lawyer.tip_en: Stress the first syllable [lɔ]: mouth open, lips slightly rounded — aw says [ɔ] as in saw and draw, not the tighter [o]. In the second syllable [jɚ], raise the middle of the tongue toward the hard palate to glide into [j], then curl straight into [ɚ]; learners often skip the curl or drop the [j], so the two syllables don't join smoothly.

examples.en: My aunt is a lawyer in Taichung.
examples.zh: 我阿姨是台中的律師。

examples.en: The lawyer helps people with problems.
examples.zh: 律師幫助有問題的人。

lazy.tip_zh: 中間的 [z] 要有聲：舌尖靠近上齒齦，送氣時喉嚨振動，像蜜蜂嗡嗡的聲音；容易唸成無聲的 [s]，聽起來像 lacy（有蕾絲的）。重音在第一音節 [le]，[e] 要從 [e] 滑到 [ɪ]；結尾 [ɪ] 輕而短。和 crazy 押韻。
lazy.tip_en: The middle [z] must be voiced: tongue tip near the gum ridge, throat buzzing like a bee as the air flows; learners often make it a voiceless [s], so it sounds like lacy. Stress the first syllable [le], gliding [e] toward [ɪ]; the final [ɪ] is short and light. It rhymes with crazy.

examples.en: My cat is lazy and sleeps all day.
examples.zh: 我的貓很懶，整天都在睡覺。

examples.en: Don't be lazy, let's clean up together.
examples.zh: 別偷懶，我們一起打掃吧。

leader.tip_zh: 第一音節 [li] 重讀、拉長，嘴角往兩旁拉。第二音節的 [d] 在美式口語中只是舌尖輕彈一下，接著是捲舌的 [ɚ]：舌尖往後捲、不碰上顎，嘴唇略圓。容易把結尾唸成不捲舌的 [də]，或把 [d] 唸得太重，讓整個字變得一頓一頓的。
leader.tip_en: The first syllable [li] is stressed and long, with spread lips. In casual American speech the [d] of the second syllable is just a light tap of the tongue tip, followed by the r-colored [ɚ]: curl the tongue tip back without touching the roof of the mouth, lips slightly rounded. Learners often end with an uncurled [də], or hit the [d] too hard so the word sounds choppy.

examples.en: Amy is the leader of our group.
examples.zh: 艾美是我們這組的組長。

examples.en: A good leader listens to everyone.
examples.zh: 好的領導者會聽每個人的意見。

learn.tip_zh: 拼字 ear 在這裡不是 [i] 也不是 [ɛr]，而是捲舌的 [ɝ]，和 burn、turn 押韻。發音時舌尖往後捲起、不碰上顎，從母音開始就一直捲住，最後舌尖再往前頂住上齒齦收成 [n]。容易照 ear 的拼字唸成 [lir]，或完全沒捲舌。
learn.tip_en: Here ear is neither [i] nor [ɛr] but the r-colored [ɝ]; it rhymes with burn and turn. Curl the tongue tip back without touching the roof of the mouth and keep it curled from the start of the vowel, then bring the tip forward to the gum ridge to close on [n]. Learners often follow the letters ear and say [lir], or don't curl at all.

examples.en: I want to learn how to swim.
examples.zh: 我想學游泳。

examples.en: We learn new English words every day.
examples.zh: 我們每天學新的英文單字。

least.tip_zh: least [list] 和 list [lɪst] 只差母音：least 的 [i] 長而緊、嘴角拉開，list 的 [ɪ] 短而鬆。拼字 ea 在這裡唸 [i]，和 east 押韻。字尾 [st] 先送出 [s]，再讓舌尖頂住上齒齦停成 [t]；常用的 at least 裡，[t] 也不要漏掉。
least.tip_en: Least [list] and list [lɪst] differ only in the vowel: least's [i] is long and tense with spread lips, list's [ɪ] is short and lax. Here ea says [i], rhyming with east. For the final [st], push out [s], then stop with the tongue tip on the gum ridge for [t]; in the common phrase at least, don't drop that [t] either.

examples.en: You need to sleep at least eight hours.
examples.zh: 你至少需要睡八個小時。

examples.en: Who has the least homework today?
examples.zh: 今天誰的功課最少？

leave.tip_zh: 字尾 [v] 要用上排牙齒輕碰下唇，喉嚨振動；容易唸成無聲的 [f]，就變成 leaf（葉子），或嘴唇沒碰到牙齒唸成 [b]。母音 [i] 要拉長；在有聲的 [v] 前面，[i] 本來就比 leaf 的長。拼字結尾 e 不發音。也別和 love 混淆，leave 的母音是嘴角拉開的長 [i]。
leave.tip_en: For the final [v], rest the upper teeth lightly on the lower lip and keep the throat buzzing; learners often make it a voiceless [f] — which gives leaf — or use [b] without the teeth touching the lip. Hold the [i] long; before voiced [v] it's naturally longer than in leaf. The final e is silent. Don't confuse it with love: leave has a long, spread [i].

examples.en: We leave for school at seven.
examples.zh: 我們七點出門去上學。

examples.en: Please leave your shoes by the door.
examples.zh: 請把鞋子放在門邊。

left.tip_zh: 字尾 [ft] 是兩個無聲子音：上齒輕碰下唇送出 [f] 的氣流，再馬上把舌尖抬到上齒齦停成 [t]。容易漏掉 [t] 只剩 [f]，或在 [f] 和 [t] 之間加母音。母音 [ɛ] 嘴巴半開、短而不滑動，不要唸成會滑到 [ɪ] 的 [e]。
left.tip_en: The final [ft] is two voiceless consonants: upper teeth lightly on the lower lip to push out the air of [f], then quickly raise the tongue tip to the gum ridge and stop for [t]. Learners often drop the [t], leaving just [f], or put a vowel between [f] and [t]. The vowel [ɛ] is half-open, short and steady — not an [e] that glides to [ɪ].

examples.en: Turn left at the bakery.
examples.zh: 在麵包店左轉。

examples.en: The library is on your left.
examples.zh: 圖書館在你的左邊。

leg.tip_zh: 母音 [ɛ] 短、嘴巴半開、不滑動，和 egg 押韻；不要拉長並滑向 [ɪ]，唸成 [e]。字尾 [g] 是有聲子音，舌根頂住軟顎、喉嚨振動，輕輕放開即可；容易唸成無聲的 [k]，或在後面多加一個母音。可以先唸 egg，再在前面加上舌尖頂住上齒齦的 [l]。
leg.tip_en: The vowel [ɛ] is short, half-open and steady, rhyming with egg; don't stretch it and glide toward [ɪ], which turns it into [e]. The final [g] is voiced: back of the tongue on the soft palate, throat buzzing, then a gentle release; learners often devoice it to [k] or add a vowel after it. Say egg first, then add an [l] in front with the tongue tip on the gum ridge.

examples.en: My leg feels tired after the long walk.
examples.zh: 走了很久，我的腿好累。

examples.en: Can you stand on one leg like a bird?
examples.zh: 你可以像鳥一樣單腳站立嗎？

lemon.tip_zh: 重音在第一音節 [lɛ]，第二音節 [mən] 很輕，拼字 o 弱化成 [ə]，不要照拼字唸成 [mɑn] 或 [mon]。字尾 [n] 要用舌尖頂住上齒齦收住，不要收成舌根的 [ŋ]。lemon 和 lesson 只差中間的子音：lemon 是雙唇閉合的 [m]，lesson 是無聲的 [s]。
lemon.tip_en: Stress the first syllable [lɛ]; the second syllable [mən] is very light — the o reduces to [ə], so don't follow the spelling and say [mɑn] or [mon]. Close the final [n] with the tongue tip on the gum ridge, not with the back of the tongue as [ŋ]. Lemon and lesson differ only in the middle consonant: lips closed for [m] in lemon, a voiceless [s] in lesson.

examples.en: Grandma puts lemon in her tea.
examples.zh: 奶奶在茶裡加檸檬。

examples.en: This lemon is very sour!
examples.zh: 這顆檸檬好酸！

lend.tip_zh: 母音是嘴巴半開的 [ɛ]，和 end、send、friend 押韻；若下巴拉得太低唸成 [æ]，就會變成 land。字尾 [nd]：舌尖頂住上齒齦先發 [n]，舌頭不動，再放出有聲的 [d]；常見錯誤是 [d] 消失，聽起來只剩 [lɛn]。可以先唸 end，再在前面加上 [l]。
lend.tip_en: The vowel is a half-open [ɛ], rhyming with end, send and friend; drop the jaw too far into [æ] and it becomes land. For the final [nd], put the tongue tip on the gum ridge for [n], keep it still, then release a voiced [d]; a common mistake is losing the [d] so only [lɛn] is left. Say end first, then add [l] in front.

examples.en: Can you lend me a pencil?
examples.zh: 你可以借我一支鉛筆嗎？

examples.en: I will lend you my comic book.
examples.zh: 我會把我的漫畫書借給你。

less.tip_zh: [ɛ] 短而不滑動，嘴巴半開，和 yes、dress 押韻；若拉長並滑向 [ɪ]，就會唸成 lace [les]（蕾絲）。字尾 ss 只唸一個無聲的 [s]，氣流持續送出、喉嚨不振動，不要唸成 [z]，也不要在後面加母音。less 和 lesson 的開頭 [lɛs] 完全一樣。
less.tip_en: [ɛ] is short and steady with the mouth half open, rhyming with yes and dress; stretch it and glide toward [ɪ] and you get lace [les]. The double ss is one voiceless [s] — a steady stream of air with no buzz — so don't voice it as [z] or add a vowel after it. Less sounds exactly like the beginning [lɛs] of lesson.

examples.en: Please use less sugar in the cake.
examples.zh: 蛋糕裡請少放一點糖。

examples.en: I have less homework than my sister.
examples.zh: 我的功課比我姊姊少。

lesson.tip_zh: 中間拼字 ss 唸無聲的 [s]，不要唸成有聲的 [z]。重音在第一音節 [lɛ]，第二音節 [sən] 很輕，o 弱化成 [ə]，不要照拼字唸成 [sɑn]。也要和 listen [ˈlɪsṇ] 分開：lesson 第一音節是嘴巴較開的 [ɛ]，listen 是短而鬆的 [ɪ]。
lesson.tip_en: The double ss in the middle is a voiceless [s], not a voiced [z]. Stress the first syllable [lɛ]; the second syllable [sən] is very light, with the o reduced to [ə] — don't follow the spelling and say [sɑn].
