Keep it apart from listen [ˈlɪsṇ]: lesson's first syllable has the more open [ɛ], listen's has the short lax [ɪ].

examples.en: We have a piano lesson on Tuesday.
examples.zh: 我們星期二有鋼琴課。

examples.en: Today's English lesson was really fun.
examples.zh: 今天的英文課真的很好玩。

let.tip_zh: [ɛ] 短而不滑動，嘴巴半開；若拉長並滑向 [ɪ]，就變成 late [let]。字尾 [t] 舌尖頂住上齒齦就停，美式說話時常常不放氣。在最常用的 let's 裡，[t] 直接接 [s] 變成 [ts]，中間不要加母音唸成三個音。和 get、pet、wet 押韻。
let.tip_en: [ɛ] is short and steady with the mouth half open; stretch it and glide toward [ɪ] and it becomes late [let]. For the final [t], press the tongue tip to the gum ridge and stop — Americans often don't release it. In the very common let's, [t] runs straight into [s] as [ts]; don't put a vowel between them. It rhymes with get, pet and wet.

examples.en: Let me help you carry that.
examples.zh: 讓我幫你拿那個。

examples.en: Mom will let us watch TV after dinner.
examples.zh: 媽媽晚餐後會讓我們看電視。

letter.tip_zh: 拼字 tt 只代表一個 [t]，而且夾在重讀的 [ɛ] 和 [ɚ] 之間，美式英語會唸成舌尖輕點一下就離開的彈音，接近輕的 d，不要用力送氣唸成兩個 t。字尾 [ɚ] 舌尖往後捲起。[ɛ] 要短、不滑動；拉長滑向 [ɪ] 就會被聽成 later。
letter.tip_en: The double tt stands for a single [t], and between the stressed [ɛ] and [ɚ] American English turns it into a quick touch-and-go tap, close to a light d — don't puff it out like two t's. Curl the tongue tip back for the final [ɚ]. Keep [ɛ] short and steady; stretch it and glide toward [ɪ] and it will be heard as later.

examples.en: I wrote a letter to my pen pal.
examples.zh: 我寫了一封信給我的筆友。

examples.en: A is the first letter of the alphabet.
examples.zh: A 是字母表的第一個字母。

level.tip_zh: level 前後拼字一樣，但兩個 l 不一樣：開頭是亮 L，舌尖頂上齒齦、舌頭往前；字尾 [ḷ] 是暗 L，舌根往後抬，而且前面沒有母音。學生常把 [ɛ] 拉長成 [e]，或把 [v] 唸成 [b]，結尾再加一個「喔」。做法：上齒咬下唇發 [v]，舌尖馬上頂上齒齦接暗 L。
level.tip_en: level is spelled the same both ways, but its two l's are different: the first is a clear L, tongue tip on the gum ridge with the tongue forward; the final [ḷ] is a dark L with the back of the tongue raised, and there's no vowel before it. Learners often stretch [ɛ] into [e], turn [v] into [b], and add an 'o' at the end. How to do it: bite the lower lip for [v], then put the tongue tip straight on the gum ridge for the dark L.

examples.en: I finished the last level of the game!
examples.zh: 我破了遊戲的最後一關！

examples.en: What level is your English class?
examples.zh: 你的英文課是什麼程度？

library.tip_zh: library 有兩個 [r]：[br] 和後面的 [r]。學生常在 [b] 和 [r] 中間多加一個母音，變成四個音節，或乾脆漏掉第一個 [r]，唸成 [ˈlaɪbɛri]。做法：雙唇閉上準備 [b] 時，舌頭就先捲好，嘴唇一放開就是 [br]，像 brown 的開頭。開頭 [l] 舌尖碰上齒齦，[r] 舌尖不碰任何地方。重音在 [ˈlaɪ]。
library.tip_en: library has two [r] sounds: in [br] and the one after it. Learners often slip a vowel between [b] and [r], making four syllables, or drop the first [r] altogether and say [ˈlaɪbɛri]. How to do it: while the lips are closed for [b], have the tongue already curled, so opening the lips gives [br] at once, like the start of brown. For the opening [l] the tongue tip touches the gum ridge; for [r] it touches nothing. The stress is on [ˈlaɪ].

examples.en: I borrow books from the library.
examples.zh: 我從圖書館借書。

examples.en: Let's meet at the school library after lunch.
examples.zh: 我們午餐後在學校圖書館見面吧。

library.kk_flag: Secondary stress is misplaced: GA is [ˈlaɪˌbrɛrɪ] (secondary on brɛ, final syllable unstressed); the given KK puts ˌ before ri. The final [i] is also inconsistent with January's -ɛrɪ in this batch.

lie.tip_zh: 拼字 ie 在這裡唸 [aɪ]，和 fly、high、eye 押韻，不要唸成 [i]，也不要分成 [i] 加 [ɛ] 兩個音。[aɪ] 要先張大嘴發 [a]，再往 [ɪ] 收小，嘴形要有滑動；只唸到 [a] 會聽起來不完整。開頭 [l] 舌尖頂住上齒齦，不要用鼻音 [n] 代替。
lie.tip_en: The letters ie say [aɪ] here, rhyming with fly, high and eye — not [i], and not split into [i] plus [ɛ]. For [aɪ], open wide for [a], then close toward [ɪ] so the mouth visibly glides; stopping at [a] sounds incomplete. Start [l] with the tongue tip on the gum ridge, and don't replace it with a nasal [n].

examples.en: Please don't lie to your parents.
examples.zh: 請不要對你的爸媽說謊。

examples.en: It's always better to tell the truth than to lie.
examples.zh: 說實話永遠比說謊好。

life.tip_zh: life、like、light、line 都是 [laɪ] 開頭，只靠最後一個子音分辨，所以字尾一定要清楚：life 的 [f] 是上齒輕碰下唇、吹出無聲的氣流，不要漏掉，也不要加母音。拼字結尾 e 不發音。注意複數 lives 的 [f] 會變成有聲的 [v]。
life.tip_en: Life, like, light and line all start with [laɪ] and are told apart only by the last consonant, so the ending must be clear: for life's [f], rest the upper teeth on the lower lip and blow voiceless air — don't drop it or add a vowel. The final e is silent. Note that in the plural lives the [f] changes to a voiced [v].

examples.en: Grandpa has lived a happy life.
examples.zh: 爺爺過著快樂的生活。

examples.en: School life is busy but fun.
examples.zh: 學校生活很忙，但很有趣。

light.tip_zh: 拼字 gh 不發音，igh 一起唸 [aɪ]，和 night、kite 押韻。開頭是 [l]：舌尖頂住上齒齦，氣流從舌頭兩側出來；不要和 right 的 [r] 混淆，[r] 的舌尖不碰任何地方、往後捲。字尾 [t] 舌尖停住就好，不要多加母音。
light.tip_en: The gh is silent; igh together say [aɪ], rhyming with night and kite. The word starts with [l]: tongue tip on the gum ridge, air flowing around the sides of the tongue. Don't mix it up with the [r] of right, where the tongue tip touches nothing and curls back. For the final [t], just stop with the tongue tip — no extra vowel.

examples.en: Please turn off the light when you leave.
examples.zh: 離開時請關燈。

examples.en: This box is light, so I can carry it.
examples.zh: 這個箱子很輕，所以我拿得動。

like.tip_zh: 字尾 [k] 舌根頂住軟顎停住，不要在後面多加母音。說 I like it 時，[k] 會直接連到 it 的母音，聽起來像 [laɪ kɪt]，中間不停頓。和 lake [lek] 比較：like 的母音要從張大嘴的 [a] 開始滑到 [ɪ]，lake 則從半開的 [e] 開始。
like.tip_en: Stop the final [k] with the back of the tongue on the soft palate; don't add a vowel after it. In I like it, the [k] links straight into the vowel of it, sounding like [laɪ kɪt] with no pause. Compared with lake [lek]: like's vowel starts from a wide-open [a] and glides to [ɪ], while lake's starts from a half-open [e].

examples.en: I like to draw pictures of animals.
examples.zh: 我喜歡畫動物的圖。

examples.en: Do you like ice cream?
examples.zh: 你喜歡冰淇淋嗎？

line.tip_zh: 字尾 [n] 舌尖要頂住上齒齦，聲音從鼻子出來；容易收成舌根的 [ŋ]，或舌尖還沒碰到就結束。和 nine、fine 押韻：nine 頭尾都是同一個 [n]，可以用它練習收尾。[aɪ] 要從張大嘴的 [a] 滑到 [ɪ]。拼字結尾 e 不發音。
line.tip_en: End [n] with the tongue tip on the gum ridge and the sound through the nose; learners often close with the back of the tongue ([ŋ]) or stop before the tip touches. It rhymes with nine and fine — nine starts and ends with the same [n], so use it to practice the ending. Glide [aɪ] from an open [a] to [ɪ]. The final e is silent.

examples.en: Please stand in line for lunch.
examples.zh: 請排隊領午餐。

examples.en: Draw a straight line with your ruler.
examples.zh: 用你的尺畫一條直線。

lion.tip_zh: lion 有兩個音節 [ˈlaɪ]·[ən]，學生常把它縮成一個音節，聽起來像 line。第一音節 [laɪ] 重而完整，從張大嘴滑到 [ɪ]；第二音節 [ən] 輕而短，兩拍要分清楚。字尾是舌尖頂住上齒齦的 [n]，不是舌根的 [ŋ]，結束時舌尖要碰到上面。
lion.tip_en: lion has two syllables, [ˈlaɪ]·[ən]; learners often squeeze it into one, which sounds like line. The first syllable [laɪ] is strong and complete, gliding from an open mouth to [ɪ]; the second, [ən], is light and short—the two beats must be clearly separate. The final sound is a tongue-tip [n] on the gum ridge, not the back-of-tongue [ŋ]; the tongue tip must touch up there at the end.

examples.en: The lion is sleeping under a tree.
examples.zh: 獅子在樹下睡覺。

examples.en: We saw a lion at the zoo.
examples.zh: 我們在動物園看到一隻獅子。

lip.tip_zh: [ɪ] 短而鬆，舌頭比 [i] 低、嘴角不用拉；拉長成 [i] 就變成 leap（跳）。字尾 [p] 雙唇閉合即停住，美式常常不放氣，不要再張開嘴加母音。和 ship、trip 押韻，可以三個字一起練短 [ɪ] 加 [p] 的結尾。
lip.tip_en: [ɪ] is short and lax, the tongue lower than for [i], lips not pulled wide; stretch it into [i] and it becomes leap. For the final [p], close the lips and stop — Americans often don't release it — and don't open again to add a vowel. It rhymes with ship and trip; practice the short [ɪ] plus [p] ending with all three.

examples.en: My lip feels dry in winter.
examples.zh: 冬天我的嘴唇覺得很乾。

examples.en: She put on lip balm before going outside.
examples.zh: 她出門前擦了護唇膏。

list.tip_zh: list 的 [ɪ] 短而鬆，舌頭比 [i] 低一點，嘴角不必用力；拉長就變成 least [list]。字尾 [st] 先送出無聲的 [s]，再讓舌尖頂住上齒齦停成 [t]。複數 lists 結尾有 [sts] 三個子音，可以先慢慢唸 [lɪst] 再加 [s]，不要在中間塞母音。
list.tip_en: List's [ɪ] is short and lax, the tongue a little lower than for [i], lips relaxed; stretch it and it becomes least [list]. For the final [st], push out voiceless [s], then stop with the tongue tip on the gum ridge for [t]. The plural lists ends in three consonants, [sts]: say [lɪst] slowly, then add [s], with no vowel squeezed in.

examples.en: Mom wrote a shopping list.
examples.zh: 媽媽寫了一張購物清單。

examples.en: Is my name on the list?
examples.zh: 我的名字在名單上嗎？

listen.tip_zh: listen 的 t 不發音，唸 [ˈlɪsən]，學生常照拼字唸成 [ˈlɪstən]。第一音節是短而放鬆的 [ɪ]，不要拉長成 [i]，也不要張嘴到 [ɛ]，不然會變成 lesson。[s] 之後直接接很輕的 [ən]，字尾 [n] 舌尖頂上齒齦收住。重音在第一音節。
listen.tip_en: The t in listen is silent: say [ˈlɪsən]; learners often follow the spelling and say [ˈlɪstən]. The first syllable has a short, relaxed [ɪ]—don't stretch it into [i] or open up to [ɛ], or it becomes lesson. After [s], go straight into a very light [ən], and finish the [n] with the tongue tip on the gum ridge. The stress is on the first syllable.

examples.en: Please listen to your teacher.
examples.zh: 請聽老師說話。

examples.en: I like to listen to music at night.
examples.zh: 我喜歡晚上聽音樂。

listen.spelling_zh: 中間的 t 不發音，和 Christmas 的 t 一樣。
listen.spelling_en: The t in the middle is silent, as in Christmas.

little.tip_zh: 第二音節 [tḷ] 沒有母音，[ḷ] 自己就是一個音節。美式說話時，tt 會變成舌尖輕點上齒齦的彈音；舌尖接著留在原位，舌根往後抬，發出暗 L。容易在 [t] 和 [ḷ] 之間多塞一個清楚的母音，或乾脆把結尾的 [ḷ] 漏掉，只剩 [lɪt]。
little.tip_en: The second syllable [tḷ] has no vowel; [ḷ] is a syllable by itself. In American speech, tt becomes a quick tap of the tongue tip on the gum ridge; the tip then stays put while the back of the tongue rises for a dark L. Learners often squeeze a clear vowel between [t] and [ḷ], or simply drop the final [ḷ] and leave just [lɪt].

examples.en: I have a little brother.
examples.zh: 我有一個弟弟。

examples.en: Can I have a little more rice?
examples.zh: 我可以再多吃一點飯嗎？

lonely.tip_zh: 拼字中間的 e 不發音，所以只有兩個音節 [lon·lɪ]，不要唸成三個音節。[n] 和 [l] 舌尖位置都在上齒齦：舌尖頂住不放，從鼻音 [n] 直接換成 [l]，中間不加母音。[o] 嘴唇收圓、拉長，和 only 押韻，可以先唸 only 再加 [l]。
lonely.tip_en: The e in the middle is silent, so there are only two syllables, [lon·lɪ] — not three. [n] and [l] both use the gum ridge: keep the tongue tip there and switch straight from nasal [n] to [l], with no vowel between. Round the lips for a long [o]; it rhymes with only, so say only and then add [l] in front.

examples.en: The puppy felt lonely, so I played with it.
examples.zh: 小狗覺得很孤單，所以我陪牠玩。

examples.en: Call your grandma so she won't feel lonely.
examples.zh: 打電話給奶奶，她才不會覺得寂寞。

lonely.spelling_zh: 中間的 e 不發音，只有兩個音節。
lonely.spelling_en: The middle e is silent; only two syllables.

long.tip_zh: 母音 [ɔ] 嘴巴要張開、嘴唇稍圓；容易套用中文「龍」的音，母音太接近 [u]，嘴巴也開得太小。字尾 [ŋ] 用舌根頂住軟顎，聲音從鼻子出來，之後不要再補一個 [g]。和 song、strong 押韻，可以先唸 song 再換開頭的 [l]。
long.tip_en: The vowel [ɔ] needs an open mouth with slightly rounded lips; learners often borrow the Mandarin syllable for 'dragon', whose vowel is too close to [u] with the mouth too closed. For the final [ŋ], press the back of the tongue to the soft palate and let the sound out through the nose — don't add a [g] after it. It rhymes with song and strong: say song, then switch the start to [l].

examples.en: Giraffes have very long necks.
examples.zh: 長頸鹿有很長的脖子。

examples.en: It was a long day at school.
examples.zh: 今天在學校是漫長的一天。

look.tip_zh: [ʊ] 短而鬆，嘴唇只微微圓起，和 book、cook 的母音相同；容易唸成長而噘唇的 [u]，聽起來像人名 Luke。拼字 oo 在這裡不是 food 的 [u]。字尾 [k] 舌根頂住軟顎停住；look at 連讀時，[k] 直接接到 at 的母音。
look.tip_en: [ʊ] is short and lax, with the lips only slightly rounded — the same vowel as in book and cook; learners often use a long, pouted [u], which sounds like the name Luke. Here oo is not the [u] of food. Stop the final [k] with the back of the tongue on the soft palate; in look at, the [k] links straight into the vowel of at.

examples.en: Look at the rainbow!
examples.zh: 看那道彩虹！

examples.en: Let's look for your lost sock.
examples.zh: 我們來找你不見的襪子。

lose.tip_zh: 拼字看起來像 nose，但 lose 的母音是長的 [u]，和 choose、whose 押韻，不要唸成 [o]。字尾 s 唸有聲的 [z]，喉嚨要振動；唸成無聲的 [s] 就變成 loose（鬆的）。在有聲的 [z] 前面，[u] 會拉得比較長，可以利用這點把兩個字分開。
lose.tip_en: It looks like nose, but lose has a long [u], rhyming with choose and whose — not [o]. The s is a voiced [z], so the throat buzzes; make it voiceless [s] and you get loose. Before voiced [z] the [u] is held longer, which also helps keep the two words apart.

examples.en: Don't lose your eraser again!
examples.zh: 不要再把橡皮擦弄丟了！

examples.en: It's okay to lose a game sometimes.
examples.zh: 有時候輸掉比賽也沒關係。

lose.spelling_zh: o 唸 [u]，s 唸 [z]；和 loose 不同。
lose.spelling_en: o says [u] and s says [z]; not the same as loose.

loud.tip_zh: 母音 [aʊ] 是雙母音：從張大嘴的 [a] 開始，再把嘴唇收圓滑到 [ʊ]，要有明顯的動作，和 cloud、proud 押韻。字尾 [d] 是有聲子音，舌尖頂住上齒齦、喉嚨振動；容易唸成無聲的 [t]，或把 [d] 漏掉只剩母音。
loud.tip_en: [aʊ] is a two-part vowel: start from a wide-open [a], then round the lips and glide to [ʊ] with a clear movement; it rhymes with cloud and proud. The final [d] is voiced — tongue tip on the gum ridge, throat buzzing; learners often devoice it to [t] or drop the [d] and end on the vowel.

examples.en: The music is too loud.
examples.zh: 音樂太大聲了。

examples.en: Please read the story in a loud voice.
examples.zh: 請大聲唸這個故事。

love.tip_zh: 拼字 o 在這裡唸短而放鬆的 [ʌ]，和 above、glove 押韻，不要唸成圓唇的 [o] 或 [ɑ]。字尾 [v] 要用上齒輕碰下唇、喉嚨振動；容易唸成無聲的 [f]、改成 [b]，或結尾乾脆不發音。拼字結尾的 e 不發音。
love.tip_en: The o here says a short, relaxed [ʌ], rhyming with above and glove — not a rounded [o] or [ɑ]. For the final [v], rest the upper teeth on the lower lip and keep the throat buzzing; learners often turn it into a voiceless [f], change it to [b], or leave it out. The final e is silent.

examples.en: I love my family.
examples.zh: 我愛我的家人。

examples.en: We love to play in the snow.
examples.zh: 我們很喜歡在雪地裡玩。

love.spelling_zh: o 唸 [ʌ]；結尾 e 不發音。
love.spelling_en: o says [ʌ]; the final e is silent.

lovely.tip_zh: 中間 [v] 接 [l] 是重點：上齒碰下唇發完有聲的 [v] 後，舌尖馬上抬到上齒齦接 [l]；容易漏掉 [v]，或在 [v] 和 [l] 之間多加母音。拼字中間的 e 不發音，所以只有兩個音節。第一音節 [lʌv] 重讀，[ʌ] 短而放鬆。
lovely.tip_en: The key is [v] running into [l] in the middle: after a voiced [v] with upper teeth on the lower lip, lift the tongue tip straight to the gum ridge for [l]; learners often drop the [v] or slip a vowel between [v] and [l]. The middle e is silent, so there are only two syllables. Stress the first syllable [lʌv], with a short, relaxed [ʌ].

examples.en: What a lovely day for a picnic!
examples.zh: 今天真是野餐的好天氣！

examples.en: Thank you for the lovely card.
examples.zh: 謝謝你送的可愛卡片。

lovely.spelling_zh: 中間的 e 不發音，只有兩個音節。
lovely.spelling_en: The middle e is silent; only two syllables.

low.tip_zh: 母音 [o] 嘴唇收圓、拉長，結尾嘴唇再稍微往內收；拼字 ow 在這裡和 snow、slow 一樣唸 [o]，不是 cow 的 [aʊ]。開頭 [l] 要用舌尖頂住上齒齦，不要唸成鼻音 [n]，否則會聽起來像 no。和 go、show 押韻。
low.tip_en: For [o], round the lips and hold the sound, closing them in slightly at the end; here ow says [o] as in snow and slow, not the [aʊ] of cow. Start [l] with the tongue tip on the gum ridge — don't turn it into a nasal [n], or it will sound like no. It rhymes with go and show.

examples.en: The shelf is low, so I can reach it.
examples.zh: 書架很低，所以我搆得到。

examples.en: Please speak in a low voice in the library.
examples.zh: 在圖書館請小聲說話。

lucky.tip_zh: 第一音節的母音是短而放鬆的 [ʌ]，嘴巴半開、嘴唇不圓；容易受拼字 u 影響，唸成噘唇的 [u]。拼字 ck 只代表一個 [k]，不要唸成兩個 k 停頓一下。重音在第一音節 [lʌ]，結尾的 [ɪ] 輕而短，不要拉長成 [i]。
lucky.tip_en: The first vowel is a short, relaxed [ʌ]: mouth half open, lips unrounded; the letter u tempts learners into a pouted [u]. The letters ck stand for one [k] — don't pause as if there were two k's. Stress the first syllable [lʌ]; the final [ɪ] is short and light, not a stretched [i].

examples.en: You are lucky to have such nice friends.
examples.zh: 你很幸運有這麼好的朋友。

examples.en: Seven is my lucky number.
examples.zh: 七是我的幸運數字。

lunch.tip_zh: 字尾 [ntʃ] 是重點：舌尖先頂住上齒齦發 [n]，接著舌頭往後一點、嘴唇微噘，放出無聲的 [tʃ]；結尾不要加上 [i] 之類的母音，讓一個音節變兩個。母音 [ʌ] 短而放鬆，嘴巴半開，不要照拼字 u 唸成噘唇的 [u]。
lunch.tip_en: The key is the final [ntʃ]: put the tongue tip on the gum ridge for [n], then move it slightly back and round the lips a little to release a voiceless [tʃ]; don't add a vowel such as [i] that turns one syllable into two. The vowel [ʌ] is short and relaxed with the mouth half open — don't follow the letter u into a pouted [u].

examples.en: What did you have for lunch?
examples.zh: 你午餐吃了什麼？

examples.en: We eat lunch in our classroom.
examples.zh: 我們在教室吃午餐。

machine.tip_zh: 拼字 ch 在這裡唸 [ʃ]，不是 [tʃ]，因為這個字來自法文；發 [ʃ] 時嘴唇噘起，只有氣流、舌頭不碰上顎。重音在第二音節 [ʃin]，[i] 要拉長；第一音節 [mə] 很輕，不要把重音放在前面，也不要唸成清楚的 [mæ]。拼字結尾 e 不發音。
machine.tip_en: Here ch says [ʃ], not [tʃ], because the word comes from French; for [ʃ], round the lips and let air through without the tongue touching the roof of the mouth. Stress the second syllable [ʃin] and hold the [i]; the first syllable [mə] is very light — don't stress it or make it a clear [mæ]. The final e is silent.

examples.en: This machine sells cold drinks.
examples.zh: 這台機器在賣冷飲。

examples.en: Mom put the clothes in the washing machine.
examples.zh: 媽媽把衣服放進洗衣機。

machine.spelling_zh: ch 唸 [ʃ]，不是 [tʃ]；結尾 e 不發音。
machine.spelling_en: ch says [ʃ], not [tʃ]; the final e is silent.

mad.tip_zh: [æ] 下巴大大拉低、嘴角往兩邊咧開；唸成短而放鬆的 [ʌ] 就變成 mud（泥巴），開口不夠成 [ɛ] 則像 med。字尾 [d] 是有聲子音，舌尖頂住上齒齦、喉嚨振動，不要唸成 [t]；[æ] 在 [d] 前面會稍微拉長。和 bad、sad 押韻。
mad.tip_en: For [æ], drop the jaw a lot and pull the lip corners wide; a short, relaxed [ʌ] turns it into mud, and too small an opening ([ɛ]) sounds like 'med'. The final [d] is voiced — tongue tip on the gum ridge, throat buzzing — not [t]; the [æ] is held a little longer before it. It rhymes with bad and sad.

examples.en: Mom was mad because I didn't clean my room.
examples.zh: 媽媽生氣了，因為我沒有打掃房間。

examples.en: Don't be mad at me, it was an accident.
examples.zh: 別生我的氣，那是不小心的。

magic.tip_zh: 重音在第一音節 [mæ]，[æ] 要把嘴巴張大、嘴角咧開。拼字 g 在 i 前面唸 [dʒ]，不是 [g]，嘴唇微噘、聲帶振動。第二音節 [dʒɪk] 的 [ɪ] 短而鬆，字尾 [k] 舌根頂住軟顎就停，不要再加母音。不要把重音移到第二音節。
magic.tip_en: Stress the first syllable [mæ], with the mouth wide open and the lip corners spread for [æ]. The g before i says [dʒ], not [g]: lips slightly rounded, voice on. In the second syllable [dʒɪk], [ɪ] is short and lax, and the final [k] simply stops with the back of the tongue on the soft palate — no extra vowel. Don't shift the stress to the second syllable.

examples.en: The clown did a magic trick.
examples.zh: 小丑變了一個魔術。

examples.en: Please is a magic word.
examples.zh: 「請」是一個神奇的字。

mail.tip_zh: [e] 先從 [e] 滑到 [ɪ]，接著還要接字尾的暗 L：舌尖碰上齒齦，舌根同時往後抬起。容易漏掉 [l] 只剩 [me]，聽起來像 may；也有人在 [l] 後面多加母音，唸成兩個音節。mail 和 male（男性）發音完全相同。和 nail、tail 押韻。
mail.tip_en: Glide [e] toward [ɪ], then still finish with the dark L: tongue tip touching the gum ridge while the back of the tongue rises. Learners often drop the [l], leaving [me], which sounds like may; others add a vowel after [l] and make two syllables. Mail and male sound exactly the same. It rhymes with nail and tail.

examples.en: Did we get any mail today?
examples.zh: 我們今天有收到信嗎？

examples.en: Grandpa checks the mail every morning.
examples.zh: 爺爺每天早上都會看信箱。

mailman.tip_zh: mailman 的重音在 mail。最容易出錯的是 mail 結尾的 [l]：因為後面緊接 [m]，學生常把它吞掉，唸成 [ˈmemæn]。做法：發完 [e] 之後，舌尖往上頂上齒齦、舌根抬起，停一下再閉上雙唇發 [m]。第二音節 [mæn] 帶次重音，嘴巴張大、嘴角往兩邊拉。先分開說 mail、man，再慢慢連起來。
mailman.tip_en: The stress in mailman is on mail. The easiest place to go wrong is the [l] at the end of mail: because [m] follows right after, learners often swallow it and say [ˈmemæn]. How to do it: after [e], push the tongue tip up to the gum ridge and raise the back of the tongue, pause briefly, then close the lips for [m]. The second syllable [mæn] has secondary stress: open the mouth wide with the corners spread. Say mail and man separately first, then join them slowly.

examples.en: The mailman brings letters every morning.
examples.zh: 郵差每天早上送信來。

examples.en: Our mailman always waves to us.
examples.zh: 我們的郵差總是向我們揮手。

main.tip_zh: main [men]、man [mæn]、mean [min] 三個字只差中間的母音，唸錯就會變成別的字：main 的 [e] 要拉長，從 [e] 滑向 [ɪ]，嘴巴開度比 man 小、比 mean 大。拼字 ai 在這裡唸 [e]，和 rain、train 押韻。字尾 [n] 要用舌尖頂住上齒齦收住，不要收成舌根的 [ŋ]，也不要在後面多加母音。
main.tip_en: Main [men], man [mæn] and mean [min] differ only in the middle vowel, so a wrong vowel makes a different word: hold main's [e] and glide it toward [ɪ], with the mouth less open than for man but more open than for mean. Here ai says [e], rhyming with rain and train. Close the final [n] with the tongue tip on the gum ridge — not with the back of the tongue ([ŋ]) — and don't add a vowel after it.

examples.en: The main door of the school is red.
examples.zh: 學校的大門是紅色的。

examples.en: Rice is the main food in Taiwan.
examples.zh: 米飯是台灣的主食。

make.tip_zh: [e] 要唸夠長，並從 [e] 滑到 [ɪ]；容易唸成短而不滑動的 [ɛ]，聽起來像 meck。拼字結尾 e 不發音，讓 a 唸 [e]，和 cake、take 押韻。字尾 [k] 舌根頂住軟顎停住；make a 連讀時，[k] 直接接後面的母音，中間不停頓。
make.tip_en: Hold [e] long enough and glide from [e] to [ɪ]; learners often make it a short, steady [ɛ], so it sounds like 'meck'. The final e is silent and makes the a say [e], rhyming with cake and take. Stop the final [k] with the back of the tongue on the soft palate; in make a, the [k] links straight into the next vowel with no pause.

examples.en: Let's make a card for Mom.
examples.zh: 我們來做一張卡片給媽媽。

examples.en: Can you make a paper plane?
examples.zh: 你會摺紙飛機嗎？

man.tip_zh: man 的母音是 [æ]，台灣學生常把嘴巴張得不夠大，唸得像 men（複數「男人們」）的 [ɛ]，單數和複數就分不清了。發 [æ] 時下巴往下拉、嘴角同時往兩邊拉開，嘴巴要比說「欸」時張得更大。字尾 [n] 要把舌尖頂住上排牙齒後方的齒齦停一下，不要收成 [ŋ]。
man.tip_en: The vowel in man is [æ]. Taiwanese students often don't open the mouth wide enough, so it sounds like the [ɛ] of men (the plural, 'men'), and singular and plural blur together. For [æ], drop the jaw and pull the corners of the mouth wide at the same time, opening wider than for 'eh'. For the final [n], press the tongue tip on the ridge behind the upper front teeth and hold it briefly; don't let it turn into [ŋ].

examples.en: The man next door walks his dog every morning.
examples.zh: 隔壁那位先生每天早上都會遛狗。

examples.en: Ask the man at the front desk for help.
examples.zh: 去請櫃台的那位先生幫忙。

many.tip_zh: 拼字是 a，但第一音節唸 [ɛ]，和 any 一樣；照拼字唸成 [æ] 是很典型的錯誤。重音在第一音節 [mɛ]，結尾 [ɪ] 輕而短。也要和 money [ˈmʌnɪ] 分開：many 的 [ɛ] 嘴角稍微展開，money 的 [ʌ] 放鬆、嘴巴半開。
many.tip_en: It's spelled with a, but the first syllable says [ɛ], just like any; reading it as [æ] from the spelling is a typical mistake. Stress the first syllable [mɛ]; the final [ɪ] is short and light. Keep it apart from money [ˈmʌnɪ]: many's [ɛ] has slightly spread lips, money's [ʌ] is relaxed with the mouth half open.

examples.en: How many books do you have?
examples.zh: 你有幾本書？

examples.en: There are many birds in the tree.
examples.zh: 樹上有很多鳥。

many.spelling_zh: a 唸 [ɛ]，和 any 一樣。
many.spelling_en: The a says [ɛ], just like in any.

map.tip_zh: [æ] 下巴拉低、嘴角咧開；開口太小唸成 [ɛ] 會像 mep，嘴角沒咧開、舌頭太後面成 [ɑ] 則變成 mop（拖把）。字尾 [p] 雙唇閉上就停住，美式常常不放氣，不要再張開嘴多加母音。和 cap、clap 押韻。
map.tip_en: For [æ], drop the jaw and spread the lip corners; open too little ([ɛ]) and it sounds like 'mep', while unspread lips with the tongue too far back ([ɑ]) give mop. For the final [p], close the lips and stop — Americans often don't release it — and don't open again to add a vowel. It rhymes with cap and clap.

examples.en: Let's look at the map of Taiwan.
examples.zh: 我們來看台灣地圖。

examples.en: I drew a map of my school.
examples.zh: 我畫了一張我們學校的地圖。

march.tip_zh: 先張大嘴發 [ɑ]，再把舌尖往後捲起帶出 [r]；接著舌頭從捲舌的位置移到上齒齦後方，嘴唇噘起放出無聲的 [tʃ]。容易漏掉 [r]，或在 [tʃ] 後面多加母音。March 和 mark 只差最後一個音：March 是 [tʃ]，mark 是舌根的 [k]。
march.tip_en: Open wide for [ɑ], then curl the tongue tip back to add [r]; next, move the tongue from the curled position to just behind the gum ridge and round the lips to release a voiceless [tʃ]. Learners often drop the [r] or add a vowel after [tʃ]. March and mark differ only in the last sound: [tʃ] for March, a back-of-the-tongue [k] for mark.

examples.en: My sister was born in March.
examples.zh: 我妹妹是三月出生的。

examples.en: The weather gets warmer in March.
examples.zh: 三月天氣會變暖。

mark.tip_zh: [ɑr] 是重點：嘴巴張大發 [ɑ] 後，舌尖往後捲、不碰上顎；沒有捲舌的話會聽起來像 mock。字尾 [k] 舌根頂住軟顎就停住，不要多加母音。和 park、dark 押韻，可以先唸 park 再把開頭換成雙唇閉合的 [m]。
mark.tip_en: [ɑr] is the key: after opening wide for [ɑ], curl the tongue tip back without touching the roof of the mouth; without the curl it sounds like mock. Stop the final [k] with the back of the tongue on the soft palate — no extra vowel. It rhymes with park and dark: say park, then change the start to [m] with closed lips.

examples.en: Mark the right answer with a circle.
examples.zh: 用圓圈標出正確答案。

examples.en: Please mark the date on the calendar.
examples.zh: 請在月曆上把日期做記號。

marker.tip_zh: marker 有兩個捲舌音：第一音節 [mɑr] 嘴巴張大後舌尖往後捲，字尾 [kɚ] 也要捲舌。台灣學生常把兩個 r 都省掉，唸成「媽可」。先唸 car [kɑr] 練好 [ɑr]，再換成 [mɑr]，最後收在捲舌的 [kɚ]，重音放在前面。
marker.tip_en: Marker has two r-colored sounds: in the first syllable [mɑr] open the mouth wide and then curl the tongue back, and the ending [kɚ] is also r-colored. Taiwanese learners often drop both r's and say something like 'ma-ke'. Practice [ɑr] with car [kɑr], switch to [mɑr], then finish on an r-colored [kɚ], stress on the first syllable.

examples.en: I need a red marker for my poster.
examples.zh: 我需要一支紅色簽字筆來畫海報。

examples.en: Please put the cap back on the marker.
examples.zh: 請把簽字筆的蓋子蓋回去。

market.tip_zh: 重音在第一音節 [mɑr]，嘴巴張大再捲舌，r 不能省。第二音節 [kət] 很輕，母音只是弱弱的 [ə]，不要唸成清楚的 [kɛt]。字尾 [t] 舌尖頂住上牙齦停住就好，不要多加母音唸成「馬克特」三拍。
market.tip_en: Stress the first syllable [mɑr]: open wide, then curl the tongue; don't drop the r. The second syllable [kət] is very light with a weak [ə], not a clear [kɛt]. For the final [t], just stop with the tongue tip on the gum ridge; don't add a vowel and make it three beats like 'ma-ke-te'.

examples.en: We buy fresh fruit at the market.
examples.zh: 我們在市場買新鮮水果。

examples.en: My grandma goes to the morning market every Sunday.
examples.zh: 我奶奶每個星期天都去早市。

married.tip_zh: 第一音節是 [mɛ]，嘴巴半開，不是 [mɑ]；學生常被拼字 a 誤導。結尾 -ied 只唸 [ɪd]，不是 tried 的 [aɪd]，也不要拆成三個音節。字尾 [d] 要輕輕發出聲音，否則聽起來只剩 marry。
married.tip_en: The first syllable is [mɛ], mouth half open, not [mɑ]; learners are often misled by the letter a. The ending -ied is just [ɪd], not the [aɪd] of tried, and don't split it into three syllables. Voice the final [d] lightly, or it sounds like just 'marry'.

examples.en: My aunt got married last spring.
examples.zh: 我阿姨去年春天結婚了。

examples.en: My uncle is married and has two kids.
examples.zh: 我叔叔已經結婚，有兩個小孩。

mask.tip_zh: [æ] 嘴巴要張大、嘴角往兩旁拉，比 [ɛ] 開得多；學生常唸成 [mɛsk]。字尾 [sk] 兩個子音要緊接著，不要在中間或後面加母音唸成「妹斯克」。先唸熟 ask [æsk]，再在前面加上雙唇閉起的 [m]。
mask.tip_en: For [æ] open the mouth wide and pull the corners of the lips back, wider than [ɛ]; learners often say [mɛsk]. The final [sk] must be one tight cluster: don't add a vowel in or after it ('mei-si-ke'). Get ask [æsk] smooth first, then put a closed-lip [m] in front.

examples.en: Please wear a mask when you have a cold.
examples.zh: 感冒的時候請戴口罩。

examples.en: I made a lion mask in art class.
examples.zh: 我在美術課做了一個獅子面具。

math.tip_zh: math 結尾是無聲的 [θ]，台灣學生常唸成 [s]，聽起來像 mass，或乾脆把尾音吞掉。發 [θ] 時舌尖輕輕伸到上下門牙之間，讓氣流從舌頭和牙齒的縫隙送出，聲帶不震動；送完氣就停，不要再加一個母音唸成「麥斯」。前面的 [æ] 嘴巴也要張大，不要唸成 [ɛ]。
math.tip_en: math ends in voiceless [θ]. Taiwanese students often say [s], so it sounds like mass, or they drop the final sound. For [θ], put the tongue tip lightly between the upper and lower front teeth and push air through the gap between tongue and teeth, with no voice; stop once the air is out and don't add a vowel (like 'mai-si'). The [æ] before it also needs a wide-open mouth, not [ɛ].

examples.en: Math is my favorite subject at school.
examples.zh: 數學是我在學校最喜歡的科目。

examples.en: We have a math test on Friday.
examples.zh: 我們星期五有數學考試。

matter.tip_zh: matter 重音在第一音節 [mæ]，[æ] 要張大嘴。美式口語中，夾在兩個母音之間的 [t] 常變成輕快的閃音：舌尖在上齒齦輕彈一下，聽起來接近輕的 [d]。台灣學生常把 [t] 唸得又重又用力，再把字尾 [ɚ] 唸成「特」不捲舌。第二音節要輕而短，舌頭往後捲。
matter.tip_en: matter is stressed on the first syllable [mæ], with a wide-open [æ]. In everyday American speech, a [t] between two vowels often becomes a quick flap: the tongue tip taps the ridge behind the upper teeth once, sounding close to a light [d]. Taiwanese students often hit the [t] hard and then say the final [ɚ] like 'te' without curling the tongue. Keep the second syllable light and short, with the tongue curled back.

examples.en: What's the matter? You look tired.
examples.zh: 怎麼了？你看起來很累。

examples.en: No matter how busy she is, Mom reads to us at night.
examples.zh: 不管多忙，媽媽晚上都會唸書給我們聽。

may.tip_zh: KK 的 [e] 要從 [e] 往 [ɪ] 滑，嘴巴由半開慢慢收小；學生常唸成短而平的 [mɛ]，或和 my [maɪ] 搞混。my 嘴巴開得很大，may 開口小得多。用同韻的 day [de]、gray 來練，只把開頭換成雙唇的 [m]。
may.tip_en: KK [e] glides from [e] toward [ɪ], the mouth closing a little; learners often say a short, flat [mɛ] or confuse it with my [maɪ]. My opens the mouth wide; may opens it much less. Practice with rhymes day [de] and gray, just changing the start to a lip [m].

examples.en: May I use the bathroom, please?
examples.zh: 請問我可以去上廁所嗎？

examples.en: It may rain this afternoon, so bring an umbrella.
examples.zh: 今天下午可能會下雨，帶把傘吧。

may.spelling_zh: 大寫 May 是「五月」，發音一樣。
may.spelling_en: Capital May is the month of May; same pronunciation.

maybe.tip_zh: 重音在第一音節 [me]，第二音節 [bɪ] 輕而短。學生常把兩個音節唸得一樣重，或把 be 拉長成 [bi]，聽起來像兩個字 may be。當「也許」用時要連成一個字、前重後輕；[e] 記得往 [ɪ] 滑。
maybe.tip_en: Stress the first syllable [me]; the second syllable [bɪ] is short and light. Learners often give both syllables equal weight or stretch 'be' to [bi], so it sounds like two words, 'may be'. As the adverb 'perhaps' it is one word, strong then weak; remember [e] glides toward [ɪ].

examples.en: Maybe we can play outside after lunch.
examples.zh: 也許我們午餐後可以去外面玩。

examples.en: Maybe Dad will cook noodles tonight.
examples.zh: 也許爸爸今晚會煮麵。

meal.tip_zh: [i] 要拉長、嘴角往兩旁，接著是字尾暗 L：舌尖頂住上牙齦，舌根往後抬。學生常把 l 省掉唸成「米」，或多加母音唸成「米歐」。也要和 mail [mel]、mile [maɪl] 分清楚，三個字只差中間的母音，meal 嘴形最扁、最長。
meal.tip_en: Hold [i] long with spread lips, then the dark L at the end: tongue tip on the gum ridge, back of the tongue raised. Learners often drop the l ('mi') or add a vowel ('mi-o'). Keep it apart from mail [mel] and mile [maɪl]; only the vowel differs, and meal has the flattest, longest one.

examples.en: We eat our evening meal at seven.
examples.zh: 我們七點吃晚餐。

examples.en: Let's wash our hands before the meal.
examples.zh: 吃飯前我們先洗手吧。

mean.tip_zh: 字尾 [n] 舌尖要頂在上牙齦停住，不能只用鼻子哼或改成舌根的 [ŋ]；學生常把 mean 唸得像帶 ng 尾巴的 [miŋ]。[i] 要拉長，並和 man [mæn]、main [men] 分清楚。練習時唸完 [n] 先別放開舌尖，感覺它還貼著上牙齦。
mean.tip_en: For the final [n], stop with the tongue tip pressed on the gum ridge; don't just hum through the nose or switch to the back-of-tongue [ŋ]. Learners often make mean sound like [miŋ]. Keep [i] long and distinct from man [mæn] and main [men]. In practice, keep the tongue tip on the gum ridge after [n] to feel it.

examples.en: What does this word mean?
examples.zh: 這個字是什麼意思？

examples.en: I didn't mean to wake you up.
examples.zh: 我不是故意要吵醒你的。

meat.tip_zh: meat 和 meet 發音完全一樣，都是 [mit]，要靠句子判斷意思。難點在字尾 [t]：舌尖頂住上牙齦後停住，學生常把 t 吞掉只剩「咪」，或多加母音唸成「咪特」。[i] 要長而扁，別唸成短的 [ɪ]。
meat.tip_en: Meat and meet sound exactly the same, [mit]; context tells you which. The hard part is the final [t]: stop with the tongue tip on the gum ridge. Learners often swallow the t ('mi') or add a vowel ('mi-te'). Keep [i] long and spread, not a short [ɪ].

examples.en: My little brother doesn't like to eat meat.
examples.zh: 我弟弟不喜歡吃肉。

examples.en: We put meat and vegetables on the grill.
examples.zh: 我們把肉和蔬菜放在烤架上。

meat.spelling_zh: 和 meet 同音，ea 與 ee 都唸 [i]。
meat.spelling_en: Sounds the same as meet; ea and ee are both [i].

medicine.tip_zh: medicine 重音在第一音節 [mɛ]，後面兩個音節都是輕的 [ə]。台灣學生常照拼字把每個字母都唸清楚，三拍一樣重，或把 di 唸成 [di]。正確節奏是重－輕－輕：第一拍用力，[də] 和 [sən] 快速帶過，嘴巴放鬆。字尾 [n] 舌尖要頂住上齒齦，不要變成 [ŋ]。
medicine.tip_en: medicine is stressed on the first syllable [mɛ]; the next two syllables both have the weak [ə]. Taiwanese students often pronounce every letter clearly from the spelling, giving three equal beats, or say di as [di]. The correct rhythm is strong–weak–weak: hit the first beat, then run [də] and [sən] quickly with a relaxed mouth. For the final [n], press the tongue tip to the ridge behind the upper teeth; don't let it become [ŋ].

examples.en: Please take your medicine after dinner.
examples.zh: 晚餐後請記得吃藥。

examples.en: The doctor gave me some medicine for my cold.
examples.zh: 醫生開了一些感冒藥給我。

medium.tip_zh: medium 重音在第一音節，me 唸長音 [i]，不是 medicine 裡的短音 [ɛ]；台灣學生看到 med 常順口唸成 [ɛ]。後面的 [dɪ] 和 [əm] 輕輕帶過。字尾是 [m]：中文沒有以 m 結尾的字，學生常收成 [n]，或多加一個「姆」的母音。正確做法是最後雙唇輕輕閉上就停，不要再出聲。
medium.tip_en: medium is stressed on the first syllable, and me is the long [i], not the short [ɛ] of medicine; seeing 'med', Taiwanese students often slip into [ɛ]. The following [dɪ] and [əm] are said lightly. The word ends in [m]: Mandarin has no syllables ending in m, so students often finish with [n] or add an extra 'mu' vowel. Instead, just close the lips gently at the end and stop, with no extra sound.

examples.en: Can I have a medium cup of milk tea?
examples.zh: 我可以點一杯中杯奶茶嗎？

examples.en: This T-shirt comes in small, medium, and large.
examples.zh: 這件 T 恤有小號、中號和大號。

meet.tip_zh: meet 的 [i] 要拉長、嘴角往兩邊拉開，學生常唸成短促的 [ɪ]，聽起來不像「見面」。字尾 [t] 接 you 時常連成像 [mitʃu] 的音，這是自然的美式連音；單獨說時 t 輕輕收住，不要加母音唸成兩拍。
meet.tip_en: Hold the [i] of meet long with the lips spread; learners often make it a short [ɪ]. Before you, the final [t] often blends into something like [mitʃu], a natural American linking; said alone, just stop the t lightly without adding a vowel or a second beat.

examples.en: Nice to meet you!
examples.zh: 很高興認識你！

examples.en: Let's meet at the park after school.
examples.zh: 放學後我們在公園見面吧。

meet.spelling_zh: 和 meat 同音，ee 唸 [i]。
meet.spelling_en: Sounds the same as meat; ee is [i].

meeting.tip_zh: 重音在第一音節 [mi]，[i] 要長。中間的 t 夾在兩個母音之間，美式英語會變成很快的彈舌音，聽起來接近輕輕的 d，不要用力送氣。字尾 [ɪŋ] 是舌根頂住軟顎的鼻音，不要唸成 [ɪn]，也別把 [ɪ] 拉成長 [i]。
meeting.tip_en: Stress the first syllable [mi] with a long [i]. The t between two vowels becomes a quick flap in American English, close to a light d; don't puff it out. The ending [ɪŋ] is a nasal with the back of the tongue against the soft palate, not [ɪn], and don't stretch [ɪ] into a long [i].

examples.en: My mom has a meeting at nine o'clock.
examples.zh: 我媽媽九點要開會。

examples.en: We have a class meeting every Friday.
examples.zh: 我們每個星期五都有班會。

member.tip_zh: 第一音節 [mɛm] 結尾要閉上雙唇發 m，再直接爆出 [b]；學生常把中間的 m 省掉，唸成 [mɛbɚ]。字尾 [ɚ] 要捲舌，不能唸成平的「伯」。同韻的 remember、November 結尾都是 [mbɚ]，可以一起練。
member.tip_en: The first syllable [mɛm] ends with closed lips for m, then the [b] pops straight out; learners often drop that middle m and say [mɛbɚ]. The final [ɚ] must be r-colored, not a flat 'bo'. Rhymes remember and November end the same way, [mbɚ], so practice them together.

examples.en: She is a member of the school band.
examples.zh: 她是學校樂隊的成員。

examples.en: Every family member helps clean the house.
examples.zh: 每位家人都幫忙打掃家裡。

menu.tip_zh: 重音在第一音節 [mɛn]，嘴巴半開。第二音節是 [ju]，開頭有一個 [j] 滑音，學生常漏掉唸成 [mɛnu]，或多加一拍變成 [mɛnɪu]。[n] 結束時舌尖還在上牙齦，就直接滑進 [ju]，像 [n] 後面接著唸 you。
menu.tip_en: Stress the first syllable [mɛn], mouth half open. The second syllable is [ju], starting with a [j] glide; learners often skip it ([mɛnu]) or add an extra beat ([mɛnɪu]). As [n] ends, with the tongue tip still on the gum ridge, slide straight into [ju], like saying you right after [n].

examples.en: Can I see the menu, please?
examples.zh: 請給我看一下菜單好嗎？

examples.en: Click the menu to find the games.
examples.zh: 點選單就可以找到遊戲。

metro.tip_zh: 第一音節 [mɛ] 重讀、短促，第二音節 [tro] 有次重音。[t] 和 [r] 要黏成一組，學生常在中間加母音唸成「妹特羅」。舌尖碰到上牙齦後立刻往後捲，聽起來帶一點 ch 的感覺；字尾 [o] 嘴唇收圓並滑向 [u]。
metro.tip_en: The first syllable [mɛ] is stressed and short; the second, [tro], has secondary stress. Keep [t] and [r] together as one cluster; learners often add a vowel between them ('mei-te-luo'). Touch the gum ridge and curl back immediately, so it sounds a little like ch; end with rounded [o] gliding toward [u].

examples.en: We take the metro to school every day.
examples.zh: 我們每天搭捷運上學。

examples.en: The metro station is near my house.
examples.zh: 捷運站在我家附近。

middle.tip_zh: 第二音節是成音節的 [ḷ]：發完 [d] 舌尖不離開上牙齦，直接放下舌頭兩側發 l，中間沒有母音。學生常唸成「米豆」或把 l 唸成「歐」。第一音節的 [ɪ] 短而放鬆，不是長 [i]，重音在前。
middle.tip_en: The second syllable is a syllabic [ḷ]: after [d], keep the tongue tip on the gum ridge and just drop the sides of the tongue for l, with no vowel in between. Learners often say 'mi-dou' or turn the l into an 'o'. The first [ɪ] is short and relaxed, not a long [i]; stress is on the front.

examples.en: Write your name in the middle of the page.
examples.zh: 把名字寫在這一頁的中間。

examples.en: My sister is the middle child.
examples.zh: 我妹妹是家裡排行中間的孩子。

mile.tip_zh: [aɪ] 從大開口的 [a] 滑到 [ɪ]，接著是字尾暗 L：舌尖頂上牙齦、舌根抬高。學生常把 l 吞掉，mile 聽起來就像 my。也要和 meal [mil]、mail [mel] 分清楚，三個字只差中間的母音，mile 嘴巴開得最大。
mile.tip_en: [aɪ] glides from a wide-open [a] to [ɪ], then the dark L: tongue tip on the gum ridge, back of the tongue raised. Learners often swallow the l, so mile sounds like my. Also keep it apart from meal [mil] and mail [mel]; only the vowel differs, and mile opens the mouth widest.

examples.en: The park is one mile from our house.
examples.zh: 公園離我們家一英里。

examples.en: We walked a mile to the beach.
examples.zh: 我們走了一英里到海邊。

milk.tip_zh: [ɪ] 短而放鬆，不要拉長成 [i]。難點在字尾 [lk]：舌尖先頂上牙齦發 l，接著舌根抬起發 k。學生常省掉 l 唸成 [mɪk]，或把 l 變成母音唸成「米歐克」。k 之後立刻停，不要再多加母音。
milk.tip_en: [ɪ] is short and relaxed, not stretched into [i]. The hard part is the final [lk]: tongue tip on the gum ridge for l, then raise the back of the tongue for k. Learners often drop the l ([mɪk]) or turn it into a vowel ('mi-o-ke'). Stop right after k with no extra vowel.

examples.en: I drink a glass of milk every morning.
examples.zh: 我每天早上喝一杯牛奶。

examples.en: Can you buy some milk on the way home?
examples.zh: 你回家路上可以買點牛奶嗎？

million.tip_zh: million 只有兩個音節 [mɪl·jən]：l 後面直接接 [j] 滑音，學生常唸成三拍「米利恩」，或把 [lj] 唸成清楚的 [li]。重音在 [mɪl]，[ɪ] 短而放鬆；第二音節 [jən] 很輕，母音是弱的 [ə]，字尾 [n] 舌尖頂住上牙齦收音，不要變成 [ŋ]。
million.tip_en: Million has only two syllables, [mɪl·jən]: the l runs straight into a [j] glide. Learners often make it three beats ('mi-li-en') or turn [lj] into a clear [li]. Stress [mɪl] with a short, relaxed [ɪ]; the second syllable [jən] is very light with a weak [ə], ending with the tongue tip on the gum ridge for [n], not [ŋ].

examples.en: A million stars filled the night sky.
examples.zh: 上百萬顆星星布滿了夜空。

examples.en: Thanks a million for your help!
examples.zh: 超級感謝你的幫忙！

mind.tip_zh: 字尾 [nd] 兩個子音都要發：舌尖頂上牙齦發 n，不放開就直接放出輕輕的 d。學生常只唸 [maɪn] 丟掉 d，聽起來就變成 mine。[aɪ] 嘴巴先張大再往 [ɪ] 收。同韻的 find、kind 結尾一樣，可以一起練。
mind.tip_en: Both consonants of the final [nd] count: tongue tip on the gum ridge for n, then without lifting it release a light d. Learners often say only [maɪn], which sounds like mine. Open wide for [aɪ], then close toward [ɪ]. Rhymes find and kind end the same way; practice them together.

examples.en: Do you mind if I sit here?
examples.zh: 你介意我坐這裡嗎？

examples.en: Never mind, I found my pencil.
examples.zh: 沒關係，我找到我的鉛筆了。

miss.tip_zh: [ɪ] 短而放鬆，下巴微開，不要拉長成 [i]。字尾 [s] 是無聲的嘶聲，喉嚨不振動；這是 Miss 和 Ms. [mɪz] 的差別，Ms. 結尾是有振動的 [z]。學生常在 s 後面加母音唸成「蜜斯」兩拍，s 要乾淨收尾。
miss.tip_en: [ɪ] is short and relaxed, jaw slightly open, not stretched into [i]. The final [s] is a voiceless hiss with no throat buzz; that is what separates Miss from Ms. [mɪz], which ends in a buzzing [z]. Learners often add a vowel after s ('mi-si', two beats); end cleanly on the s.

examples.en: I miss my grandma a lot.
examples.zh: 我很想念我奶奶。

examples.en: Miss Lin is our English teacher.
examples.zh: 林老師是我們的英文老師。

miss.spelling_zh: 大寫 Miss 是對女性的稱呼（小姐）。
miss.spelling_en: Capital Miss is a title for a woman.

mistake.tip_zh: 重音在第二音節 [stek]，學生常放到第一音節唸成 MIS-take。[s] 後面的 t 不送氣，聽起來接近輕的 [d]，不要用力唸成「斯特」。[e] 要往 [ɪ] 滑，字尾 k 輕輕收住。第一音節 [mɪ] 短而弱。
mistake.tip_en: Stress the second syllable [stek]; learners often stress the first ('MIS-take'). The t after [s] has no puff of air, so it sounds close to a light [d]; don't hit it hard. Let [e] glide toward [ɪ] and stop the final k lightly. The first syllable [mɪ] is short and weak.

examples.en: It's okay to make a mistake.
examples.zh: 犯錯沒有關係。

examples.en: I found a spelling mistake in my homework.
examples.zh: 我在作業裡發現一個拼字錯誤。

modern.tip_zh: modern 的 o 唸 [ɑ]，嘴巴張大、下巴往下，不是 [o]。第二音節 [dɚn] 是捲舌的 [ɚ] 再接 [n]，台灣學生常照外來語唸成「摩登」，把 dern 唸成「登」不捲舌，有時還把重音移到第二音節。正確是第一音節用力；第二音節舌頭先往後捲出 [ɚ]，再把舌尖頂到上齒齦收 [n]，整拍輕而短。
modern.tip_en: The o in modern is [ɑ], with the mouth open wide and the jaw down, not [o]. The second syllable [dɚn] is the r-colored [ɚ] followed by [n]. Taiwanese students often say it like the loanword 'mo-deng', saying dern as 'deng' without curling the tongue, and sometimes move the stress to the second syllable. Stress the first syllable; in the second, curl the tongue back for [ɚ], then touch the tongue tip to the ridge behind the upper teeth for [n], keeping the beat light and short.

examples.en: Our new library is big and modern.
examples.zh: 我們的新圖書館又大又現代化。

examples.en: Taipei is a modern city with many tall buildings.
examples.zh: 台北是一座有很多高樓的現代化城市。

moment.tip_zh: 重音在第一音節 [mo]，[o] 嘴唇收圓並滑向 [u]。第二音節 [mənt] 要很輕，母音弱化成 [ə]；學生常唸成清楚的 [mɛnt]，兩個音節一樣重。字尾 [nt] 舌尖頂上牙齦停住，t 輕輕收住，不要再加母音。
moment.tip_en: Stress the first syllable [mo]: round the lips and glide toward [u]. The second syllable [mənt] is very light, its vowel reduced to [ə]; learners often say a clear [mɛnt] and give both syllables equal weight. For the final [nt], hold the tongue tip on the gum ridge and stop the t lightly, no extra vowel.

examples.en: Please wait a moment.
examples.zh: 請稍等一下。

examples.en: Just a moment, I'm putting on my shoes.
examples.zh: 等我一下，我正在穿鞋。

monday.tip_zh: 第一音節是 [mʌn]，拼字是 o，卻唸短而放鬆的 [ʌ]，嘴巴只微開，和 money、month 的開頭一樣。學生常照拼字唸成 [mon] 或 [mɑn]。重音在前，第二音節 [dɪ] 輕而短，不要兩拍一樣重。
monday.tip_en: The first syllable is [mʌn]: spelled with o but said with a short, relaxed [ʌ], mouth only slightly open, just like the start of money and month. Learners often follow the spelling and say [mon] or [mɑn]. Stress the front; the second syllable [dɪ] is short and light, not equal in weight.

examples.en: We have P.E. on Monday.
examples.zh: 我們星期一有體育課。

examples.en: School starts again on Monday morning.
examples.zh: 星期一早上又要開始上學了。

monday.variant_en: The second syllable is also often said [de]: [ˈmʌnˌde].

money.tip_zh: 拼字 o 唸 [ʌ]，嘴巴微開、舌頭放在中間，學生常照拼字唸成 [mɑnɪ] 或 [monɪ]。money 也很容易和 many [ˈmɛnɪ] 混淆：money 的母音比較低沉，像 funny、honey 的開頭；many 是嘴角較開的 [ɛ]。重音在第一音節。
money.tip_en: The o is said [ʌ], mouth slightly open, tongue in the middle; learners often follow the spelling and say [mɑnɪ] or [monɪ]. Money is also easily confused with many [ˈmɛnɪ]: money has the deeper vowel, like the start of funny and honey, while many has a more spread [ɛ]. Stress the first syllable.

examples.en: I save my money in a piggy bank.
examples.zh: 我把錢存在小豬撲滿裡。

examples.en: Do you have money for lunch?
examples.zh: 你有帶午餐錢嗎？

monkey.tip_zh: monkey 的 o 唸 [ʌ]，和 cup、sun 的母音一樣，台灣學生常照拼字唸成 [ɑ] 或 [o]。中間的 n 要唸 [ŋ]：因為後面接 [k]，舌根先抬起頂住上顎後方發 [ŋ]，接著在同一個位置直接放開成 [k]，不要用舌尖頂前面唸成 [n]。重音在第一音節，字尾 [kɪ] 輕而短。
monkey.tip_en: The o in monkey is [ʌ], the same vowel as in cup and sun; Taiwanese students often read it from the spelling as [ɑ] or [o]. The n must be [ŋ]: because [k] follows, raise the back of the tongue against the back of the roof of the mouth for [ŋ], then release from the same spot into [k]; don't use the tongue tip at the front for [n]. Stress the first syllable; the final [kɪ] is light and short.

examples.en: The monkey is eating a banana in the tree.
examples.zh: 猴子在樹上吃香蕉。

examples.en: We saw a funny monkey at the zoo.
examples.zh: 我們在動物園看到一隻好笑的猴子。

month.tip_zh: 難點在字尾 [nθ]：[n] 結束時，舌尖直接往前移到上下齒之間吹氣發 [θ]。學生常唸成 [mʌns] 或 [mʌnt]，甚至把 n 也丟掉。拼字 o 唸 [ʌ]，和 money 開頭一樣。慢慢唸 [mʌn]，再把舌尖伸出齒縫輕輕吹氣。
month.tip_en: The hard part is the final [nθ]: as [n] ends, slide the tongue tip forward between the teeth and blow for [θ]. Learners often say [mʌns] or [mʌnt], or even drop the n. The o is [ʌ], like the start of money. Say [mʌn] slowly, then push the tongue tip out between the teeth and breathe out gently.

examples.en: My birthday is next month.
examples.zh: 我的生日在下個月。

examples.en: We read three books this month.
examples.zh: 我們這個月讀了三本書。

moon.tip_zh: moon 的 oo 是長音 [u]，嘴唇要嘟圓往前推並維持住，台灣學生常唸得太短、嘴唇太鬆。字尾 [n] 更容易出錯：學生常把結尾收成 [ŋ]，變成 [muŋ]，或尾音不見只剩「木」。發完 [u] 後，舌尖要往上頂住上排牙齒後方的齒齦，讓聲音從鼻子出來，結尾和 noon、soon 一樣。
moon.tip_en: The oo in moon is the long [u]: round the lips, push them forward and hold them. Taiwanese students often make it too short with lips too relaxed. The final [n] is even easier to get wrong: students often end with [ŋ], making [muŋ], or drop the ending so only 'mu' is left. After the [u], lift the tongue tip to the ridge behind the upper front teeth and let the sound come out through the nose; the ending is the same as in noon and soon.

examples.en: The moon is very bright tonight.
examples.zh: 今晚的月亮好亮。

examples.en: At Mid-Autumn Festival, we eat mooncakes and look at the moon.
examples.zh: 中秋節時，我們會吃月餅、賞月。

mop.tip_zh: [ɑ] 下巴往下、嘴巴張大，不圓唇；學生常唸成圓唇的 [ɔ] 或 [o]，聽起來像「摸普」。也要和 map [mæp] 分清楚：map 嘴角往兩旁拉，mop 是下巴往下掉。字尾 [p] 雙唇閉起就停，不要再加 [ə]。
mop.tip_en: For [ɑ], drop the jaw and open wide without rounding; learners often round it into [ɔ] or [o] ('mo-pu'). Keep it apart from map [mæp]: map pulls the lip corners back, mop drops the jaw. For the final [p], just close the lips and stop; don't add [ə].

examples.en: I help my dad mop the floor.
examples.zh: 我幫爸爸拖地。

examples.en: The mop is in the closet.
examples.zh: 拖把在櫃子裡。

more.tip_zh: [ɔr] 嘴唇先收圓、開口中等，接著舌尖往後捲。學生常把 r 省掉，唸成平平的「摸」，聽起來少了英文味。more 和 door、four 同韻；練習時先把 [ɔ] 拉長，再慢慢把舌頭往後捲，整個字還是一個音節。
more.tip_en: For [ɔr], first round the lips with a medium opening, then curl the tongue tip back. Learners often drop the r and say a flat 'mo', which loses the English sound. More rhymes with door and four; in practice, stretch [ɔ] first, then slowly curl the tongue back, keeping it all one syllable.

examples.en: Can I have more rice, please?
examples.zh: 我可以再多要一點飯嗎？

examples.en: Read more books and you will learn more words.
examples.zh: 多讀書，你就會學到更多單字。

morning.tip_zh: 第一音節 [mɔr] 要捲舌，學生常省掉 r 唸成 [mɔnɪŋ]。捲完舌後，舌尖直接往前頂到上牙齦接 [n]。字尾 [ɪŋ] 用舌根頂住軟顎，不要唸成 [ɪn]。重音在 [mɔr]，第二音節輕。
morning.tip_en: The first syllable [mɔr] needs the r curl; learners often drop it and say [mɔnɪŋ]. After the curl, move the tongue tip forward to the gum ridge for [n]. For the final [ɪŋ], press the back of the tongue to the soft palate; don't say [ɪn]. Stress [mɔr]; the second syllable is light.

examples.en: I eat eggs every morning.
examples.zh: 我每天早上吃蛋。

examples.en: We go jogging in the morning.
examples.zh: 我們早上去慢跑。

most.tip_zh: [o] 要從 [o] 滑向 [u]、嘴唇收圓；學生常唸成短的 [ɔ]，或和 must [mʌst] 混淆，must 不圓唇。字尾 [st] 兩個音都要發，常見錯誤是漏掉 t，或加母音唸成「摩斯特」。ghost、toast 結尾同樣是 [ost]。
most.tip_en: [o] glides from [o] toward [u] with rounded lips; learners often make it a short [ɔ] or confuse it with must [mʌst], which is unrounded. Both sounds of the final [st] count; common errors are dropping the t or adding a vowel ('mo-si-te'). Ghost and toast end the same way, [ost].

examples.en: Most of my friends like soccer.
examples.zh: 我大部分的朋友都喜歡足球。

examples.en: Which fruit do you like the most?
examples.zh: 你最喜歡哪一種水果？

mother.tip_zh: mother 中間是有聲的 [ð]，台灣學生常唸成 [d] 或 [z]，因為中文沒有這個音。發 [ð] 時舌尖輕放在上下門牙之間，喉嚨要震動，用手摸喉嚨應該感覺得到。第一個母音是 [ʌ]，嘴巴半開放鬆，不要照拼字唸成 [o] 或 [ɑ]。字尾 [ɚ] 舌頭往後捲、輕輕帶過，和 brother、other 的結尾一樣。
mother.tip_en: mother has the voiced [ð] in the middle; Taiwanese students often say [d] or [z] because Mandarin has no such sound. For [ð], rest the tongue tip lightly between the upper and lower front teeth and let the throat vibrate; you should feel it if you touch your throat. The first vowel is [ʌ], with a half-open, relaxed mouth; don't read it from the spelling as [o] or [ɑ]. For the final [ɚ], curl the tongue back and say it lightly, the same ending as in brother and other.

examples.en: My mother makes the best fried rice.
examples.zh: 我媽媽做的炒飯最好吃。

examples.en: I made a card for my mother on Mother's Day.
examples.zh: 母親節時，我做了一張卡片給媽媽。

motorcycle.tip_zh: motorcycle 有四個音節，主重音在第一音節 [mo]，[saɪ] 是次重音，中間的 [tɚ] 輕而捲舌。最常見的錯在字尾：台灣學生常把 cle 唸成「扣」，在 [k] 後面多加一個母音。字尾其實是成音節的 [ḷ]：[k] 一放開，舌尖就頂住上齒齦、舌根往後抬，發出暗 L，中間不插入任何母音。
motorcycle.tip_en: motorcycle has four syllables; the main stress is on the first syllable [mo], [saɪ] has secondary stress, and the middle [tɚ] is light with a tongue curl. The most common mistake is at the end: Taiwanese students often say cle like 'kou', adding a vowel after [k]. The ending is actually a syllabic [ḷ]: as soon as [k] is released, the tongue tip presses the ridge behind the upper teeth and the back of the tongue lifts for a dark L, with no vowel inserted.

examples.en: My dad rides a motorcycle to work every day.
examples.zh: 我爸爸每天騎機車上班。

examples.en: Please wear a helmet on the motorcycle.
examples.zh: 坐機車時請戴安全帽。

mountain.tip_zh: 第二音節沒有清楚的母音：美式英語的 [t] 在這裡常變成喉嚨輕輕一頓，接著是成音節的 [ṇ]，舌尖頂上牙齦，聲音直接從鼻子出來。學生常照拼字唸成「貓聽」或 [ˈmaʊntɛn]。重音在 [maʊn]，嘴形從 [a] 滑到 [ʊ]。
mountain.tip_en: The second syllable has no clear vowel: in American English the [t] here often becomes a light catch in the throat, followed by a syllabic [ṇ], tongue tip on the gum ridge, sound out through the nose. Learners often follow the spelling ('mao-ting') or say [ˈmaʊntɛn]. Stress [maʊn], gliding from [a] to [ʊ].

examples.en: We climbed a mountain last summer.
examples.zh: 我們去年夏天爬了一座山。

examples.en: There is snow on top of the mountain.
examples.zh: 山頂上有雪。

mouse.tip_zh: [aʊ] 嘴巴從大開的 [a] 滑到圓唇的 [ʊ]。字尾是無聲的 [s]，不是 [z]，學生常唸成 [maʊz]，或把 s 拉成「斯」多一拍。mouse 和 mouth [maʊθ] 只差最後一個音：mouse 舌尖在牙齒後面，mouth 舌尖伸到上下齒之間。
mouse.tip_en: [aʊ] glides from a wide-open [a] to rounded [ʊ]. The ending is a voiceless [s], not [z]; learners often say [maʊz] or stretch the s into an extra 'si' beat. Mouse and mouth [maʊθ] differ only in the last sound: for mouse the tongue tip stays behind the teeth, for mouth it comes out between them.

examples.en: The cat is chasing a mouse.
examples.zh: 貓在追一隻老鼠。

examples.en: Click the mouse to open the file.
examples.zh: 按一下滑鼠打開檔案。

mouth.tip_zh: mouth 結尾是無聲的 [θ]，台灣學生常唸成 [s]，結果變成 mouse（老鼠），意思完全不同。[aʊ] 要從張大嘴的 [a] 滑到圓唇的 [ʊ]，滑完之後舌尖馬上伸到上下門牙之間吹氣，聲帶不震動。可以先慢慢說 [maʊ]，再把舌頭伸出來送氣，對照練習 mouth 和 mouse 的差別。
mouth.tip_en: mouth ends in voiceless [θ]; Taiwanese students often say [s], turning it into mouse, which means something completely different. [aʊ] glides from an open-mouthed [a] to rounded [ʊ]; right after the glide, put the tongue tip between the upper and lower front teeth and blow air with no voice. Say [maʊ] slowly first, then stick the tongue out and push air, practicing mouth and mouse side by side.

examples.en: Open your mouth and say 'ah.'
examples.zh: 張開嘴巴，說「啊」。

examples.en: Don't talk with your mouth full.
examples.zh: 嘴巴裡有食物時不要說話。

move.tip_zh: 拼字 o 在這裡唸 [u]，不唸 [o]，學生常照拼字唸成 [mov]。字尾 [v] 上齒輕咬下唇，聲帶要振動；常見錯誤是唸成 [f]、[b] 或乾脆省掉，結果聽起來像牛叫的 moo。結尾的 e 不發音。
move.tip_en: Here the o is said [u], not [o]; learners often follow the spelling and say [mov]. For the final [v], rest the top teeth on the lower lip and keep the voice buzzing; common errors are [f], [b], or dropping it so it sounds like a cow's moo. The final e is silent.

examples.en: Please move your chair to the left.
examples.zh: 請把你的椅子往左邊移。

examples.en: We will move to a new house next year.
examples.zh: 我們明年要搬新家。

move.spelling_zh: o 唸 [u]，字尾 e 不發音。
move.spelling_en: The o is [u]; the final e is silent.

movie.tip_zh: 第一音節 [mu] 重讀，o 唸 [u]，嘴唇圓而且拉長。中間的 [v] 上齒輕碰下唇並振動聲帶，學生常唸成 [b] 變成「木比」，或嘴唇沒碰到變成 [w]。第二音節 [vɪ] 輕而短，ie 唸短 [ɪ]。
movie.tip_en: Stress the first syllable [mu]: the o is [u], lips round and long. For the middle [v], touch the top teeth to the lower lip and buzz; learners often say [b] ('mu-bi') or let it slip to [w]. The second syllable [vɪ] is short and light; the ie is a short [ɪ].

examples.en: Let's watch a movie on Saturday night.
examples.zh: 我們星期六晚上看電影吧。

examples.en: This movie is about a funny dog.
examples.zh: 這部電影是在講一隻好笑的狗。

much.tip_zh: [ʌ] 短促，嘴巴只微開，不要唸成張大的 [æ]，否則像 match。字尾 [tʃ] 嘴唇微微噘起，舌尖頂上牙齦後一放開就停；常見錯誤是後面多加母音唸成「罵去」，或只發 [ʃ]。much 和 touch 同韻。
much.tip_en: [ʌ] is short with the mouth only slightly open; don't open it to [æ], or it sounds like match. For the final [tʃ], push the lips out slightly, press the tongue tip to the gum ridge and release, then stop. Common errors are adding a vowel ('ma-chi') or saying only [ʃ]. Much rhymes with touch.

examples.en: Thank you very much!
examples.zh: 非常謝謝你！

examples.en: How much is this notebook?
examples.zh: 這本筆記本多少錢？

mud.tip_zh: [ʌ] 是短而放鬆的中央母音，嘴巴只微開；學生常唸成張大的 [æ]，結果變成 mad，或拉長成 [mɑd]。字尾 [d] 要有聲帶振動，舌尖頂上牙齦後輕輕放開，不要唸成 [t]，也不要加母音唸成「罵的」。
mud.tip_en: [ʌ] is a short, relaxed central vowel with the mouth only slightly open; learners often open it to [æ], turning it into mad, or stretch it to [mɑd]. The final [d] is voiced: tongue tip on the gum ridge, released gently; not a [t], and no added vowel ('ma-de').

examples.en: My shoes are covered in mud.
examples.zh: 我的鞋子沾滿了泥巴。

examples.en: The kids played in the mud after the rain.
examples.zh: 雨後孩子們在泥巴裡玩。

museum.tip_zh: museum 重音在第二音節 [zi]，台灣學生常把重音放在第一音節 mu，整個字的節奏就跑掉了。正確是輕－重－輕：[mju] 輕短，[zi] 拉長用力，最後 [əm] 輕輕帶過。中間的 s 唸有聲的 [z]，不是 [s]，喉嚨要震動，像 zoo 的開頭。字尾 [m] 要把雙唇閉起來，不要收成 [n]。
museum.tip_en: museum is stressed on the second syllable [zi]; Taiwanese students often stress the first syllable mu, which throws off the rhythm of the whole word. The correct pattern is weak–strong–weak: [mju] short and light, [zi] long and strong, then [əm] said lightly. The s is the voiced [z], not [s]; the throat vibrates, like the start of zoo. For the final [m], close the lips; don't end with [n].

examples.en: Our class visited the science museum last week.
examples.zh: 我們班上週去參觀了科學博物館。

examples.en: The museum has a big dinosaur model.
examples.zh: 博物館裡有一個很大的恐龍模型。

music.tip_zh: music 的 s 唸有聲的 [z]，台灣學生常照拼字唸成 [s]，聽起來像「謬昔克」。發 [z] 時舌尖靠近上齒齦，像蜜蜂嗡嗡叫，喉嚨要震動。開頭是 [mju]，m 後面有 [j] 滑音，嘴唇從閉合直接滑到圓唇的 [u]，不要只唸成 [mu]。重音在第一音節，字尾 [k] 輕輕收住，不要多加母音。
music.tip_en: The s in music is the voiced [z]; Taiwanese students often read it as [s] from the spelling, sounding like 'miu-si-ke'. For [z], hold the tongue tip near the ridge behind the upper teeth and buzz like a bee, with the throat vibrating. It begins with [mju]: there is a [j] glide after m, so the lips go from closed straight into rounded [u]; don't say just [mu]. Stress the first syllable, and close the final [k] lightly without adding a vowel.

examples.en: We have music class on Tuesday.
examples.zh: 我們星期二有音樂課。

examples.en: My sister listens to music while she does homework.
examples.zh: 我妹妹一邊寫功課一邊聽音樂。

must.tip_zh: [ʌ] 短促、嘴唇不圓，和 most [most] 不同：most 要收圓嘴唇並滑向 [u]。字尾 [st] 兩個音都要有，學生常漏掉 t 或唸成「罵斯特」三拍。在 must be 這類快速口語中 t 常會變弱，但單獨說時要清楚。
must.tip_en: [ʌ] is short with unrounded lips, unlike most [most], which rounds and glides toward [u]. Both sounds of the final [st] count; learners often drop the t or make it three beats ('ma-si-te'). In quick phrases like must be the t often weakens, but said alone it should be clear.

examples.en: You must wear a helmet when you ride a bike.
examples.zh: 騎腳踏車時一定要戴安全帽。

examples.en: We must finish our homework first.
examples.zh: 我們必須先寫完功課。

nail.tip_zh: [e] 要往 [ɪ] 滑，接著是字尾暗 L：舌尖往上頂上牙齦，舌根往後抬。學生常把 l 丟掉，nail 聽起來只剩 [ne]，或多加母音唸成「內歐」。開頭的 [n] 也要舌尖頂住並從鼻子出聲，不要唸成 [l]。
nail.tip_en: [e] glides toward [ɪ], then the dark L: tongue tip up to the gum ridge, back of the tongue raised. Learners often drop the l so nail sounds like just [ne], or add a vowel ('nei-o'). The opening [n] also needs the tongue tip pressed up with sound through the nose, not an [l].

examples.en: Dad used a hammer and a nail to hang the picture.
examples.zh: 爸爸用鐵鎚和釘子把畫掛起來。

examples.en: Be careful, there is a nail on the floor.
examples.zh: 小心，地上有一根釘子。

name.tip_zh: [e] 要從 [e] 滑向 [ɪ]，學生常唸成短而平的 [nɛm]。字尾 [m] 雙唇要閉起來並保持鼻音，不能張開加母音唸成「內姆」，也不能鬆成 [n]。說 my name is 時，m 閉唇的動作要做完再接下一個字。
name.tip_en: [e] glides from [e] toward [ɪ]; learners often say a short, flat [nɛm]. For the final [m], close the lips and hold the hum; don't open them and add a vowel ('nei-mu'), and don't let it slip to [n]. In 'my name is', finish closing the lips for m before moving to the next word.

examples.en: Please write your name on the paper.
examples.zh: 請把你的名字寫在紙上。

examples.en: My dog's name is Lucky.
examples.zh: 我的狗叫 Lucky。

national.tip_zh: national 的 na 唸 [næ]，是嘴巴張大的 [æ]。台灣學生因為先學過 nation [ˈneʃən]，常把開頭也唸成 [ne]，這是最常見的錯：nation 變成 national 時，母音會改變。中間的 [ʃə] 輕輕帶過；字尾 [nəl] 的 l 是暗 L，舌尖頂住上齒齦、舌根抬起，不要唸成「喔」或省略。
national.tip_en: The na in national is [næ], with the wide-open [æ]. Because Taiwanese students learned nation [ˈneʃən] first, they often start this word with [ne] too; this is the most common mistake: the vowel changes when nation becomes national. The middle [ʃə] is said lightly; the l at the end of [nəl] is a dark L, with the tongue tip on the ridge behind the upper teeth and the back of the tongue raised; don't turn it into 'o' or drop it.

examples.en: We visited a national park during summer vacation.
examples.zh: 暑假時我們去了一座國家公園。

examples.en: Everyone stood up for the national anthem.
examples.zh: 奏國歌時，大家都站了起來。

national.variant_zh: 口語常縮成兩個音節 [ˈnæʃnəl]，兩種都對。
national.variant_en: In casual speech it is often two syllables, [ˈnæʃnəl]; both are correct.

nature.tip_zh: 拼字 -ture 唸 [tʃɚ]：舌尖頂上牙齦後放開成 [tʃ]，嘴唇微微噘起，接著直接捲舌發 [ɚ]。學生常照拼字唸成 [tjur]，或唸成沒有捲舌的平音。第一音節 [ne] 重讀，a 唸 [e] 並往 [ɪ] 滑，不唸 [æ]。picture、future 的結尾也是同樣的 [tʃɚ]。
nature.tip_en: The spelling -ture is said [tʃɚ]: tongue tip on the gum ridge, released into [tʃ] with the lips pushed out slightly, then straight into an r-colored [ɚ]. Learners often follow the spelling and say [tjur], or a flat ending with no r. Stress the first syllable [ne]; the a is [e] gliding toward [ɪ], not [æ]. Picture and future end in the same [tʃɚ].

examples.en: We learn about nature in science class.
examples.zh: 我們在自然課學習大自然。

examples.en: I love walking in nature with my family.
examples.zh: 我喜歡和家人在大自然裡散步。

near.tip_zh: near 只有一個音節 [nɪr]：[ɪ] 放鬆短促，接著舌尖往後捲成 r。學生常先唸長 [i] 再加 [ɚ]，拆成兩拍，或乾脆省掉 r。dear、year、clear 都同韻，可以一起練，注意捲舌要在 [ɪ] 之後馬上出現。
near.tip_en: Near is one syllable, [nɪr]: a short, relaxed [ɪ], then curl the tongue tip back for r. Learners often say a long [i] plus [ɚ], splitting it into two beats, or drop the r entirely. Dear, year and clear rhyme with it; practice them together and bring the curl in right after [ɪ].

examples.en: The library is near my school.
examples.zh: 圖書館在我學校附近。

examples.en: Please sit near the window.
examples.zh: 請坐在靠窗的地方。

neck.tip_zh: [ɛ] 嘴巴半開，不要張大成 [æ]，也不要唸成往 [ɪ] 滑的 [e]。字尾 [k] 舌根頂住軟顎後收住，學生常加母音唸成「內克」或把 k 吞掉。也要和 knock [nɑk] 分清楚：knock 下巴往下張大，neck 只半開。
neck.tip_en: For [ɛ], open the mouth halfway: not wide like [æ], and not the gliding [e]. For the final [k], press the back of the tongue to the soft palate and stop; learners often add a vowel ('nei-ke') or swallow the k. Keep it apart from knock [nɑk]: knock drops the jaw wide, neck only opens halfway.

examples.en: The giraffe has a very long neck.
examples.zh: 長頸鹿的脖子非常長。

examples.en: Wear a scarf around your neck.
examples.zh: 把圍巾圍在脖子上。

need.tip_zh: [i] 要拉長、嘴角往兩旁。字尾 [d] 聲帶要振動，學生常唸成無聲的 [t]，或把 d 整個省掉。英文母音在有聲子音前會唸得比較長，所以 need 的 [i] 要比 neat [nit] 拖得更長一點，最後舌尖輕放出 d。
need.tip_en: Hold [i] long with spread lips. The final [d] is voiced; learners often make it a voiceless [t] or drop it. English vowels are longer before voiced consonants, so the [i] of need is a bit longer than in neat [nit]; finish by releasing the tongue tip gently for d.

examples.en: I need a new eraser.
examples.zh: 我需要一個新的橡皮擦。

examples.en: Do you need help with your homework?
examples.zh: 你的功課需要幫忙嗎？

neighbor.tip_zh: neighbor 的 eigh 只唸一個 [e]，和 eight 的開頭一樣，gh 完全不發音。台灣學生看到這麼多字母，常想把 g 唸出來，或把 ei 拆成兩個音。正確是 [ne] 接 [bɚ]：重音在第一音節，發 [e] 時嘴角往兩邊拉。第二音節雙唇先閉合發 [b]，接著舌頭往後捲出 [ɚ]，不要唸成「伯」就停住不捲舌。
neighbor.tip_en: The eigh in neighbor is just one sound, [e], the same as the start of eight; the gh is completely silent. Seeing so many letters, Taiwanese students often try to pronounce the g, or split ei into two sounds. Say [ne] then [bɚ]: stress the first syllable and pull the corners of the mouth wide for [e]. For the second syllable, close the lips for [b], then curl the tongue back for [ɚ]; don't stop at 'bo' without the curl.

examples.en: Our neighbor has a big orange cat.
examples.zh: 我們的鄰居有一隻大橘貓。

examples.en: We gave our neighbor some homemade cookies.
examples.zh: 我們送了一些自己做的餅乾給鄰居。

neighbor.spelling_en: eigh is just [e]; the gh is silent.

never.tip_zh: never 中間的 [v] 是上排門牙輕咬下唇再震動，台灣學生常唸成 [w] 或 [b]，聽起來像「內握」或「內伯」。發 [v] 時牙齒要真的碰到下唇，喉嚨同時震動，下唇會有麻麻的感覺。第一音節 [nɛ] 重而短，嘴巴微開。字尾 [ɚ] 輕輕捲舌，和 ever 的結尾一樣。
never.tip_en: The [v] in the middle of never is made by lightly biting the lower lip with the upper front teeth while voicing; Taiwanese students often say [w] or [b], sounding like 'nei-wo' or 'nei-bo'. For [v], the teeth must actually touch the lower lip while the throat vibrates; the lower lip will feel a slight buzz. The first syllable [nɛ] is stressed and short, with the mouth slightly open. The final [ɚ] is a light tongue curl, the same ending as in ever.

examples.en: My grandma never forgets my birthday.
examples.zh: 奶奶從來不會忘記我的生日。

examples.en: Never cross the street when the light is red.
examples.zh: 紅燈時絕對不要過馬路。

new.tip_zh: 美式英語一般唸 [nu]，開頭 [n] 舌尖頂上牙齦，接著嘴唇收圓往前噘，把 [u] 拉長。學生常把 [u] 唸得太短太鬆，或嘴唇沒有圓，聽起來像 no [no]。開頭也不要發成 [l]。new 和 knew 同音。
new.tip_en: American English usually says [nu]: tongue tip on the gum ridge for [n], then round and push the lips forward and hold [u] long. Learners often make the [u] too short and loose, or don't round the lips, so it drifts toward no [no]. Don't start with an [l] either. New sounds the same as knew.

examples.en: I got a new backpack for school.
examples.zh: 我有一個新的上學用書包。

examples.en: We have a new student in our class.
examples.zh: 我們班上有一位新同學。

new.variant_zh: 也有人唸 [nju]，英式英語較常見。
new.variant_en: Some say [nju]; it is more common in British English.
new.spelling_zh: 和 knew 同音，knew 的 k 不發音。
new.spelling_en: Sounds like knew, whose k is silent.

news.tip_zh: 字尾是有聲的 [z]，不是 [s]；學生常照拼字唸成 [nus]。發 [z] 時喉嚨要振動，像蜜蜂的嗡嗡聲。美式開頭是 [nu]，嘴唇收圓。也要和 nose [noz]、noise [nɔɪz] 分清楚：三個字結尾都是 [z]，差在中間母音。
news.tip_en: The ending is a voiced [z], not [s]; learners often follow the spelling and say [nus]. For [z], keep the throat buzzing like a bee. In American English it starts [nu] with rounded lips. Keep it apart from nose [noz] and noise [nɔɪz]: all three end in [z] and differ only in the vowel.

examples.en: Do you have any good news?
examples.zh: 你有什麼好消息嗎？

examples.en: My grandpa watches the news every night.
examples.zh: 我爺爺每天晚上看新聞。

news.variant_en: Some say [njuz], more common in British English.
news.spelling_en: The final s is a voiced [z].

newspaper.tip_zh: newspaper 是 news 加 paper 組成的，重音在第一音節 [nuz]，paper 的部分變輕。台灣學生常把兩個字分開唸，在 news 後面多加一個母音，唸成「紐斯－配波」四拍。正確是 [nuz] 結尾的子音直接連到 [pe]，中間不停頓、不加母音。[pe] 的 [e] 嘴角往兩邊拉，最後 [pɚ] 輕輕捲舌。美式開頭是 [nu]，不加 [j]。
newspaper.tip_en: newspaper is news plus paper; the stress is on the first syllable [nuz], and the paper part becomes lighter. Taiwanese students often say the two words separately and add a vowel after news, making four beats like 'niu-si-pei-po'. Instead, link the final consonant of [nuz] straight into [pe], with no pause and no added vowel. The [e] in [pe] pulls the corners of the mouth wide, and the final [pɚ] has a light tongue curl. American English starts with [nu], without a [j].

examples.en: Grandpa reads the newspaper every morning.
examples.zh: 爺爺每天早上看報紙。

examples.en: We covered the table with an old newspaper.
examples.zh: 我們用舊報紙把桌子蓋起來。

next.tip_zh: 字尾 [kst] 有三個子音連在一起，學生常只唸成 [nɛks]，或在中間加母音變成「內克斯特」。舌根先頂軟顎發 [k]，馬上滑進 [s]，最後舌尖輕頂上牙齦收 [t]。快速說 next week 時 t 常被省略，但單獨說要清楚。
next.tip_en: The ending [kst] is three consonants in a row; learners often say only [nɛks] or put vowels between them ('nei-ke-si-te'). Back of the tongue to the soft palate for [k], slide straight into [s], then a light tongue-tip [t]. In quick phrases like next week the t is often dropped, but said alone it should be clear.

examples.en: Who is next in line?
examples.zh: 下一個排隊的是誰？

examples.en: We will have a test next Monday.
examples.zh: 我們下星期一要考試。

nice.tip_zh: [aɪ] 嘴巴先張大，再往 [ɪ] 收。字尾 -ce 唸無聲的 [s]，舌尖放在下齒後方送氣，學生常在 s 後面加母音唸成「耐斯」兩拍。也要和 night [naɪt]、knife [naɪf] 分清楚，這三個字只差最後一個子音。
nice.tip_en: For [aɪ], open the mouth wide and then close toward [ɪ]. The -ce at the end is a voiceless [s], a hiss with the tongue tip behind the lower teeth; learners often add a vowel after it ('nai-si', two beats). Keep it apart from night [naɪt] and knife [naɪf]; only the last consonant differs.

examples.en: It's nice to see you again.
examples.zh: 很高興再見到你。

examples.en: Our new teacher is very nice.
examples.zh: 我們的新老師人很好。

nice.spelling_zh: c 在 e 前唸 [s]，字尾 e 不發音。
nice.spelling_en: c before e is [s]; the final e is silent.

night.tip_zh: gh 不發音，整個字只有 [n]、[aɪ]、[t] 三個音。學生常把字尾 [t] 吞掉，只剩 [naɪ]，或加母音唸成「耐特」。t 舌尖頂住上牙齦停住即可。[aɪ] 要有從大開口到小開口的滑動。night 和 knight 同音。
night.tip_en: The gh is silent; the word is just three sounds, [n], [aɪ], [t]. Learners often swallow the final [t], leaving [naɪ], or add a vowel ('nai-te'). Just stop with the tongue tip on the gum ridge for t. [aɪ] needs a glide from wide open to nearly closed. Night sounds the same as knight.

examples.en: I read a story every night before bed.
examples.zh: 我每天晚上睡前讀一個故事。

examples.en: We saw many stars last night.
examples.zh: 我們昨晚看到很多星星。

night.spelling_zh: gh 不發音；和 knight 同音。
night.spelling_en: The gh is silent; sounds the same as knight.

nine.tip_zh: 字尾 [n] 舌尖要頂住上牙齦收音，學生常改成舌根的 [ŋ]，聽起來拖著一個 ng 的尾巴，或乾脆省掉。開頭的 [n] 一樣是舌尖頂上牙齦，不要唸成 [l]。nine 頭尾都是 [n]，中間 [aɪ] 從大開口滑到 [ɪ]。和 fine、line 同韻。
nine.tip_en: End with the tongue tip pressed on the gum ridge for [n]; learners often switch to the back-of-tongue [ŋ], leaving an 'ng' tail, or drop it. The opening [n] is also tongue tip on the gum ridge, not [l]. Nine starts and ends with [n], with [aɪ] gliding from wide open to [ɪ] in between. It rhymes with fine and line.

examples.en: My little brother is nine years old.
examples.zh: 我弟弟九歲。

examples.en: Class starts at nine o'clock.
examples.zh: 九點開始上課。

nineteen.tip_zh: 單獨說時主重音在第二音節 [tin]，學生常放在第一音節，聽起來就像 ninety。-teen 的 [i] 要拉長，t 清楚送氣，字尾 [n] 要收住；ninety 則是前重，結尾是短的 [ɪ]。第一音節 [naɪn] 的 n 也要做完再接 t。
nineteen.tip_en: Said alone, the main stress is on the second syllable [tin]; learners often stress the first, so it sounds like ninety. Hold the [i] of -teen long, give the t a clear puff of air, and close on [n]; ninety is stressed at the front and ends in a short [ɪ]. Finish the n of [naɪn] before the t.

examples.en: My cousin is nineteen years old.
examples.zh: 我表哥十九歲。

examples.en: There are nineteen students in my class.
examples.zh: 我們班有十九個學生。

ninety.tip_zh: 重音在第一音節 [naɪn]，第二音節 [tɪ] 短而輕，不要拉成 -teen 的長 [i]，否則會和 nineteen 混淆。拼字中間的 e 不發音，nine 直接接 ty，不要唸成三個音節。[n] 和 [t] 要緊接著，舌尖都在上牙齦。
ninety.tip_en: Stress the first syllable [naɪn]; the second syllable [tɪ] is short and light. Don't stretch it into the long [i] of -teen, or it will be confused with nineteen. The middle e is silent: nine runs straight into ty, not three syllables. [n] and [t] sit right together, both with the tongue tip on the gum ridge.

examples.en: My great-grandma is ninety years old.
examples.zh: 我曾祖母九十歲了。

examples.en: I got ninety on my math test.
examples.zh: 我數學考試考了九十分。

ninety.spelling_zh: 中間的 e 不發音。

no.tip_zh: KK 的 [o] 要從 [o] 滑向 [u]，嘴唇越收越圓；學生常唸成短而平的「挪」，沒有滑動。開頭 [n] 舌尖頂上牙齦、聲音從鼻子出來，別發成 [l]，否則 no 會聽起來像 low。no 和 know 同音。
no.tip_en: KK [o] glides from [o] toward [u], the lips rounding more and more; learners often say a short, flat 'nuo' with no glide. For the opening [n], press the tongue tip to the gum ridge and send the sound through the nose; don't say [l], or no will sound like low. No sounds the same as know.

examples.en: No, thank you. I'm full.
examples.zh: 不用了，謝謝，我吃飽了。

examples.en: There is no milk in the fridge.
examples.zh: 冰箱裡沒有牛奶了。

nobody.tip_zh: nobody 是 no 加 body，重音在第一音節 [no]，台灣學生常把重音移到 bo 上，唸成 no-BO-dy，聽起來像兩個分開的字。正確是第一拍最重：[no] 要唸足，嘴唇圓起來並略帶滑音；接著 [bɑ] 嘴巴張開但放輕，最後 [dɪ] 短短帶過。可以想成 NO-body：先大聲說 no，再小聲接 body。
nobody.tip_en: nobody is no plus body, stressed on the first syllable [no]; Taiwanese students often move the stress onto bo, saying no-BO-dy, which sounds like two separate words. The first beat should be strongest: give [no] its full length, with rounded lips and a slight glide; then [bɑ] with an open but lighter mouth, and finally [dɪ] said briefly. Think of it as NO-body: say no loudly, then body softly.

examples.en: Nobody was late for class today.
examples.zh: 今天沒有人上課遲到。

examples.en: Nobody knows where the cat went.
examples.zh: 沒有人知道貓跑去哪裡了。

nobody.variant_zh: 口語常把中間弱化，唸成 [ˈnobədɪ]。
nobody.variant_en: In casual speech the middle is often reduced: [ˈnobədɪ].
nobody.kk_flag: Given KK [ˈnoˌbɑˌdi] puts a secondary-stress mark on the last syllable; in General American the final -dy is unstressed, so [ˈnoˌbɑdɪ] (or reduced [ˈnobədɪ]) is expected. Also, the batch's rhyme list (agree, be, bee, free, he, key) matches only the last syllable and does not really rhyme with nobody.

noise.tip_zh: 字尾 -se 唸有聲的 [z]，學生常照拼字唸成 [s]；[z] 要讓喉嚨振動。[ɔɪ] 嘴唇先圓再滑向 [ɪ]，和 boy 的母音一樣。也要和 nose [noz]、news [nuz] 分清楚，三個字都以 [z] 結尾，只差中間母音。
noise.tip_en: The -se at the end is a voiced [z]; learners often follow the spelling and say [s]. Keep the throat buzzing for [z]. [ɔɪ] starts rounded and glides to [ɪ], the same vowel as in boy. Keep it apart from nose [noz] and news [nuz]; all three end in [z] and differ only in the vowel.

examples.en: What is that loud noise?
examples.zh: 那個很大的聲音是什麼？

examples.en: Please don't make noise in the library.
examples.zh: 在圖書館裡請不要發出噪音。

noisy.tip_zh: 中間的 s 唸有聲的 [z]，學生常唸成無聲 [s]，變成「諾伊西」。重音在第一音節 [nɔɪ]，嘴唇先圓再滑向 [ɪ]，[ɔɪ] 要一口氣滑完，不要拆成兩拍。字尾 y 唸短而輕的 [ɪ]。
noisy.tip_en: The middle s is a voiced [z]; learners often make it a voiceless [s] ('nuo-yi-xi'). Stress the first syllable [nɔɪ]: start rounded and glide to [ɪ] in one movement, not two beats. The final y is a short, light [ɪ].

examples.en: The classroom is very noisy today.
examples.zh: 今天教室很吵。

examples.en: The birds are so noisy in the morning.
examples.zh: 早上鳥兒好吵。

noodle.tip_zh: 第一音節 [nu] 嘴唇圓、[u] 要拉長。第二音節是成音節的 [ḷ]：發完 [d] 舌尖留在上牙齦，直接放下舌頭兩側發 l，中間沒有母音。學生常唸成「努豆」，或在後面加「歐」。重音在前。
noodle.tip_en: In the first syllable [nu], round the lips and hold [u] long. The second syllable is a syllabic [ḷ]: after [d], leave the tongue tip on the gum ridge and drop the sides for l, with no vowel in between. Learners often say 'nu-dou' or add an 'o' at the end. Stress is on the front.

examples.en: Grandma makes noodle soup on cold days.
examples.zh: 天冷的時候奶奶會煮湯麵。

examples.en: I like beef noodle soup.
examples.zh: 我喜歡牛肉麵。

noon.tip_zh: noon 頭尾都是 [n]，兩個 n 都要用舌尖頂住上牙齦；學生常把字尾唸成舌根的 [ŋ]，或開頭發成 [l]。中間的 [u] 嘴唇圓而且拉長，不要唸成短的 [ʊ]。和 moon、June 同韻，可以一起練。
noon.tip_en: Noon begins and ends with [n], and both need the tongue tip pressed on the gum ridge; learners often turn the final one into the back-of-tongue [ŋ], or start with [l]. The middle [u] is rounded and long, not a short [ʊ]. It rhymes with moon and June; practice them together.

examples.en: We eat lunch at noon.
examples.zh: 我們中午吃午餐。

examples.en: The store opens at noon on Sundays.
examples.zh: 這家店星期天中午開門。

north.tip_zh: [ɔr] 嘴唇圓、接著捲舌，然後舌尖從捲起的位置直接往前伸到上下齒之間吹氣發 [θ]。學生常唸成 [nɔrs] 或 [nɔrt]，或把 r 省掉。字尾 th 是無聲的，只有氣、沒有聲帶振動。
north.tip_en: For [ɔr], round the lips and curl the tongue; then move the tongue tip straight from the curl to between the teeth and blow for [θ]. Learners often say [nɔrs] or [nɔrt], or drop the r. The final th is voiceless: just air, no buzzing.

examples.en: Taipei is in the north of Taiwan.
examples.zh: 台北在台灣的北部。

examples.en: The wind is coming from the north.
examples.zh: 風是從北方吹來的。

nose.tip_zh: [o] 嘴唇收圓並滑向 [u]，字尾 -se 唸有聲的 [z]，喉嚨要振動；學生常照拼字唸成 [nos]，或在後面加母音唸成「諾斯」兩拍。結尾 e 不發音。nose 和 knows 同音，也要和 noise [nɔɪz]、news [nuz] 分清楚，差在中間母音。
nose.tip_en: Round the lips for [o] and glide toward [u]; the -se at the end is a voiced [z], so keep the throat buzzing. Learners often follow the spelling and say [nos], or add a vowel ('nuo-si', two beats). The final e is silent. Nose sounds the same as knows; keep it apart from noise [nɔɪz] and news [nuz], which differ in the vowel.

examples.en: I have a runny nose today.
examples.zh: 我今天流鼻水。

examples.en: The clown has a big red nose.
examples.zh: 小丑有一個大大的紅鼻子。

nose.spelling_zh: -se 唸有聲 [z]；和 knows 同音。
nose.spelling_en: The -se is a voiced [z]; sounds like knows.

not.tip_zh: [ɑ] 下巴往下、嘴巴張大，不圓唇；學生常唸成圓唇的「諾」，聽起來接近 note [not]。字尾 [t] 舌尖頂住上牙齦停住，不加母音。美式口語中 not 後面接母音時，t 會變成輕快的彈舌音，例如 not at all。
not.tip_en: For [ɑ], drop the jaw and open wide without rounding; learners often round it ('nuo'), which sounds close to note [not]. Stop the final [t] with the tongue tip on the gum ridge, no added vowel. In American speech, when a vowel follows, the t becomes a quick flap, as in not at all.

examples.en: I am not hungry right now.
examples.zh: 我現在不餓。

examples.en: This is not my pencil.
examples.zh: 這不是我的鉛筆。

note.tip_zh: [o] 要滑向 [u]、嘴唇收圓，和 not [nɑt] 的大開口不同；學生常把兩個字唸成一樣。結尾的 e 不發音，只是讓 o 唸成 [o]。字尾 [t] 輕輕收住，不要唸成「諾特」多一拍。
note.tip_en: [o] glides toward [u] with rounded lips, unlike the wide-open [ɑ] of not [nɑt]; learners often say the two words the same. The final e is silent; it only makes the o say [o]. Stop the final [t] lightly, not 'nuo-te' with an extra beat.

examples.en: I wrote a note to my mom.
examples.zh: 我寫了一張紙條給媽媽。

examples.en: Please read this note before class.
examples.zh: 上課前請先看這張便條。

note.spelling_zh: 字尾 e 不發音，讓 o 唸 [o]。
note.spelling_en: The final e is silent and makes the o say [o].

notebook.tip_zh: 重音在第一音節 [not]。[t] 碰到後面的 [b] 時通常不放開，只是舌尖頂住停一下，就直接閉唇發 [b]；學生常把 t 唸得很重或加母音，變成「諾特布克」四拍。第二音節 [bʊk] 母音短，和 book 一樣。
notebook.tip_en: Stress the first syllable [not]. Before [b], the [t] is usually not released: the tongue tip just holds for a moment, then the lips close for [b]. Learners often hit the t hard or add vowels ('nuo-te-bu-ke', four beats). The second syllable [bʊk] has a short vowel, just like book.

examples.en: Write the new words in your notebook.
examples.zh: 把新單字寫在你的筆記本上。

examples.en: My dad uses his notebook for work.
examples.zh: 我爸爸用他的筆電工作。

notebook.spelling_zh: 中間 note 的 e 不發音。
notebook.spelling_en: The e of note in the middle is silent.

nothing.tip_zh: nothing 的 o 唸 [ʌ]，和 nut、bus 的母音一樣，台灣學生常照拼字唸成 [o]，變成「挪性」。中間的 th 是無聲的 [θ]，常被唸成 [s] 或 [f]：舌尖伸到上下門牙之間吹氣，接著舌頭快速收回發 [ɪ]。字尾 -ing 是 [ɪŋ]，舌根抬起頂住上顎後方，舌尖不要碰上齒齦收成 [n]。
nothing.tip_en: The o in nothing is [ʌ], the same vowel as in nut and bus; Taiwanese students often read it as [o] from the spelling, making it sound like 'nuo-sing'. The th in the middle is voiceless [θ] and is often said as [s] or [f]: put the tongue tip between the upper and lower front teeth and blow, then quickly pull the tongue back for [ɪ]. The -ing ending is [ɪŋ]: raise the back of the tongue against the back of the roof of the mouth, and don't let the tongue tip touch the ridge behind the teeth to make [n].

examples.en: There is nothing in the box.
examples.zh: 盒子裡什麼都沒有。

examples.en: I have nothing to do this afternoon.
examples.zh: 我今天下午沒事做。

notice.tip_zh: 重音在第一音節 [no]，嘴唇收圓並滑向 [u]。-tice 不唸 ice 的 [aɪs]，而是很輕的 [təs]；學生常唸成「諾太斯」。美式英語裡中間的 t 夾在母音之間，常變成輕快的彈舌音，聽起來接近輕的 d。
notice.tip_en: Stress the first syllable [no], lips rounding toward [u]. The -tice is not the [aɪs] of ice but a light [təs]; learners often say 'nuo-tai-si'. In American English the middle t, between vowels, often becomes a quick flap that sounds close to a light d.

examples.en: Did you notice my new haircut?
examples.zh: 你有注意到我的新髮型嗎？

examples.en: I didn't notice the rain.
examples.zh: 我沒注意到下雨了。

november.tip_zh: November 重音在第二音節 [vɛm]，台灣學生常把重音放在開頭的 no，唸成 NO-vember。正確是輕－重－輕：[no] 輕輕帶過，[vɛm] 用力。[v] 要上齒輕咬下唇並震動，不要唸成 [w] 或 [b]。[vɛm] 結尾雙唇閉合發 [m]，直接接 [b]，嘴唇不用打開；最後 [bɚ] 捲舌，和 December、remember 的結尾一樣。
november.tip_en: November is stressed on the second syllable [vɛm]; Taiwanese students often stress the opening no, saying NO-vember. The pattern is weak–strong–weak: [no] said lightly, [vɛm] strong. For [v], lightly bite the lower lip with the upper teeth and voice it; don't say [w] or [b]. At the end of [vɛm], close the lips for [m] and go straight into [b] without opening them; the final [bɚ] has a tongue curl, the same ending as December and remember.

examples.en: My birthday is in November.
examples.zh: 我的生日在十一月。

examples.en: The weather gets cooler in November.
examples.zh: 十一月天氣會變涼。

now.tip_zh: [aʊ] 要從大開口的 [a] 滑到圓唇的 [ʊ]，下巴先往下、再把嘴唇收圓，嘴形變化要明顯；學生常唸成平的 [nɑ]，沒有收圓，或和 know [no] 混淆。拼字 ow 在 now、how、cow 唸 [aʊ]，在 know、snow 卻唸 [o]，要分開記。開頭 [n] 別發成 [l]。
now.tip_en: [aʊ] must glide clearly from a wide-open [a] to rounded [ʊ]: drop the jaw first, then round the lips. Learners often say a flat [nɑ] without rounding, or confuse it with know [no]. The spelling ow is [aʊ] in now, how and cow, but [o] in know and snow; learn them separately. Don't start with [l].

examples.en: Let's go home now.
examples.zh: 我們現在回家吧。

examples.en: It's time to clean up now.
examples.zh: 現在該收拾了。

now.spelling_zh: ow 在這裡唸 [aʊ]，在 know 唸 [o]。
now.spelling_en: Here ow is [aʊ]; in know it is [o].

number.tip_zh: [nʌm] 之後雙唇已經閉起，直接爆出 [b]，學生常漏掉 m 或 b。字尾 -ber 要捲舌 [ɚ]，不要唸成平的「伯」。開頭的 [n] 舌尖頂上牙齦、從鼻子出聲，不要唸成 [l]。重音在第一音節。
number.tip_en: After [nʌm] the lips are already closed, so the [b] pops straight out; learners often drop the m or the b. The ending -ber needs an r-colored [ɚ], not a flat 'bo'. The opening [n] has the tongue tip on the gum ridge with sound through the nose, not [l]. Stress the first syllable.

examples.en: What is your phone number?
examples.zh: 你的電話號碼是多少？

examples.en: Pick a number from one to ten.
examples.zh: 從一到十選一個數字。

nurse.tip_zh: nurse 只有一個母音 [ɝ]，是要捲舌的重音母音。台灣學生常照拼字把 u 和 r 分開唸，或舌頭不捲，唸成像「呢斯」。發 [ɝ] 時舌尖往後捲、不碰到上顎，嘴唇微圓，把這個音拉長，和 bird、her 的母音一樣。字尾 [s] 輕輕吹氣就停，後面不要再加母音。
nurse.tip_en: nurse has only one vowel, [ɝ], a stressed vowel with a tongue curl. Taiwanese students often split u and r into two sounds from the spelling, or skip the curl, making it sound like 'ne-si'. For [ɝ], curl the tongue tip back without touching the roof of the mouth, round the lips slightly, and hold the sound; it is the same vowel as in bird and her. For the final [s], just blow a little air and stop, with no vowel after it.

examples.en: The school nurse helped me when I felt sick.
examples.zh: 我不舒服的時候，學校的護理師幫助了我。

examples.en: My aunt is a nurse at the hospital.
examples.zh: 我阿姨在醫院當護士。

october.tip_zh: October 重音在第二音節 [to]，台灣學生常把重音放在開頭的 Oc。開頭 [ɑk] 嘴巴張大，[k] 只做出舌根的動作，不要多加母音唸成「阿克」，要直接接到 [t]。[to] 的 [o] 要唸足並略帶圓唇滑音，最後 [bɚ] 舌頭往後捲、輕輕帶過。整個字的節奏是輕－重－輕。
october.tip_en: October is stressed on the second syllable [to]; Taiwanese students often stress the opening Oc. The opening [ɑk] has a wide-open mouth; the [k] is just the movement of the back of the tongue, with no extra vowel like 'a-ke', linking straight into [t]. Give the [o] in [to] its full length with a slight rounded glide, and say the final [bɚ] lightly with the tongue curled back. The rhythm of the whole word is weak–strong–weak.

examples.en: We go camping every October.
examples.zh: 我們每年十月都會去露營。

examples.en: Halloween is at the end of October.
examples.zh: 萬聖節在十月底。

of.tip_zh: of 的 f 唸有聲的 [v]，不是 [f]，這是拼字最容易誤導的地方；台灣學生常唸成 [ɔf] 或「歐夫」，和 off 混在一起。正確是短短的 [ʌ] 接 [v]：上齒輕碰下唇，喉嚨震動。在句子裡 of 通常唸得很弱，像 a glass of water 會輕到接近 [əv]，所以不要每次都唸得很重。
of.tip_en: The f in of is the voiced [v], not [f]; this is where the spelling misleads most. Taiwanese students often say [ɔf] or 'ou-fu', mixing it up with off. The correct form is a short [ʌ] plus [v]: upper teeth lightly on the lower lip, with the throat vibrating. In sentences of is usually weak; in a glass of water it becomes close to [əv], so don't stress it every time.

examples.en: Can I have a glass of water?
examples.zh: 可以給我一杯水嗎？

examples.en: One of my friends lives near the park.
examples.zh: 我有一個朋友住在公園附近。

of.spelling_en: The f here is pronounced [v], not [f].

off.tip_zh: off 和 of 很容易唸混：off 字尾是無聲的 [f]，上齒輕碰下唇吹氣，母音 [ɔ] 開口較大、較長；of 是很輕的 [əv]，結尾有聲。學生常把 turn off 唸成 turn of，或在 f 後加母音唸成「歐夫」。
off.tip_en: Off and of are easily mixed up: off ends in a voiceless [f], top teeth lightly on the lower lip, blowing air, with a more open, longer [ɔ]; of is a light [əv] ending in a voiced sound. Learners often say 'turn of' for turn off, or add a vowel after the f ('o-fu').

examples.en: Please turn off the lights.
examples.zh: 請把燈關掉。

examples.en: Take off your shoes at the door.
examples.zh: 在門口把鞋子脫掉。

off.spelling_zh: off 兩個 f 唸 [f]；of 一個 f 唸 [v]。
off.spelling_en: Off (two f's) ends in [f]; of (one f) ends in [v].
