thursday.tip_en: Thursday is often said as Sursday, or mixed up with Tuesday. Start by blowing out [θ] with the tongue between the teeth, then curl the tongue right away for [ɝ]: tongue curled back, not touching the roof of the mouth, the same vowel as bird. The s in the middle is a voiced [z]; the throat vibrates. The stress is on the first syllable; say the following [de] a little lighter and shorter.

examples.en: We have art class every Thursday.
examples.zh: 我們每個星期四都有美術課。

examples.en: My piano lesson is on Thursday afternoon.
examples.zh: 我的鋼琴課在星期四下午。

thursday.variant_en: The ending -day is often reduced to [dɪ]: [ˈθɝzdɪ].
thursday.spelling_zh: 中間的 s 唸有聲的 [z]。
thursday.spelling_en: The s in the middle is voiced [z].

ticket.tip_zh: 重音在第一音節 [ˈtɪ]，母音是短的 [ɪ]，不要拉成長 [i] 唸成 "tee-ket"。第二音節 [kət] 輕而短、母音弱化；字尾 [t] 舌尖頂住就停，不要加母音唸成「踢給特」。ck 只發一個 [k]。
ticket.tip_en: Stress the first syllable [ˈtɪ]; its vowel is a short [ɪ], so don't stretch it to a long [i] ('tee-ket'). The second syllable [kət] is light and short with a reduced vowel; for the final [t] just stop the tongue tip, without an extra vowel ('ti-gei-te'). The ck is a single [k].

examples.en: I bought a ticket for the movie.
examples.zh: 我買了一張電影票。

examples.en: Show your ticket at the gate.
examples.zh: 在入口出示你的票。

tidy.tip_zh: 第一音節是雙母音 [aɪ]，嘴巴先張大再滑向 [ɪ]；看到單字短短的就唸成短 [ɪ]，變成 "tiddy"，是常見錯誤。中間的 [d] 要有聲，舌尖輕點上牙齦；字尾 y 唸輕而短的 [ɪ]。重音在第一音節。
tidy.tip_en: The first syllable is the diphthong [aɪ]: open the mouth wide, then glide toward [ɪ]. Because the word looks short, learners often use a short [ɪ] and say 'tiddy'. The middle [d] is voiced, with a light tap of the tongue tip on the gum ridge; the final y is a light, short [ɪ]. Stress the first syllable.

examples.en: Please keep your room tidy.
examples.zh: 請保持你的房間整齊。

examples.en: Her desk is always clean and tidy.
examples.zh: 她的書桌總是乾淨又整齊。

tidy.spelling_en: The i says [aɪ]; the y says [ɪ]

tie.tip_zh: ie 在這裡唸 [aɪ]，跟 pie、lie 一樣；照 piece、field 的拼字習慣唸成 [i]，就變成 tea「茶」了。[aɪ] 要從嘴巴張大的 [a] 一路滑到 [ɪ]，滑完整，不要只唸一半變成平平的 [a]。當動詞「綁」時也是同一個音，例如 tie your shoes。
tie.tip_en: The ie here says [aɪ], as in pie and lie; read it like piece or field with [i] and you get tea. Glide [aɪ] all the way from an open-mouthed [a] to [ɪ]; don't stop halfway on a flat [a]. The verb meaning 'to tie' uses the same sound, as in tie your shoes.

examples.en: Dad wears a tie to work.
examples.zh: 爸爸打領帶去上班。

examples.en: Can you help me tie my shoes?
examples.zh: 你可以幫我綁鞋帶嗎？

tie.spelling_zh: ie 唸 [aɪ]，跟 pie 一樣

tiger.tip_zh: tiger 的難點在字尾 -er：常被唸成沒有捲舌的 [gə]，聽起來像英式發音或中文的輕聲。美式要唸 [gɚ]：舌根往上頂一下發出 [g]，接著舌頭立刻往後捲起、不碰任何地方，帶著捲舌的聲音收尾。第一音節 [taɪ] 是重音，嘴巴從大開滑向 [ɪ]，要唸得比 [gɚ] 長而有力。
tiger.tip_en: The hard part of tiger is the ending -er: it is often said as an r-less [gə], sounding British or like a Mandarin neutral-tone syllable. American English needs [gɚ]: raise the back of the tongue once for [g], then curl the tongue back right away without touching anything, ending with an r-colored sound. The first syllable [taɪ] carries the stress: open the mouth wide and glide toward [ɪ], longer and stronger than [gɚ].

examples.en: The tiger is sleeping under a tree.
examples.zh: 老虎正在樹下睡覺。

examples.en: My little brother drew a tiger in art class.
examples.zh: 我弟弟在美術課畫了一隻老虎。

time.tip_zh: 雙母音 [aɪ] 從 [a] 滑到 [ɪ] 之後，雙唇要閉起來發 [m]；嘴巴沒閉，聽起來就只剩像「太」的音。字尾 e 不發音，不要唸成「太姆」多出一個音節。跟 team [tim] 的差別在母音：time 嘴巴先張大。
time.tip_en: After the diphthong [aɪ] glides from [a] to [ɪ], close the lips for [m]; leave the mouth open and only a 'tai'-like sound is left. The final e is silent, so don't add an extra syllable ('tai-mu'). The difference from team [tim] is the vowel: time starts with a wide-open mouth.

examples.en: What time is it now?
examples.zh: 現在幾點？

examples.en: It's time for bed.
examples.zh: 該睡覺了。

tip.tip_zh: tip 的母音是短而放鬆的 [ɪ]，嘴巴微開，不要拉成長 [i] 唸成 "teep"。字尾 [p] 雙唇閉上就停，不要再彈出母音唸成「踢普」。跟 type [taɪp]、tape [tep] 比，tip 是三個字裡嘴巴動作最小、最短的一個。
tip.tip_en: The vowel in tip is a short, relaxed [ɪ] with the mouth slightly open; don't stretch it to a long [i] ('teep'). For the final [p] just close the lips and stop, without popping out a vowel ('ti-pu'). Compared with type [taɪp] and tape [tep], tip has the smallest, shortest mouth movement of the three.

examples.en: Here's a tip: read every day.
examples.zh: 給你一個訣竅：每天閱讀。

examples.en: Dad left a tip for the waiter.
examples.zh: 爸爸留了小費給服務生。

tired.tip_zh: [aɪ] 滑完之後直接接捲舌的 [ɚ]，舌尖往後捲，不要唸成「太兒」就結束；字尾 [d] 要做出來，舌尖頂上牙齦。也別照拼字唸成 "tie-red"，多出一個 [ɛ]：字尾 ed 在這裡只唸 [d]。
tired.tip_en: After the [aɪ] glide, go straight into the r-colored [ɚ] with the tongue tip curled back; don't stop at a 'tai-er' sound. Make the final [d] by touching the tongue tip to the gum ridge. And don't follow the spelling into 'tie-red' with an extra [ɛ]: the -ed ending here is only [d].

examples.en: I'm so tired after PE class.
examples.zh: 上完體育課我好累。

examples.en: The baby is tired and wants to sleep.
examples.zh: 小寶寶累了，想睡覺。

to.tip_zh: to 單獨唸是 [tu]，嘴唇噘圓；但在句子裡（例如 go to school）常弱讀成 [tə]，又輕又短。學生常每個 to 都唸得又重又長，句子就變得一個字一個字很不自然。to、too、two 唸 [tu] 時同音，要靠拼字分辨。
to.tip_en: Said alone, to is [tu] with rounded lips; inside a sentence (as in go to school) it usually weakens to a short, light [tə]. Learners often say every to strong and long, which makes the sentence sound choppy and unnatural. When said as [tu], to, too and two sound the same; only the spelling tells them apart.

examples.en: We walk to school every day.
examples.zh: 我們每天走路上學。

examples.en: I want to go to the zoo.
examples.zh: 我想去動物園。

to.variant_en: In a sentence it is usually weakened to [tə]
to.spelling_en: Sounds the same as too and two

toast.tip_zh: oa 唸雙母音 [o]，嘴唇圓起再稍微收緊，不要唸成嘴巴大開的 [ɔ]。字尾 [st] 兩個子音都要出來：先 [s] 再讓舌尖頂住發 [t]；學生常掉 t 唸成 "tose"，或加母音唸成「投斯特」。跟 taste、test 只差母音。
toast.tip_en: The oa is the diphthong [o]: round the lips, then tighten them slightly; don't open it into [ɔ]. Both consonants of the final [st] must be heard: [s], then the tongue tip stops for [t]. Learners often drop the t ('tose') or add vowels ('tou-si-te'). It differs from taste and test only in the vowel.

examples.en: I had toast and milk for breakfast.
examples.zh: 我早餐吃了吐司配牛奶。

examples.en: Mom puts butter on my toast.
examples.zh: 媽媽在我的吐司上塗奶油。

today.tip_zh: 重音在第二音節 [ˈde]，第一音節 [tə] 是輕短的弱母音；學生常把 to 唸成又長又重的 [tu]，重音跑到前面。後面的 [de] 是雙母音，要滑到 [i] 的位置，不要唸成短的 [ɛ]。整個字聽起來是「輕—重」。
today.tip_en: Stress the second syllable [ˈde]; the first syllable [tə] is a short, weak vowel. Learners often make to a long, heavy [tu], which moves the stress to the front. The [de] is a diphthong that should glide up toward [i], not a short [ɛ]. The whole word goes light then strong.

examples.en: Today is my birthday!
examples.zh: 今天是我的生日！

examples.en: What did you learn at school today?
examples.zh: 你今天在學校學了什麼？

today.variant_zh: 也有人第一音節唸 [tu]，但仍是輕音節
today.variant_en: Some say [tu] in the first syllable, but it stays unstressed

toe.tip_zh: toe 唸雙母音 [o]，嘴唇從半開的圓唇慢慢收小；學生常把它唸成噘緊的 [u]，結果跟 to、two 分不清。oe 只代表這一個母音，e 不另外發音，不要唸成兩個音節。開頭 [t] 要送氣。
toe.tip_en: Toe has the diphthong [o]: start with half-open rounded lips and slowly tighten them. Learners often say a tight [u] instead, which makes it sound like to or two. The oe spells just this one vowel; the e is not said separately, so don't make it two syllables. Give the opening [t] a puff of air.

examples.en: Wiggle your big toe in the warm sand.
examples.zh: 在溫暖的沙子裡動動你的大腳趾。

examples.en: My little sister painted her toe pink.
examples.zh: 我妹妹把她的腳趾頭塗成粉紅色。

toe.spelling_zh: oe 唸 [o]，e 不另外發音
toe.spelling_en: oe says [o]; the e is not said separately

together.tip_zh: together 的第一音節是很輕的 [tə]，常被唸成重重的 [tu]，把重音放錯在第一音節。正確重音在 [gɛ]，嘴巴半開。接下來的 [ð] 不能唸成 [d] 或 [z]，舌尖輕碰上排牙齒、喉嚨振動，然後馬上捲舌唸 [ɚ]。後半段 [gɛðɚ] 和 weather 的 [wɛðɚ] 押韻，可以放在一起練。
together.tip_en: The first syllable of together is a very light [tə]; it is often said as a heavy [tu], putting the stress wrongly on the first syllable. The real stress is on [gɛ], with the mouth half open. The following [ð] must not become [d] or [z]: the tongue tip lightly touches the upper teeth and the throat vibrates, then curl the tongue right away for [ɚ]. The second half [gɛðɚ] rhymes with [wɛðɚ] in weather, so practice them side by side.

examples.en: Let's play together after lunch.
examples.zh: 午餐後我們一起玩吧。

examples.en: My family eats dinner together every night.
examples.zh: 我們家每天晚上都一起吃晚餐。

tomato.tip_zh: tomato 常被唸成每個音節一樣重的 [tomɑto]，第二音節也張得太大。美式重音在第二音節 [me]，跟 May 的唸法一樣，嘴角往兩旁拉；第一音節只是輕輕的 [tə]，嘴巴幾乎不用動。最後一個音節 [to] 輕一點，嘴唇變圓收小；說快時這個 t 常變得像輕輕的 [d]。
tomato.tip_en: tomato is often said as [tomɑto], with every syllable equally strong and the second syllable opened too wide. In American English the stress is on the second syllable [me], said like May, with the corners of the mouth pulled sideways; the first syllable is just a light [tə], with the mouth barely moving. The last syllable [to] is lighter, the lips rounding and closing; in fast speech this t often sounds like a soft [d].

examples.en: I put a slice of tomato in my sandwich.
examples.zh: 我在三明治裡放了一片番茄。

examples.en: Mom cut a tomato for the salad.
examples.zh: 媽媽切了一顆番茄做沙拉。

tomato.variant_en: British and a few US speakers say [təˈmɑto].

tomorrow.tip_zh: tomorrow 的重音在第二音節 [mɑ]，第一音節是輕輕的 [tə]，不要唸成重重的 [tu]。拼字是 o，但美式 [mɑ] 的母音要把下巴往下拉、嘴巴張大，跟 hot 的母音一樣，不是圓唇的 [o]。拼字有兩個 r，其實只發一個 [r]：舌頭往後捲，再把嘴唇變圓，滑到最後的 [o]。
tomorrow.tip_en: tomorrow is stressed on the second syllable [mɑ]; the first syllable is a light [tə], not a heavy [tu]. The spelling has o, but the American vowel in [mɑ] needs the jaw dropped and the mouth open wide, the same vowel as hot, not a rounded [o]. There are two r's in the spelling but only one [r] sound: curl the tongue back, then round the lips and glide into the final [o].

examples.en: We have a spelling test tomorrow.
examples.zh: 我們明天有拼字考試。

examples.en: See you tomorrow at school!
examples.zh: 明天學校見！

tonight.tip_zh: 重音在第二音節 [ˈnaɪt]，第一音節 [tə] 輕而短，不要唸成又重又長的 [tu]。gh 不發音，night 只有 [naɪt] 三個音；[aɪ] 從張嘴滑向 [ɪ]，字尾 [t] 舌尖頂住就好，不要唸成「耐特」多出一個母音。
tonight.tip_en: Stress the second syllable [ˈnaɪt]; the first syllable [tə] is light and short, not a heavy, long [tu]. The gh is silent, so night is just the three sounds [naɪt]: [aɪ] glides from an open mouth toward [ɪ], and the final [t] is just a tongue-tip stop, without an extra vowel ('nai-te').

examples.en: What are we having for dinner tonight?
examples.zh: 我們今天晚餐吃什麼？

examples.en: We can see the moon tonight.
examples.zh: 今晚我們可以看到月亮。

too.tip_zh: too 是長的 [u]，嘴唇噘圓往前、維持一下；唸太短會變成鬆的 [ʊ]。它跟 to、two 同音，但 too 常在句尾當重點（Me too!），要唸得完整清楚，不能像介系詞 to 那樣弱讀成 [tə]。
too.tip_en: Too has a long [u]: push the rounded lips forward and hold it a moment; too short and it turns into the lax [ʊ]. It sounds the same as to and two, but too often carries the stress at the end of a sentence (Me too!), so say it fully and clearly; never weaken it to [tə] the way the preposition to is weakened.

examples.en: I like pizza too.
examples.zh: 我也喜歡披薩。

examples.en: This bag is too heavy for me.
examples.zh: 這個袋子對我來說太重了。

too.spelling_zh: oo 唸 [u]，跟 to、two 同音
too.spelling_en: oo says [u]; sounds the same as to and two

tool.tip_zh: [u] 嘴唇噘圓之後，舌根往後縮、舌尖最後頂到上牙齦，做出字尾暗 L；學生常把 l 唸成「歐」或乾脆省略，聽起來只剩 "too"。母音要長，不要短成 pull 的 [ʊ]。對比 tall、tell、tail，這幾個字只差母音。
tool.tip_en: After the lip-rounded [u], pull the back of the tongue back and finish with the tongue tip on the gum ridge to make the final dark L. Learners often turn the l into an 'o' sound or drop it, leaving just 'too'. Keep the vowel long rather than shortening it to the [ʊ] of pull. Compare tall, tell and tail: these words differ only in the vowel.

examples.en: A hammer is a useful tool.
examples.zh: 鐵鎚是很有用的工具。

examples.en: Which tool do you need for this?
examples.zh: 你做這個需要哪一種工具？

tooth.tip_zh: tooth 的難點在字尾 [θ]：常被唸成 [s]，聽起來像 toos，或乾脆省略只剩 too。唸完拉長的 [u] 之後，舌尖要往前伸到上下牙齒之間，輕輕吹氣收尾，可以照鏡子確認看得到舌尖。[u] 嘴唇要嘟圓、拉長，不要唸成短促的 [ʊ]。複數 teeth 的結尾也是同一個 [θ]。
tooth.tip_en: The hard part of tooth is the final [θ]: it is often said as [s], sounding like toos, or dropped so only too is left. After the long [u], push the tongue tip forward between the upper and lower teeth and blow gently to finish; check in a mirror that you can see the tongue tip. For [u], round and push out the lips and hold it long; don't make it a short [ʊ]. The plural teeth ends with the same [θ].

examples.en: My little sister lost her first tooth today.
examples.zh: 我妹妹今天掉了第一顆牙。

examples.en: The dentist gave me a sticker after checking my tooth.
examples.zh: 牙醫檢查完我的牙齒後，送我一張貼紙。

top.tip_zh: 美式 top 的母音是 [ɑ]，嘴巴張大、嘴唇不圓，像看醫生時說「啊」；學生常把嘴唇圓起來，唸成接近 [o] 的「拓」。字尾 [p] 雙唇閉上就停，不要再加母音唸成「拓普」。拼字是 o，但美式發音是 [ɑ]。
top.tip_en: In American English the vowel in top is [ɑ]: mouth wide open, lips unrounded, like saying 'ah' for the doctor. Learners often round the lips into something close to [o] ('tuo'). For the final [p], close the lips and stop without adding a vowel ('tuo-pu'). It is spelled with o, but the American sound is [ɑ].

examples.en: Put the box on top of the shelf.
examples.zh: 把箱子放在架子的最上面。

examples.en: Let's climb to the top of the hill!
examples.zh: 我們爬到山頂吧！

topic.tip_zh: 重音在第一音節 [ˈtɑ]，母音 [ɑ] 嘴巴張大、不圓唇；第二音節 [pɪk] 輕而短，母音是短 [ɪ]。學生常唸成「拓匹克」：把 [ɑ] 唸圓、把 [ɪ] 拉長成 [i]，還在字尾多加母音。字尾 [k] 舌根頂住就停。
topic.tip_en: Stress the first syllable [ˈtɑ], whose [ɑ] has a wide-open mouth and unrounded lips; the second syllable [pɪk] is light and short with a short [ɪ]. Learners often say 'tuo-pi-ke': rounding the [ɑ], stretching [ɪ] into [i], and adding a vowel at the end. For the final [k] just stop with the back of the tongue.

examples.en: What is the topic of your report?
examples.zh: 你報告的主題是什麼？

examples.en: Our topic today is animals.
examples.zh: 我們今天的主題是動物。

total.tip_zh: 第一音節是雙母音 [o]，嘴唇圓起再收小；第二音節是成音節的暗 L [tḷ]，t 後面不要加母音唸成「投頭」。美式口語中間的 t 常輕彈得像很快的 d。母音也不要捲舌成 [ɝ]，否則會像 turtle。
total.tip_en: The first syllable is the diphthong [o]: round the lips, then tighten them. The second syllable is a syllabic dark L, [tḷ]; don't add a vowel after t ('tou-tou'). In casual American speech the middle t is often a quick tap like a fast d. Don't put an r-color on the first vowel either, or it sounds like turtle.

examples.en: The total is two hundred dollars.
examples.zh: 總共是兩百元。

examples.en: What is the total of these numbers?
examples.zh: 這些數字的總和是多少？

touch.tip_zh: ou 在這裡唸短的 [ʌ]，嘴巴微開、放鬆，像 cup 的母音；照拼字唸成 house 的 [aʊ] 或 you 的 [u] 都不對。字尾 [tʃ] 嘴唇微噘、舌面放開送氣，不要再加母音唸成「他去」。跟 teach [titʃ] 結尾一樣，只差母音。
touch.tip_en: The ou here says a short [ʌ], mouth slightly open and relaxed, like the vowel in cup; reading it as the [aʊ] of house or the [u] of you is wrong. For the final [tʃ], push the lips slightly forward and release the tongue with a puff of air, without adding a vowel ('ta-chu'). It ends like teach [titʃ]; only the vowel differs.

examples.en: Don't touch the wet paint.
examples.zh: 不要碰還沒乾的油漆。

examples.en: Can you touch your toes?
examples.zh: 你摸得到你的腳趾嗎？

touch.spelling_zh: ou 唸 [ʌ]，跟 much 同韻

towel.tip_zh: [aʊ] 從嘴巴張大的 [a] 滑到圓唇的 [ʊ]，接著是輕輕的 [ə]，最後是字尾暗 L。學生常把 el 唸成「偶」，結尾沒有舌尖上抬的 l，聽起來像 "tow-o"。最後一定要讓舌尖碰到上牙齦。重音在第一音節。
towel.tip_en: [aʊ] glides from an open-mouthed [a] to a rounded [ʊ], followed by a light [ə] and then a final dark L. Learners often turn the el into an 'ou' sound with no tongue-tip l at the end, like 'tow-o'. Make sure the tongue tip touches the gum ridge at the very end. Stress the first syllable.

examples.en: Dry your hands with this towel.
examples.zh: 用這條毛巾把手擦乾。

examples.en: Don't forget your towel for the pool.
examples.zh: 別忘了帶游泳用的毛巾。

towel.variant_en: In casual speech often one syllable: [taʊl]

town.tip_zh: town 的 ow 唸 [aʊ]，嘴巴先張大再收圓；字尾是舌尖頂上牙齦的 [n]，不要唸成後鼻音 [ŋ]，也不要讓鼻音消失。跟 down 只差第一個音：[t] 不震動聲帶、要送氣，[d] 有聲。母音唸成 [ɛ] 就變成 ten。
town.tip_en: The ow in town says [aʊ]: open the mouth wide, then round the lips. The ending is a tongue-tip [n] on the gum ridge, not the back nasal [ŋ], and it shouldn't disappear. It differs from down only in the first sound: [t] is voiceless with a puff of air, [d] is voiced. Change the vowel to [ɛ] and it becomes ten.

examples.en: My grandparents live in a small town.
examples.zh: 我的爺爺奶奶住在一個小鎮。

examples.en: There's a new bookstore in town.
examples.zh: 鎮上開了一家新書店。

toy.tip_zh: oy 是雙母音 [ɔɪ]：嘴巴先張開、圓唇發 [ɔ]，再快速滑向 [ɪ]，兩段要連成一個音節。學生常把開頭唸得太閉，接近 [o]，或拆成兩拍，像「偷—依」。跟 boy、enjoy 押同一個韻，可以一起練。
toy.tip_en: oy is the diphthong [ɔɪ]: open the mouth with rounded lips for [ɔ], then glide quickly to [ɪ], all in one syllable. Learners often start too closed, near [o], or split it into two beats like 'tou-yi'. It rhymes with boy and enjoy, so practice them together.

examples.en: This toy car is my favorite.
examples.zh: 這台玩具車是我最喜歡的。

examples.en: Share your toy with your little brother.
examples.zh: 把你的玩具分給弟弟玩。

traffic.tip_zh: 開頭 [tr] 要連在一起：舌尖一離開上牙齦就往後捲成 [r]，中間不要加母音唸成「特瑞」。[æ] 嘴巴張大、嘴角往兩邊拉，不要唸成 [ɛ]。重音在第一音節，第二音節 [fɪk] 輕而短，[f] 用上排牙齒輕碰下唇送氣。
traffic.tip_en: Keep the opening [tr] together: as soon as the tongue tip leaves the gum ridge, curl it back into [r], with no vowel in between ('te-rui'). The [æ] needs a wide-open mouth with the lip corners pulled back, not [ɛ]. Stress the first syllable; the second, [fɪk], is light and short, with the upper teeth lightly touching the lower lip for [f].

examples.en: There is a lot of traffic this morning.
examples.zh: 今天早上車很多。

examples.en: Look both ways and watch the traffic.
examples.zh: 左右看，注意來往的車輛。

train.tip_zh: [tr] 中間不要插母音，舌尖從 [t] 的位置直接往後捲到 [r]。ai 唸雙母音 [e]，要滑到 [i] 的位置；字尾是舌尖頂上牙齦的 [n]，不要變成後鼻音 [ŋ]，聽起來像 "trang" 或 "treng"。
train.tip_en: Don't put a vowel inside [tr]; curl the tongue straight back from the [t] position into [r]. The ai is the diphthong [e], gliding up toward [i]; the ending is a tongue-tip [n] on the gum ridge, not the back nasal [ŋ] that makes it sound like 'trang' or 'treng'.

examples.en: We took the train to Taichung.
examples.zh: 我們搭火車去臺中。

examples.en: The train leaves at nine o'clock.
examples.zh: 火車九點開。

trash.tip_zh: [æ] 嘴巴張大、下巴往下，不要唸成較閉的 [ɛ]，變成 "tresh"。字尾 [ʃ] 嘴唇要噘起往外送氣，比中文捲舌的「師」更圓唇，而且後面不帶母音。開頭 [tr] 連著唸，t 後面不要多一個「特」。
trash.tip_en: The [æ] needs a wide-open mouth with the jaw dropped; don't close it to [ɛ] ('tresh'). For the final [ʃ], push the lips forward and blow; it is more rounded than the Mandarin retroflex 'shi' and has no vowel after it. Keep the opening [tr] together, with no extra 'te' after t.

examples.en: Please take out the trash.
examples.zh: 請把垃圾拿出去倒。

examples.en: Put your trash in the can.
examples.zh: 把你的垃圾丟進垃圾桶。

treat.tip_zh: ea 唸長 [i]，嘴角往兩邊拉、保持一下；唸太短會變成 [ɪ]，像 trick 的母音。開頭 [tr] 不要拆成兩拍，舌尖碰到上牙齦後立刻捲舌；字尾 [t] 舌尖頂住就停，不要唸成「催特」多出一個母音。
treat.tip_en: The ea is a long [i]: pull the lip corners back and hold it a moment; too short and it becomes [ɪ], the vowel of trick. Don't split the opening [tr] into two beats; curl the tongue right after the tip touches the gum ridge. For the final [t] just stop the tongue tip, without an extra vowel ('cui-te').

examples.en: Let me treat you to ice cream.
examples.zh: 我請你吃冰淇淋。

examples.en: Be kind and treat others nicely.
examples.zh: 要善良，好好對待別人。

tree.tip_zh: tree 開頭是 [tr]：舌尖碰上牙齦後立刻捲舌，不要插母音。它和 three [θri] 只差第一個音：tree 是舌尖頂牙齦的 [t]，three 要把舌尖放在上下門牙之間送氣。ee 是長 [i]，嘴角往兩邊拉，要唸夠長。
tree.tip_en: Tree starts with [tr]: touch the tongue tip to the gum ridge and curl it back at once, with no vowel in between. It differs from three [θri] only in the first sound: tree uses a [t] on the gum ridge, three puts the tongue tip between the front teeth and blows. The ee is a long [i] with the lip corners pulled back; hold it long enough.

examples.en: There is a bird in the tree.
examples.zh: 樹上有一隻鳥。

examples.en: We planted a tree in the garden.
examples.zh: 我們在花園裡種了一棵樹。

trick.tip_zh: 母音是短 [ɪ]，嘴巴微開、放鬆；唸成長 [i] 會像 "treek"，嘴巴太開又變成 truck [trʌk]。ck 只發一個 [k]，舌根頂住軟顎就停，不要加母音唸成「垂克」。開頭 [tr] 中間不要插母音。
trick.tip_en: The vowel is a short, relaxed [ɪ] with the mouth slightly open; stretch it to a long [i] and it sounds like 'treek', open too wide and it becomes truck [trʌk]. The ck is a single [k]: stop with the back of the tongue against the soft palate, without adding a vowel ('chui-ke'). Don't put a vowel inside the opening [tr].

examples.en: My dog can do a cool trick.
examples.zh: 我的狗會表演一個很酷的把戲。

examples.en: The kids shouted, "Trick or treat!"
examples.zh: 孩子們大喊：「不給糖就搗蛋！」

trip.tip_zh: trip 和 trick 只差最後一個音：[p] 是雙唇閉起來，[k] 是舌根頂住，兩個都不要再補母音，否則唸成「垂普」。中間的 [ɪ] 短而放鬆，不要拉長成 [i]。開頭 [tr] 的 t 不要單獨唸出一個「特」。
trip.tip_en: Trip and trick differ only in the last sound: [p] closes both lips, [k] uses the back of the tongue; add no vowel after either, or you get 'chui-pu'. The middle [ɪ] is short and relaxed, not a long [i]. Don't pronounce the t of the opening [tr] as a separate 'te'.

examples.en: We went on a school trip to the zoo.
examples.zh: 我們校外教學去了動物園。

examples.en: Have a nice trip!
examples.zh: 祝你旅途愉快！

trouble.tip_zh: ou 在這裡唸 [ʌ]，跟 cup 的母音一樣，不要照拼字唸成 [aʊ] 或 [u]。第二音節是成音節的暗 L [bḷ]，唸完 b 舌尖直接頂上牙齦，不要在 b 後面加母音唸成「伯」或「波」。重音在第一音節。
trouble.tip_en: The ou here says [ʌ], the same vowel as in cup; don't follow the spelling to [aʊ] or [u]. The second syllable is a syllabic dark L, [bḷ]: after b, put the tongue tip straight on the gum ridge, without a vowel after b ('bo'). Stress the first syllable.

examples.en: I have trouble with this math problem.
examples.zh: 這題數學我有困難。

examples.en: Thanks for helping; it was no trouble.
examples.zh: 謝謝你幫忙，一點都不麻煩。

trouble.spelling_zh: ou 唸 [ʌ]，字尾 le 唸 [ḷ]

truck.tip_zh: u 唸 [ʌ]：下巴微微放下、舌頭放鬆在中間，聲音短促；嘴巴太開太扁會像 track，嘴巴太閉又像 trick。開頭 [tr] 連在一起，字尾 ck 只發一個 [k]，舌根頂住就停，不要唸成「卓克」多一個母音。
truck.tip_en: The u says [ʌ]: drop the jaw a little, keep the tongue relaxed in the middle, and keep it short. Open and spread the mouth too much and it sounds like track; close it too much and it sounds like trick. Keep the opening [tr] together; the ck is a single [k], stopped with the back of the tongue, without an extra vowel ('zhuo-ke').

examples.en: A big truck is parked outside.
examples.zh: 外面停了一台大卡車。

examples.en: My little brother loves his toy truck.
examples.zh: 我弟弟很愛他的玩具卡車。

true.tip_zh: ue 唸長 [u]，嘴唇噘圓往前推；[r] 本身也帶一點圓唇，所以一開口就可以先把嘴唇圓起來。[t] 和 [r] 之間不要加母音唸成「特如」，也不要在 r 後面多加 [j] 唸成 "tryoo"。字尾 e 不另外發音。
true.tip_en: The ue is a long [u]: round the lips and push them forward. [r] itself is a little rounded, so you can round the lips from the very start. Don't put a vowel between [t] and [r] ('te-ru'), and don't add a [j] after the r ('tryoo'). The final e is not said separately.

examples.en: Is that story true?
examples.zh: 那個故事是真的嗎？

examples.en: I hope your dream comes true.
examples.zh: 希望你的夢想成真。

try.tip_zh: y 在單音節字的字尾唸 [aɪ]，跟 cry、dry 同韻；[aɪ] 要從嘴巴張大一路滑到 [ɪ]。開頭 [tr] 是一個連在一起的子音串，舌尖離開牙齦就捲舌，不要分成「特—賴」兩拍。
try.tip_en: At the end of a one-syllable word, y says [aɪ], rhyming with cry and dry; glide [aɪ] all the way from an open mouth to [ɪ]. The opening [tr] is one consonant cluster: curl the tongue as soon as the tip leaves the gum ridge, rather than splitting it into two beats like 'te-lai'.

examples.en: Try again; you can do it!
examples.zh: 再試一次，你做得到的！

examples.en: Can I try your noodles?
examples.zh: 我可以吃吃看你的麵嗎？

tuesday.tip_zh: 第一音節的 s 要唸有聲的 [z]，不是 [s]；ue 唸長 [u]，嘴唇噘圓。重音在第一音節，第二音節 [dɪ] 輕而短。常見錯誤是中間唸成無聲的 [s]，或把 day 唸得跟第一音節一樣重。字首 T 要大寫。
tuesday.tip_en: The s in the first syllable is a voiced [z], not [s]; the ue is a long [u] with rounded lips. Stress the first syllable; the second syllable [dɪ] is light and short. Common mistakes are a voiceless [s] in the middle and giving day as much weight as the first syllable. The T is always a capital.

examples.en: We have art class on Tuesday.
examples.zh: 我們星期二有美術課。

examples.en: See you next Tuesday!
examples.zh: 下星期二見！

tuesday.variant_en: The ending is also often said [de]: [ˈtuzˌde]

turn.tip_zh: ur 唸捲舌的 [ɝ]：舌尖往後捲、嘴唇微圓，整個母音都帶著 r 的色彩，不要唸成沒捲舌的「疼」。字尾 [n] 舌尖頂上牙齦，不要變成後鼻音 [ŋ]。如果不捲舌，就容易跟 ten [tɛn] 混在一起。
turn.tip_en: The ur is the r-colored [ɝ]: curl the tongue tip back and round the lips slightly, so the whole vowel carries the r sound; don't say a flat 'teng' with no curl. For the final [n], put the tongue tip on the gum ridge rather than making a back nasal [ŋ]. Without the curl, it easily blurs into ten [tɛn].

examples.en: Turn left at the corner.
examples.zh: 在轉角左轉。

examples.en: It's your turn to read.
examples.zh: 輪到你唸了。

turtle.tip_zh: turtle 的兩個音節各有一個難點。第一音節 [tɝ] 要捲舌，舌頭往後捲、不碰上顎，不要唸成平平的 [tʌ]。第二音節 [tḷ] 是成音節的 l：舌尖碰上牙齦發出 [t] 後就停在原地，直接轉成 [l]，中間不加母音，字尾也不要多出 [o] 的聲音。美式說快時，這個 t 會變得像輕輕的 [d]。
turtle.tip_en: Each of turtle's two syllables has its own trap. The first syllable [tɝ] needs a curled tongue, pulled back without touching the roof of the mouth; don't flatten it into [tʌ]. The second syllable [tḷ] is a syllabic l: after the tongue tip touches the gum ridge for [t], keep it there and turn straight into [l], with no vowel in between and no [o]-like sound added at the end. In fast American speech this t becomes like a soft [d].

examples.en: The turtle walks very slowly.
examples.zh: 烏龜走得很慢。

examples.en: We saw a big turtle at the beach.
examples.zh: 我們在海邊看到一隻大海龜。

twelve.tip_zh: 字尾 [lv] 是兩個子音：先讓舌尖頂上牙齦發暗 L，再用上排牙齒輕碰下唇、震動聲帶發 [v]。學生常省掉 l 唸成 "twev"，或把 [v] 唸成無聲的 [f] 再加母音「福」。開頭 [tw] 嘴唇一開始就要圓起來。
twelve.tip_en: The ending [lv] is two consonants: first the tongue tip on the gum ridge for a dark L, then the upper teeth lightly on the lower lip with the voice buzzing for [v]. Learners often drop the l ('twev'), or turn [v] into a voiceless [f] and add a vowel ('fu'). Round the lips from the very start for the opening [tw].

examples.en: There are twelve months in a year.
examples.zh: 一年有十二個月。

examples.en: Lunch is at twelve o'clock.
examples.zh: 午餐是十二點。

twenty.tip_zh: 重音在第一音節 [ˈtwɛn]，第二音節 [tɪ] 輕而短，不要唸成拉長、跟第一音節一樣重的「踢」。開頭 [tw] 嘴唇要先圓起來，不要只發 [t] 就直接接母音。第一音節收在舌尖頂牙齦的 [n]，不要變成 [ŋ]。
twenty.tip_en: Stress the first syllable [ˈtwɛn]; the second syllable [tɪ] is light and short, not a long 'tee' with the same weight as the first. Round the lips first for the opening [tw]; don't go straight from [t] to the vowel. The first syllable ends in a tongue-tip [n] on the gum ridge, not [ŋ].

examples.en: I have twenty stickers in my book.
examples.zh: 我的本子裡有二十張貼紙。

examples.en: Count from one to twenty.
examples.zh: 從一數到二十。

twenty.variant_en: Casual American speech often drops the t: [ˈtwɛnɪ]

twice.tip_zh: 字尾 ce 唸無聲的 [s]，而且 e 不發音，不要唸成 [z]，也不要在後面多加母音。i 唸雙母音 [aɪ]，嘴巴從張大滑到 [ɪ]。開頭 [tw] 嘴唇先圓起來，t 之後不要插母音唸成「特外斯」。
twice.tip_en: The final ce is a voiceless [s] and the e is silent; don't make it [z] or add a vowel after it. The i is the diphthong [aɪ], gliding from an open mouth to [ɪ]. Round the lips first for the opening [tw], and don't put a vowel after t ('te-wai-si').

examples.en: I brush my teeth twice a day.
examples.zh: 我一天刷兩次牙。

examples.en: Read the question twice before you answer.
examples.zh: 回答前先把題目讀兩遍。

twice.spelling_en: ce says [s]; the e is silent

two.tip_zh: two 的 w 不發音，整個字只有 [tu]：舌尖頂牙齦送氣，接嘴唇噘圓的長 [u]。看到 w 就在 t 後面多加一個圓唇滑音，唸成 "twoo"，是常見錯誤。two、to、too 同音，要靠句子判斷是哪一個。
two.tip_en: The w in two is silent; the whole word is just [tu]: a [t] with a puff of air from the gum ridge, then a long [u] with rounded lips. Seeing the w and adding a rounded glide after t ('twoo') is a common mistake. Two, to and too sound the same; context tells you which one it is.

examples.en: I have two cats at home.
examples.zh: 我家有兩隻貓。

examples.en: Two plus two is four.
examples.zh: 二加二等於四。

two.spelling_zh: w 不發音，跟 to、too 同音
two.spelling_en: The w is silent; sounds the same as to and too

type.tip_zh: y 在這裡唸 [aɪ]，跟 time 同一個母音，不是短 [ɪ]；唸成 [ɪ] 就變成 tip。字尾 [p] 雙唇閉起即停，e 不發音，不要唸成「太普」。和 tape [tep] 比：type 一開始嘴巴要張得比較大，再往 [ɪ] 滑。typing 的 y 也一樣唸 [aɪ]。
type.tip_en: The y here says [aɪ], the same vowel as in time, not a short [ɪ]; say [ɪ] and it becomes tip. For the final [p] close the lips and stop; the e is silent, so don't say 'tai-pu'. Compared with tape [tep], type starts with a wider-open mouth and then glides toward [ɪ]. The y in typing also says [aɪ].

examples.en: Can you type your name here?
examples.zh: 你可以在這裡打上你的名字嗎？

examples.en: I can type fast on the computer.
examples.zh: 我在電腦上打字很快。

type.spelling_zh: y 唸 [aɪ]，字尾 e 不發音
type.spelling_en: The y says [aɪ]; the final e is silent

typhoon.tip_zh: 重音在第二音節 [ˈfun]，第一音節 [taɪ] 輕一點。ph 唸 [f]，上排牙齒輕碰下唇；oo 是長 [u]，字尾是舌尖頂上牙齦的 [n]。常見錯誤是受中文「颱風」影響，重音放在前面，結尾唸成後鼻音，像 "tai-fong"。
typhoon.tip_en: Stress the second syllable [ˈfun]; say the first syllable [taɪ] more lightly. The ph says [f], with the upper teeth lightly on the lower lip; the oo is a long [u], and the word ends in a tongue-tip [n] on the gum ridge. A common mistake, influenced by Mandarin 'taifeng', is stressing the front and ending in a back nasal, like 'tai-fong'.

examples.en: School is closed because of the typhoon.
examples.zh: 因為颱風，學校停課了。

examples.en: A typhoon is coming this weekend.
examples.zh: 這個週末有颱風要來。

ugly.tip_zh: 第一音節 [ʌ] 嘴巴微開、短促，不要張成中文「阿」那麼大。[gl] 要連在一起：舌根頂住發 [g] 後，舌尖馬上抬起發 [l]，中間不要加母音唸成「阿古利」。重音在第一音節，字尾 y 唸輕短的 [ɪ]。
ugly.tip_en: The first-syllable [ʌ] is short with the mouth only slightly open; don't open it as wide as Mandarin 'a'. Keep [gl] together: after the back of the tongue makes [g], lift the tongue tip right away for [l], with no vowel between ('a-gu-li'). Stress the first syllable; the final y is a light, short [ɪ].

examples.en: The ugly duckling became a beautiful swan.
examples.zh: 醜小鴨變成了一隻美麗的天鵝。

examples.en: This old sweater looks ugly, but it's warm.
examples.zh: 這件舊毛衣很醜，但是很暖和。

umbrella.tip_zh: umbrella 一般美式重音在第二音節 [brɛ]，第一音節只是輕輕的 [əm]，常見錯誤是把 um 唸得又重又長。[br] 兩個子音要緊緊相連：雙唇先閉住發 [b]，馬上捲舌接 [r]，中間不要多加母音。[brɛ] 的 [ɛ] 嘴巴半開，跟 bread 的母音一樣；最後的 [lə] 舌尖碰一下上牙齦，輕輕帶過。
umbrella.tip_en: In standard American English, umbrella is stressed on the second syllable [brɛ]; the first syllable is only a light [əm], and a common mistake is making um heavy and long. The two consonants [br] must be joined tightly: close the lips for [b], then curl the tongue right away for [r], with no extra vowel between them. The [ɛ] in [brɛ] has the mouth half open, the same vowel as bread; the final [lə] is a quick touch of the tongue tip on the upper gum ridge, said lightly.

examples.en: Don't forget your umbrella today.
examples.zh: 今天別忘了帶雨傘。

examples.en: I shared my umbrella with my friend.
examples.zh: 我和朋友一起撐我的雨傘。

umbrella.variant_zh: 美國南方有些人重音放在第一音節：[ˈʌmˌbrɛlə]。

uncle.tip_zh: uncle 的 n 其實唸 [ŋ]：因為後面接 [k]，舌根要抬起頂住上顎後方，接著在同一個位置放出 [k]。開頭 [ʌ] 要短而放鬆，嘴巴微開，不要唸成張得很大的 [ɑ]。字尾 [kḷ] 是成音節的 l，舌尖往上碰牙齦就收，不要多加母音唸成 [ko]。
uncle.tip_en: The n in uncle is actually [ŋ]: because [k] follows, raise the back of the tongue against the back of the roof of the mouth, then release [k] from the same spot. The opening [ʌ] is short and relaxed, with the mouth slightly open; don't open it into a wide [ɑ]. The final [kḷ] is a syllabic l: lift the tongue tip to the gum ridge and stop there, without adding a vowel to make [ko].

examples.en: My uncle lives in Taichung.
examples.zh: 我叔叔住在台中。

examples.en: My uncle taught me how to ride a bike.
examples.zh: 我叔叔教我騎腳踏車。

uncle.spelling_zh: n 在 k 前面唸 [ŋ]；字尾的 e 不發音。
uncle.spelling_en: The n before k is said [ŋ]; the final e is silent.

under.tip_zh: 第一音節 [ʌn] 嘴巴微開、放鬆，不要唸成嘴巴大開的中文「安」。第二音節 [dɚ] 舌尖從 [d] 的位置直接往後捲成 [ɚ]，不要唸成沒捲舌的「得」。重音在第一音節，第二音節輕而短。
under.tip_en: The first syllable [ʌn] has a slightly open, relaxed mouth, not the wide-open Mandarin 'an'. In the second syllable [dɚ], curl the tongue tip back straight from the [d] position into [ɚ]; don't say a flat 'de' with no curl. Stress the first syllable; the second is light and short.

examples.en: The cat is under the bed.
examples.zh: 貓在床底下。

examples.en: Look under the table for your shoes.
examples.zh: 去桌子底下找找你的鞋子。

understand.tip_zh: understand 的主要重音在最後一個音節 [stænd]，常見錯誤是把重音放在開頭的 un。中間的 [dɚ] 要輕而捲舌。[st] 之間不要加母音，舌尖從 [s] 直接滑到 [t]；[æ] 要下巴往下拉、嘴角往兩邊開，跟 stand、hand 一樣。字尾 [nd] 舌尖頂住上牙齦收住，不要把 [d] 吞掉，也不要多加母音。
understand.tip_en: The main stress of understand is on the last syllable [stænd]; a common mistake is stressing the opening un. The middle [dɚ] is light and r-colored. Don't add a vowel between [s] and [t]; the tongue tip slides straight from [s] to [t]. For [æ], drop the jaw and spread the corners of the mouth, as in stand and hand. Finish [nd] with the tongue tip pressed on the upper gum ridge; don't swallow the [d] or add a vowel.

examples.en: I don't understand this math problem.
examples.zh: 我不懂這題數學題。

examples.en: Do you understand the story?
examples.zh: 你看懂這個故事了嗎？

unhappy.tip_zh: unhappy 的重音在第二音節 [hæ]，下巴要往下拉、嘴巴張大，[æ] 不要唸成較窄的 [ɛ]，否則會像 heppy。un 後面的 [h] 常被吃掉，連成 u-nappy；唸完 [n] 要先吐一口氣發出 [h]，再接 [æ]。字首的 [ʌn] 是次重音，唸清楚但比 [hæ] 輕，最後的 [pɪ] 短而輕，跟 happy 的結尾一樣。
unhappy.tip_en: unhappy is stressed on the second syllable [hæ]: drop the jaw and open the mouth wide; don't narrow [æ] into [ɛ], or it sounds like heppy. The [h] after un is often swallowed, so the word runs together as u-nappy; after [n], breathe out for [h] before [æ]. The prefix [ʌn] takes secondary stress: say it clearly but lighter than [hæ], and the final [pɪ] is short and light, just like the end of happy.

examples.en: The puppy looks unhappy in the rain.
examples.zh: 小狗在雨中看起來不太開心。

examples.en: Don't be unhappy; we can play again tomorrow.
examples.zh: 別不開心，我們明天可以再玩。

unhappy.kk_flag: In GA the prefix normally keeps a full vowel with secondary stress, [ˌʌnˈhæpɪ]; [ən] is only a fast-speech reduction.

uniform.tip_zh: uniform 開頭的 u 要唸 [ju]，跟 you 一樣，前面有一個 [j] 的滑音，不能只唸 [u]。重音在第一音節，中間的 [nə] 要輕而短，不要照拼字唸成清楚的 [ni]。最後一音節 [fɔrm]：上排牙齒輕碰下唇發 [f]，嘴唇變圓唸 [ɔ] 再捲舌接 [r]，最後雙唇閉上收 [m]，不要在 [m] 後面多加母音。
uniform.tip_en: The u at the start of uniform is said [ju], like you, with a [j] glide in front; don't say just [u]. The stress is on the first syllable; the middle [nə] is light and short, not a clear [ni] as the spelling suggests. For the last syllable [fɔrm], touch the upper teeth to the lower lip for [f], round the lips for [ɔ], curl the tongue for [r], and finally close the lips for [m], with no extra vowel after [m].

examples.en: We wear a uniform to school on Mondays.
examples.zh: 我們星期一要穿制服上學。

examples.en: My new soccer uniform is blue and white.
examples.zh: 我的新足球制服是藍白色的。

until.tip_zh: 重音在第二音節 [ˈtɪl]，第一音節 [ən] 輕而短，不要唸成重重的「安」。字尾暗 L 要做出來：[ɪ] 之後舌尖頂上牙齦；學生常把 l 唸成「歐」或省掉，聽起來像「安踢」。til 的 [ɪ] 要短，不要拉成長 [i]。
until.tip_en: Stress the second syllable [ˈtɪl]; the first syllable [ən] is light and short, not a heavy 'an'. Make the final dark L: after [ɪ], put the tongue tip on the gum ridge. Learners often turn the l into an 'o' sound or drop it, so it sounds like 'an-ti'. Keep the [ɪ] in til short rather than stretching it to [i].

examples.en: Wait here until I come back.
examples.zh: 在這裡等到我回來。

examples.en: We played outside until dinner time.
examples.zh: 我們在外面玩到晚餐時間。

until.spelling_en: It ends with only one l

up.tip_zh: up 只有兩個音：短促的 [ʌ] 和閉唇的 [p]。[ʌ] 嘴巴微開、舌頭放鬆，不要張成中文「阿」；字尾 [p] 雙唇閉上就停，不要彈出母音唸成「阿普」。在 Stand up! 這種句子裡，up 是句尾重音，要短而有力。
up.tip_en: Up is only two sounds: a short [ʌ] and a closed-lip [p]. For [ʌ] keep the mouth slightly open and the tongue relaxed, not as wide as Mandarin 'a'; for the final [p] close the lips and stop, without popping out a vowel ('a-pu'). In a sentence like Stand up!, up carries the final stress, so make it short and strong.

examples.en: Please stand up and say hello.
examples.zh: 請站起來打個招呼。

examples.en: Look up at the stars!
examples.zh: 抬頭看看星星！

upload.tip_zh: 重音在第一音節 [ˈʌp]，第二音節 load 帶次重音，雙母音 [o] 要圓唇滑完整。[p] 和 [l] 相連，中間不要插母音唸成「阿普—樓」。[ʌ] 嘴巴不要張太大；字尾 [d] 有聲，舌尖頂上牙齦，不要唸成 [t]。
upload.tip_en: Stress the first syllable [ˈʌp]; the second syllable load has secondary stress, with its diphthong [o] fully rounded. Join [p] and [l] with no vowel between them ('a-pu-lou'). Don't open the mouth too wide for [ʌ]; the final [d] is voiced, with the tongue tip on the gum ridge, not a [t].

examples.en: Upload your homework before Friday.
examples.zh: 星期五前把作業上傳。

examples.en: I want to upload this photo.
examples.zh: 我想上傳這張照片。

useful.tip_zh: use 當動詞是 [juz]，但 useful 裡的 s 是無聲的 [s]，不要唸成 [z]。開頭 u 唸 [ju]：先發 [j] 再到 [u]，不要只唸 [u]。字尾 ful 弱讀成 [fḷ]，不要唸成清楚的「佛」或 full [fʊl]。重音在第一音節，第二音節輕輕帶過就好。
useful.tip_en: The verb use is [juz], but in useful the s is a voiceless [s], not [z]. The opening u says [ju]: start with [j], then [u], rather than just [u]. The ending ful is weakened to [fḷ]; don't say a clear 'fo' or full [fʊl]. Stress the first syllable and let the second one pass lightly.

examples.en: A dictionary is very useful.
examples.zh: 字典非常有用。

examples.en: Thanks for the useful tip!
examples.zh: 謝謝你有用的建議！

useful.spelling_zh: s 唸 [s]；字尾 ful 只有一個 l
useful.spelling_en: The s says [s]; the ending ful has one l

usually.tip_zh: usually 中間的 [ʒ] 是中文沒有的音，常被唸成 [ʃ] 或 [dʒ]。做法是先擺出 [ʃ] 的嘴形：嘴唇往前嘟、舌頭靠近但不碰上顎，再讓喉嚨振動，就是 [ʒ]；舌頭全程不碰上顎，所以不會變成 [dʒ]。重音在第一音節 [ju]，後面的音節都要又輕又快。
usually.tip_en: The [ʒ] in the middle of usually is a sound Mandarin lacks, and it is often said as [ʃ] or [dʒ]. Set up the mouth for [ʃ]: lips pushed forward, tongue close to but not touching the roof of the mouth; then add voice from the throat, and that is [ʒ]. The tongue never touches the roof of the mouth, so it doesn't become [dʒ]. The stress is on the first syllable [ju]; the syllables after it are all light and quick.

examples.en: I usually walk to school with my brother.
examples.zh: 我通常和哥哥一起走路上學。

examples.en: We usually eat noodles on Sunday.
examples.zh: 我們星期天通常吃麵。

usually.variant_zh: 說快時常縮成三個音節：[ˈjuʒəlɪ]。
usually.variant_en: In fast speech it often shrinks to [ˈjuʒəlɪ].
usually.kk_flag: The [w] is a CMU glide artefact; Taiwan KK dictionaries write [ˈjuʒʊəlɪ] (careful) and fast speech gives [ˈjuʒəlɪ].

vacation.tip_zh: vacation 開頭的 [v] 常被唸成 [w] 或 [b]，因為中文沒有這個音；上排牙齒要輕放在下唇上，喉嚨振動，讓氣從縫隙擠出來。重音在第二音節 [ke]，它和第一音節 [ve] 都是 [e]，嘴角往兩邊拉，跟 cake 的母音一樣。字尾 [ʃən] 的 [n] 要舌尖頂住上牙齦，不要唸成 [ŋ]，和 station 的結尾相同。
vacation.tip_en: The opening [v] of vacation is often said as [w] or [b], because Mandarin has no such sound; rest the upper teeth lightly on the lower lip, let the throat vibrate, and push air through the gap. The stress is on the second syllable [ke]; it and the first syllable [ve] both have [e], with the corners of the mouth pulled sideways, the same vowel as cake. For the [n] in the final [ʃən], press the tongue tip on the upper gum ridge; don't turn it into [ŋ]. It ends the same way as station.

examples.en: We went to the beach for summer vacation.
examples.zh: 暑假我們去了海邊。

examples.en: What did you do on winter vacation?
examples.zh: 你寒假做了什麼？

vegetable.tip_zh: vegetable 照拼字常被唸成四個音節，但美式通常只有三拍：[vɛdʒ]、[tə]、[bḷ]，第二個 e 不發音。開頭 [v] 要上排牙齒輕咬下唇、喉嚨振動，不要唸成 [b] 或 [w]。重音在第一音節，[dʒ] 後面直接接 [t]。字尾 [bḷ] 是成音節的 l，雙唇放開 [b] 後，舌尖直接頂上牙齦唸 [l]，不要多加母音。
vegetable.tip_en: Going by the spelling, vegetable is often said in four syllables, but American English usually has just three beats: [vɛdʒ], [tə], [bḷ]; the second e is silent. For the opening [v], rest the upper teeth lightly on the lower lip and let the throat vibrate; don't say [b] or [w]. The stress is on the first syllable, and [dʒ] goes straight into [t]. The final [bḷ] is a syllabic l: after the lips release [b], the tongue tip goes straight up to the gum ridge for [l], with no vowel added.

examples.en: Broccoli is my favorite vegetable.
examples.zh: 花椰菜是我最喜歡的蔬菜。

examples.en: We made vegetable soup for lunch.
examples.zh: 我們午餐煮了蔬菜湯。

vegetable.spelling_zh: 第二個 e 通常不發音：三個音節，不是四個。
vegetable.spelling_en: The second e is usually silent: three syllables, not four.

very.tip_zh: very 常被唸成 berry 或 wery，因為 [v] 被換成了 [b] 或 [w]。上排牙齒輕放在下唇上，喉嚨振動，讓聲音從縫隙中嗡嗡地出來，雙唇不要合起來。接著 [ɛ] 嘴巴半開，馬上捲舌接 [r]，舌尖不碰上顎、不要彈舌。可以把 very 和 berry 排成一組練習，聽出開頭的差別。
very.tip_en: very is often said as berry or wery, because [v] is replaced by [b] or [w]. Rest the upper teeth lightly on the lower lip and let the throat vibrate so the sound buzzes out through the gap; don't close the lips. Then open the mouth halfway for [ɛ] and curl the tongue right away for [r]; the tongue tip doesn't touch the roof of the mouth and doesn't flap. Practice very and berry as a pair to hear the difference in how they start.

examples.en: Thank you very much for the gift.
examples.zh: 非常謝謝你的禮物。

examples.en: The soup is very hot, so be careful.
examples.zh: 湯很燙，要小心。

video.tip_zh: video 開頭的 [v] 常被唸成 [w] 或 [b]，上排牙齒要輕咬下唇，並讓喉嚨振動。重音在第一音節 [vɪ]，[ɪ] 短而放鬆，不要拉長成 [i]。後面兩個音節 [dɪ] 和 [o] 要輕一點，[dɪo] 跟 radio 的結尾完全一樣；最後的 [o] 嘴唇由圓慢慢收小。
video.tip_en: The opening [v] of video is often said as [w] or [b]; rest the upper teeth lightly on the lower lip and let the throat vibrate. The stress is on the first syllable [vɪ], with a short, relaxed [ɪ]; don't stretch it into [i]. The next two syllables [dɪ] and [o] are lighter; [dɪo] is exactly the end of radio. For the final [o], the lips start round and slowly close.

examples.en: We watched a funny video in English class.
examples.zh: 我們在英文課看了一部好笑的影片。

examples.en: Can I watch one more video, please?
examples.zh: 拜託，我可以再看一部影片嗎？

violin.tip_zh: 重音在最後一個音節 [lɪn]，不在開頭的 [vaɪ]；常見錯誤是把重音放在前面，或把中間的 [ə] 吞掉，變成只有兩拍的 [vaɪlɪn]。開頭 [v] 要用上排牙齒輕碰下唇再出聲，喉嚨震動，不是 [w]，也不是無聲的 [f]。字尾 [n] 用舌尖頂住上排牙齦收住，不要滑成 [ŋ]。
violin.tip_en: The stress is on the last syllable [lɪn], not on the first syllable [vaɪ]. Common mistakes are stressing the front, or swallowing the middle [ə] so the word has only two beats, [vaɪlɪn]. For the opening [v], rest the upper teeth lightly on the lower lip and voice it, with the throat vibrating; it is not [w], and not a voiceless [f]. Finish the final [n] with the tongue tip pressed on the upper gum ridge; don't let it slide into [ŋ].

examples.en: My sister practices the violin every evening.
examples.zh: 我姊姊每天晚上練小提琴。

examples.en: Can you play the violin at the school concert?
examples.zh: 你可以在學校音樂會上拉小提琴嗎？

visit.tip_zh: 開頭 [v] 要用上排牙齒輕碰下唇並震動聲帶，不要唸成 [w] 或 [b]。中間的 s 唸有聲的 [z]，不是 [s]。兩個 i 都是短 [ɪ]，重音在第一音節；字尾 [t] 舌尖頂住就停，不要加母音。
visit.tip_en: For the opening [v], rest the upper teeth lightly on the lower lip and let the voice buzz; don't say [w] or [b]. The middle s is a voiced [z], not [s]. Both i's are short [ɪ], and the stress is on the first syllable; for the final [t] just stop the tongue tip, without adding a vowel.

examples.en: We visit our grandparents every weekend.
examples.zh: 我們每個週末都去看爺爺奶奶。

examples.en: Come and visit us in Taipei!
examples.zh: 來臺北找我們玩！

visitor.tip_zh: 中間的 s 在這裡要唸有聲的 [z]，喉嚨要震動，跟 zoo 的開頭一樣；常見錯誤是照拼字唸成 [s]。開頭 [v] 上排牙齒輕碰下唇，不要發成 [w]。字尾 -or 不唸 [ɔr]，而是輕輕捲舌的 [tɚ]。重音只在第一音節 [vɪ]，後面兩拍要又輕又快。
visitor.tip_en: The s in the middle is the voiced [z] here, with the throat vibrating, like the start of zoo; a common mistake is following the spelling and saying [s]. For the opening [v], rest the upper teeth lightly on the lower lip; don't turn it into [w]. The final -or is not [ɔr] but a light, curled [tɚ]. Only the first syllable [vɪ] is stressed; the other two beats should be light and quick.

examples.en: We had a visitor from Japan in our class today.
examples.zh: 今天我們班上來了一位從日本來的訪客。

examples.en: The visitor brought a gift for my grandma.
examples.zh: 那位訪客帶了一份禮物給我奶奶。

visitor.spelling_en: The s here is said [z], not [s].

voice.tip_zh: [v] 上排牙齒輕碰下唇、聲帶震動；學生常唸成 [w] 或 [b]，就不像 voice 了。oi 是雙母音 [ɔɪ]，嘴巴先圓開再滑到 [ɪ]。字尾 ce 只唸無聲的 [s]，不要變成 [z] 或多加母音。跟 choice 押韻，只差第一個音。
voice.tip_en: For [v], rest the upper teeth lightly on the lower lip with the voice buzzing; learners often say [w] or [b], and it no longer sounds like voice. The oi is the diphthong [ɔɪ]: open and round the mouth, then glide to [ɪ]. The final ce is just a voiceless [s]; don't make it [z] or add a vowel. It rhymes with choice; only the first sound differs.

examples.en: She has a beautiful singing voice.
examples.zh: 她的歌聲很好聽。

examples.en: Please use a quiet voice in the library.
examples.zh: 在圖書館請小聲說話。

voice.spelling_en: ce says [s]; the e is silent

wait.tip_zh: ai 是雙母音 [e]，要從 e 滑到 i；唸太短就成了 wet [wɛt]「濕的」。開頭 [w] 嘴唇先圓起來再放開，不要省略成直接發母音。字尾 [t] 舌尖頂住就停，不要加母音唸成「位特」。
wait.tip_en: The ai is the diphthong [e], gliding from e to i; cut it short and it becomes wet [wɛt]. For the opening [w], round the lips first and then open them, rather than starting straight on the vowel. For the final [t], just stop the tongue tip, without adding a vowel ('wei-te').

examples.en: Please wait for me!
examples.zh: 請等等我！

examples.en: Wait a minute, I'm coming.
examples.zh: 等一下，我來了。

waiter.tip_zh: 第一音節 [we] 要唸出雙母音，嘴角從 e 滑向 i；如果嘴巴張大圓唇，就會變成 water。美式口語中間的 t 常輕彈得像很快的 d；字尾 [ɚ] 舌尖往後捲，不要唸成「特」。重音在第一音節。
waiter.tip_en: Give the first syllable [we] its full diphthong, with the lip corners gliding from e toward i; open and round the mouth and it becomes water. In casual American speech the middle t is often a quick tap like a fast d; for the final [ɚ] curl the tongue tip back instead of saying 'te'. Stress the first syllable.

examples.en: The waiter brought us some water.
examples.zh: 服務生幫我們送來了一些水。

examples.en: Let's ask the waiter for the menu.
examples.zh: 我們跟服務生要菜單吧。

waiter.spelling_zh: ai 唸 [e]，字尾 er 唸 [ɚ]

waitress.tip_zh: 重音在第一音節 [we]，[e] 要從 [e] 滑到 [ɪ]，不要唸成短短的 [ɛ]。第二音節 [trəs] 的 [t] 和 [r] 要黏在一起，中間不加母音，常見錯誤是唸成「威特瑞斯」三四個音節。[tr] 聽起來有點像 [tʃr]，字尾 [s] 是清音，輕輕收掉，不要拉長。
waitress.tip_en: Stress the first syllable [we], gliding [e] toward [ɪ] instead of a short [ɛ]. In the second syllable [trəs], keep [t] and [r] glued together with no vowel between them; a common mistake is turning the word into three or four syllables. [tr] sounds a little like [tʃr]. The final [s] is voiceless — end it lightly, don't stretch it.

examples.en: The waitress brought us two glasses of water.
examples.zh: 女服務生幫我們拿來兩杯水。

examples.en: My aunt works as a waitress on weekends.
examples.zh: 我阿姨週末在當女服務生。

wake.tip_zh: [e] 是會滑動的長母音，嘴型從 [e] 滑向 [ɪ]；學生常唸成短 [ɛ]，聽起來像 wreck 的母音，或縮成「威」。字尾 [k] 要收乾淨，舌根頂住軟顎就停，不要多加母音變成「威克」。和 walk [wɔk]、week [wik] 比較：wake 的嘴巴開度介於兩者之間。
wake.tip_en: [e] is a long, gliding vowel that moves from [e] toward [ɪ]; learners often shorten it to [ɛ] (like the vowel in wreck) or clip it. End cleanly on [k]: press the back of the tongue to the soft palate and stop — don't add a vowel after it. Compared with walk [wɔk] and week [wik], wake's mouth opening sits in between.

examples.en: I wake up at seven every morning.
examples.zh: 我每天早上七點起床。

examples.en: Please don't wake the baby.
examples.zh: 請不要吵醒小嬰兒。

walk.tip_zh: 拼字裡的 l 不發音，常見錯誤是照字母唸成 [wɔlk]。母音 [ɔ] 嘴巴張大、嘴唇微圓，舌頭平放不捲；一捲舌就變成 work [wɝk]（工作），意思完全不同。可以跟 talk 一起練，兩個字只差開頭的子音。字尾 [k] 用舌根輕輕收住，不要在後面多加一個母音。
walk.tip_en: The l in the spelling is silent; a common mistake is reading every letter and saying [wɔlk]. For the vowel [ɔ], open the mouth wide with the lips slightly rounded and keep the tongue flat, not curled; if you curl it, the word becomes work [wɝk] (job), with a completely different meaning. Practice it together with talk: the two words differ only in the first consonant. Close the final [k] lightly with the back of the tongue, and don't add a vowel after it.

examples.en: I walk to school with my brother every day.
examples.zh: 我每天和哥哥一起走路上學。

examples.en: Let's walk the dog after dinner.
examples.zh: 我們晚餐後去遛狗吧。

walk.variant_zh: 不少美國人唸 [wɑk]，嘴唇不圓、嘴巴張更開，兩種都正確。
walk.variant_en: Many Americans say [wɑk], lips unrounded; both are correct.
walk.spelling_zh: l 不發音，跟 talk 一樣。
walk.spelling_en: The l is silent, just as in talk.

wall.tip_zh: wall 的母音是 [ɔ]，嘴巴張大、嘴唇微圓，不是 well 的 [ɛ]。最常見的錯誤是字尾 [l] 沒發，只剩「我」，或多加一個母音唸成「哇露」。[l] 在字尾是暗 L：舌尖輕碰上齒後方的牙齦，舌根往後抬，聲音收在喉嚨，像 ball、tall 的結尾。
wall.tip_en: The vowel in wall is [ɔ] — mouth wide open, lips slightly rounded, not the [ɛ] of well. The most common mistake is dropping the final [l], so only a bare vowel is left, or adding an extra vowel after it. A final [l] is a dark L: the tongue tip lightly touches the ridge behind the upper teeth while the back of the tongue lifts, the same ending as ball and tall.

examples.en: There is a big map on the classroom wall.
examples.zh: 教室的牆上有一張大地圖。

examples.en: We painted the wall light blue.
examples.zh: 我們把牆壁漆成淺藍色。

wallet.tip_zh: 重音在第一音節 [wɔ]，第二音節 [lət] 要唸得又輕又短，母音是弱化的 [ə]。學生常把後半唸成清楚的 let [lɛt]，兩個音節一樣重，聽起來像「哇雷特」。字尾 [t] 只要舌尖頂住牙齦停住，不必用力爆開，也不要加母音。
wallet.tip_en: Stress the first syllable [wɔ]; the second syllable [lət] is quick and light, with a reduced [ə]. Learners often say the second half as a clear let [lɛt], making both syllables equally strong. For the final [t], just stop with the tongue tip on the gum ridge — no strong burst and no added vowel.

examples.en: I left my wallet on the bus.
examples.zh: 我把皮夾忘在公車上了。

examples.en: Dad keeps his money in a brown wallet.
examples.zh: 爸爸把錢放在一個咖啡色皮夾裡。

wallet.variant_zh: 許多美國人唸 [ˈwɑlət]，母音嘴唇不圓。
wallet.variant_en: Many Americans say [ˈwɑlət], with unrounded lips.

want.tip_zh: want 的母音是 [ɑ]，嘴巴張大、不圓唇；不要唸成 won't [wont]，那個 [o] 嘴唇要變圓，意思完全相反（想要 vs 不會）。字尾子音串 [nt] 常被吃掉 [t]，或加母音變成「萬特」。舌尖先頂牙齦發 [n]，原地輕輕停住就是 [t]。
want.tip_en: The vowel in want is [ɑ] — open mouth, unrounded lips. Don't say won't [wont]; that [o] rounds the lips and means the opposite (want vs won't). In the final cluster [nt], learners often drop the [t] or add a vowel after it. Put the tongue tip on the gum ridge for [n], then stop right there to make [t].

examples.en: I want a glass of milk, please.
examples.zh: 我想要一杯牛奶，謝謝。

examples.en: Do you want to play outside?
examples.zh: 你想要去外面玩嗎？

want.variant_en: Some speakers say [wɔnt], with slightly rounded lips.

warm.tip_zh: warm 的母音是 [ɔr]，嘴唇先圓，再把舌尖往後捲；學生常唸成 worm [wɝm]（蟲），那是捲舌的 [ɝ]，嘴巴幾乎不張開。warm 的嘴巴要張得比較大。字尾 [rm] 要兩個都發：捲舌後雙唇閉上發 [m]，不要只剩「我」或加母音。
warm.tip_en: The vowel in warm is [ɔr]: round the lips first, then curl the tongue back. Learners often say worm [wɝm] instead, which uses the r-colored [ɝ] with an almost closed mouth. For warm, open the mouth wider. Pronounce both sounds of [rm]: after the r, close the lips for [m] — don't drop it or add a vowel.

examples.en: It is warm and sunny today.
examples.zh: 今天天氣溫暖又晴朗。

examples.en: Wear a warm coat in winter.
examples.zh: 冬天要穿一件保暖的外套。

warm.spelling_zh: ar 在 w 後面唸 [ɔr]，不是 car 的 [ɑr]。
warm.spelling_en: After w, the letters ar sound [ɔr], not the [ɑr] of car.

wash.tip_zh: 字尾 [ʃ] 是嘴唇往前噘、送出長長氣流的「噓」聲，學生常在後面多加母音，唸成「哇細」或「哇許」。[ʃ] 結束時就讓氣流停下，不要加 [i]。也別和 watch [wɑtʃ] 搞混：wash 的 [ʃ] 可以一直延長，watch 的 [tʃ] 一開始先有舌尖頂住的停頓。
wash.tip_en: The final [ʃ] is a long 'shh' with the lips pushed forward; learners often add a vowel after it. When [ʃ] ends, just let the air stop — no [i] after it. Don't mix it up with watch [wɑtʃ]: the [ʃ] in wash can be stretched, while the [tʃ] in watch begins with a brief stop of the tongue tip.

examples.en: Wash your hands before dinner.
examples.zh: 吃晚餐前要洗手。

examples.en: I help my mom wash the dishes.
examples.zh: 我幫媽媽洗碗。

wash.spelling_zh: a 在 w 後面唸 [ɑ]，不是 cat 的 [æ]。
wash.spelling_en: After w, the a sounds [ɑ], not the [æ] of cat.

watch.tip_zh: 字尾 [tʃ] 是舌尖先頂住上齒齦、再一口氣放開的音，學生常在後面加母音，唸成「哇取」。收尾時氣放出去就停，不要帶出 [i] 或 [u]。和 wash [wɑʃ] 的差別在開頭那一下停頓：watch 的舌尖要先擋住氣流，wash 沒有。母音 [ɑ] 嘴巴張大。
watch.tip_en: The final [tʃ] starts with the tongue tip pressed on the gum ridge, then released in one burst; learners often add a vowel after it. Release the air and stop — no trailing [i] or [u]. The difference from wash [wɑʃ] is that brief stop at the start: in watch the tongue tip blocks the air first; in wash it doesn't. Open the mouth wide for [ɑ].

examples.en: We watch cartoons on Saturday morning.
examples.zh: 我們星期六早上看卡通。

examples.en: My new watch is red and black.
examples.zh: 我的新手錶是紅黑色的。

watch.variant_en: Some speakers say [wɔtʃ], with slightly rounded lips.
watch.spelling_zh: t 不是另一個音，tch 合起來唸 [tʃ]。
watch.spelling_en: The t is not a separate sound; tch together makes [tʃ].

water.tip_zh: 美式發音中，[t] 夾在兩個母音之間會變成輕彈的音：舌尖快速碰一下上排牙齦就離開，聽起來像很輕的 [d]；用力送氣的 [t] 聽起來比較像英式發音。字尾 [ɚ] 一定要捲舌，不能唸成沒捲舌的 [ə]。重音在第一音節 [wɔ]，嘴巴張開、嘴唇微圓。
water.tip_en: In American English, a [t] between two vowels becomes a light tap: the tongue tip quickly touches the upper gum ridge and leaves, sounding like a very light [d]; a strongly aspirated [t] sounds more British. The final [ɚ] must be curled; don't say it as an uncurled [ə]. The stress is on the first syllable [wɔ], with the mouth open and the lips slightly rounded.

examples.en: Please drink some water after you play outside.
examples.zh: 在外面玩完之後，請喝點水。

examples.en: Can I have a glass of water, please?
examples.zh: 可以給我一杯水嗎？

water.variant_zh: 不少美國人第一音節唸 [wɑ]，即 [ˈwɑtɚ]，嘴唇不圓。
water.variant_en: Many Americans say [ˈwɑtɚ], with unrounded lips.

watermelon.tip_zh: 這個字有四拍：主重音在 [wɔ]，[mɛ] 是次重音，其他兩拍要輕。最後的 -on 不要照拼字唸成 [ɑn]，而是輕輕的 [lən]，母音弱到幾乎聽不見，再用舌尖頂住牙齦收 [n]。中間的 [tɚ] 要捲舌，美式的 t 在這裡會輕彈，像很快的 [d]。可以先分成 water 和 melon 兩段練，再連起來。
watermelon.tip_en: This word has four beats: the main stress is on [wɔ], [mɛ] has secondary stress, and the other two beats are light. Don't read the final -on as [ɑn]; it is a light [lən], with a vowel so weak it is almost inaudible, then close the [n] with the tongue tip on the gum ridge. The middle [tɚ] must be curled, and the American t here is a light tap, like a quick [d]. Practice it in two parts, water and melon, then join them.

examples.en: We ate cold watermelon at the beach.
examples.zh: 我們在海邊吃了冰涼的西瓜。

examples.en: This watermelon is big and very sweet.
examples.zh: 這顆西瓜又大又甜。

wave.tip_zh: 字尾 [v] 是最常出錯的地方：學生常唸成 [f]，或嘴唇圓起來變成 [w]，甚至整個掉掉只剩「威」。發 [v] 時上排牙齒輕咬下唇，喉嚨要震動，可以摸著喉嚨確認。[e] 是長母音，要從 [e] 滑到 [ɪ] 再接 [v]，像 save 的結尾。
wave.tip_en: The final [v] is where most mistakes happen: learners say [f], round the lips into a [w], or drop it and stop on the vowel. For [v], rest the upper teeth lightly on the lower lip and let the throat buzz — touch your throat to check. [e] is long, gliding toward [ɪ] before the [v], the same ending as save.

examples.en: We saw a big wave at the beach.
examples.zh: 我們在海邊看到一個大浪。

examples.en: Wave goodbye to Grandma!
examples.zh: 跟奶奶揮手說再見！

wave.spelling_zh: 字尾 e 不發音，讓 a 唸長音 [e]。
wave.spelling_en: The final e is silent; it makes the a say the long [e].

way.tip_zh: way 只有 [w] 加 [e]，但 [e] 要從 [e] 滑到 [ɪ]，嘴角往兩邊拉。學生常把它和 we [wi]、why [waɪ] 唸混：we 嘴型一直是微笑扁平，why 嘴巴先張大，way 介於中間。另一個錯誤是把 [e] 唸成短 [ɛ]，聽起來沒有滑動、太短。
way.tip_en: way is just [w] plus [e], but the [e] glides from [e] toward [ɪ] with the corners of the mouth spreading. Learners mix it up with we [wi] and why [waɪ]: we keeps a flat smile the whole time, why starts with a wide-open mouth, and way sits in between. Another mistake is cutting [e] down to a short [ɛ] with no glide.

examples.en: Which way is the library?
examples.zh: 圖書館要往哪條路走？

examples.en: This is the best way to learn new words.
examples.zh: 這是學新單字最好的方法。

we.tip_zh: [w] 開頭嘴唇先圓、往前噘，接著馬上拉開成微笑的 [i]，並且拉長。常見錯誤是唸成中文的「威」，母音中間多了一個 [e] 的滑動，聽起來反而像 way [we]。唸 we 時，嘴角從圓到扁一次到位，[i] 保持扁平不要再動。
we.tip_en: Start [w] with the lips rounded and pushed forward, then spread them straight into a smiling [i] and hold it. A common mistake is gliding through an extra [e] in the middle, which makes it sound like way [we]. For we, go from round to flat in one move and keep the [i] steady.

examples.en: We go to school by bus.
examples.zh: 我們搭公車上學。

examples.en: We are best friends.
examples.zh: 我們是最好的朋友。

weak.tip_zh: weak 和 week 唸法完全一樣，都是 [wik]，靠前後文分辨。母音 [i] 是長音，嘴角拉開、舌頭往前抬；學生常唸成短的 [ɪ]，聽起來像 wick。字尾 [k] 要清楚收住，不要省略，也不要多加母音變成「威克」，否則聽起來像兩個音節。
weak.tip_en: weak and week sound exactly the same, [wik]; context tells them apart. The [i] is long — spread the lips and raise the front of the tongue. Learners often shorten it to [ɪ], which sounds like wick. Close clearly on [k]: don't drop it, and don't add a vowel after it, or it sounds like two syllables.

examples.en: I felt weak after a long run.
examples.zh: 跑了很久之後我覺得很虛弱。

examples.en: The tea is too weak for Grandpa.
examples.zh: 這杯茶對爺爺來說太淡了。

weak.spelling_zh: ea 唸 [i]，和 week 同音。
weak.spelling_en: The ea says [i]; it sounds the same as week.

wear.tip_zh: wear 是 [wɛr]，母音 [ɛ] 嘴巴半開，再把舌頭往後捲出 [r]。學生常唸成 we're 或 ear 那種 [ɪr]，嘴巴太扁；或者 [r] 沒捲，只剩「威」。wear 和 where 在多數美國人口中同音，和 hair、chair 押韻，可以用這兩個字來練。
wear.tip_en: wear is [wɛr]: half-open mouth for [ɛ], then curl the tongue back for [r]. Learners often say it with the [ɪr] of ear, with the mouth too flat, or skip the [r] entirely. For most Americans, wear and where sound the same, and it rhymes with hair and chair — practice with those.

examples.en: I wear a uniform to school.
examples.zh: 我穿制服上學。

examples.en: Wear your raincoat today.
examples.zh: 今天要穿你的雨衣。

wear.spelling_zh: ear 在這裡唸 [ɛr]，不是 ear 單字的 [ɪr]。
wear.spelling_en: Here ear says [ɛr], not the [ɪr] of the word ear.

weather.tip_zh: 中間的 th 是有聲的 [ð]：舌尖輕輕伸到上下排牙齒之間，一邊送氣一邊讓喉嚨震動。中文沒有這個音，所以常被唸成 [z] 或 [d]。第一音節 [wɛ] 重讀，嘴巴半開；字尾 [ɚ] 要捲舌。weather 和 whether 唸法完全一樣，靠句子分辨意思。
weather.tip_en: The th in the middle is the voiced [ð]: put the tongue tip lightly between the upper and lower teeth, and let the throat vibrate as you push air out. Mandarin has no such sound, so it is often said as [z] or [d]. The first syllable [wɛ] is stressed, with the mouth half open; the final [ɚ] must be curled. Weather and whether sound exactly the same; the sentence tells you which is meant.

examples.en: The weather is sunny and warm today.
examples.zh: 今天天氣晴朗又溫暖。

examples.en: What is the weather like in Taipei?
examples.zh: 台北的天氣怎麼樣？

weather.spelling_zh: ea 在這裡唸短的 [ɛ]，不是 eat 的 [i]。
weather.spelling_en: Here ea is the short [ɛ], not the [i] of eat.

wednesday.tip_zh: 常見錯誤是照拼字唸成三拍的 [wɛd·nɛs·de]。第一個 d 和中間的 e 都不發音，整個字只有兩拍：[wɛnz] 和 [dɪ]。注意 s 唸有聲的 [z]，[n]、[z]、[d] 三個子音要緊緊相連，中間不要加母音。重音在 [wɛnz]，可以先唸 when [wɛn]，再加上 [zdɪ]。
wednesday.tip_en: A common mistake is following the spelling and saying three beats, [wɛd·nɛs·de]. The first d and the middle e are both silent, so the word has only two beats: [wɛnz] and [dɪ]. Note that the s is the voiced [z], and the three consonants [n], [z], [d] must be tightly joined with no vowel between them. The stress is on [wɛnz]; start by saying when [wɛn], then add [zdɪ].

examples.en: We have art class every Wednesday.
examples.zh: 我們每個星期三都有美術課。

examples.en: My piano lesson is on Wednesday afternoon.
examples.zh: 我的鋼琴課在星期三下午。

wednesday.variant_zh: 字尾也常唸成 [de]，即 [ˈwɛnzˌde]，兩種都很普遍。
wednesday.variant_en: The ending is often [de] too: [ˈwɛnzˌde]; both common.
wednesday.spelling_zh: 第一個 d 和 nes 裡的 e 都不發音。
wednesday.spelling_en: The first d and the e in nes are silent.

week.tip_zh: week 的 [i] 要拉長，嘴角往兩邊拉成微笑；最常見的錯誤是唸得太短變成 [ɪ]，聽起來像 wick。字尾 [k] 用舌根頂住軟顎收住，不要省掉，因為 week 和 we 只差這個 [k]。week 和 weak 同音，說 one week 時兩個字的 [w] 都要圓唇。
week.tip_en: Hold the [i] in week long, with the mouth spread in a smile; the most common mistake is making it too short, like [ɪ], which sounds like wick. Close [k] with the back of the tongue against the soft palate — don't drop it, because week and we differ only by that [k]. week sounds the same as weak; in one week, round the lips for both [w] sounds.

examples.en: We have English class three times a week.
examples.zh: 我們一個星期上三次英文課。

examples.en: See you next week!
examples.zh: 下星期見！

week.spelling_zh: ee 唸 [i]，和 weak 同音。
week.spelling_en: The ee says [i]; it sounds the same as weak.

weekend.tip_zh: 重音在第一音節 [wi]，學生常把重音放到 end 上，唸成「威肯德」後面最重。前面 [wi] 要拉長、音調高，後面 [kɛnd] 次重音、稍輕。字尾子音串 [nd] 常被吃掉 [d]，或加母音變成「德」；舌尖頂在牙齦上不動，從 [n] 直接停成 [d]。
weekend.tip_en: Stress the first syllable [wi]; learners often put the stress on end instead. Make [wi] long and higher in pitch; [kɛnd] carries secondary stress and is a little lighter. In the final cluster [nd], the [d] is often dropped or followed by an extra vowel; keep the tongue tip on the gum ridge and go straight from [n] into a stop for [d].

examples.en: What did you do last weekend?
examples.zh: 你上週末做了什麼？

examples.en: We visit Grandma every weekend.
examples.zh: 我們每個週末都去看奶奶。

welcome.tip_zh: 重音在第一音節 [wɛl]，其中的 [l] 很容易被省掉，唸成「威康」。舌尖要先碰到上齒齦發出 [l]，再接舌根的 [k]。第二音節是弱化的 [kəm]，比 come [kʌm] 更輕更短，不要兩個音節一樣重。字尾 [m] 雙唇閉起來。
welcome.tip_en: Stress the first syllable [wɛl]; the [l] is easy to drop. Touch the tongue tip to the gum ridge for [l] before moving to [k] at the back. The second syllable is a reduced [kəm], lighter and shorter than come [kʌm] — don't give both syllables equal weight. Close the lips for the final [m].

examples.en: Welcome to our school!
examples.zh: 歡迎來到我們學校！

examples.en: You are always welcome at our house.
examples.zh: 我們家永遠歡迎你。

welcome.spelling_zh: 拼字是一個 l：welcome，不是 wellcome。
welcome.spelling_en: Spelled with one l: welcome, not wellcome.

well.tip_zh: well 的母音是 [ɛ]，嘴巴半開；學生常唸成 will [wɪl]（太扁）或 wall [wɔl]（太開）。字尾暗 L 常被省略，只剩「威」，或加母音變成「威歐」。結尾時舌尖往上碰上齒齦，舌根同時往後抬，不要再加母音。
well.tip_en: The vowel in well is [ɛ], with a half-open mouth; learners slide into will [wɪl] (too narrow) or wall [wɔl] (too open). The final dark L is often dropped, or followed by an extra vowel. At the end, lift the tongue tip to the gum ridge while the back of the tongue rises — and add nothing after it.

examples.en: She sings very well.
examples.zh: 她唱歌唱得很好。

examples.en: I hope you feel well soon.
examples.zh: 希望你很快就好起來。

west.tip_zh: 字尾子音串 [st] 是重點：學生常省掉 [t] 唸成 wes，或在後面加母音唸成「威斯特」。[s] 送氣後，舌尖直接頂住牙齦停住就是 [t]，中間不要有母音。母音 [ɛ] 嘴巴半開，和 rest、test 押韻。
west.tip_en: The final cluster [st] is the key: learners drop the [t] or add a vowel after it. After the hiss of [s], press the tongue tip to the gum ridge and stop — that is the [t], with no vowel in between. The vowel [ɛ] is half-open; west rhymes with rest and test.

examples.en: The sun sets in the west.
examples.zh: 太陽從西邊落下。

examples.en: Our house is west of the park.
examples.zh: 我們家在公園的西邊。

wet.tip_zh: wet 的母音是短的 [ɛ]，嘴巴半開、不滑動；學生常拉長成 [e]，就變成 wait [wet]（等待）。字尾 [t] 在美式英語常常不爆開，舌尖頂住牙齦就停，但要讓人聽出母音被切斷，不能直接省掉。
wet.tip_en: wet has a short [ɛ] — half-open mouth, no glide. Learners often stretch it into [e], which turns it into wait [wet]. In American English the final [t] is often unreleased: the tongue tip touches the gum ridge and stops. The vowel must still be clearly cut off; don't simply drop the [t].

examples.en: My shoes are wet from the rain.
examples.zh: 我的鞋子被雨淋濕了。

examples.en: Be careful, the floor is wet.
examples.zh: 小心，地板是濕的。

what.tip_zh: KK 的母音是 [ʌ]，嘴巴輕鬆半開、舌頭平放，跟 but、cut 同一個音。字尾 [t] 是重點：美式英語常把舌尖頂住上排牙齦就停住、不爆開，不要在後面多加一個母音唸成兩拍。在 What is 這類句子裡，t 夾在母音之間會輕彈，聽起來像很快的 [d]。
what.tip_en: The KK vowel is [ʌ]: mouth relaxed and half open, tongue flat, the same sound as in but and cut. The key is the final [t]: in American English the tongue tip often just presses on the upper gum ridge and stops without releasing; don't add a vowel after it and make two beats. In phrases like What is, the t sits between vowels and becomes a light tap that sounds like a quick [d].

examples.en: What is your favorite color?
examples.zh: 你最喜歡什麼顏色？

examples.en: What time does the movie start?
examples.zh: 電影幾點開始？

what.variant_zh: 也常聽到嘴巴較開的 [wɑt]；少數人開頭帶 [h]，唸 [hwʌt]。
what.variant_en: Also often [wɑt], mouth wider; a few say [hwʌt].
what.spelling_zh: wh 通常只唸 [w]，h 不發音。
what.spelling_en: wh is usually just [w]; the h is silent.

when.tip_zh: when 的母音是 [ɛ]，嘴巴半開；學生常唸得太扁，聽起來像 win [wɪn]。字尾是舌尖頂住上齒齦的 [n]，不是舌根的 [ŋ]，尾巴不要變成 weng。結尾時舌尖頂住不放，不要放開再加母音。可以用 ten、pen 練同樣的 [ɛn]。
when.tip_en: The vowel in when is [ɛ], with a half-open mouth; learners often make it too narrow, so it sounds like win [wɪn]. The ending is [n] with the tongue tip on the upper gum ridge — not the back-of-tongue [ŋ], so don't let it end like 'weng'. Keep the tongue tip pressed at the end; don't release it into a vowel. Practice the same [ɛn] with ten and pen.

examples.en: When is your birthday?
examples.zh: 你的生日是什麼時候？

examples.en: Call me when you get home.
examples.zh: 你到家的時候打電話給我。

when.variant_zh: 少數美國人唸 [hwɛn]，開頭帶一點 h 的氣音。
when.variant_en: Some Americans say [hwɛn], with a light h breath at the start.
when.spelling_zh: wh 的 h 在多數美式發音不發音。
when.spelling_en: The h in wh is silent for most American speakers.

where.tip_zh: 母音是 [ɛ]，嘴巴半開，不要滑成 way 的 [e]；接著舌頭往後捲成 [r]，整個字只有一拍。常見錯誤是把 [ɛ] 和 [r] 分開唸成兩拍，或字尾完全不捲舌。where 跟 hair、chair、care 押韻，可以一起練；它和 wear（穿）的唸法也一樣。
where.tip_en: The vowel is [ɛ], with the mouth half open; don't let it glide into the [e] of way. Then curl the tongue back for [r]; the whole word is one beat. Common mistakes are splitting [ɛ] and [r] into two beats, or not curling at the end at all. Where rhymes with hair, chair and care, so practice them together; it also sounds the same as wear.

examples.en: Where is my pencil case?
examples.zh: 我的鉛筆盒在哪裡？

examples.en: Where do you want to eat lunch?
examples.zh: 你想去哪裡吃午餐？

where.spelling_zh: wh 的 h 不發音，跟 wear 同音。
where.spelling_en: The h in wh is silent; it sounds the same as wear.

whether.tip_zh: whether 跟 weather 唸法完全相同，只能從句子判斷意思。關鍵在第二音節開頭的 [ð]：舌尖放在上下排牙齒之間，喉嚨震動；唸成 [z] 會聽起來像 [wɛzɚ]，唸成 [d] 會像 [wɛdɚ]。字尾 [ɚ] 是輕輕的捲舌音，舌頭往後捲但不碰上顎。開頭的 wh 只唸 [w]，嘴唇先嘟圓。
whether.tip_en: Whether sounds exactly like weather; only the sentence shows which one is meant. The key is the [ð] that starts the second syllable: tongue tip between the upper and lower teeth, throat vibrating. Said as [z] it sounds like [wɛzɚ]; said as [d] it sounds like [wɛdɚ]. The final [ɚ] is a light curled sound: the tongue curls back without touching the roof of the mouth. The opening wh is just [w]; round the lips first.

examples.en: I don't know whether it will rain today.
examples.zh: 我不知道今天會不會下雨。

examples.en: Ask your mom whether you can come to my party.
examples.zh: 問問你媽媽你能不能來參加我的派對。

whether.spelling_zh: wh 的 h 不發音，所以和 weather 同音。
whether.spelling_en: The h in wh is silent, so it sounds the same as weather.

which.tip_zh: 母音是短的 [ɪ]：嘴巴放鬆、舌頭比 [i] 稍低，時間很短；拉長成 [i] 就會變成 [witʃ]，聽起來不對。字尾 [tʃ] 要把嘴唇往前嘟，舌尖先頂住牙齦再放開送氣，但後面不要加母音變成兩拍。which 和 witch（女巫）同音，跟 rich 押韻，可以一起練。
which.tip_en: The vowel is the short [ɪ]: mouth relaxed, tongue a little lower than for [i], and very short; stretch it into [i] and it becomes [witʃ], which sounds wrong. For the final [tʃ], push the lips forward, press the tongue tip on the gum ridge, then release with a puff of air, but don't add a vowel afterward and make two beats. Which sounds the same as witch and rhymes with rich, so practice them together.

examples.en: Which color do you like better?
examples.zh: 你比較喜歡哪一個顏色？

examples.en: Which book did you read last week?
examples.zh: 你上星期讀了哪一本書？

which.spelling_zh: wh 只唸 [w]，和 witch 同音。
which.spelling_en: wh is just [w]; it sounds the same as witch.

while.tip_zh: [aɪ] 要從嘴巴張大的 [a] 滑到 [ɪ]，然後一定要接字尾暗 L，學生常停在 [aɪ] 就結束，聽起來像 why。發完 [aɪ] 後舌尖往上碰上齒齦、舌根往後抬，聲音收在喉嚨，不要變成「歪喔」多一個母音。可以用 smile、mile 練同樣的結尾。
while.tip_en: Glide [aɪ] from an open [a] to [ɪ], and then you must add the final dark L — learners often stop on [aɪ], so it sounds like why. After [aɪ], lift the tongue tip to the gum ridge and raise the back of the tongue, without adding another vowel. Practice the same ending with smile and mile.

examples.en: Please wait here for a while.
examples.zh: 請在這裡等一下。

examples.en: I read a book while Mom cooked dinner.
examples.zh: 媽媽煮晚餐的時候我在看書。

while.variant_zh: 少數人唸 [hwaɪl]，開頭帶 h 的氣音。
while.variant_en: A few speakers say [hwaɪl], with an h breath at the start.
while.spelling_zh: wh 的 h 通常不發音。
while.spelling_en: The h in wh is usually silent.

white.tip_zh: white 最常見的錯誤是字尾 [t] 沒發，唸成 why；或加母音變成「歪特」。[aɪ] 滑完後舌尖頂住上齒齦，把聲音切斷，美式常常不爆氣。也要和 wait [wet] 分開：white 的嘴巴一開始要張大，wait 只開一半。
white.tip_en: The most common mistake with white is dropping the final [t], so it sounds like why, or adding a vowel after it. After the [aɪ] glide, press the tongue tip to the gum ridge to cut the sound off; Americans often don't release it. Keep it apart from wait [wet]: white starts with a wide-open mouth, wait only half-open.

examples.en: I have a white cat named Snow.
examples.zh: 我有一隻叫「小雪」的白貓。

examples.en: The clouds are big and white.
examples.zh: 雲又大又白。

white.variant_zh: 少數人唸 [hwaɪt]，開頭帶 h 的氣音。
white.variant_en: A few speakers say [hwaɪt], with an h breath at the start.
white.spelling_zh: wh 的 h 通常不發音，字尾 e 也不發音。
white.spelling_en: The h in wh is usually silent, and so is the final e.

who.tip_zh: wh 在這裡只唸 [h]，w 不發音；常見錯誤是照拼字唸成 [wu]。[h] 只是輕輕呼出一口氣，喉嚨不要摩擦，跟注音ㄏ那種從喉嚨後方擠出來的聲音不同。接著嘴唇嘟圓往前推，發長的 [u]，跟 do、new、blue 押韻。
who.tip_en: Here wh is just [h]; the w is silent. A common mistake is following the spelling and saying [wu]. [h] is only a light breath with no friction in the throat, unlike Mandarin ㄏ, which is squeezed out from the back of the throat. Then round the lips and push them forward for a long [u]; it rhymes with do, new and blue.

examples.en: Who is your English teacher?
examples.zh: 你的英文老師是誰？

examples.en: Who wants to play tag with me?
examples.zh: 誰想跟我玩鬼抓人？

who.spelling_zh: w 不發音，wh 在這裡唸 [h]。
who.spelling_en: The w is silent; wh is said [h] here.

whose.tip_zh: whose 的拼字很騙人：wh 在這裡唸 [h]，w 完全不發音，學生常唸成 [w] 開頭。母音是長的 [u]，嘴唇圓而小。字尾是有聲的 [z]，不是 [s]，喉嚨要震動，像蜜蜂嗡嗡聲。whose 和 who's（who is）唸法完全一樣，都是 [huz]。
whose.tip_en: The spelling of whose is misleading: here wh is pronounced [h] and the w is silent, yet learners often start with [w]. The vowel is a long [u] with small, rounded lips. The ending is a voiced [z], not [s] — let the throat buzz like a bee. whose and who's (who is) sound exactly the same: [huz].

examples.en: Whose pencil is this?
examples.zh: 這是誰的鉛筆？

examples.en: I know whose bag that is.
examples.zh: 我知道那是誰的包包。

whose.spelling_zh: w 不發音，wh 唸 [h]；字尾 se 唸 [z]。
whose.spelling_en: The w is silent, so wh says [h]; the final se says [z].

why.tip_zh: 母音 [aɪ] 是雙母音：先把嘴巴張大發 [a]，再往 [ɪ] 滑，嘴巴慢慢合起來。如果嘴巴張得不夠大、滑得不完整，容易跟 way [we] 混淆。開頭 [w] 嘴唇要先嘟圓再放開，不要直接從 [a] 開始。why 跟 buy、cry、dry 押韻，可以一起練。
why.tip_en: The vowel [aɪ] is a diphthong: open the mouth wide for [a], then glide toward [ɪ] as the mouth closes. If the mouth doesn't open wide enough or the glide is incomplete, it is easily confused with way [we]. For the opening [w], round the lips first and then release; don't start straight from [a]. Why rhymes with buy, cry and dry, so practice them together.

examples.en: Why are you late for class today?
examples.zh: 你今天上課為什麼遲到？

examples.en: Why don't we go to the park?
examples.zh: 我們何不去公園呢？

why.spelling_zh: wh 唸 [w]，h 不發音；y 在這裡唸 [aɪ]。
why.spelling_en: wh is said [w] with a silent h; the y here is [aɪ].

wide.tip_zh: wide 的字尾是有聲的 [d]，學生常唸成無聲的 [t]，結果變成 white [waɪt]。分辨的方法是母音長度：[d] 前面的 [aɪ] 要拉長一點，最後舌尖頂住牙齦、喉嚨保持震動。也不要在 [d] 後面加母音變成「歪的」。
wide.tip_en: wide ends in a voiced [d], but learners often devoice it to [t], so it turns into white [waɪt]. The way to keep them apart is vowel length: stretch the [aɪ] a little before [d], then press the tongue tip to the gum ridge while the throat keeps buzzing. Don't add a vowel after the [d] either.

examples.en: The river is very wide.
examples.zh: 這條河很寬。

examples.en: Open your mouth wide, please.
examples.zh: 請把嘴巴張大。

wide.spelling_zh: 字尾 e 不發音，讓 i 唸 [aɪ]。
wide.spelling_en: The final e is silent; it makes the i say [aɪ].

wife.tip_zh: 字尾 [f] 是上排牙齒輕碰下唇送氣，學生常省掉它唸成 why，或加母音變成「歪夫」。[aɪ] 滑完後立刻用牙齒碰下唇，只送氣不出聲。注意複數 wives 的字尾變成有聲的 [vz]，和 wife 的 [f] 不一樣。
wife.tip_en: The final [f] is made by resting the upper teeth on the lower lip and blowing air; learners often drop it, so it sounds like why, or add a vowel after it. Right after the [aɪ] glide, touch the teeth to the lip and push out air with no voice. Note that the plural wives ends in a voiced [vz], unlike the [f] of wife.

examples.en: This is my uncle and his wife.
examples.zh: 這是我叔叔和他的太太。

examples.en: Mr. Lee and his wife run a bakery.
examples.zh: 李先生和他太太開了一家麵包店。

wife.spelling_zh: 字尾 e 不發音；複數拼成 wives。
wife.spelling_en: The final e is silent; the plural is spelled wives.

will.tip_zh: 字尾 [l] 是暗 L：舌尖頂住上排牙齦，舌根同時往後抬。常見錯誤是省略不發，或收成一個像「喔」的母音。母音 [ɪ] 短而放鬆，拉長成 [i] 會變成 wheel 的音。跟 fill、hill、still 押韻，可以一起練。在句子裡常縮成 'll，例如 I'll、we'll。
will.tip_en: The final [l] is a dark L: the tongue tip presses on the upper gum ridge while the back of the tongue lifts. Common mistakes are dropping it, or ending on a vowel like Mandarin 喔 (o). The vowel [ɪ] is short and relaxed; stretching it into [i] makes it sound like wheel. It rhymes with fill, hill and still, so practice them together. In sentences it often contracts to 'll, as in I'll and we'll.

examples.en: I will help you with your homework.
examples.zh: 我會幫你寫功課。

examples.en: We will go to the zoo on Sunday.
examples.zh: 我們星期天會去動物園。

will.variant_zh: 在句子裡不重讀時常弱讀成 [wəl]。
will.variant_en: When unstressed in a sentence it is often weakened to [wəl].

win.tip_zh: win 的母音是短而放鬆的 [ɪ]，學生常唸成長的 [i]，聽起來像 ween。另一個錯誤是字尾唸成舌根的 [ŋ]，變成 wing（翅膀）。win 結尾時舌尖要頂住上齒齦發 [n]；可以把 win 和 wing 對照練習，感受舌頭位置不同。
win.tip_en: The vowel in win is a short, relaxed [ɪ]; learners often make it a long [i], so it sounds like ween. Another mistake is ending with the back-of-tongue [ŋ], which turns it into wing. End win with the tongue tip on the upper gum ridge for [n]; practice win and wing side by side to feel the different tongue positions.

examples.en: I hope our team will win today.
examples.zh: 希望我們這隊今天會贏。

examples.en: Did you win the spelling contest?
examples.zh: 你贏了拼字比賽嗎？

window.tip_zh: 重音在第一音節 [wɪn]，母音是短 [ɪ]，學生常唸成「溫」那種較低較暗的母音。中間 [nd] 要連起來，舌尖頂住牙齦不放。最後的 [o] 是會滑動的長音，嘴唇從半圓收到更圓，不要唸成扁扁的「斗」或拉成 [u]。
window.tip_en: Stress the first syllable [wɪn], with a short [ɪ]; learners often use the lower, darker vowel of Mandarin 溫 there. Join [nd] in the middle by keeping the tongue tip on the gum ridge. The final [o] is a long, gliding vowel — the lips go from half-round to rounder — so don't flatten it or stretch it into [u].

examples.en: Please open the window.
examples.zh: 請打開窗戶。

examples.en: A bird is sitting by the window.
examples.zh: 有一隻鳥停在窗戶旁邊。

window.spelling_zh: 字尾 ow 唸 [o]，w 不另外發音。
window.spelling_en: The final ow says [o]; the w is not a separate sound.

windy.tip_zh: windy 常被唸成「溫蒂」，聽起來就是人名 Wendy [ˈwɛndɪ]。第一音節要用短 [ɪ]，嘴巴比 [ɛ] 更扁、開口更小，重音放在這裡。中間 [nd] 舌尖頂住牙齦一次完成，最後 [dɪ] 輕而短。可以把 wind 和 windy 一起練，前半完全一樣。
windy.tip_en: windy is often said like 溫蒂, which sounds just like the name Wendy [ˈwɛndɪ]. Use a short [ɪ] in the stressed first syllable, with a flatter, smaller mouth opening than [ɛ]. Do [nd] in one move with the tongue tip on the gum ridge, and keep the final [dɪ] light and short. Practice wind and windy together — the first part is exactly the same.

examples.en: It is cold and windy today.
examples.zh: 今天又冷又颳風。

examples.en: Windy days are great for flying kites.
examples.zh: 颳風的日子很適合放風箏。

winter.tip_zh: 重音在第一音節 [wɪn]，第二音節是捲舌的 [ɚ]。學生常把結尾唸成「特」或 [tɑ]，舌頭沒有捲。[t] 之後舌尖要往後捲、嘴巴不要張大，發出像 teacher 結尾的 [ɚ]。第一音節的 [ɪ] 要短，不要唸成「溫」。
winter.tip_en: Stress the first syllable [wɪn]; the second syllable has the r-colored [ɚ]. Learners often end the word with a flat [tɑ]-like sound and no curl. After [t], curl the tongue back and keep the mouth fairly closed, making the same [ɚ] as at the end of teacher. Keep the [ɪ] in the first syllable short — not like Mandarin 溫.

examples.en: We go skiing in winter.
examples.zh: 我們冬天去滑雪。

examples.en: Winter is my favorite season.
examples.zh: 冬天是我最喜歡的季節。

wise.tip_zh: wise 的字尾是有聲的 [z]，學生常唸成無聲的 [s]，或在後面加母音變成「歪子」。發 [z] 時舌頭位置和 [s] 一樣，但喉嚨要震動，像蜜蜂的嗡嗡聲；[z] 前的 [aɪ] 也要拉長一點。和 size、prize 押韻，可以一起練。
wise.tip_en: wise ends in a voiced [z]; learners often devoice it to [s] or add a vowel after it. The tongue is in the same place as for [s], but the throat buzzes like a bee, and the [aɪ] before [z] is a little longer. wise rhymes with size and prize — practice them together.

examples.en: My grandpa is kind and wise.
examples.zh: 我爺爺既親切又有智慧。

examples.en: It was wise to bring an umbrella.
examples.zh: 帶雨傘是明智的決定。

wise.spelling_zh: s 在這裡唸 [z]，字尾 e 不發音。
wise.spelling_en: The s here says [z], and the final e is silent.

wish.tip_zh: wish 的母音是短而放鬆的 [ɪ]，學生常拉長成 [i]，唸成「威許」。字尾 [ʃ] 嘴唇往前噘，送氣後直接停，不要加母音變成「細」。也別和 wash [wɑʃ] 混淆：wish 的嘴巴幾乎不張開，wash 要張大。
wish.tip_en: The vowel in wish is a short, relaxed [ɪ]; learners often stretch it into a long [i]. For the final [ʃ], push the lips forward, blow, and stop — don't add a vowel after it. Don't confuse it with wash [wɑʃ]: wish keeps the mouth nearly closed, while wash opens wide.

examples.en: I wish you a happy birthday!
examples.zh: 祝你生日快樂！

examples.en: Close your eyes and make a wish.
examples.zh: 閉上眼睛許個願。

with.tip_zh: 字尾 th 在這個 KK 是有聲的 [ð]：舌尖伸到上下排牙齒之間，喉嚨震動，然後把音收住。常見錯誤是唸成 [s]、[z]，或乾脆把 th 吞掉，只剩 [wɪ]。前面的 [ɪ] 要短，不要拉成 [i]。with 跟 which、will、wish 只差最後一個子音，可以拿來對照練習。
with.tip_en: In this KK the final th is the voiced [ð]: put the tongue tip between the upper and lower teeth, let the throat vibrate, then end the sound. Common mistakes are saying [s] or [z], or swallowing the th and leaving only [wɪ]. Keep the [ɪ] before it short; don't stretch it into [i]. With differs from which, will and wish only in the last consonant, so use them for contrast practice.

examples.en: I go to school with my best friend.
examples.zh: 我和我最好的朋友一起上學。

examples.en: Can you help me with this math problem?
examples.zh: 你可以幫我解這道數學題嗎？

with.variant_zh: 也常唸成無聲的 [wɪθ]，兩種都正確。
with.variant_en: Also often said with voiceless th, [wɪθ]; both correct.

without.tip_zh: 重音在第二音節 [θaʊt]，學生常把重音放在第一音節。最大的問題是 [θ]：常被唸成 [s]（wi-sout）或 [f]。發 [θ] 時舌尖輕輕放在上下牙齒之間送氣。後面 [aʊ] 從嘴巴張大滑到圓唇，和 about、out 押韻；字尾 [t] 要收住。
without.tip_en: Stress the second syllable [θaʊt]; learners often stress the first. The biggest problem is [θ], often replaced with [s] or [f]. For [θ], rest the tongue tip lightly between the upper and lower teeth and blow. Then [aʊ] glides from a wide-open mouth to rounded lips, rhyming with about and out; close with the [t].

examples.en: I can't sleep without my teddy bear.
examples.zh: 沒有我的泰迪熊我睡不著。

examples.en: He left without his jacket.
examples.zh: 他沒帶外套就走了。

without.variant_en: Also commonly said with a voiced th: [wɪˈðaʊt].

woman.tip_zh: woman 的第一個母音是 [ʊ]，像 book、good 裡那個短而放鬆的音；學生常照拼字唸成 [wo] 或 [wɑ]。重音在第一音節，第二音節是弱化的 [mən]，不是 man [mæn]。也要分清楚複數 women [ˈwɪmɪn]：單複數的差別在第一個母音。字尾 [n] 舌尖頂住牙齦。
woman.tip_en: The first vowel of woman is [ʊ], the short, relaxed sound in book and good; learners often follow the spelling and say [wo] or [wɑ]. Stress the first syllable; the second is a reduced [mən], not man [mæn]. Keep it apart from the plural women [ˈwɪmɪn] — the difference is in the first vowel. End [n] with the tongue tip on the gum ridge.

examples.en: The woman in the red dress is my teacher.
examples.zh: 穿紅色洋裝的那位女士是我的老師。

examples.en: A kind woman helped us find the station.
examples.zh: 一位親切的女士幫我們找到車站。

woman.spelling_zh: o 唸 [ʊ]；複數 women 的 o 卻唸 [ɪ]。
woman.spelling_en: The o says [ʊ]; in the plural women, the o says [ɪ].

wonderful.tip_zh: 開頭 [wʌn] 跟數字 one 的發音一樣，o 唸 [ʌ]，不要照拼字唸成 [wɑn] 或 [won]。中間的 [dɚ] 要捲舌。最後的 -ful 只是很輕的 [fḷ]：上排牙齒輕碰下唇後，舌尖馬上頂到上排牙齦，不要唸成完整的 full [fʊl]，也不要把 [l] 省掉。重音在第一音節。
wonderful.tip_en: The opening [wʌn] sounds exactly like the number one: the o is [ʌ], so don't follow the spelling and say [wɑn] or [won]. The middle [dɚ] must be curled. The final -ful is just a very light [fḷ]: after the upper teeth lightly touch the lower lip, the tongue tip goes straight up to the upper gum ridge; don't say it as the whole word full [fʊl], and don't drop the [l]. The stress is on the first syllable.

examples.en: We had a wonderful time at the beach.
examples.zh: 我們在海邊玩得很開心。

examples.en: What a wonderful picture you drew!
examples.zh: 你畫的圖好棒喔！

wonderful.spelling_zh: won 的 o 唸 [ʌ]，跟 one 同音。
wonderful.spelling_en: The o in won is [ʌ]; it sounds like one.

word.tip_zh: 拼字是 or，但這裡唸捲舌的 [ɝ]，跟 bird、third 押韻；常見錯誤是照 for 的 or 唸成 [wɔrd]，聽起來會像 ward。嘴巴不用張大、嘴唇微圓，舌頭往後捲並一直保持到 [d]。字尾 [d] 舌尖頂住牙齦輕輕收，不要在後面加母音。
word.tip_en: The spelling is or, but here it is the curled [ɝ], rhyming with bird and third. A common mistake is reading it like the or in for and saying [wɔrd], which sounds like ward. Don't open the mouth wide; round the lips slightly, curl the tongue back and hold it until [d]. Close the final [d] lightly with the tongue tip on the gum ridge, and don't add a vowel after it.

examples.en: Can you spell this word for me?
examples.zh: 你可以幫我拼這個字嗎？

examples.en: I learned a new English word today.
examples.zh: 我今天學了一個新的英文單字。

word.spelling_zh: wor 的 or 唸 [ɝ]，不唸 for 的 [ɔr]。
word.spelling_en: The or in wor is [ɝ], not the [ɔr] of for.

work.tip_zh: work 和 walk 常被搞混：work 的 [ɝ] 要捲舌，舌頭往後縮、嘴巴半開；walk 的 [ɔ] 不捲舌、嘴巴張大。如果照拼字把 or 唸成 [ɔr]，聽的人可能以為你說的是 walk。練習時可以兩個字輪流唸，感覺舌頭捲與不捲的差別。字尾 [k] 用舌根頂住上顎收住，不要多加母音。
work.tip_en: Work and walk are often mixed up: the [ɝ] in work is curled, with the tongue pulled back and the mouth half open; the [ɔ] in walk is not curled and the mouth opens wide. If you follow the spelling and say or as [ɔr], listeners may think you said walk. Practice by saying the two words in turn and feel the difference between a curled and a flat tongue. Close the final [k] with the back of the tongue against the roof of the mouth, and don't add a vowel.
